RECAL uses forward KL between an unpruned teacher and a pruned probe to identify teacher-supported predictions disrupted by pruning, then reweights calibration statistics to guide existing pruning criteria toward preserving these predictions. Across multiple models and pruning methods, RECAL consistently improves mathematical reasoning after OPD, achieving gains of up to 16.7 percentage points on AIME, alongside improvements in most code-generation comparisons. Further analysis shows that RECAL reduces residual damage at heavily affected tokens and establishes performance advantages that persist through recovery. These results demonstrate the value of recovery-aware calibration for improving on-policy distillation recovery of pruned reasoning models.
papers.ja_title: ReCal:オンポリシー蒸留の回復を見据えた枝刈り前キャリブレーション
papers.summary: 推論用言語モデルを構造的に枝刈り (structured pruning) して軽量化すると性能が落ち、その後にオンポリシー蒸留 (OPD、生徒自身の出力を使う蒸留) で性能を回復させようとしても枝刈りの損傷が残って回復しにくいという課題があった。本研究の RECAL は枝刈り前のキャリブレーション段階で、枝刈りしていない教師モデルと枝刈り後の試験モデルの KL ダイバージェンスを使い、枝刈りで壊れやすい予測を特定して重み付けし直す。複数のモデルと枝刈り手法で、数学推論ベンチマーク AIME において OPD 後の精度を最大 16.7 ポイント改善した。
papers.why: 枝刈りしたモデルをオンポリシー蒸留で性能回復させる開発者にとって、枝刈り前の準備段階を工夫するだけで後工程の回復効果を大きく上げられるという実践的な知見になる。
papers.summary_en: Structured pruning reduces deployment cost of reasoning language models but degrades capability, and this damage can persist and limit the effectiveness of subsequent on-policy distillation (OPD) recovery. RECAL addresses this by using forward KL between an unpruned teacher and a pruned probe, before pruning, to identify teacher-supported predictions that pruning would disrupt, then reweighting calibration statistics to protect them. Across multiple models and pruning methods, RECAL consistently improves post-OPD mathematical reasoning, with gains of up to 16.7 percentage points on AIME.
papers.why_en: For practitioners doing structured pruning followed by on-policy distillation recovery, this shows that a recovery-aware calibration step before pruning can substantially improve downstream recovery with no architectural changes.

papers.title: RaReCache: Bridging the Gap in Cross-Model KV Cache Reuse via Rank disagreement-based Selective Recomputation
papers.abstract: Cross-model KV-cache reuse remains a key challenge in modern LLM serving. Coding agents and multi-model systems increasingly route a shared context across models: a user may switch models mid-session, or a cascade may escalate a difficult query. Because KV caches contain model-specific representations, each switch typically forces the receiving model to prefill the entire context from scratch. Recent work shows that closed-form linear maps can translate KV caches between models in the same family, but transfer accuracy degrades as the model-size gap widens. In this paper, we establish that these transfer failures are concentrated in a small subset of information-dense tokens. To bridge this gap, we introduce RaReCache, a framework that enables a large target model to decode accurately from a cache prefilled by a much smaller source via selective recomputation. RaReCache identifies these critical positions using a novel rank disagreement metric, scoring each token by the energy of its mapped KV in output directions weakly supported by the calibration data. Across two model families and five benchmarks, on a 23x parameter gap (Qwen3-0.6B to 14B) recomputing just 30% of positions retains 95-99% of the target accuracy, whereas on a 8.8x gap (Llama3-8B to 70B), recomputing 40% retains 96.5% of the target accuracy. RaReCache largely removes sensitivity to source-model size, and achieves up to a 3.04x prefill speedup. For online serving, it handles 1.8x the request throughput of target prefill on a single GPU, and at the target's saturation load, reduces median and 99th-percentile time-to-first-token (TTFT) by 5.0x and 6.4x respectively, with a 30% recompute budget. RaReCache establishes an efficient serving paradigm where small models prefill on behalf of massive targets, enabling large models to recompute only critical tokens, drastically reducing prefill latency.
papers.ja_title: RaReCache:モデル間 KV キャッシュ再利用のためのランク不一致に基づく選択的再計算
papers.summary: コーディングエージェントなどでモデルを切り替えると、KV キャッシュ (注意機構の中間結果) はモデル固有で使い回せず、毎回コンテキスト全体を再計算 (プリフィル) する必要があり無駄が大きかった。本研究の RaReCache は小さいモデルでプリフィルしたキャッシュを大きいモデルに変換する際、「ランク不一致」という指標で変換が失敗しやすい少数の重要トークンを特定し、そこだけ再計算する。パラメータ差 23 倍の Qwen3-0.6B→14B では全体のわずか 30% のトークンを再計算するだけで目標モデルの精度の 95〜99% を保持し、プリフィルを最大 3.04 倍高速化、単一 GPU でのスループットを目標モデル単体の 1.8 倍に、TTFT (最初のトークンが出るまでの時間) を最大 6.4 倍短縮した。
papers.why: マルチモデルサービング基盤を作る人にとって、小さいモデルで事前計算したキャッシュを大きいモデルに部分的に転用することでプリフィルコストを大幅削減できる実用的な手法。
papers.summary_en: When LLM serving systems switch between models mid-session, KV caches are model-specific and typically force a full context reprefill, wasting compute. RaReCache instead lets a much smaller source model prefill the context and transfers the cache to a large target model, using a "rank disagreement" metric to find the small subset of information-dense tokens where transfer fails and recomputing only those. With a 23x parameter gap (Qwen3-0.6B to 14B), recomputing just 30% of positions retains 95-99% of target accuracy, giving up to 3.04x prefill speedup, 1.8x the throughput of target-only prefill on a single GPU, and up to 6.4x lower 99th-percentile time-to-first-token.
papers.why_en: For people building multi-model serving infrastructure, this offers a practical way to reuse cheap small-model prefill work for large target models, cutting prefill latency and cost substantially.

papers.title: Residual Advantage: Student-Relative Teacher Guidance for RL with Verifiable Rewards
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and on-policy distillation (OPD) have become two main paradigms for post-training reasoning models. RLVR gives each response a single outcome label, leaving the steps inside it without separate credit. OPD provides token-level guidance at student-visited prefixes, but its pointwise signal does not directly reflect the pattern of teacher--student disagreement across the vocabulary. Dense, unbounded log-ratio supervision can amplify the teacher's influence, yet a strong solver is not necessarily a suitable guide when the student's solution paths depart from the teacher's. We propose Residual Advantage (\RA{}), which treats the teacher--student probability residual as a bounded one-step reward, subtracts the corresponding state value under the student policy to form a standard advantage, and centers the result within each response before adding it to the verifier advantage. The guidance term has zero mean within each response, so the verifier advantage remains the response's mean label and the teacher only redistributes credit among the steps within it. \CoRA{} further updates a teacher LoRA with verifier advantages on the same scored student batch and uses the updated teacher in the next iteration's residual, adapting guidance to the student's attempts. With Qwen3-1.7B-Base and Qwen3-4B-Base students and a Qwen3-8B teacher, \RA{} combined with GRPO or REINFORCE++ improves the underlying sequence-advantage algorithm in all 24 comparisons on three mathematical benchmarks, raising macro Avg@8 by 1.7--3.6 points and Pass@8 by 3.9--6.3 points. Both combinations surpass teacher-only OPD, and \CoRA{} adds a further 1.0--1.5 Avg@8 points.
papers.ja_title: Residual Advantage:生徒基準で教師を使う RL 後学習の信用割当
papers.summary: 検証可能な報酬での強化学習 (RLVR) は応答全体に1つの正解・不正解ラベルしか与えないため途中の手順に個別の評価ができず、オンポリシー蒸留 (OPD) は各ステップに教師の確率を使うがその信号は強すぎたり生徒の解法と食い違うことがあった。本研究の Residual Advantage (RA) は教師と生徒の確率の差を「有界な1ステップ報酬」とみなし、生徒自身の価値を引いて応答内で中心化することで、教師信号が検証者の評価ラベルを変えずにステップ間の信用だけを再配分するようにした。Qwen3-1.7B/4B を生徒、Qwen3-8B を教師として GRPO や REINFORCE++ と組み合わせたところ、3つの数学ベンチマークの全 24 通りの比較で改善し、平均正解率 (Avg@8) を 1.7〜3.6 ポイント、Pass@8 を 3.9〜6.3 ポイント向上させ、教師のみを使う OPD を上回った。
papers.why: RL 後学習の報酬設計・信用割当を作る人にとって、教師モデルの確率情報を検証者ラベルと衝突させずに各ステップへの信用割当として安全に混ぜ込む具体的な方法を示している。
papers.summary_en: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) gives only one outcome label per response, leaving steps inside without separate credit, while on-policy distillation (OPD) gives token-level teacher guidance that can be too dense/unbounded and may not reflect where the student's own solution path departs from the teacher's. Residual Advantage (RA) treats the teacher-student probability residual as a bounded one-step reward, subtracts the student's own value to form an advantage, and centers it within each response so the verifier's response-level label is preserved while the teacher only redistributes credit among steps. With Qwen3-1.7B/4B students and a Qwen3-8B teacher, RA combined with GRPO or REINFORCE++ improves all 24 comparisons across three math benchmarks, raising macro Avg@8 by 1.7-3.6 points and Pass@8 by 3.9-6.3 points, surpassing teacher-only OPD.
papers.why_en: For those designing reward shaping and credit assignment in RL post-training, this gives a concrete way to mix teacher-probability information into step-level credit without disturbing the verifier's response-level label.

papers.title: ReTeach: Building a Self-Teacher through Multi-Round Reflection and Retry
papers.abstract: Self-distillation can improve reasoning without a separately trained, more capable teacher, but its effectiveness depends on how the self-teacher gains an advantage over the student. Conditioning the teacher on reference answers or solutions can provide such an advantage, but this information may be unavailable. Reflection offers a way to derive explicit error diagnoses and revision guidance from self-generated attempts, yet existing reflection-based methods often combine it with reference information, rich task feedback, or persistent memory. We introduce ReTeach, a Reflective self-distillation framework that constructs its self-Teacher through multi-round reflection and retry using only self-generated attempts and outcome-level verification. Starting from an unsuccessful student rollout, the teacher alternates explicit reflection with renewed attempts until success or the retry budget is exhausted, without reference answers or solutions, external diagnostic feedback, or cross-example memory. Each failed retry informs subsequent reflection, while successful correction provides outcome-level evidence for the potential utility of the resulting teacher context. An outcome-aware selection and weighting strategy distinguishes initially correct, reflection-corrected, and unresolved examples, assigning separate weights to their category-normalized distillation losses. Through on-policy distillation, the student matches the teacher's context-conditioned token-level predictive distributions at prefixes of its own rollouts, transferring the benefits of iterative correction while retaining single-pass inference. Across six benchmarks spanning mathematical reasoning, science question answering, and tool use, ReTeach improves average accuracy over GRPO by 1.39 percentage points.
papers.ja_title: ReTeach:多段階の振り返りと再挑戦で作る自己教師
papers.summary: 正解例などの参照情報なしで自己蒸留 (自分自身をより良い教師に育てて蒸留する手法) の効果を上げるには、生徒より優れた教師をどう作るかが課題だった。本研究の ReTeach は、生徒が失敗した出力から始めて、正解・不正解の判定のみを使い、明示的な「振り返り (reflection)」と再挑戦を複数回繰り返すことで自己教師を構築し、参照解答や外部フィードバック、記憶の蓄積を使わない。最初から正解していた例・振り返りで修正できた例・最後まで解けなかった例を分けて重み付けする蒸留を行い、数学推論・科学QA・ツール利用の6つのベンチマークで GRPO に対して平均正解率を 1.39 ポイント改善した。
papers.why: 参照解答やコストの高いフィードバックが使えない場面で自己蒸留による RL 後学習の性能を上げたい人にとって、振り返りと再挑戦だけで教師の優位性を作る設計指針を示している。
papers.summary_en: Self-distillation can improve reasoning without a separately trained teacher, but it needs some way for the self-teacher to gain an advantage over the student, and reference answers or rich feedback may not be available. ReTeach builds its self-teacher using only self-generated attempts and outcome-level (correct/incorrect) verification, alternating explicit reflection with retries from a failed student rollout until success or budget exhaustion, with no reference answers, external diagnostic feedback, or cross-example memory. By weighting distillation losses differently for initially-correct, reflection-corrected, and unresolved examples, ReTeach improves average accuracy over GRPO by 1.39 percentage points across six benchmarks spanning math, science QA, and tool use.
papers.why_en: For those wanting to improve RL post-training via self-distillation when reference answers or expensive feedback aren't available, this shows a concrete design for building teacher advantage purely from reflection and retry.

papers.title: Smoothing the Top-k Exposure Boundary for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
papers.abstract: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts models scale parameter capacity efficiently while maintaining a fixed compute budget per token. However, traditional training paradigms enforce a static choice of top-$k$ experts, which converts a continuous routing distribution into a rigid step function. This constraint introduces a brittle boundary where highly competitive experts are arbitrarily separated into full-supervision and zero-feedback zones based on minor score fluctuations. To address this issue, we propose Elastic Expert Routing, which stochastically samples the active expert budget from a localized discrete distribution centered at $k$. Over multiple training iterations, this mechanism softens the sharp threshold into a gradual probability distribution. Because the sampling neighborhood remains symmetric, this approach matches the expected computational cost of deterministic training, while preserving the inference budget. During supervised fine-tuning, elastic routing improves downstream macro-averages on OLMoE-1B-7B and Qwen3-30B-A3B by $+0.84$ and $+2.02$ points, respectively. In addition, in from-scratch pretraining, it reduces validation LM loss by up to $0.04$ and outperforms the static top-$k$ baseline by $1.6$ points on average across downstream tasks. Comparisons on Qwen3 fine-tuning and from-scratch pretraining further show higher average scores than Noisy top-$k$, expert FFN dropout, and DefaultMoE.
papers.ja_title: スパース MoE の top-k 境界を滑らかにする Elastic Expert Routing
papers.summary: スパース MoE (専門家混合) モデルでは top-k で専門家を選ぶため、スコアがわずかに違うだけで「完全に学習される専門家」と「一切フィードバックを受けない専門家」に分かれてしまう問題があった。この論文は k を局所的な分布からランダムに選ぶ Elastic Expert Routing を提案し、計算量と推論時のコストは変えずに境界を滑らかにした。結果、SFT (教師あり微調整) では OLMoE-1B-7B で +0.84 点、Qwen3-30B-A3B で +2.02 点改善し、事前学習からの実験でも検証損失が最大 0.04 下がり、静的な top-k より平均 1.6 点上回った。
papers.why: MoE の学習アルゴリズムを作る人にとって、推論コストを変えずにルーティングの学習効率を上げる具体的な手法として使える。
papers.summary_en: Sparse MoE training enforces a rigid top-k boundary, so experts with nearly identical scores are arbitrarily split into fully-supervised and zero-feedback groups. The paper proposes Elastic Expert Routing, which stochastically samples k from a localized distribution to smooth this boundary while matching the expected compute cost and preserving the inference budget. It improves SFT macro-averages by +0.84 and +2.02 points on OLMoE-1B-7B and Qwen3-30B-A3B respectively, and in from-scratch pretraining reduces validation LM loss by up to 0.04 while outperforming static top-k by 1.6 points on average.
papers.why_en: Offers builders of MoE training recipes a concrete way to improve routing learning efficiency without changing inference-time compute cost.

papers.title: Probing for Long-Horizon Deductive Reasoning Capabilities in Language Models with Prolog
papers.abstract: Current frontier LLMs can theoretically process long contexts with 1M tokens or more. But to what extent can they go beyond simple retrieval and perform deeper reasoning over such long contexts? We empirically investigate long-horizon reasoning capabilities of LLMs, focusing on deductive logic expressed in Prolog. We construct ProloNg, a synthetic testbed to probe Prolog Long Reasoning, which systematically varies the complexity (reasoning depth) of problems, where the hardest case has a reasoning depth of 22 and 62k context length. We study 8 reasoning models across 5 families of frontier LLMs, and find that performance degrades substantially as reasoning depth grows, with the majority of models approaching chance beyond depth 10.

papers.title: TAM: Task-Aware Memory Distillation for Efficient Spatiotemporal Prediction
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation enables efficient spatiotemporal prediction by transferring knowledge from an accurate teacher to a compact student. However, matching outputs or features independently for each sample leaves cross-sample predictive structure underused. Exploiting this structure requires representations and historical references that reflect the dynamics of each task. We propose TAM, a Task-Aware Memory Distillation framework that organizes a frozen teacher's knowledge into a bounded, retrievable history. Memory entries encode latent features, forecast changes, or flow residuals, while task-specific selection rules identify relevant historical references. The student either matches the teacher's similarity distribution over shared references or regresses observation-conditioned residual prototypes. These objectives complement supervised prediction and conventional distillation. The teacher, memory, and auxiliary adapters are used only during training, leaving student inference unchanged. We evaluate TAM on video prediction, weather forecasting, and traffic flow prediction across multiple teacher-student configurations. Averaged over four paired runs, adding TAM improves SSIM on all six video datasets and reduces MSE on five relative to the corresponding KD baselines. Mean paired MSE reductions reach 1.86% on KittiCaltech, 1.93% on WeatherBench with a gSTA teacher, and 1.01% on TaxiBJ. These results demonstrate the utility of historical teacher supervision across distinct forecasting tasks without additional student inference cost.

papers.title: Event-Centric Memory with Query-Aware Graph Augmentation for Long-Term Conversational Agents
papers.abstract: For persistent and personalized conversational agents, memory systems can enable them to remember, update, and reason over long histories by storing past interactions and retrieving relevant information. Existing memory systems typically follow two paradigms: flat-structured memory and graph-based memory. The former is lightweight but leaves event relations and state updates implicit, while the latter explicitly models memory structure but incurs additional construction cost and introduces irrelevant relations over long histories. To address these limitations, we propose QGMem, a novel memory construction and activation framework motivated by human memory, in which experience is organized into events and query-relevant events are modeled by graph as working memory. QGMem converts long dialogue histories into event-indexed atomic memory units that preserve individual experiences and consolidates related units into dynamic memory traces that retain state trajectories and current states. When a query arrives, hybrid memory retrieval gathers complementary candidate memories, and query-aware reranking activates the most relevant units as a compact working memory. To expose relational dependencies in the working memory and support conflict-aware reasoning, QGMem organizes the working memory as a local graph, which is then encoded as a graph token and provided to the LLM together with the textual working memory to improve evidence utilization during answer generation. Experiments across six benchmarks validate the framework and show consistent gains in retrieval, multi-hop evidence composition, conflict resolution, and ultra-long dialogue reasoning with compact contexts and moderate inference cost.

papers.title: When History Helps and Hurts: Selective History Use across Multimodal Turns
papers.abstract: Reliable multimodal interaction depends on selective use of conversational history: an earlier question may remain relevant while its previous answer is outdated, whereas a current request may depend on historical evidence despite conflicting new observations. Existing multi-turn evaluations rarely separate these history-use demands from underlying question difficulty. To address this gap, we introduce ReTurn, a benchmark of 7,000 base tasks spanning visual and audio evidence for evaluating selective history use. For task-carrying history, Reconfirm/Reground require applying a historical question to current media while varying historical agreement; for evidence-carrying history, Retrieve/Rebind require answering a current question using historical media while varying current-media competition. Each pair preserves the target question, media, and answer. Tasks support open-ended and multiple-choice evaluation, with matched single-turn counterparts serving as answerability references. Across 13 omni-modal, vision-language, and audio-language models, median model-level open-ended accuracy falls from 93.7% with direct input to 72.3% in conversation. Behavioral probes show that high question recall can coexist with weaker task application, while competing media can redirect answers away from historical targets. Supervised adaptation yields only partial gains. ReTurn provides a controlled framework for assessing whether multimodal models select and use the historical information required by each request.

papers.title: Agentic-TTT: Training test-time policy for test-time training
papers.abstract: Test-time training (TTT) adapts an LLM's parameters using signals derived from test inputs, and can make striking improvements in pre-specified settings such as IMO competitions or designated open problems. By turning deployment experience into parameter updates, TTT provides a direct mechanism for model-level self-improvement. Yet TTT is not universally beneficial: each TTT algorithm works in different settings, and applying an ill-suited method could waste test-time compute or even damage model performance. Therefore, such parameter-level self-improvement requires agency: the model must decide when TTT is warranted, which algorithm to invoke, and whether an existing skill can be reused. To fill this gap, we introduce Agentic-TTT, which learns a test-time policy to govern those decisions. Agentic-TTT turns TTT procedures into callable tools, treats accumulated skills as an evolving deployment environment, and trains its policy using the observed utility gains from its decisions. On our benchmark, Agentic-TTT nearly doubles the utility over the backbone model, learns to trade off utility against compute, and generalizes to domains unseen during training. Together, these results point toward autonomous self-improvement: models that can decide how to learn from their own deployment experience.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: いつテスト時学習を使うべきかを自分で決める Agentic-TTT
papers.summary: テスト時学習 (TTT: テスト入力の信号でモデルの重みを更新する手法) は IMO などの特定の課題で大きく性能を伸ばせるが、場面に合わない手法を使うと計算を無駄にしたり性能を落とすことがある。この論文は、いつ TTT を使うか、どの手法を呼ぶか、既存のスキルを再利用できるかを学習するテスト時方針 Agentic-TTT を提案し、TTT 手順を呼び出し可能な道具として扱い、使った結果の有用性から方針を学ばせた。自作ベンチマークでは、元モデルに比べて有用性をほぼ 2 倍にし、計算量と有用性のトレードオフも学び、学習時に見ていない領域にも一般化した。
papers.why: RL 後学習や自己改善の基盤を作る人にとって、テスト時計算をいつ・どれだけ使うかを方針として学習させる仕組みの具体例になる。
papers.summary_en: Test-time training (TTT) can yield striking gains in specific settings like IMO problems, but applying an ill-suited method can waste test-time compute or even hurt performance. The paper introduces Agentic-TTT, which learns a test-time policy deciding when to invoke TTT, which algorithm to use, and whether to reuse an existing skill, by treating TTT procedures as callable tools and training on observed utility gains. On their benchmark, Agentic-TTT nearly doubles utility over the backbone model, learns to trade off utility against compute, and generalizes to domains unseen during training.
papers.why_en: Gives builders of self-improvement and post-training pipelines a concrete mechanism for learning a policy over when and how much test-time compute to spend.

papers.title: VINCIE-NExT: Unlocking Video Editing from Images via In-Context Modeling
papers.abstract: Building a capable video editor remains significantly harder than a video generator: editing requires (source, instruction, edited) triplets that are prohibitively expensive to annotate and difficult to synthesize at scale, whereas image editing has already reached maturity with millions of such pairs readily available. In this work, we introduce VINCIE-NExT, a unified framework that transfers editing capability from images to videos through in-context visual demonstrations, alleviating the need for large-scale paired video editing data. VINCIE-NExT decomposes video editing into a structured chain of composable sub-tasks (Video -> Image -> Image -> Video), routing editing intent through the image domain and enabling scalable joint training from heterogeneous image and video corpora under a unified diffusion objective. An image editing pair, synthesized by the model or supplied by the user, is prepended as an in-context visual demonstration that serves as a spatial appearance blueprint for every output frame. To ground appearance edits across the interleaved context, we introduce a novel position encoding that links image demonstrations and video frames in a shared spatial coordinate system, enabling pixel-faithful propagation of appearance changes to every output frame. Chain-of-Editing further provides principled test-time scaling: by executing the sub-task chain as progressive diffusion stages, editing quality can be improved by investing additional compute without retraining. Comprehensive experiments on OpenVE-Bench demonstrate the state-of-the-art performance across diverse editing categories, with ablations confirming the effectiveness of each component.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング

papers.title: ReSI: Recursive Safety Improvement toward Resistant and Resilient AI
papers.abstract: Recursive self-improvement, the participation of AI systems in improving their own capabilities, is beginning to move from theoretical prospect to practice, posing both challenges and opportunities for safety alignment. Models evolve through frequent updates, and their safety alignment requires continual adaptation to each new checkpoint. Meanwhile, with evolving red-teaming methods exposing new vulnerabilities, safety improvement for each checkpoint needs to mitigate exposed vulnerabilities and generalize to risks not yet revealed. Following R$^2$AI, we term these goals resistance to known threats and resilience to unforeseen risks. Recursive self-improvement, in turn, inspires an approach to both goals: safety alignment could likewise advance through successive rounds of evaluation and update. We therefore introduce ReSI, a recursive safety improvement framework that implements this approach through automated research. In each round, ReSI applies diverse red-teaming methods to identify vulnerabilities in the current target model, develops training recipes, and promotes the update with the largest safety gain among those passing a Pareto gate on capability retention as the next target model. Across four dense and mixture-of-experts models, ReSI matches or exceeds evaluated frontier models on in-distribution and out-of-distribution safety benchmarks, and outperforms alignment baselines on nearly all safety evaluations while largely preserving general capabilities. In particular, ReSI reduces the mean X-Teaming attack success rate across the four models from 86.01% to 31.45%, well below GPT-5.6-Luna's leading frontier result of 56.69%, indicating stronger resilience to attacks unseen during training. These findings support recursive safety improvement as a practical path toward resistant and resilient AI.
papers.ja_title: 既知の攻撃に強く未知の攻撃にも粘り強い ReSI: 再帰的安全性改善
papers.summary: モデルは頻繁に更新されるため、安全性の調整も各チェックポイントごとに続ける必要があり、既知の攻撃に対する強さ (resistance) と、まだ知られていない攻撃への粘り強さ (resilience) の両方が求められる。この論文は、毎ラウンドで多様なレッドチーム手法で脆弱性を見つけ、学習レシピを作り、能力を保つパレートゲートを通った中で最も安全性が上がった更新を次の対象モデルとする再帰的な枠組み ReSI を提案した。4 つの密モデルと MoE モデルで、X-Teaming 攻撃の成功率の平均を 86.01% から 31.45% まで下げ、フロンティアモデル GPT-5.6-Luna の 56.69% よりも低く抑えた。
papers.why: RL 後学習の基盤を作る人にとって、レッドチーム評価と学習を繰り返して安全性を自動で上げる仕組みと、能力低下とのトレードオフを管理する手法の具体例になる。
papers.summary_en: Because models evolve through frequent updates, safety alignment must continually adapt to each checkpoint, requiring both resistance to known threats and resilience to unforeseen risks. The paper introduces ReSI, a recursive safety improvement framework that each round applies diverse red-teaming to the current model, develops training recipes, and promotes the update with the largest safety gain among those passing a Pareto gate on capability retention. Across four dense and mixture-of-experts models, ReSI reduces the mean X-Teaming attack success rate from 86.01% to 31.45%, well below GPT-5.6-Luna's leading frontier result of 56.69%.
papers.why_en: Offers builders of post-training safety pipelines a concrete pattern of iterative red-teaming plus training with a Pareto gate to improve robustness while largely preserving capability.

papers.title: TokenRouter: Efficient Serving System for Token-Level LLM Routing
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) routing distributes inference work across different models, advancing the cost-quality Pareto frontier of LLM serving. While coarse-grained routing at the session or query level has been widely adopted in production systems, recent algorithmic work shows that fine-grained token-level routing can yield substantial efficiency and quality gains. However, efficiently serving token-level routed inference poses significant challenges to existing systems. Built on single-LLM assumptions, current systems suffer from severe step desynchronization and frequent batch admission delays under token-level routing, and they also impose high implementation complexity on developers. To address these challenges, we design TokenRouter, an efficient and developer-friendly serving system for token-level routed LLM inference. TokenRouter follows the principle of request-centric programming, model-centric execution: developers describe routing logic from the perspective of a single request, while the runtime launches a subserver for each LLM and dispatches requests asynchronously. Each subserver employs a delayed-batching scheduler, whose optimal hyperparameters are derived from a mathematical throughput model of the system. Across diverse routing algorithms, workloads, and model pairs, TokenRouter achieves 2.01-64.15x higher decoding throughput than existing systems, substantially advancing the serving efficiency of token-level LLM routing. Our code is available at https://github.com/thu-nics/TokenRouter.
papers.ja_title: トークン単位でモデルを振り分けるLLMルーティングを高速に動かすサービング基盤
papers.summary: 質問の単語(トークン)ごとに異なる LLM へ振り分けるルーティングは効率と精度を上げられるが、既存のサービング系は 1 つの LLM を前提にしており、ステップのずれやバッチ受け入れの遅延が多発し、実装も複雑だった。TokenRouter は、開発者が 1 つのリクエストの視点でルーティングを書き、実行時にはモデルごとのサブサーバーが非同期に処理する仕組みを作り、スループットの数式モデルから最適な遅延バッチスケジューラを導いた。多様なルーティング手法・負荷・モデル組み合わせで、既存システムより 2.01〜64.15 倍高いデコードスループットを達成した。
papers.why: トークンレベルルーティングという新しい推論スタイルを実運用レベルで動かすためのサービングシステム設計として、分散推論基盤を作る人に直接参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Token-level LLM routing can improve the cost-quality Pareto frontier, but existing single-LLM serving systems suffer severe step desynchronization and batch admission delays, with high implementation complexity. TokenRouter introduces request-centric programming with model-centric execution, running a subserver per LLM with a delayed-batching scheduler whose hyperparameters are derived from a throughput model. Across diverse routing algorithms, workloads, and model pairs, it achieves 2.01-64.15x higher decoding throughput than existing systems.
papers.why_en: The system design for serving token-level routed inference is directly useful for anyone building distributed LLM serving infrastructure.

papers.title: HarnessSQL: Harness-Native Training for SQL Agents in Realistic Database Environments
papers.abstract: Text-to-SQL models are commonly trained to map questions directly to static queries, whereas real-world database agents operate through stateful, multi-turn interaction with live databases -- inspecting schemas, executing probe queries, diagnosing errors, and revising hypotheses. This creates a critical train-deploy mismatch, as the execution harness that mediates this interaction is introduced only at inference time. To bridge this gap, we propose HarnessSQL, a harness-native post-training framework that preserves the full interaction structure throughout both supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning. HarnessSQL builds isolated, executable database environments paired with hidden execution oracles, rolls out teachers directly inside the target SQL harness, and retains only verified trajectories for full-sequence SFT, followed by execution-reward RL. Across Spider 2.0-SQLite, HarnessSQL dramatically boosts the execution accuracy of compact models, raising Qwen3-8B from 15.5% to 45.2% and Qwen3-14B from 22.2% to 54.8%, while transferring effectively to out-of-distribution interactive benchmarks such as BIRD-Interact and LiveSQLBench. Our findings demonstrate that training database agents directly within their execution harness is essential for mastering complex, long-horizon database workflows.
papers.ja_title: 実行ハーネスの中で学習する SQL エージェント訓練法 HarnessSQL
papers.summary: Text-to-SQL モデルは質問から静的なクエリへの変換として学習されるが、実際のデータベースエージェントはスキーマ確認や試しクエリの実行、エラー診断といった多段のやりとり(ハーネス)を通じて動くため、学習時と実運用時でずれが生じていた。HarnessSQL は、教師モデルを実際のハーネス内で動かして検証済みの軌跡だけを使う教師あり微調整を行い、続けて実行結果に基づく報酬で強化学習する枠組みを提案した。Spider 2.0-SQLite で Qwen3-8B の実行精度を 15.5% から 45.2%、Qwen3-14B を 22.2% から 54.8% まで上げ、分布の異なる BIRD-Interact や LiveSQLBench にも効果が移った。
papers.why: 推論時にしか現れない対話的な実行環境を学習の最初から組み込むという RL 後学習の設計方針は、エージェント型タスクの訓練基盤を作る人に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Text-to-SQL models are usually trained to map questions directly to static queries, but real database agents interact statefully with live databases via an execution harness introduced only at inference time, creating a train-deploy mismatch. HarnessSQL rolls out teachers directly inside the target SQL harness, keeps only verified trajectories for full-sequence SFT, and follows with execution-reward RL. On Spider 2.0-SQLite it raises Qwen3-8B from 15.5% to 45.2% and Qwen3-14B from 22.2% to 54.8%, transferring effectively to out-of-distribution benchmarks like BIRD-Interact and LiveSQLBench.
papers.why_en: The practice of preserving the full interaction harness throughout both SFT and RL is directly useful for anyone building post-training pipelines for interactive agent tasks.

papers.title: SparseDecoding: Decoding-Aware Pruning for Accurate and Efficient LLM Inference
papers.abstract: The memory-bound nature of the decoding stage of large language model (LLM) inference incurs significant latency. Layer-wise training-free network pruning approaches guided by the Hessian have been a prominent solution to this problem, as pruning reduces the number of nonzero parameters read from memory during decoding. Nevertheless, typical methods in this line compute the Hessian using pre-collected natural sequences, whereas the model is fed self-generated tokens during decoding, creating a distribution shift between the two sequences. The Hessian calculated on the natural sequence is different from that calculated on the generated sequence. We observe that this discrepancy causes the activation distribution during generation to deviate from that used for pruning, further hurting the pruned model performance. Moreover, most existing LLM pruning methods that bring actual speedup primarily target the sparse matrix-matrix (SpMM) multiplication, providing limited support for the sparse matrix-vector (SpMV) operations, which dominate decoding. To solve these problems, we introduce SparseDecoding, a principled decoding-aware pruning framework tailored for accurate and efficient LLM decoding. Specifically, at the algorithmic axis, SparseDecoding constructs calibration matrices from layer-wise activations collected during the dense-model autoregressive generation, excluding prefill, thereby aligning the pruning objective with the decoding activations. At the system axis, we develop an optimized N:M sparse matrix-vector kernel with bitmask indexing and fixed-step traversal. Substantial empirical results on representative LLMs (Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, Qwen3-14B / 32B) demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms standard fixed-text calibration on the long-form generation benchmarks while achieving up to 1.48x end-to-end wall-clock decoding speedup on A100 GPUs.
papers.ja_title: デコード時の分布に合わせた LLM 枝刈りと専用カーネル SparseDecoding
papers.summary: LLM 推論のデコード段階はメモリ読み込みが遅延の原因(メモリバウンド)になるが、既存のヘシアンに基づく枝刈り(不要な重みを削る手法)は事前収集した自然文でヘシアンを計算するため、実際に自分の生成したトークンを入力にするデコード時の分布とずれて性能が落ちていた。また既存手法は疎行列×行列の高速化が中心で、デコードで主に使う疎行列×ベクトル演算の高速化は不十分だった。SparseDecoding は密モデルの自己回帰生成中の活性化からキャリブレーションを作り、ビットマスク索引と固定ステップ走査による専用カーネルを開発し、Llama-3.1-8B や Qwen3-32B などで長文生成ベンチマークを従来の固定テキストキャリブレーションより一貫して改善し、A100 GPU 上で最大 1.48 倍のデコード高速化を達成した。
papers.why: デコード専用の枝刈り目的設計と疎行列ベクトル積カーネルの組み合わせは、低精度・カーネル最適化による推論高速化を作る人に直結する知見。
papers.summary_en: Decoding in LLM inference is memory-bound, and Hessian-guided training-free pruning typically calibrates on pre-collected natural sequences, creating a distribution shift from the self-generated tokens actually fed during decoding, which hurts pruned-model performance. Most existing pruning methods also target sparse matrix-matrix multiplication, offering limited support for the sparse matrix-vector operations that dominate decoding. SparseDecoding builds calibration matrices from layer-wise activations collected during dense-model autoregressive generation and develops an optimized N:M sparse matrix-vector kernel with bitmask indexing, consistently outperforming fixed-text calibration on long-form generation benchmarks for Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.3-70B, and Qwen3-14B/32B while achieving up to 1.48x end-to-end decoding speedup on A100 GPUs.
papers.why_en: Aligning the pruning calibration objective with actual decoding activations, paired with a dedicated SpMV kernel, is directly useful for engineers optimizing low-precision kernels for inference.

papers.title: Which Skill to Distill? SGUID: Selecting a Compact Skill Bank for Model-Skill Co-Evolution
papers.abstract: Skills, reusable procedural guidance added at inference, can substantially improve LLM downstream performance (Li et al., 2026). Prior work retrieves skills from a bank by semantic relevance, then uses them as inference-time patches or for model distillation. The individual utility of each skill, however, is largely neglected. We first show that, in on-policy distillation where skill-conditioned policies serve as teachers, fewer than 25% of retrieved skills provide useful distillation signals. We then propose SGUID, a method for selecting a compact subset of skills for distillation. SGUID retains a skill only if it consistently yields effective learning signals during training. The selected skills are then distilled to produce a better model. Our results show that not all skills are worth distilling. Across four models from the Olmo and Qwen families, distilling 6 selected skills matches or exceeds full-bank distillation in mean avg@12 on three of the four models, and on all four after a second round that distills 3 newly selected skills, while the full banks are up to 11x larger. Importantly, SGUID supports stable model-skill co-evolution: after a distillation round, a new candidate bank is curated from the updated model's rollouts, and SGUID selects which skills to internalize next. In the second round, this loop selects 3 new skills and improves Qwen3-8B from 64.3% to 66.3%. The selection step is essential for stability: on Qwen3-4B, naively updating the model with unfiltered skills degrades performance, including a 0.3 percentage point drop on HMMT25, whereas SGUID improves HMMT25 by 0.5 points after the first round and 1.1 points after the second. These results identify skill selection as the key mechanism for stable model-skill co-evolution.
papers.ja_title: 蒸留に効くスキルだけを選ぶ SGUID、モデルとスキルの共進化
papers.summary: 推論時に追加できる再利用可能な手順(スキル)はバンクから検索して蒸留に使われるが、個々のスキルの有用性は見過ごされており、検索されたスキルのうち実際に有効な学習信号を与えるのは 25% 未満しかないことが分かった。SGUID は蒸留中に一貫して有効な信号を与えるスキルだけを少数精選する手法で、モデル更新後に新しいロールアウトからスキルバンクを作り直して再度選び直す共進化ループを組む。Olmo と Qwen の 4 モデルで、6 個の精選スキルの蒸留はフルバンク(最大 11 倍の規模)蒸留と同等以上の成績を 4 モデル中 3 モデルで示し、2 周目で 3 個の新スキルを選ぶと 4 モデル全てで上回り、Qwen3-8B は 64.3% から 66.3% に向上した。フィルタなしでスキルを与えると Qwen3-4B では HMMT25 が 0.3 ポイント低下したのに対し、SGUID は 1 周目で 0.5 ポイント、2 周目で 1.1 ポイント改善した。
papers.why: 蒸留用データ(スキル)の個別有用性を測って絞り込むという発想は、強化学習・蒸留のデータ設計を安定させたい人に有用。
papers.summary_en: Reusable procedural skills retrieved by semantic relevance can boost LLM performance when used for distillation, but the individual utility of each skill is largely neglected, and the authors find fewer than 25% of retrieved skills provide useful distillation signals. SGUID selects a compact subset of skills that consistently yield effective learning signals, and supports model-skill co-evolution by re-curating a new candidate bank from the updated model's rollouts. Across four Olmo and Qwen models, distilling 6 selected skills matches or exceeds full-bank distillation (up to 11x larger) on three of four models, and all four after a second round that distills 3 newly selected skills, improving Qwen3-8B from 64.3% to 66.3%; naive unfiltered updates instead degrade Qwen3-4B (e.g. a 0.3-point drop on HMMT25), whereas SGUID improves HMMT25 by 0.5 and then 1.1 points.
papers.why_en: The idea of measuring per-skill utility before including it in distillation is useful for anyone trying to stabilize data design for RL/distillation pipelines.

papers.title: Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization
papers.abstract: Quantizing AdamW's optimizer states reduces persistent storage, but quantization errors propagate through the moment recurrences and perturb subsequent adaptive updates. We redesign 4-bit optimizer-state quantization for AdamW from the perspective of \emph{rounding space}: the coordinate in which a quantizer chooses between adjacent reconstruction levels. For the second moment, a local analysis of the quantization cell adjacent to zero shows that small mean state error need not imply small mean preconditioner error at the next step. A one-dimensional quadratic construction further shows qualitatively different optimization dynamics under state-space and preconditioner-space rounding. These results motivate Zero-Inclusive Preconditioner-space Stochastic Rounding (\textbf{ZIP-SR}), which retains zero in the second-moment codebook and computes stochastic-rounding probabilities in preconditioner space. As a complementary route, Zero-Excluding EDEN calibration (\textbf{ZE-EDEN}) uses a zero-excluding second-moment codebook and rescales the quantized second-moment block to mitigate the preconditioner distortion caused by the positive quantization floor. Both configurations use 4-bit NormalFloat (NF4) for the first moment, with targeted stochastic rounding of the LM-head first moment during the final 10\% of training. Across GPT- and Llama-style pretraining experiments ranging from \textbf{130M} to \textbf{2.7B} parameters, both methods reduce TorchAO 4-bit AdamW's mean validation-loss gap to 32-bit AdamW at every evaluated model size, with the largest reported gap reduction reaching \textbf{70\%}. In full-parameter supervised fine-tuning, both recipes achieve lower validation loss than TorchAO while remaining close to 32-bit AdamW on downstream tasks.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 丸める空間を工夫して AdamW の状態量子化誤差を減らす ZIP-SR
papers.summary: AdamW の最適化状態(モーメント)を 4bit に量子化すると保存容量は減るが、量子化の誤差がモーメントの再帰計算を通じて伝わり、次ステップの適応更新(プレコンディショナー)を乱す。研究チームはゼロに近いセルの解析から、状態の誤差が小さくても次段のプレコンディショナー誤差は小さいとは限らないことを示し、ゼロを残したコードブックでプレコンディショナー空間上で確率的丸めを行う ZIP-SR と、ゼロを除くコードブックで量子化後にスケール補正する ZE-EDEN を提案した。130M から 2.7B パラメータの GPT・Llama 系の事前学習実験で、両手法は TorchAO の 4bit AdamW と 32bit AdamW との検証損失の差を全サイズで縮め、最大 70% の差の削減を達成した。
papers.why: 量子化を「状態空間」でなく「プレコンディショナー空間」で設計し直すという着眼点は、大規模学習のメモリ削減を狙う低精度カーネル開発者に直接使える知見。
papers.summary_en: Quantizing AdamW's optimizer states to 4 bits reduces storage, but quantization errors propagate through the moment recurrences and perturb subsequent adaptive updates. A local analysis near zero shows small mean state error need not imply small mean preconditioner error at the next step, motivating ZIP-SR (zero-inclusive stochastic rounding in preconditioner space) and a complementary ZE-EDEN calibration with a zero-excluding codebook. Across GPT- and Llama-style pretraining from 130M to 2.7B parameters, both methods reduce TorchAO 4-bit AdamW's mean validation-loss gap to 32-bit AdamW at every model size, with the largest reported gap reduction reaching 70%.
papers.why_en: Redesigning quantization from the perspective of 'rounding space' (preconditioner space vs. state space) is directly useful for engineers building low-precision kernels aimed at reducing optimizer memory in large-scale training.

papers.title: One Block, Multiple Depths: Recurrent Vision Transformers with Depth-Programmed Experts
papers.abstract: In this work, we show that a single Transformer block, applied recurrently, can match the accuracy of a full-depth vision encoder at comparable inference FLOPs without intermediate feature distillation. reViT restores depth-specific transformations by representing the FFN at each recurrent depth as a convex combination of a small shared expert bank. A continuous normalized-depth coordinate programs this mixture, defining a resampleable trajectory through FFN parameter space. We evaluate this design in two regimes: supervised ImageNet-1k training and distillation from a DINOv2 teacher. Across both regimes, controlled adaptations identify weight-space merging as the strongest tested MoE family at a matching one-FFN budget, ahead of the token-dispatch and output-mixture alternatives. Trained from scratch, reViT-B/16 attains DeiT III accuracy with about 70\% fewer stored parameters. An 8-experts model distilled using only the teacher's output features retains nearly all of its DINOv2 teacher's linear-probe accuracy and transfers across classification, segmentation, and depth prediction. Elastic-depth training allows one checkpoint (trained model) to operate at multiple tested depths by resampling the same normalized coordinate interval. For fixed-depth deployment, the recurrent block can be materialized as a conventional dense graph, removing online routing and merging without changing the one-FFN-per-depth compute but expanding deployment storage.
papers.ja_title: 1 つのブロックを使い回して深さを可変にする再帰 Vision Transformer reViT
papers.summary: Vision Transformer は層を増やすほど精度が上がるが計算量も増え、1 つのブロックを繰り返し使う再帰的手法は計算量を抑えられるものの層ごとの違う変換ができず精度が落ちやすい。reViT は各再帰深さの FFN(順伝播層)を少数の共有エキスパートの重み付き合成として表し、連続的な深さの座標でその混合比を決める方式を導入した。スクラッチ学習した reViT-B/16 は DeiT III と同等の精度を約 70% 少ないパラメータ保存量で達成し、DINOv2 からの蒸留でも教師の出力特徴だけでほぼ同等のリニアプローブ精度を保ち、分類・セグメンテーション・深度予測にも転移した。
papers.why: 深さを後から選べる再帰モデルの構造設計は、推論コストと精度のトレードオフを柔軟に調整したい人に新しい選択肢を示す。
papers.summary_en: A single Transformer block applied recurrently can reduce compute, but typically cannot reproduce depth-specific transformations and loses accuracy. reViT represents the FFN at each recurrent depth as a convex combination of a small shared expert bank, programmed by a continuous normalized-depth coordinate. Trained from scratch, reViT-B/16 matches DeiT III accuracy with about 70% fewer stored parameters, and an 8-expert model distilled from DINOv2 using only output features retains nearly all of the teacher's linear-probe accuracy while transferring to classification, segmentation, and depth prediction.
papers.why_en: A recurrent block design whose effective depth can be resampled after training offers a new option for engineers who want to flexibly trade inference cost against accuracy.

papers.title: One Model to Loop Them All: Elastic Latent Recurrence for Language Models
papers.abstract: A latent recurrent language model applies a shared block of layers repeatedly, so one checkpoint can trade inference compute for accuracy by changing the loop count. At one loop, however, such models typically fall well short of a non-recurrent model of the same size, a one-loop tax that makes a separate non-recurrent model the better choice whenever latency matters. We present Elastic Latent Recurrence (ELR), a recipe for training looped language models without this tax. At one loop, an ELR model costs the same to serve as a non-recurrent model of the same size and, trained on the same data, reaches similar accuracy. Each additional loop then buys more accuracy for more inference compute. Three choices make this work: a gated state update with a learned step size, loop counts mixed within each optimizer update, and conditioning each pass on its loop index and budget. The first two preserve one-loop accuracy, and the third lowers loss at every additional loop. Mixed depths can be introduced late in pretraining to limit the added training cost, and with zero-initialized conditioning added at the switch, this late schedule reaches lower loss than mixed-depth training from scratch. In MoE models, reusing first-loop expert routes on later loops cuts mixed-depth update time by 11.7% with no measurable change in accuracy. At inference, keeping only the last loop's attention KV cache holds attention KV memory at its one-loop level while retaining most of the gain from additional loops. On 4B dense and 30B-A3B MoE hybrid models, ELR at one loop is 0.52 points below and 1.04 points above its matched baseline on a ten-task average, and four loops add 7.25 and 4.75 points. Carried through post-training, the recipe yields Koi-4B, a single checkpoint that scores an estimated 18 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index at one loop, matching Qwen3.5-4B, and 29 at four loops.
papers.ja_title: 1 ループでも損をしない再帰言語モデル学習法 Elastic Latent Recurrence
papers.summary: 層のまとまりを繰り返し使う潜在再帰モデルは 1 つのチェックポイントでループ回数を変えて推論計算と精度を調整できるが、ループ 1 回では同サイズの通常モデルより精度が劣る「1 ループ税」があり、低遅延が重要な場面では不利だった。ELR はゲート付き状態更新に学習可能なステップ幅を使い、1 回の更新内で複数のループ回数を混ぜて学習し、各処理をループ番号と計算予算で条件づけるという 3 つの工夫を組み合わせた。4B の密モデルと 30B-A3B の MoE モデルで、ELR は 1 ループ時に基準モデルと同等(-0.52〜+1.04 ポイント)の精度を保ちながら、4 ループでは 7.25 ポイントと 4.75 ポイントの向上を得て、後学習後の Koi-4B は 1 ループで Qwen3.5-4B 相当、4 ループでスコアが 29 まで伸びた。
papers.why: 推論時にループ回数を変えるだけで精度と速度を選べる再帰モデルの訓練レシピは、サービング側で動的に計算量を調整したい人にとって実用的な設計指針になる。
papers.summary_en: A latent recurrent language model lets one checkpoint trade inference compute for accuracy via loop count, but at one loop such models typically fall well short of a non-recurrent model of the same size, a 'one-loop tax' that hurts latency-sensitive deployments. Elastic Latent Recurrence (ELR) combines a gated state update with a learned step size, loop counts mixed within each optimizer update, and conditioning each pass on its loop index and budget. On 4B dense and 30B-A3B MoE models, ELR at one loop is 0.52 points below and 1.04 points above its matched baseline on a ten-task average, while four loops add 7.25 and 4.75 points; carried through post-training, Koi-4B scores an estimated 18 at one loop (matching Qwen3.5-4B) and 29 at four loops.
papers.why_en: A training recipe that removes the 'one-loop tax' for recurrent models gives a practical path for serving systems that want to dynamically trade latency against accuracy from a single checkpoint.

papers.title: STAPLE: Static Sparse Upcycling of Pretrained Checkpoints via Embedding Modules
papers.abstract: Sparse computation can scale the parametric capacity of LLMs without proportionally increasing active computation, but pretraining sparse architectures remains expensive and data-hungry. Existing sparse upcycling methods mainly target Mixture-of-Experts models, where expert homogeneity, sample inefficiency, and system overheads can limit practical scalability. Static sparse memory offers predictable access and token-specific updates that can help address these challenges, but naively integrating it into pretrained computation yields poor returns. In this work, we introduce STAPLE, a recipe built upon STEM for integrating static sparse memory into pretrained models. Whereas STEM replaces FFN up-projections with token-indexed embeddings, STAPLE retains them and adds the embeddings as a residual pathway, preserving pretrained computation while learning complementary token-specific information in a scalable manner. On OLMo-2 1B, STAPLE improves over continued dense training by 4.27 points on HumanEval, 2.80 on MBPP, 2.27 on GSM8K, and 1.65 on DROP. Average performance increases with static capacity, and improvements persist on the larger OLMo-2 7B backbone. STAPLE also outperforms static sparse baselines such as STEM and an Engram-style model, and achieves a higher average score than an MoE upcycling baseline while decoding 2x faster with less than half its GPU model memory and measured GPU energy per token in our throughput-oriented decoding evaluation. Importantly, despite introducing billions of parameters late in training, our host-offloaded implementation keeps generation throughput within 1.5% and training throughput within 3% of the dense baseline, while caching only the ~5% most frequent embeddings on GPU. These results show that static sparse memory can provide a sample-efficient, scalable, and sustainable path for expanding pretrained models without sparse pretraining from scratch.
papers.ja_title: 事前学習済みモデルに静的な疎メモリを後付けで統合する STAPLE
papers.summary: 疎な計算(MoE など)は計算量を増やさずにパラメータ容量を増やせるが、疎なアーキテクチャを最初から事前学習するのはコストが高い。トークンごとの埋め込みを使う静的な疎メモリは予測可能なアクセスができるが、既存の事前学習済みモデルにそのまま組み込んでも効果が薄かった。STAPLE は FFN の up-projection をそのまま残し、埋め込みを残差経路として追加することで、学習済みの計算を保ちつつトークン固有の情報を補完的に学習できるようにした。OLMo-2 1B では継続密学習に比べ HumanEval で 4.27 ポイント、MBPP で 2.80 ポイント、GSM8K で 2.27 ポイント、DROP で 1.65 ポイント向上し、デコードは MoE アップサイクリングより 2 倍速く、GPU メモリは半分以下で済み、終盤に数十億パラメータを追加しても生成スループットは密モデルの 1.5% 以内、学習スループットは 3% 以内に保たれた。
papers.why: 既存の事前学習済みモデルに後から疎メモリを統合し、GPU には頻出分だけ(約 5%)をキャッシュするという設計は、分散学習・推論のメモリオフロードを考える人に新しい選択肢を示す。
papers.summary_en: Sparse computation can scale parametric capacity without proportionally increasing active compute, but pretraining sparse architectures from scratch is expensive and data-hungry, and naively integrating static sparse memory into a pretrained model yields poor returns. STAPLE builds on STEM by retaining the FFN up-projection and adding token-indexed embeddings as a residual pathway, preserving pretrained computation while learning complementary token-specific information. On OLMo-2 1B it improves over continued dense training by 4.27 points on HumanEval, 2.80 on MBPP, 2.27 on GSM8K, and 1.65 on DROP, with gains persisting on OLMo-2 7B, decoding 2x faster with less than half the GPU memory of an MoE upcycling baseline, and keeping generation throughput within 1.5% and training throughput within 3% of the dense baseline while caching only about 5% of embeddings on GPU.
papers.why_en: A design that retrofits static sparse memory onto an already-pretrained model, caching only the most frequent embeddings on GPU, offers a new option for anyone designing memory-offloading schemes for distributed training and inference.

papers.title: Kronecker Product Attention: Memory-Efficient KV Compression via Structured Factorization
papers.abstract: Efficient autoregressive generation is increasingly limited by the memory footprint of the key-value (KV) cache, which grows linearly with sequence length, batch size, and model depth. Existing approaches such as Multi-Query Attention (MQA), Grouped-Query Attention (GQA), Multi-Head Latent Attention (MLA), and Tensor Product Attention (TPA) reduce this cost through different trade-offs, but often sacrifice expressivity, require additional positional-encoding machinery, or impose restrictive low-rank structure. We propose Kronecker Product Attention (KPA), which represents key and value activations as sums of Kronecker products of compact, token-dependent matrix factors. KPA strictly generalizes TPA: rank-one vector-outer-product factorization arises as a degenerate Kronecker split, while non-degenerate matrix factors can represent richer block-structured patterns. We further show that a structured rotary embedding operator matched to the Kronecker representation preserves the relative-position property of RoPE while rotating only the compact factors, removing the need for a decoupled RoPE branch as in MLA. Empirically, KPA matches or exceeds TPA, MHA, MQA, GQA, and MLA across four model scales and nine downstream benchmarks under identical training conditions, while achieving up to 10x KV cache compression. The Kronecker head split is a tuneable hyperparameter that allows practitioners to navigate the compression-accuracy trade-off at design time without architectural changes.
papers.ja_title: クロネッカー積アテンションでKVキャッシュを最大10倍圧縮
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルの推論では、生成時に過去情報を保持する「KVキャッシュ」がシーケンス長やバッチサイズに比例して増え、メモリを圧迫する。本研究は、キーとバリューの表現をクロネッカー積 (行列同士の組み合わせ) で表すクロネッカー積アテンション (KPA) を提案し、既存の Tensor Product Attention を特殊な場合として含むよう一般化した。4 つのモデル規模と 9 つの評価タスクで、同じ学習条件のもと MHA・MQA・GQA・MLA・TPA と同等以上の性能を保ちながら、KV キャッシュを最大 10 倍圧縮できることを示した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュ圧縮と位置エンコーディング (RoPE) の両立を、アーキテクチャ変更なしに設計時のハイパーパラメータで調整できる手法で、推論基盤の省メモリ化に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: KV cache memory grows linearly with sequence length, batch size, and depth during autoregressive LLM generation. The paper proposes Kronecker Product Attention (KPA), which represents key/value activations as sums of Kronecker products of compact factors, strictly generalizing Tensor Product Attention (TPA). Across four model scales and nine benchmarks under identical training conditions, KPA matches or exceeds MHA, MQA, GQA, MLA, and TPA while achieving up to 10x KV cache compression.
papers.why_en: A tuneable Kronecker head split lets practitioners navigate the compression-accuracy trade-off at design time without architectural changes, and it removes the need for a decoupled RoPE branch as in MLA.

papers.title: Zebra3D: Efficient Hybrid Foundation Models For Scalable 3D Reconstruction
papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D foundation models reconstruct scenes from unposed images, but the quadratic cost of global attention limits their scalability to large view sets. We present Zebra3D, a layerwise sparse-linear hybrid attention framework that improves the efficiency of pretrained 3D foundation models without training from scratch. Across VGGT, HunyuanWorld-Mirror, and $π^3$, we observe a broadly consistent depth-wise pattern: early stages are relatively tolerant to linear replacement, while sensitive middle-to-late stages tend to exhibit more concentrated attention. Zebra3D exploits this structure by assigning linear-centered attention to tolerant stages and tile-sparse attention to sensitive stages, using landmark summaries to preserve unselected context. Closed-form affine fitting enables training-free conversion, while optional post-conversion training combines task supervision with output and relational feature distillation. Across all three backbones, Zebra3D achieves strong reconstruction and camera-pose accuracy at high attention sparsity, with training-free variants remaining close to their dense counterparts. End-to-end speedups increase with input view count, reaching up to $7.1\times$ at 1,024 views. After post-conversion training, Zebra3D-VGGT reaches 80.5\% RealEstate10K AUC@30 at 94\% mean attention sparsity, within 1.1 percentage points of dense VGGT fine-tuned on the same data and schedule.
papers.ja_title: 層ごとに疎アテンションを使い分けて3D基盤モデルを高速化するZebra3D
papers.summary: 複数画像から3Dシーンを復元する基盤モデルは、画像枚数が増えるとアテンションの計算量が二乗で増えて遅くなる。本研究は、層ごとに「線形アテンション向き」か「疎 (スパース) アテンション向き」かを見分け、事前学習済みモデルを学習なしで変換する Zebra3D を提案した。VGGT など 3 種のモデルに適用し、1024 枚の画像入力で最大 7.1 倍の高速化を達成しつつ、追加学習後は密なアテンションに対して RealEstate10K の AUC@30 で 1.1 ポイント差まで性能を保った。
papers.why: 既存の 3D 基盤モデルをアーキテクチャ変更やフルの再学習なしに高速化できる手法で、視点数の多い推論コストを削減する実務的な指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Feed-forward 3D foundation models suffer from the quadratic cost of global attention as the number of input views grows. Zebra3D is a layerwise sparse-linear hybrid attention framework that converts pretrained 3D foundation models (VGGT, HunyuanWorld-Mirror, π³) training-free, assigning linear attention to tolerant stages and tile-sparse attention to sensitive stages. It reaches up to 7.1x end-to-end speedup at 1,024 views, and after post-conversion training, Zebra3D-VGGT reaches 80.5% RealEstate10K AUC@30 at 94% mean attention sparsity, within 1.1 points of dense fine-tuned VGGT.
papers.why_en: It offers a training-free way to speed up existing 3D foundation models without architectural changes, giving practitioners a practical recipe for scaling view counts.

papers.title: A Categorical Atlas of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning: Cones, Orbits, and Gauges
papers.abstract: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning has hundreds of methods, usually compared by parameter count and benchmark score. We compare them as maps. A pretrained checkpoint is a base point in weight space, and a weight-space method is a smooth map from a small parameter space that starts at that point. These maps form a slice category in which the frozen model is initial and full fine-tuning terminal. Three invariants of the map do most of the work. Its image near the base point governs expressivity, through the first-order image, the dimension, a min-cut bound on rank and whether that point is smooth or an apex. Its fibres, with the optimizer's metric, govern training dynamics. Base change moves the base point and covers splitting initialisations, quantisation, restarts and merging. We prove, for example, that zero-initialised LoRA, and Householder reflection adaptation at its default start under stated rank and parity conditions, begin at the apex of a cone; that no exact initialisation lets LoRA reach an update of rank above twice its own; that exactly orthogonal methods never change a weight's singular values in exact arithmetic, however often they are merged; that under Adam with no epsilon, weight decay or clipping and one shared schedule, LoRA+ from the standard zero initialisation follows exactly the trajectory of plain LoRA with its scale multiplied by the learning-rate ratio; that Adam with shared hyperparameters respects only the signed permutations inside LoRA's continuous symmetry group of full-rank factors; and that the activation function decides when a scaling adapter folds into preceding weights. We classify 382 methods from 138 papers by seven coordinates read off their formulas, with 403 simulation arrows and 485 obstructions. Every numbered result is proved in full, and results due to others are credited where we re-derive them.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: LoRA など382種のパラメータ効率的微調整手法を圏論で整理した地図
papers.summary: パラメータ効率的な微調整 (PEFT) 手法は数百種あり、これまではパラメータ数とベンチマーク精度でしか比較されてこなかった。本研究は、事前学習済みモデルの重みを起点とする写像として各手法を圏論的に捉え、像の次元やランク、学習時の軌道などの数学的な性質から比較する枠組みを示した。例えば、ゼロ初期化の LoRA は厳密な初期化ではその自身のランクの 2 倍を超える更新に到達できないことや、LoRA+ が学習率比だけスケールの異なる通常の LoRA の軌道をそのまま辿ることなどを証明し、138 件の論文から 382 の手法を 7 つの座標で分類した。
papers.why: 手法同士の表現力や学習動態を数式レベルで比較する枠組みで、PEFT 手法の選定や新手法の性質を厳密に評価する研究者に有用。
papers.summary_en: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) has hundreds of methods usually compared only by parameter count and benchmark score. This paper treats each weight-space PEFT method as a map from a small parameter space starting at a pretrained checkpoint, within a slice category, and analyzes invariants such as image dimension, rank, fibres, and base change. The authors prove results such as: zero-initialized LoRA begins at the apex of a cone; LoRA cannot reach an update of rank above twice its own under any exact initialisation; and LoRA+ from standard zero initialisation follows exactly the trajectory of plain LoRA scaled by the learning-rate ratio, classifying 382 methods from 138 papers along seven coordinates.
papers.why_en: It gives a rigorous mathematical framework, beyond parameter count and benchmark score, for comparing the expressivity and training dynamics of PEFT methods, useful for researchers designing or vetting new methods.

papers.title: The Expressive Power of Random-Feature MPNNs Across Graph Sizes
papers.abstract: Continuous random node features increase the expressivity of message-passing neural networks (MPNNs), but existing theoretical analyses are not fine-grained enough to capture their limitations, particularly in approximating functions across graph sizes or under a fixed number of random bits. We develop a population-level framework for size-uniform approximation. For MPNNs with a graph-size-independent Lipschitz bound in their initial features, including standard mean, max, and order-normalized sum architectures, we show that continuous random features can be quantized to finitely many colors with arbitrarily small uniform error in expected output. This reduction lets us transfer limitations on finite-color distinguishability to limitations on size-uniform approximation with continuous random features. We use this framework to prove that these MPNNs are not size-uniformly universal, analyze the expressivity gains from colors and independent trials, and establish incomparability between random-color MPNNs and higher-order Weisfeiler-Leman methods. We also give finite-color MPNN constructions for tree subgraph isomorphism via color coding and a local MST task.

papers.title: Deploying RDMA for Distributed Inference and Training At Scale
papers.abstract: RDMA can reduce communication overhead in distributed machine learning systems, but realizing these benefits in production requires more than replacing TCP. Variable-size messages, concurrent connections, bursty incasts, and service failures introduce challenges that hardware offload alone cannot address. This paper reports our experience deploying ByteExpress, a software communication layer over hardware RDMA, in ByteDance's parameter-server-based inference and training systems. We present three lessons from the deployment: efficient RDMA requires buffer management across application and transport layers; scalable communication requires coordinated management of connections, receive capacity, and outstanding data; and service availability requires recovery above the transport layer. ByteExpress combines an RDMA-aware allocator, zero-copy transfers, QP multiplexing, receive-credit flow control, a software send window, and RPC-assisted recovery. In production inference, ByteExpress reduces mean and P99 model parameter fetch latency by 35.7% and 43.7%, respectively, and total CPU usage by 10.69% compared with kernel TCP. In training, ByteExpress reduces P99 model parameter push latency by up to 74.0% compared with TCP, with no PFC pauses observed at runtime.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: ByteDance の RDMA 通信層 ByteExpress、推論レイテンシを最大 43.7% 削減
papers.summary: RDMA (CPU を介さず直接メモリ転送する通信技術) は分散機械学習の通信コストを減らせるが、TCP を単純に置き換えるだけでは本番運用に必要な性能が出ない。ByteDance は、バッファ管理・接続とフロー制御の協調・輸送層より上での障害回復を組み合わせたソフトウェア通信層 ByteExpress を開発し、パラメータサーバー型の推論・学習システムに本番導入した。推論ではモデルパラメータ取得レイテンシの平均を 35.7%、P99 を 43.7% 削減し CPU 使用率を 10.69% 削減、学習ではパラメータ push の P99 レイテンシを最大 74.0% 削減した。
papers.why: RDMA をハードウェアオフロードだけに頼らず本番運用で成立させるための、バッファ・接続・復旧の設計知見がそのまま分散学習・推論基盤の実装に転用できる。
papers.summary_en: RDMA can cut communication overhead in distributed ML, but realizing the benefit in production requires more than swapping TCP for hardware offload; variable-size messages, bursty incasts, and failures remain unaddressed. ByteDance reports deploying ByteExpress, a software communication layer over RDMA with an RDMA-aware allocator, zero-copy transfers, QP multiplexing, receive-credit flow control, and RPC-assisted recovery, in its parameter-server-based inference and training systems. In production inference it reduces mean and P99 parameter fetch latency by 35.7% and 43.7% respectively and CPU usage by 10.69% versus kernel TCP, and in training it reduces P99 parameter push latency by up to 74.0% versus TCP.
papers.why_en: Their lessons on buffer management, coordinated connection/flow control, and recovery above the transport layer are directly transferable to anyone building RDMA-based distributed training/inference infrastructure.

papers.title: HART: Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time series Foundation Model
papers.abstract: Non-autoregressive multi-step forecasting (NAF) enables time series foundation models to predict an entire future horizon in a single forward pass. Despite its strong sequence modeling capabilities, RWKV-7 exhibits long-horizon degradation in our NAF experiments. In this setup, future patches are represented as missing inputs, requiring the recurrent state to evolve across the prediction horizon without new observations. Our analysis of RWKV-7's generalized delta rule suggests a mechanism we term Placeholder Idling Decay (PID): repeated state transitions can attenuate historical information when placeholder-driven writes provide insufficient compensation. Layer-wise analysis reveals reduced state-injection norms in most layers, while transition-matrix norms remain similar between historical and prediction regions, consistent with PID. Motivated by this analysis, we propose HART, a Hybrid Attention-RWKV Time-series Foundation Model that alternates attention and RWKV blocks, combining direct access to historical tokens with recurrent temporal modeling. Controlled experiments on GIFT-Eval and TIME-Benchmark show that HART improves over pure RWKV at medium and long horizons while maintaining comparable short-horizon performance, and achieves better aggregate performance than a comparably sized pure Transformer. With 36M parameters, HART achieves long-horizon MASE comparable to Toto-2.0-1B on GIFT-Eval (0.752 vs. 0.754), using approximately 1/28 of its parameters.
papers.ja_title: 時系列基盤モデルの長期予測劣化を分析し改善するハイブリッド RWKV-Attention モデル HART
papers.summary: 時系列を一度に全区間予測する「非自己回帰型」予測では、RWKV-7 という再帰型モデルは予測区間が長くなると性能が落ちることが分かった。著者らはこれを、新しい観測がないまま状態遷移が繰り返されることで過去の情報が薄れる「プレースホルダー・アイドリング減衰 (PID)」と名付け、層ごとの分析で原因を特定した。これを踏まえ、アテンション層と RWKV 層を交互に重ねたハイブリッドモデル HART を提案し、GIFT-Eval で 36M パラメータのモデルが 1B パラメータの Toto-2.0 とほぼ同等の長期予測誤差 (MASE 0.752 対 0.754) を、約 1/28 のパラメータ数で達成した。
papers.why: 再帰型モデル特有の長期劣化メカニズムを明らかにし、アテンションと再帰を組み合わせる設計指針を示した点で、軽量な時系列・シーケンスモデルの構造設計に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: In non-autoregressive multi-step forecasting, the recurrent RWKV-7 model degrades at long horizons because future patches are missing inputs and its state must evolve without new observations. The authors identify a mechanism they call Placeholder Idling Decay (PID), where repeated state transitions attenuate historical information when placeholder-driven writes under-compensate, and propose HART, which alternates attention and RWKV blocks. With 36M parameters, HART achieves a long-horizon MASE on GIFT-Eval comparable to the 1B-parameter Toto-2.0 (0.752 vs. 0.754), using about 1/28 of its parameters.
papers.why_en: The PID analysis explains a specific failure mode of recurrent state models at long horizons, and the attention-RWKV hybrid offers a lightweight structural fix applicable to other recurrent sequence foundation models.

papers.title: Surfing the Activation Wave: Analyzing the Information and Geometry of LLM Hidden States for Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Decoder hidden states from different layers of large language models (LLMs) often encode complementary information. However, existing speculative decoding methods typically rely on a small set of target-model layers chosen using fixed, position-based heuristics. Selecting an optimal subset of layers is inherently a combinatorial problem, making exhaustive evaluation infeasible even for moderately deep models. In this work, we present a principled framework for multi-layer hidden-state selection for speculative decoding based on two complementary criteria: informativeness, measured through matrix-entropy analysis, and diversity, quantified using centered kernel alignment (CKA). We investigate layer-wise Shannon entropy, aggregate entropy under hidden-state concatenation, and pairwise CKA dynamics across depth, revealing distinct geometric and informational compartments within decoder representations. Motivated by these findings, we propose entropy and CKA-based layer selection algorithms that favor hidden-state sets that are both highly informative and minimally redundant. As part of this framework, we introduce token-entropy filtering, which removes hidden states associated with low predictive-entropy tokens, thereby improving the quality of layer-selection statistics. In EAGLE3-style speculative decoding, our selected sets outperform fixed baseline choices, including the default $[2, N//2, N-3]$ rule, while providing a clearer explanation of why some defaults can remain competitive. Our results provide a practical recipe for multi-layer hidden-state selection for speculative decoding, insights into the geometry and information in LLM decoder states, and a foundation for extending similar analysis to related applications.
papers.ja_title: どの層の隠れ状態を使うべきか、エントロピーと CKA で選ぶ投機的デコーディング
papers.summary: 投機的デコーディング (小さいモデルで候補トークンを先に作り、大きいモデルで検証して生成を高速化する手法) では、どの層の隠れ状態を使うかは従来固定の位置ルールで決めていた。本研究は、行列エントロピーで測る「情報量」と CKA (層同士の類似度指標) で測る「多様性」の 2 基準で層を選ぶ枠組みを提案し、低エントロピーなトークンの隠れ状態を除くフィルタリングも導入した。EAGLE3 形式の投機的デコーディングで、デフォルトの [2, N//2, N-3] という層選択ルールより良い選択を見つけつつ、なぜそのデフォルトがそこそこ良いのかも説明した。
papers.why: 層選択をヒューリスティックから定量的な基準に置き換えることで、投機的デコーディングの受理率やスループットを改善する実務的な手がかりになる。
papers.summary_en: Speculative decoding typically picks a small, fixed set of target-model layers by position-based heuristics. This work proposes selecting layers by two criteria, informativeness (matrix entropy) and diversity (centered kernel alignment), plus token-entropy filtering to clean up the selection statistics. In EAGLE3-style speculative decoding, the selected layer sets outperform fixed baselines including the default [2, N//2, N-3] rule, while also explaining why that default remains competitive.
papers.why_en: Replacing position-based heuristics with quantitative informativeness/diversity criteria gives a practical recipe for choosing which hidden states to use in speculative decoding, directly improving inference throughput work.

papers.title: CacheFlex: Direct Software-Managed Access to Higher-Level Cache for Scalable Vector Support
papers.abstract: Wider vector/SIMD lanes multiply compute throughput, but cache improvements remain challenging. We identify L1 data cache capacity as the most impactful parameter for performance and efficiency. L1 capacity is constrained by pipeline coupling and latency requirements; private L2 offers an order of magnitude more capacity but is inaccessible from software. This work proposes CacheFlex, an ISA and microarchitecture co-design that enables software-managed, direct access to private L2 SRAM by allowing runtime conversion of parts of L2 into a scratchpad memory (SPM). Through a lightweight ISA extension, software explicitly controls data placement and lifetime within the L2. CacheFlex integrates into an out-of-order pipeline with cross-domain memory consistency and OS context-switch support, with merely 2.02% area overhead relative to the L2 in a post-layout 12 nm implementation. We prototype CacheFlex based on the Armv8-A SVE ISA, model it in gem5, and evaluate it using optimized general matrix multiplication (GEMM) kernels with diverse model-derived shapes, FlashAttention-based fused attention, and full-layer workloads from LLaMA-3.2-1B and BERT-Base in the prefill phase. As the vector length (VL) scales from VL = 4 (512-bit) to VL = 16 (2048-bit), CacheFlex's kernel-level geometric-mean speedup and memory-subsystem energy reduction grow from 1.12x and 26% to 1.44x and 40%, respectively, bridging the widening gap between per-instruction data demand and memory performance. On full transformer layers combining CacheFlex with FlashAttention, the design delivers up to 1.78x speedup and 45% memory-subsystem energy savings (BERT-Base, sequence length T=4096, VL = 16; LLaMA-3.2-1B: 1.64x and 38%). CacheFlex is complementary to hardware prefetching, and its benefit grows as vector width and peak compute throughput increase for compute-intensive AI kernels.
papers.ja_title: L2 キャッシュをスクラッチパッドに変換して SIMD 性能を伸ばす CacheFlex
papers.summary: ベクトル演算の幅 (SIMD レーン) を広げると計算性能は上がるが、L1 データキャッシュの容量はパイプラインの制約で増やせず、ボトルネックになっている。本研究は、容量の大きい L2 キャッシュの一部を実行時にソフトウェアが直接制御できるスクラッチパッドメモリに変換する ISA 拡張 CacheFlex を提案し、12nm 実装でレイアウト後の L2 面積オーバーヘッドを 2.02% に抑えた。GEMM や FlashAttention、LLaMA-3.2-1B・BERT-Base の層全体の評価で、ベクトル幅が 512 ビットから 2048 ビットに広がるほど効果が増し、最大 1.78 倍の高速化と 45% のメモリサブシステム省電力を達成した。
papers.why: ベクトル幅のスケーリングに対してメモリ階層が追いつかないという課題への、ハードウェア・ソフトウェア協調設計の具体的な解法で、カーネル実装者がキャッシュ活用を見直す参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Wider SIMD vector lanes increase compute throughput, but L1 data cache capacity, constrained by pipeline coupling and latency, becomes the bottleneck, while the much larger private L2 is inaccessible from software. CacheFlex is an ISA/microarchitecture co-design that lets software convert part of private L2 SRAM into a scratchpad at runtime, with only 2.02% area overhead relative to L2 in a post-layout 12nm implementation. As vector length scales from 512-bit to 2048-bit, CacheFlex's kernel-level speedup and memory-subsystem energy reduction grow from 1.12x/26% to 1.44x/40%, and on full transformer layers (BERT-Base, LLaMA-3.2-1B) it delivers up to 1.78x speedup and 45% energy savings.
papers.why_en: It addresses the widening gap between per-instruction data demand and memory performance as vector width scales, giving kernel/low-level implementers a concrete hardware-software co-design for AI workloads.

papers.title: MotionCoach: Constructing Multimodal Guidance for Video Professional Motion Editing
papers.abstract: Video editing models achieve strong performance in modifying appearance, backgrounds, styles, and motions, empowered by large-scale training data. Beyond general scenarios, professional motions are significant in performance, sports, and martial arts. This paper focuses on professional motion editing, which involves fine-grained motion technique and temporal structure. Given professional motion names but lacking detailed descriptions, existing models often fail to generate professional motions, such as incorrectly lifting the front wheel under a Stoppie instruction. To address this challenge, we introduce MotionCoach, a trained multimodal agent that uses multi-turn tools and performs self-verification, producing a grounded prompt and a reference clip as reliable and sufficient multimodal guidance to inject external professional motion knowledge into video editing models. To supply training data, we build a data pipeline to construct trajectories. We cold-start the agent on MotionCoach-SFT-10k and apply Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) on MotionCoach-RL-2k with rewards on the motion guidance prompt, the motion outcome video, and the format. For evaluation, we introduce VPMEBench, comprising 314 professional motion editing tasks with fine-grained references and annotations. Extensive experiments show that MotionCoach improves the overall score from 55.1 to 65.6 on Seedance 2.0 and from 51.2 to 64.5 on MiniMax-H3. Learning to construct multimodal guidance enables precise professional motion editing without retraining video editing models.

papers.title: Minions: A Dynamic and Distributed Virtual GPU Cloud Built on Idle Apple Silicon Devices
papers.abstract: The increasing demand for GPU-accelerated machine learning inference has exposed limitations in centralized GPU infrastructures, including high cost, limited elasticity, and long wait times under resource constraints. At the same time, modern Apple Silicon-based macOS devices are equipped with powerful GPUs that remain largely idle during normal usage.
