This paper presents Minions, a dynamic and distributed virtual GPU cloud that aggregates idle Apple Silicon GPUs across macOS devices to execute large-scale machine learning inference workloads. Minions enables teams to leverage existing hardware without requiring additional GPU procurement. The system provides flexible GPU inference task execution, fault tolerance, and efficient resource utilization. Our experience shows that idle macOS devices can be transformed into a practical distributed GPU inference platform in environments where centralized GPU resources are constrained.
papers.ja_title: 遊休 Apple Silicon 端末を束ねた分散 GPU 推論クラウド
papers.summary: 集中管理された GPU 基盤は費用が高く、資源が足りないと待ち時間が長くなるという困りごとがある。この論文は、普段使われていない macOS 機の Apple Silicon GPU を集めて、大規模な機械学習の推論処理をこなす分散型の仮想 GPU クラウド「Minions」を作った。追加の GPU 購入をせずに、故障への耐性と効率的な資源の使い方を両立した推論実行環境を実現できたと報告している。
papers.why: 専用の GPU クラスタに依存せず、既存の端末資源を使って分散推論基盤を作る実例であり、低コストな推論サービング設計の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Centralized GPU infrastructure for ML inference suffers from high cost, limited elasticity, and long wait times. This paper presents Minions, a dynamic and distributed virtual GPU cloud that aggregates idle Apple Silicon GPUs across macOS devices to execute large-scale ML inference workloads, providing flexible task execution, fault tolerance, and efficient resource utilization without requiring additional GPU procurement.
papers.why_en: It offers a concrete example of turning idle end-user hardware into a practical distributed GPU inference platform, useful for people designing low-cost inference serving systems outside centralized GPU clusters.

papers.title: Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization: Closing the State Distribution Gap in Long-Horizon LLM RL
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) has become a dominant paradigm for enhancing LLMs' reasoning capabilities. Yet long-horizon autoregressive rollouts introduce a fundamental limitation: local policy mismatch can compound into severe state distribution shift over trajectories. Existing LLM RL methods, such as GRPO and GSPO, control policy mismatch at the token or sequence level, but overlook this trajectory-induced shift, causing training instability and eventual collapse as the horizon grows. To close the state distribution gap, we propose Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization (TAPO), a principled framework that theoretically derives the state-distribution correction from the off-policy policy gradient and incorporates it into the RL objective. TAPO further employs a geometric-mean estimator for variance reduction, together with a length-aware dynamic clipping that prevents overly deviated updates across the trajectory. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TAPO significantly surpasses existing LLM RL algorithms across eight competition-level benchmarks, achieving up to 48% and 12% improvement over GRPO on mathematical reasoning and algorithmic coding, with substantially enhanced training stability.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 長い推論系列での状態分布のズレを補正する方針最適化 TAPO
papers.summary: LLM の強化学習では、長い系列を自己回帰で生成するうちに、方針の小さなズレが積み重なって状態分布が大きくずれ、学習が不安定になるという困りごとがある。この論文は、オフポリシーの方針勾配から状態分布のズレを補正する項を理論的に導き、分散を抑える幾何平均推定器と系列の長さに応じた動的クリッピングを組み合わせた TAPO を提案した。数学推論で GRPO に比べ最大 48%、アルゴリズムコーディングで最大 12% の改善があり、学習の安定性も大きく向上したという。
papers.why: トークン単位・系列単位の補正しか行わない GRPO や GSPO では見落としていた「軌跡全体のズレ」を扱う補正項を提供し、長期ホライズンの RL 後学習を安定化させる具体的な手段になる。
papers.summary_en: Long-horizon autoregressive rollouts in LLM RL can compound local policy mismatch into severe state distribution shift, causing training instability and collapse as horizon grows. The paper derives a state-distribution correction from the off-policy policy gradient, combined with a geometric-mean variance-reduction estimator and length-aware dynamic clipping, in a method called Trajectory-Aware Policy Optimization (TAPO). Experiments show TAPO achieves up to 48% improvement over GRPO on mathematical reasoning and 12% on algorithmic coding, with substantially enhanced training stability.
papers.why_en: It addresses a trajectory-induced distribution shift that token- or sequence-level corrections like GRPO/GSPO overlook, giving builders of long-horizon LLM RL pipelines a principled stabilization mechanism.

papers.title: Evo$^2$: Evolving the Evolver through Weight-Harness Co-Evolution
papers.abstract: Self-evolving agents are increasingly used to improve language model systems without human intervention through either weight updates or harness improvements. Existing approaches typically pursue these directions separately: some methods update model weights using self-generated experience, while others rewrite the harness that defines how an agent uses prompts, tools, context, and execution feedback. However, these approaches overlook the relationship between model weights and the agent harness. To connect these processes and ensure effective and smooth agent self-evolving, we propose Evo$^2$, a framework for weight-harness co-evolution. For harness updates, we design a unified dual-role pipeline that a single policy serves as both a Proposer, which writes harness edits, and a Reflector, which diagnoses their effects and guides revision. For weight updates, harness modifications and their execution outcomes guide the training of both the Proposer and the Reflector. We further develop EvoTIDE, a training pipeline that recovers usable trajectories through edit extraction and prefix continuation, then combines SFT with interleaved GRPO across the two roles. Extensive experiments across three coding benchmarks demonstrate that Evo$^2$ significantly outperforms existing self-evolution methods. It achieves 82.1% on Polyglot and 48.3% on SWE-bench Verified, compared with 62.6% and 41.0% for the strongest baseline, respectively. We also show that the evolved harnesses transfer to different tasks without further evolution and rank first in cross-benchmark evaluations. Our dual-role harness improvement framework is also able to extend to self-evolution with proprietary models, improving a GPT-5-mini agent's performance from 24.4% to 48.3%. These results demonstrate the applicability of the framework Evo$^2$ across domains and its broad transferability across models and tasks.
papers.ja_title: 重みとハーネスを同時に育てる自己進化エージェント Evo^2
papers.summary: 自己進化エージェントは、モデルの重みを更新する方法とエージェントの動かし方 (ハーネス) を書き換える方法を別々に行っており、両者の関係を活かせていないという困りごとがある。この論文は、1 つのポリシーがハーネスを編集する Proposer と効果を診断する Reflector の二役を担い、その実行結果を使って重みも学習する Evo^2 を提案した。コーディングのベンチマークで Polyglot は 82.1% (最強の既存手法は 62.6%)、SWE-bench Verified は 48.3% (41.0%) まで性能が上がり、GPT-5-mini エージェントでも 24.4% から 48.3% に改善したという。
papers.why: ハーネス設計とモデル重みの学習を結びつけて共進化させる枠組みで、エージェント型の RL 後学習基盤をどう設計するかの新しい手掛かりを与える。
papers.summary_en: Self-evolving agents typically update model weights and rewrite the agent harness separately, overlooking their relationship. The paper proposes Evo^2, a weight-harness co-evolution framework where a single policy serves as both a Proposer (writing harness edits) and a Reflector (diagnosing effects), trained via SFT combined with interleaved GRPO. It achieves 82.1% on Polyglot and 48.3% on SWE-bench Verified versus 62.6% and 41.0% for the strongest baseline, and improves a GPT-5-mini agent from 24.4% to 48.3%.
papers.why_en: It connects harness design and weight training into a co-evolving loop, offering a new way to think about building RL post-training infrastructure for agentic systems.

papers.title: Towards Easier-to-Tune Training Algorithms: New Results from AlgoPerf
papers.abstract: Evaluating deep learning optimizer is challenging because confounding factors such as hyperparameter tuning and optimizer-model co-design often obscure true algorithmic performance. We present results of the updated AlgoPerf V1 benchmark, in which we evaluate a new set of training algorithms on wall-clock time-to-target across nine workloads on fixed hardware. This report focuses on the results of the benchmark's self-tuning ruleset, which requires submissions to use a single configuration across all workloads. Out of the 13 submissions in PyTorch and JAX, Schedule-Free AdamW ranked first. In addition to the wall-clock scores, we also analyze the trade-offs between step efficiency and wall-clock execution, revealing that matrix-preconditioned and two-loop methods achieve good sample efficiency but require more aggressive computational optimizations to be competitive in runtime. Finally, our hyperparameter saliency and retention analyses show that the learning rate and momentum are highly sensitive across domains and algorithms, highlighting the need for methods that are more robust against hyperparameter tuning and can generalize well to new tasks.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: AlgoPerf ベンチマーク新結果: 調整しやすい学習アルゴリズムを探る
papers.summary: 深層学習の最適化手法は、ハイパーパラメータ調整やモデルとの組み合わせ次第で見え方が変わり、本当の性能を比べにくいという困りごとがある。この論文は AlgoPerf V1 ベンチマークで、固定ハードウェア上の 9 種類の作業に対して、全作業に 1 つの設定だけを使う「自己調整ルール」で PyTorch と JAX の 13 件の提出を壁時計時間で比較した。Schedule-Free AdamW が 1 位になり、行列前処理型や二重ループ法はサンプル効率は良いが実行時間で競うには積極的な計算最適化が必要なこと、学習率とモーメンタムの感度が分野や手法を問わず高いことが分かった。
papers.why: 最適化アルゴリズムを公平に比べる測り方と、ハイパーパラメータ感度の分析手法を具体例付きで示しており、学習効率の評価基盤を作る人に役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Evaluating deep learning optimizers is confounded by hyperparameter tuning and optimizer-model co-design. This report presents AlgoPerf V1 benchmark results on wall-clock time-to-target across nine fixed-hardware workloads under a self-tuning ruleset requiring a single configuration across workloads. Among 13 PyTorch/JAX submissions, Schedule-Free AdamW ranked first; matrix-preconditioned and two-loop methods show good sample efficiency but need aggressive computational optimization to be competitive in runtime, and hyperparameter saliency analysis shows learning rate and momentum are highly sensitive across domains and algorithms.
papers.why_en: It demonstrates a fair methodology for comparing optimizers and analyzing hyperparameter sensitivity, useful for anyone building infrastructure to measure training efficiency.

review.note: 最適化手法の比較では、単一設定での汎化を要求する自己調整ルールや、学習率・モーメンタムの感度分析のように、交絡因子を排除する測り方の工夫がある。
review.note_en: When comparing optimizers, techniques like a self-tuning ruleset requiring a single config across workloads and hyperparameter saliency/retention analysis help remove confounding factors from the measurement.

papers.title: Execution-Feasible Dispatch of LLM Pre-training Loads for Renewable-Dominant AI Data Centers
papers.abstract: AI data centers (AIDCs) are emerging as large power-system loads, making their operational flexibility increasingly valuable. Existing studies often treat AIDC demand as continuously adjustable or generically delay-tolerant, which overstating the flexibility of large language model (LLM) pretraining. This paper proposes an execution-feasible dispatch framework for LLM pre-training in renewable-dominant AIDCs. LLM descriptors are first converted into checkpoint-domain daily workloads, then mapped to feasible 3D-parallel GPU modes with explicit throughput, GPU-capacity, memory, and IT-power limits. The resulting checkpoint- and mode-constrained load states are embedded into a day-ahead power dispatch model. Case studies on a 2048 GPUs AIDC with two LLaMA pretraining tasks show that checkpoint-aware 3D dispatch reduces operating cost by 20.02% and renewable curtailment from 1.077 to 0.014 MWh relative to fixed continuous training. Related results also show that checkpoint records alone do not create load flexibility,practical grid-interactive flexibility arises from checkpoint waiting combined with execution-feasible 3D-mode compensation.

papers.title: Capturing Electrical Windows Through Reconfigurable Optical Networks: Transfer-aware Scheduling of Multi-Region AI Data Centers
papers.abstract: Artificial-intelligence data centers (AIDCs) can provide spatiotemporal load flexibility by migrating training workloads in response to regional electricity prices and renewable-energy (RE) availability. However, transfer-blind scheduling may overestimate migration benefits by overlooking transfer time or prevent training from resuming within renewable-rich or low-price windows when considering transfer time. This paper proposes a transfer-aware compute-electricity-network scheduling framework that coordinates training placement, checkpoint transmission, and optical circuit switching (OCS) to improve local RE utilization and reduce grid-purchase cost. A compact compute-electricity master problem generates candidate schedules using estimated transfer delays. The framework then schedules optical circuits, verifies checkpoint delivery under shared-link capacity constraints, and revises infeasible schedules using updated delay estimates. It integrates day-ahead planning, event-triggered intraday updates, and real-time dispatch. In a five-AIDC benchmark with equal completed work and network resources, the proposed method reduces the real-time grid purchase cost by 12.50% and increases the local RE utilization by 2.724 percentage points relative to static optical operation. Sensitivity and ablation analyses indicate that OCS is particularly beneficial when renewable-rich or low-price windows shift across sites and network bottlenecks hinder timely checkpoint delivery.

papers.title: Continually Post-training Small Models via Synthetic Self-distillation
papers.abstract: Continual post-training faces a dual challenge of acquisition and retention: models must learn new capabilities while preserving prior knowledge. While Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) mitigates this using self-supervision with in-context demonstrations, it relies on strong in-context learning and instruction-following abilities. Consequently, SDFT fails on smaller models critical for low-latency, on-device use. To enable continual learning at smaller scales, we first identify the root cause of failure. We show that poor acquisition and forgetting correlate linearly with the post-trained model's distribution shift, revealing the necessity of in-distribution learning. We thus introduce Synthetic Self-Distillation (SynthSelf), imitating SDFT's in-distribution rewrite by outsourcing the task to a minimally larger, same-family aligner. Coupled with off-policy supervision and rejection sampling, this provides the high-quality supervision small models require without breaking their original distribution. Evaluations spanning 4 acquisition datasets (including a mixture) and 14 retention benchmarks show SynthSelf consistently outperforms 6 methods (including off- and on-policy distillation) across 3 small model scales. Extensive further analyses confirm SynthSelf paves the way toward effective small-model continual learning.
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 小さいモデルを継続学習させる合成自己蒸留 SynthSelf
papers.summary: モデルの継続事後学習では、新しい能力を身につけつつ以前の知識を忘れないようにする必要があるが、既存の Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) は強い文脈内学習力を前提とするため、オンデバイス向けの小さいモデルでは失敗するという困りごとがある。この論文は、能力の低下や忘却が学習後のモデルの分布のズレと線形に相関することを示し、少しだけ大きい同系列モデル (aligner) に書き換えを任せて、オフポリシーの教師信号と拒否サンプリングを組み合わせる SynthSelf を提案した。4 種類の獲得データセットと 14 種類の保持ベンチマーク、3 つの小モデル規模で、オン/オフポリシー蒸留を含む 6 つの既存手法を一貫して上回ったという。
papers.why: 低遅延・オンデバイス向けの小モデルを安全に継続学習させるための蒸留設計を示し、学習効率と知識保持を両立する手法の選択肢を広げる。
papers.summary_en: Continual post-training requires models to acquire new capabilities while retaining prior knowledge, but existing Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning (SDFT) relies on strong in-context learning, causing it to fail on smaller, low-latency on-device models. The paper shows poor acquisition and forgetting correlate linearly with the post-trained model's distribution shift, and introduces Synthetic Self-Distillation (SynthSelf), which outsources in-distribution rewriting to a minimally larger same-family aligner combined with off-policy supervision and rejection sampling. Across 4 acquisition datasets and 14 retention benchmarks at 3 small model scales, SynthSelf consistently outperforms 6 methods including off- and on-policy distillation.
papers.why_en: It provides a distillation design for safely continually training small, latency-critical models, broadening the toolkit for balancing learning efficiency with knowledge retention.

papers.title: PCM: Programmable Congestion Management for Terabit RDMA NICs
papers.abstract: Datacenter congestion control (CC) and load balancing (LB) evolve rapidly as workload demands change, but deployment depends on RDMA hardware and transport interfaces. Emerging programmable RDMA engines tie policy code to vendor APIs. Operators must therefore port each policy for every platform they deploy. We address this with PCM, a programming model that separates portable congestion management from platform integration on datacenter NICs. Developers write event-driven handlers that they can debug in simulation and reuse on real hardware. PCM exposes flow telemetry as signals and uses triggers to support per-event reactions and coarser responses to accumulated feedback. Vendors provide optimized backends that map signals and output controls to native NIC mechanisms with defined feedback and control semantics. We demonstrate PCM's expressivity by implementing eleven well-known datacenter CC and LB algorithms. We deploy PCM across four distinct datapaths: an Ultra Ethernet simulator, CPU-based UCCL, and on-NIC offloads on NVIDIA ConnectX-8 and Microsoft 1P. On CX-8, PCM-Swift achieves processing capacity equivalent to one reaction per three 4 KiB packets at 800 Gbit/s, using one-fifth of the NIC's hardware threads. In UCCL, it matches native Swift's 1.56 Tbit/s goodput with 64 KiB chunk-level control. PCM's design informed ongoing Ultra Ethernet work toward a portable congestion management interface.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: 可搬な輻輳制御フレームワーク PCM、Terabit RDMA NIC 向け
papers.summary: データセンターの輻輳制御・負荷分散は頻繁に方式が更新されるが、RDMA ハードウェアごとにベンダー API が違うため、新しい方式をハードウェア間で移植するのに手間がかかる。PCM はポータブルな輻輳管理のプログラミングモデルを提供し、イベント駆動のハンドラをシミュレーションでデバッグしてから実機に流用できるようにする。11 種類の既知の輻輳制御・負荷分散アルゴリズムを実装し、NVIDIA ConnectX-8 では 800 Gbit/s で NIC のハードウェアスレッドの 5 分の 1 だけで 4 KiB パケット 3 個につき 1 回の反応に相当する処理能力を達成し、UCCL では 64 KiB チャンク単位の制御でネイティブ Swift と同じ 1.56 Tbit/s のスループットを再現した。
papers.why: 分散学習・推論で使う RDMA NIC の輻輳制御をベンダー非依存で書けるようにする設計は、通信基盤を作る人に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Datacenter congestion control (CC) and load balancing (LB) policies must be re-ported for every vendor's RDMA NIC, since programmable engines tie policy code to vendor APIs. PCM introduces a portable programming model where event-driven handlers can be debugged in simulation and reused across real hardware; the authors implement eleven well-known CC/LB algorithms and deploy PCM across an Ultra Ethernet simulator, CPU-based UCCL, and NIC offloads on ConnectX-8 and Microsoft 1P. On CX-8, PCM-Swift achieves processing capacity equivalent to one reaction per three 4 KiB packets at 800 Gbit/s using only one-fifth of the NIC's hardware threads, and in UCCL it matches native Swift's 1.56 Tbit/s goodput with 64 KiB chunk-level control.
papers.why_en: A vendor-agnostic programming model for congestion control on RDMA NICs is directly useful to people building the communication fabric underlying distributed training and inference.

papers.title: DP-MIND: Differentially private memory-guided Long context Inference
papers.abstract: LLM-as-a-Service has become a dominant paradigm for accessing large language models without requiring local deployment. However, the process raises severe privacy concerns when user queries may include sensitive or confidential contexts. Differential privacy (DP) provides a principled approach to protecting such inputs, but existing DP inference methods are primarily designed for short- or moderate-context settings and struggle with million-token-scale inputs due to limited context capacity and severe utility degradation under DP perturbation. In this paper, we propose DP-MIND, a memory-guided framework that scales differentially private inference to million-token contexts. DP-MIND enables private long-context inference by locally perturbing the input and processing it chunk by chunk with a compact memory that preserves task-relevant information across the sequence. To make this memory robust to DP noise, we optimize the memory construction policy directly on perturbed inputs using reinforcement learning, guided by both final answer correctness and memory consistency. We further recover perturbation-corrupted answer spans through a local denoising module without exposing the original context to the external model. We provide theoretical privacy analysis of DP-MIND and further conduct extensive empirical analysis across multiple long-context benchmarks with context lengths up to the million-token scale, demonstrating that DP-MIND consistently outperforms existing DP and long-context inference baselines in both scalability and utility.

papers.title: Rethinking Relative Policy Differences Transfer of On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) trains a target policy on its own rollouts using token-level supervision from a stronger teacher, but typically relies on the teacher being substantially more capable than the target. Recent work relaxes this requirement by transferring the relative policy difference between an expert and a reference policy rather than the expert's absolute distribution. Yet it remains unclear which differences provide useful supervision and which targets can benefit from them. We develop a unified view in which the log-probability ratio between a proxy expert and a proxy reference defines an implicit reward for KL-regularized policy optimization. This formulation induces an on-policy update for the target, recovers conventional OPD as a special case, and enables any-to-any transfer across models that differ in scale, training stage or generation. Our systematic experiments yield three findings. First, a stronger expert is not necessarily a better source of supervision: differences induced by task-specific training, including reinforcement learning and supervised fine-tuning, transfer consistently, whereas those arising from model scale alone transfer weakly or not at all. Second, the expert and reference serve complementary roles: the expert provides the capability to be transferred, while the reference filters out shared behavior and isolates the relevant residual. Third, even a useful difference does not transfer to every target: success requires the induced update to move the target toward the expert and generalize beyond sampled rollouts. Raw policy distance does not predict transferability, whereas an appropriate reference can rescue otherwise unsuccessful transfer. These results characterize when relative policy differences provide effective supervision for OPD.
papers.ja_title: オンポリシー蒸留における相対方針差分の転移条件
papers.summary: 強い教師モデルの絶対分布をそのまま使う従来のオンポリシー蒸留 (生成した行動を教師で添削する学習法) は、教師が生徒より十分強いことを前提とする。本研究は教師と基準モデルの対数確率比を暗黙の報酬として扱う統一的な枠組みを示し、スケールだけが違うモデル間の差分はほとんど転移しないが、強化学習や教師ありファインチューニングで得たタスク固有の差分は一貫して転移することを実験で確かめた。さらに、基準モデルが共有的な振る舞いを取り除いて本当に必要な差分だけを残す役割を持つことも示した。
papers.why: 蒸留のための教師選びや基準モデルの設計指針を与えるため、RL 後学習パイプラインを設計する人に役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Standard on-policy distillation (OPD) typically assumes the teacher is substantially stronger than the target, but this work develops a unified view where the log-probability ratio between a proxy expert and proxy reference acts as an implicit reward for KL-regularized policy optimization, enabling any-to-any transfer across models differing in scale, training stage, or generation. Experiments show that differences induced by task-specific training (RL or SFT) transfer consistently, whereas differences from model scale alone transfer weakly or not at all, and that the reference model's role of filtering shared behavior is key to successful transfer.
papers.why_en: This gives concrete guidance on choosing teacher/reference pairs for distillation, useful to anyone designing RL post-training pipelines.

papers.title: State-OPD: State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Agents
papers.abstract: On-Policy Distillation (OPD) has emerged as a powerful paradigm for transferring reasoning capabilities from frontier models to smaller models, while extending its success to multi-turn agentic environments remains challenging. We study agentic OPD through interaction states, distinguishing the objective task and executed action-observation record from the internal semantic trajectory of student reasoning. Through this lens, we identify two roles of student reasoning in multi-turn OPD: prior reasoning distorts teacher supervision, while current reasoning shapes the action alternatives sampled at the same state. Specifically, at matched interaction states, removing prior student reasoning improves teacher continuation success and changes the teacher's token-level targets, with larger continuation gains at later turns. Meanwhile, resampling complete reasoning-action responses yields greater action diversity at the same state than resampling actions under a fixed reasoning trace. We introduce State-Grounded On-Policy Distillation, a framework that grounds teacher supervision in interaction states and reallocates the sampling budget to generate multiple complete reasoning-action responses at states with high response entropy, while retaining full-history student generation. Comprehensive evaluations across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld and WebShop demonstrate that State-OPD achieves the highest macro-average success rate among the evaluated methods for both Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-4B students. Notably, for Qwen3-4B, State-OPD raises macro-average success from 26.07\% with the strongest baseline to 31.74\% and surpasses its Qwen3-32B teacher on ALFWorld Seen. Further analyses reveal that State-OPD achieves higher task success with fewer supervised turn responses and substantially reduces persistent failed-action repetition; qualitative traces illustrate decision revision based on interaction feedback.
papers.ja_title: 状態に基づくオンポリシー蒸留でマルチターンエージェントを強化
papers.summary: マルチターンのエージェント学習でオンポリシー蒸留を行う際、生徒モデル自身の推論が教師の添削を歪めたり、同じ状態で生成される行動の多様性を左右したりする問題があった。State-OPD は相互作用状態 (タスクと行動・観測の履歴) を基準に教師の添削対象を固定し、応答のばらつきが大きい状態にサンプリング予算を重点配分する手法で、ALFWorld・ScienceWorld・WebShop の評価で Qwen3-4B を使った場合、最強のベースラインの平均成功率 26.07% を 31.74% に改善し、教師の Qwen3-32B を ALFWorld Seen で上回った。
papers.why: マルチターン RL 蒸留で教師信号をどの単位で与えるべきかという設計を具体的な性能改善で示しており、RL 後学習基盤の実装に直結する。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) for multi-turn agentic environments is complicated by the student's own reasoning distorting teacher supervision and shaping the diversity of sampled actions at a given state. State-OPD grounds teacher supervision in interaction states and reallocates sampling budget toward high-entropy states; for Qwen3-4B, it raises macro-average success from 26.07% (strongest baseline) to 31.74% across ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, and WebShop, and even surpasses its Qwen3-32B teacher on ALFWorld Seen.
papers.why_en: This gives a concrete recipe for how to allocate teacher supervision and sampling budget in multi-turn RL distillation, directly relevant to building RL post-training infrastructure.

papers.title: CAST: Credit Alignment for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: Cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation (OPD) requires aligning teacher and student sequences before their scores can be compared. Decoded-text alignment provides such correspondence at the chunk level, but leaves a distinct problem unresolved: credit alignment. A chunk-level signal specifies how much a span should change, but not how that signal should be distributed across student tokens, while tokens without teacher correspondence remain unconstrained. We propose CAST (Chunk-aware credit Assignment with Selective Token Anchoring), a shift-or-stay framework that addresses both issues. For aligned chunks, CAST redistributes each chunk's advantage across student tokens using predictive uncertainty and local teacher-signal smoothness, emphasizing learning opportunities supported by locally consistent teacher feedback while preserving the chunk's total advantage. The resulting weights exactly solve a KL-regularized credit-allocation problem. For unaligned positions, CAST selectively anchors the student to its initial policy through a KL penalty, limiting drift where teacher supervision is unavailable. Because credit assignment is separated from chunk construction, CAST also applies to punctuation-defined or fixed-length chunks under shared tokenization. Across six mathematics, science, and code benchmarks, CAST improves the average over the strongest evaluated baseline by $2.45$ and $1.32$ points for cross-tokenizer transfer from Qwen3-8B to Mistral-7B and Llama-3.1-8B, respectively, and by $2.10$ points for shared-tokenizer transfer to Qwen3-1.7B.
papers.ja_title: トークナイザが異なるモデル間のオンポリシー蒸留のための信用割り当て手法 CAST
papers.summary: トークナイザが異なる教師・生徒モデル間でオンポリシー蒸留を行うとき、文字列の塊 (チャンク) 単位では整合が取れても、どのトークンにどれだけ学習信号を配分するかが未解決だった。CAST は予測の不確実性とチャンク内の教師信号の滑らかさを使ってチャンクのアドバンテージをトークンへ再配分し、整合しない位置では KL 正則化で元の方針から離れすぎないようにする。数学・科学・コードの 6 つのベンチマークで、Qwen3-8B から Mistral-7B・Llama-3.1-8B への転移で最強ベースラインより平均 2.45 点・1.32 点改善し、同一トークナイザの Qwen3-1.7B への転移でも 2.10 点改善した。
papers.why: トークナイザが違うモデル間の蒸留という実務上よくある課題にトークン単位の信用割り当てという具体策を与える。
papers.summary_en: Cross-tokenizer on-policy distillation requires not just chunk-level alignment between teacher and student sequences but also deciding how to distribute a chunk's learning signal across student tokens. CAST redistributes each chunk's advantage using predictive uncertainty and local teacher-signal smoothness, and anchors unaligned tokens to the initial policy via a KL penalty. Across six math/science/code benchmarks, CAST improves over the strongest baseline by 2.45 and 1.32 points for Qwen3-8B to Mistral-7B/Llama-3.1-8B transfer, and by 2.10 points for same-tokenizer transfer to Qwen3-1.7B.
papers.why_en: This offers a concrete token-level credit-assignment technique for the practically common problem of distilling across models with different tokenizers.

papers.title: Taking Tokenization off the Host for Agentic LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Agentic workloads resend long contexts that barely change between calls. Prefix caching now skips most of their prefill, yet every request must still be tokenized in full before the cache can even be consulted. Tokenization, a CPU stage long treated as negligible, becomes the largest part of time-to-first-token (TTFT), and a frontend that tokenizes for a whole GPU fleet limits how many GPUs it can feed. We present GraphTok, a GPU tokenizer that runs the entire encoding pipeline, from pre-tokenization through byte-pair encoding (BPE) merging to token-ID assembly, as one replayable CUDA graph. GraphTok reproduces the reference token IDs bit-for-bit on GPT-2, Llama 3, Qwen 2.5, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemma 3, hands short inputs to a CPU engine where the GPU cannot win, and plugs into unmodified vLLM and NVIDIA Dynamo. GraphTok encodes one million GPT-2 tokens in 1.7-3.2 ms including data transfers, and on Llama 3 it is 4.7-6.0x faster than gigatoken, the strongest CPU tokenizer. On TokTier's own single-request benchmark, it is 2.6-3.9x faster than gigatoken and up to 18.1x faster than TokTier. In vLLM with a cached prefix, it lowers mean TTFT by 2.1-2.4x. The largest gain is capacity. Within a 2 s P99 target, one Dynamo frontend with GraphTok sustains 518 requests/s of 121k-token traffic, the busiest-hour load of 56 GPUs, against 296 with gigatoken and 18.5 with the default tokenizer. Across 121k to one million tokens, this is 1.75-2.5x the load gigatoken sustains, with a P99 up to 64x lower where gigatoken's tail breaks.
papers.ja_title: GPU 上で丸ごと動くトークナイザ GraphTok、エージェント型 LLM サービングの隠れた遅延を解消
papers.summary: プレフィックスキャッシュ (繰り返し使う文脈を再計算せず再利用する機構) があっても、どのリクエストもまず全文をトークン化する必要があるため、CPU で行うトークン化が最初の 1 トークン生成までの時間 (TTFT) の最大のボトルネックになっていた。GraphTok は前処理から BPE マージ、トークン ID の組み立てまで全体を 1 つの再実行可能な CUDA グラフとして GPU 上で実行し、GPT-2・Llama 3・Qwen 2.5・DeepSeek-V3・Gemma 3 で参照実装とビット単位で同じトークン ID を再現する。Llama 3 では最強の CPU トークナイザ gigatoken より 4.7〜6.0 倍速く、vLLM でキャッシュ済みプレフィックスがある場合は平均 TTFT を 2.1〜2.4 倍短縮し、2 秒の P99 目標のもとで 1 台の Dynamo フロントエンドが gigatoken の 296 req/s・デフォルトの 18.5 req/s に対して 518 req/s (12 万 1 千トークンの通信、56 GPU 分のピーク負荷相当) を維持した。
papers.why: トークン化という見過ごされがちな CPU ステージが推論サービングのスループットの天井になることを定量的に示し、GPU 推論基盤のフロントエンド設計に直結する知見を与える。
papers.summary_en: Even with prefix caching, every request must still be tokenized in full before the cache can be consulted, making CPU-side tokenization the largest part of time-to-first-token (TTFT) and limiting how many GPUs a single frontend can feed. GraphTok runs the entire tokenization pipeline (pre-tokenization, BPE merging, token-ID assembly) as one replayable CUDA graph, reproducing reference token IDs bit-for-bit across GPT-2, Llama 3, Qwen 2.5, DeepSeek-V3, and Gemma 3. On Llama 3 it is 4.7-6.0x faster than the strongest CPU tokenizer (gigatoken), lowers mean TTFT by 2.1-2.4x in vLLM with a cached prefix, and under a 2 s P99 target one Dynamo frontend with GraphTok sustains 518 requests/s (the busiest-hour load of 56 GPUs) versus 296 for gigatoken and 18.5 for the default tokenizer.
papers.why_en: This quantifies how an overlooked CPU stage, tokenization, becomes the throughput ceiling for agentic LLM serving, giving concrete design guidance for GPU inference frontends.

papers.title: DuoRate: Two-Rate Per-Expert Precision Allocation for Mixture-of-Experts Serving
papers.abstract: Serving a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model pays for expert precision twice: the resident footprint pays for every expert the router can reach, while each batch-one decode step pays only for the experts it selects. These are two different rate functionals over the same per-expert widths, yet published per-expert MoE allocators constrain only the first. We call the difference the store-read gap; in the released BitsMoE checkpoint, 2.54 bits per weight (bpw) of storage become 7.50 bpw of decode traffic. We propose DuoRate, which stores once and reads per workload. Offline, it stores one uniform tier of a prefix-readable weight stream and bakes a distortion tensor. Online, it profiles a workload's own prefill without labels and solves a Lagrangian rate-distortion allocation under the decode functional; routing frequency provably cancels from every per-expert decision, and the solve costs one dot product per expert and a bisection. A deployment therefore keeps a single artifact that prefill reads at the stored rate and decode reads at the workload's own rate. On Qwen3-30B-A3B, DuoRate reading 2.3 bpw exceeds every 2-bit-class baseline by 6.3 to 47.0 points of average accuracy, and at 2.9 bpw it matches 4-bit formats that read 1.4-1.6 bpw more. The advantage is largest under long decoding: on GSM8K, DuoRate at 2.9 bpw matches or exceeds every 4-bit format and trails BF16 by only 0.25 points, and at 2.6 bpw it still matches or exceeds the 4.5-bit NF4 and FP4. Against controls in its own format, the allocation alone is worth 0.07-0.11 bpw of read rate. Code will be released upon publication.
papers.ja_title: MoE サービングにおける保存用と推論用で精度を分けるビット配分 DuoRate
papers.summary: MoE (複数の専門家ネットワークを切り替えて使うモデル) をサービングする際、常駐メモリに必要な精度 (ルーターが到達できる全専門家分) と、1 ステップのデコードで実際に読み出す精度 (選ばれた専門家分) は別物だが、既存の専門家ごとの精度割り当て手法は前者しか制約していなかった。公開されている BitsMoE では保存時 2.54 bits per weight (bpw) が実際のデコード時通信では 7.50 bpw に膨らんでいた。DuoRate はオフラインで 1 種類の均一精度のストリームを保存し、オンラインでワークロードのプリフィルからラベルなしで決定分布を推定してビット配分を最適化する。Qwen3-30B-A3B では、DuoRate が 2.3 bpw で既存の 2 bit 系手法を平均精度で 6.3〜47.0 点上回り、2.9 bpw では 1.4〜1.6 bpw 多く読む 4 bit 形式と同等の性能を達成した。
papers.why: 保存精度とデコード読み出し精度を分離するという着眼点は、MoE 推論の低精度化・メモリ設計を作る人にとって実利が大きい具体策。
papers.summary_en: Serving a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model pays for expert precision twice: resident storage covers every expert the router can reach, while each decode step only reads the experts it actually selects, yet existing per-expert allocators constrain only the storage rate. In the released BitsMoE checkpoint, 2.54 bits per weight (bpw) of storage become 7.50 bpw of actual decode traffic. DuoRate stores a single uniform-tier weight stream offline and solves a per-workload rate-distortion allocation from unlabeled prefill online; on Qwen3-30B-A3B, DuoRate at 2.3 bpw exceeds every 2-bit-class baseline by 6.3-47.0 points of average accuracy, and at 2.9 bpw matches 4-bit formats that read 1.4-1.6 bpw more.
papers.why_en: Separating storage precision from decode-read precision is a concrete, practically valuable idea for people designing low-precision memory schemes for MoE inference.

papers.title: PDE-PFN: Prior-Data Fitted Neural PDE Solver
papers.abstract: Motivated by the success of large language models (LLMs) with broad generalizability and robustness to noisy or unreliable pre-training data, we explore in-context prediction of PDE solution fields using approximate pre-training data. In addition, inspired by the posterior predictive mean-based inference mechanism of the in-context learning in prior-data fitted networks (PFNs), we propose PDE-PFN, a prior-data fitted neural solver that approximates the posterior predictive mean of PDE solutions via in-context learning. PDE-PFN builds on a PFN architecture with self- and cross-attention mechanisms of Transformer and is pre-trained on noisy approximate solutions generated by physics-informed neural networks, serving as diverse but not necessarily exact priors. Through experiments on a range of two-dimensional PDEs, we demonstrate that PDE-PFN achieves empirical generalization across heterogeneous equations, robustness under noisy priors, and zero-gradient-update in-context inference capability. PDE-PFN achieves competitive or improved predictive accuracy relative to the evaluated baselines while supporting flexible context and query representations.

papers.title: Understanding Mamba-3 Through Oscillatory Dynamics
papers.abstract: Mamba-3 introduces input-dependent rotations into recurrent state updates, but their contribution beyond state retention remains unclear. We interpret these rotations as underdamped second-order dynamics, providing a framework for investigating the role of oscillation in sequence modeling. Controlled comparisons show that underdamped dynamics outperform non-oscillatory damping regimes on state-tracking tasks, while language-model pretraining demonstrates benefits for long-context prediction and length generalization. Interventions in pretrained models further establish the importance of learned phase, and state analysis suggests that rotation regulates how retained information combines with incoming updates. Taken together, these findings identify underdamped dynamics as a useful mechanism for recurrent computation and suggest that oscillation supports long-context processing by regulating how information accumulates.
papers.ja_title: Mamba-3の回転機構を減衰振動として理解する
papers.summary: Mamba-3 という系列モデルは状態更新に入力に応じた回転を加えるが、その役割は不明だった。この研究は回転を「減衰振動(ばねのようにゆっくり揺れる動き)」として捉える枠組みを作り、振動が残る設定の方が振動を抑えた設定よりも状態追跡タスクで優れ、言語モデルの事前学習でも長い文脈の予測や長さ一般化に有利だと示した。学習済みモデルに介入する実験では、学習された位相(振動のタイミング)を変えると性能が変わることも確認された。
papers.why: 状態空間モデル(SSM)の回転機構の意味を説明し、長文脈処理に有利な設計指針を示す点でモデル構造の研究者に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Mamba-3 adds input-dependent rotations to its recurrent state updates, but their role beyond state retention was unclear. The authors interpret these rotations as underdamped second-order (oscillatory) dynamics and show that underdamped regimes outperform non-oscillatory damping on state-tracking tasks, while also benefiting long-context prediction and length generalization during LM pretraining. Interventions on pretrained models further show that the learned phase of oscillation matters, and state analysis suggests rotation regulates how retained information combines with new updates.
papers.why_en: The work explains what the rotation mechanism in SSM-style recurrences actually does, offering a design principle (oscillatory dynamics) that could guide future long-context sequence model architectures.

papers.title: Overcoming Data Imbalances with Expert Selection Biases
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have become the standard architecture for frontier LLMs. The multiple parallel experts in each transformer block theoretically enable expert specialization according to categories such as domains, languages, or modalities during pretraining. However, when data is imbalanced across categories, minority categories can become concentrated in a small fraction of the expert pool or spread inefficiently across them, effectively limiting their available capacity. In this work, we demonstrate that category-conditioned expert-selection biases can preferentially route tokens from different categories toward specialized expert pools. By applying biases based on input category, we provide a simple way to induce soft category-aligned specialization. This intervention encourages categories toward distinct expert subsets while retaining cross-category sharing when useful. More importantly, it enables the over-allocation of expert capacity to categories that would otherwise be disadvantaged by data scarcity. We observe performance improvements across modalities, low-resource languages, and code in models up to 10.6B parameters. At our smallest and largest model scales, these gains are equivalent to allocating 18.5% and 2.7% additional baseline training tokens, respectively. Overall, our results show that expert biases can serve as a lightweight control for category-level expert allocation, making room for low-resource categories while retaining standard MoE inference.
papers.ja_title: MoE で少数派カテゴリの専門家を増やすルーティングバイアス
papers.summary: MoE (複数の専門家ネットワークを切り替えて使うモデル) では、学習データの言語やモダリティの比率が偏っていると、少数派のカテゴリ用のトークンが専門家の一部に押し込められたり分散しすぎたりして、使える容量が実質的に減ってしまう。この研究は入力カテゴリに応じたルーティングバイアスを加えることで、少数派カテゴリに多くの専門家の容量を割り当てる簡単な方法を提案した。10.6B パラメータまでのモデルで、モダリティ・低資源言語・コードの性能が改善し、最小モデルと最大モデルでそれぞれ追加学習トークン 18.5% と 2.7% 分に相当する効果があった。
papers.why: 推論の仕組み (MoE のルーティング) を変えずに、データの偏りに対応する軽量な制御手段を示しており、事前学習の設計者が低資源データを活かす際に使える。
papers.summary_en: In Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, when pretraining data is imbalanced across categories (domains, languages, modalities), minority categories can get crowded into a small fraction of experts or spread too thin, effectively losing capacity. The authors introduce category-conditioned expert-selection biases that softly steer tokens from different categories to specialized expert subsets while retaining useful cross-category sharing. Across modalities, low-resource languages, and code, this yields performance gains in models up to 10.6B parameters, equivalent to about 18.5% and 2.7% extra baseline training tokens at the smallest and largest scales respectively.
papers.why_en: This offers a lightweight, inference-compatible way to allocate expert capacity to underrepresented categories, useful for anyone designing MoE pretraining pipelines with imbalanced data.

papers.title: Branching On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides teacher supervision on student-generated trajectories, but a single trajectory realizes only one continuation at each decision, limiting supervision coverage under a finite sampling budget. We propose BranchOPD (Branching On-Policy Distillation), which selects informative decision points using student uncertainty and teacher-student disagreement, resamples student-policy continuations from shared prefixes, and applies token-level teacher supervision to both main trajectories and branches. BranchOPD operates at token-level decisions in mathematics and within-turn decisions in agent tasks. Shared-prefix reuse reduces student-generated token costs by approximately 19% on ALFWorld and 31% on WebShop relative to seven independent trajectories. We also introduce protocol-boundary repair (PBR), which uses targeted supervision under protocol constraints to mitigate repetition and wasted generation. BranchOPD outperforms Vanilla OPD and Multi-Rollout OPD (n=7) across all evaluated benchmarks, with gains over Vanilla OPD of 18.55 percentage points in mean mathematics accuracy over 16 sampled answers (avg@16) and 13.8 points in mean ALFWorld ID/OOD success. Mechanistic analyses and selection ablations show that branching at uncertain decisions expands subsequent behavior coverage and outperforms random selection and turn-initial branching.
papers.ja_title: 分岐でオンポリシー蒸留のカバレッジを広げる BranchOPD
papers.summary: オンポリシー蒸留 (生徒モデル自身が作った軌跡に教師モデルが指導を与える手法) は、各時点で 1 つの続きしか試せないため、限られたサンプル数では指導の網羅性が足りなかった。この研究の BranchOPD は、生徒の不確かさと教師との意見の不一致が大きい決定点を選んで、その地点から複数の続き (枝) を再サンプリングし、本流と枝の両方にトークン単位で教師の指導を与える。共有部分を再利用することでトークン生成コストを ALFWorld で約 19%、WebShop で約 31% 削減しつつ、数学タスクの正解率 (avg@16) で通常のオンポリシー蒸留より 18.55 ポイント、ALFWorld の成功率で 13.8 ポイント高い性能を達成した。
papers.why: 限られた計算予算の中で教師の指導範囲を広げる具体的な分岐戦略を示しており、RL 後学習・蒸留パイプラインの効率化に直接使える工夫。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation (OPD) lets a teacher supervise a student's own generated trajectories, but a single trajectory realizes only one continuation per decision, limiting supervision coverage under a finite sampling budget. BranchOPD selects decision points with high student uncertainty and teacher-student disagreement, resamples multiple continuations from shared prefixes, and applies token-level teacher supervision to both the main trajectory and branches. Reusing shared prefixes cuts student-generated token cost by about 19% on ALFWorld and 31% on WebShop versus seven independent trajectories, and BranchOPD beats Vanilla OPD by 18.55 points in mean math accuracy (avg@16) and 13.8 points in ALFWorld success.
papers.why_en: It gives a concrete branching strategy for extending teacher supervision coverage under a fixed compute budget, directly applicable to RL post-training / distillation pipelines.

papers.title: Simulating Training Spikes of Deep Neural Networks by Layer-wise Random Feature Models
papers.abstract: Intermittent ``spikes'' in loss, during the pre-training of Large Language Models (LLMs), remains a mysterious phenomenon both theoretically and empirically. In this paper, we show that simple quadratic models with heavy-tailed, power-law distributed inputs can replicate these spikes. We introduce a theoretical framework and simulation algorithm to model per-layer training dynamics of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), using such quadratic models. In a case study on an Adam hyperparameter configuration (where $β_2$ is set close to $1$) known to induce spikes in Transformer LMs, our simulation successfully predicts bumps indicating spiky behavior from a given checkpoint. Furthermore, we derive an appropriate $β_2$ schedule from observed metrics, which empirically improves performance.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 層ごとの乱数特徴モデルで学習時の損失スパイクを再現する
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルの事前学習中に時々起こる損失の急な跳ね上がり (スパイク) は、理論的にも実験的にも原因がよく分かっていなかった。この研究は、べき乗則に従う重い裾を持つ入力を使う単純な二次モデルで、層ごとの学習の動きを模擬するとスパイクが再現できることを示した。Adam の β2 を 1 に近づけるとスパイクが起きやすいという既知の設定について、シミュレーションはあるチェックポイントからスパイクが起きそうな箇所をうまく予測し、観測した指標から適切な β2 のスケジュールを導いて実際に性能を改善した。
papers.why: 学習が不安定になる現象をおもちゃモデルで説明・予測する枠組みを提供し、大規模学習の監視やハイパーパラメータ調整の実務に使える。
papers.summary_en: Loss "spikes" that occasionally occur during LLM pretraining remain poorly understood both theoretically and empirically. The authors show that simple quadratic models with heavy-tailed, power-law distributed inputs can replicate these spikes, and introduce a framework/simulation algorithm for per-layer training dynamics using such models. In a case study with an Adam setting (β2 close to 1) known to induce spikes, the simulation successfully predicts spiky bumps from a given checkpoint, and the authors derive a β2 schedule from observed metrics that empirically improves performance.
papers.why_en: This offers a tractable toy-model framework for explaining and predicting training instabilities, which could help practitioners monitor and tune hyperparameters during large-scale pretraining.

papers.title: Rationally Linearized MLPs
papers.abstract: We present Rationally Linearized Multilayer Perceptrons(RaLiMPs), a new approach to efficiently linearizing MLPs using low-degree rational approximations of standard activation functions. Inspired by polynomial-based MLP linearization, we show that rational approximations can provide accurate representations at substantially lower degree. RaLiMPs exploit these approximations to construct kernel representations with narrow bottlenecks, enabling efficient composition across MLP layers. We provide theoretical guarantees for the resulting approximation and evaluate RaLiMPs across applications ranging from implicit 3D models to large language models. Our experiments demonstrate favorable accuracy--efficiency tradeoffs, with RaLiMPs achieving competitive or improved accuracy while substantially reducing inference cost.
papers.ja_title: 有理式近似で MLP を軽量化する RaLiMP
papers.summary: MLP (多層パーセプトロン) の活性化関数を多項式で近似して線形化する手法は知られていたが、精度を保つには高次の多項式が必要でコストが高かった。この研究は活性化関数を低次の有理式 (分数の形の近似) で近似する RaLiMP を提案し、同じ精度でも多項式より低い次数で済むことを示した。3D モデルの表現から大規模言語モデルまで複数の用途で評価し、同等以上の精度を保ちながら推論コストを大きく減らせることを確認した。
papers.why: MLP の計算を軽量なカーネル表現に落とし込む具体的な近似手法を示し、推論高速化を狙うエンジニアに使える手がかりになる。
papers.summary_en: Linearizing MLPs with polynomial approximations of activation functions has been studied before, but keeping accuracy required high-degree polynomials and thus high cost. The authors propose Rationally Linearized MLPs (RaLiMPs), which use low-degree rational approximations instead, showing they achieve accurate representations at substantially lower degree and enable narrow-bottleneck kernel representations for efficient layer composition. Across applications from implicit 3D models to LLMs, RaLiMPs achieve competitive or improved accuracy while substantially reducing inference cost.
papers.why_en: It provides a concrete lower-degree approximation technique for turning MLP computation into cheaper kernel representations, useful for engineers aiming to speed up inference.

papers.title: Multi-Stream Attention Residuals
papers.abstract: Attention Residuals (AttnRes) enables content-dependent retrieval over network depth, which can be viewed as single-stream softmax attention along the depth axis. Inspired by the success of multi-head attention along the sequence axis, we introduce Multi-Stream Attention Residuals (MSAR), an extension of AttnRes that generalizes this mechanism to multi-head depth attention, yielding substantial performance gains with minimal additional overhead. MSAR draws stream diversity from sequence context through multi-scale causal convolutions, allowing different heads to retrieve historical representations through distinct contextual views while preserving the integrity of the hidden representation. The retrieved streams are combined through lightweight adaptive mixing to generate the single-stream layer input. By retaining single-stream sources and expanding them on demand, MSAR supports multi-stream computation without requiring persistent multi-stream storage or communication. Across all 12 downstream benchmarks at the 18B and 28B MoE scales, MSAR consistently outperforms prior residual variants, including standard residual connections, manifold-constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), and AttnRes. Scaling-law experiments yield an iso-loss compute speedup of $1.58\times$ over the standard residual baseline, compared with $1.35\times$ for AttnRes and $1.30\times$ for mHC. These results make MSAR a promising residual architecture for large-scale pre-training.
papers.ja_title: 深さ方向のアテンションをマルチヘッド化する MSAR
papers.summary: AttnRes という手法は、ネットワークの深さ方向に対してソフトマックス注意を使い、過去の層の内容を取り出す仕組みだったが、1 つの流れしか扱えなかった。この研究の MSAR は、系列方向のマルチヘッド注意と同様に、深さ方向の注意を複数ヘッド化し、多段の因果畳み込みで各ヘッドに異なる文脈の見方を与え、取り出した複数の流れを軽量な適応混合でまとめる。18B と 28B の MoE 規模で 12 種類の下流タスク全てにおいて標準の残差接続・mHC・AttnRes より性能が良く、同じ損失に達するまでの計算量で標準残差より 1.58 倍、AttnRes より 1.35 倍、mHC より 1.30 倍速かった。
papers.why: 残差接続という基本部品を深さ方向の注意として再設計した例で、大規模事前学習のスケーリング効率を上げる新しい構造として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Attention Residuals (AttnRes) enables content-dependent retrieval across network depth as a single-stream softmax attention along the depth axis, but it can only carry one stream. The authors propose Multi-Stream Attention Residuals (MSAR), which generalizes this to multi-head depth attention, drawing stream diversity from multi-scale causal convolutions over the sequence and combining retrieved streams via lightweight adaptive mixing. Across all 12 downstream benchmarks at 18B and 28B MoE scale, MSAR consistently beats standard residual connections, mHC, and AttnRes, giving an iso-loss compute speedup of 1.58x over the standard residual baseline (vs. 1.35x for AttnRes and 1.30x for mHC).
papers.why_en: This is a redesign of the basic residual-connection building block as depth-wise attention, offering a new architecture that improves pretraining compute efficiency at scale.

papers.title: LAPT-Scale: Scaling Embodied Policies with Latent Action Pre-Training on Human Videos
papers.abstract: Scaling generalist robotic policies is limited by the high cost of collecting embodied interaction data. Large-scale egocentric human videos offer a rich alternative, but they lack robot action labels, and existing action annotation methods are often noisy under real-world visual complexity and diverse manipulation dynamics. We introduce LAPT-Scale, a scalable latent action pre-training paradigm with two components: LAPT-Scale-LAM learns continuous latent actions by explaining frame-to-frame visual transitions in human videos and uses them as human-derived supervision, while LAPT-Scale-Policy trains a VLA policy through human-video latent-action pre-training, target-robot embodiment alignment, and task-specific post-training. Unlike prior vector-quantized LAMs, LAPT-Scale-LAM uses a continuous latent space to preserve fine-grained motion and interaction dynamics. We further combine perceptual, semantic, and optical-flow alignment signals to improve transition-level supervision beyond pixel reconstruction. Trained on 23.3K hours of egocentric video, LAPT-Scale-LAM provides implicit action supervision for policy pre-training, yielding consistent scaling gains and improving real-robot success from 63.3% to 85.0% as annotated human video scales from 1K to 5K hours. The learned policy also generalizes to unseen visual conditions.

papers.title: Geometry-Aware Multi-Objective Optimization: Norm-Constrained Oracles with Entropic Weight Updates
papers.abstract: Multiple-gradient descent is typically formulated in Euclidean geometry, whereas matrix-aware optimizers use directions induced by other norms. We analyze a single-loop multi-objective method combining a norm-constrained linear minimization oracle with entropic updates of task weights. For any finite-dimensional norm pair, we establish an $O(T^{-1/2})$ ergodic stationarity rate in the deterministic setting, deriving the required trajectory gradient bound from smoothness and lower-boundedness in the unregularized case. With stochastic gradients and a bounded-gradient assumption, one persistent blended-gradient momentum buffer yields an $O(T^{-1/4})$ rate whose leading term has no explicit dependence on the number of tasks. We also establish static regret for the inner weighting objective on arbitrary bounded gradient sequences and, with entropy regularization and a weight floor, iteration-wise inner-gap control after burn-in while retaining ergodic stationarity, conditional on a trajectory gradient bound. The optimal blended gradient can be nonunique in spectral and sign geometries, motivating a selection-independent inner gap. Our analysis extends the spectral construction studied by concurrent MOON to general norms. Experiments compare the method with existing multi-task optimizers and examine its oracle, weighting, and momentum choices.
papers.ja_title: 幾何を考慮した多目的最適化の収束保証
papers.summary: 複数の目的関数を同時に最適化する手法は通常ユークリッド幾何で考えられるが、行列を意識した最適化手法は別のノルムに基づく方向を使う。この研究はノルム制約付きの線形最小化オラクルとエントロピーによる重み更新を組み合わせた単一ループの多目的最適化法を解析し、決定論的な設定で O(T^-1/2) の収束率、確率的な勾配を使う設定で O(T^-1/4) の収束率を導いた。複数のマルチタスク最適化手法と比較する実験も行っている。
papers.why: マルチタスク学習や複数報酬を持つ RL 後学習の最適化で使われる重み付け手法に理論的な収束保証を与え、最適化器の設計・比較に使える。
papers.summary_en: Multiple-gradient descent is usually formulated in Euclidean geometry, while matrix-aware optimizers use directions induced by other norms. The authors analyze a single-loop multi-objective method combining a norm-constrained linear minimization oracle with entropic task-weight updates, establishing an O(T^{-1/2}) ergodic stationarity rate in the deterministic setting and an O(T^{-1/4}) rate with stochastic gradients using a single persistent momentum buffer, whose leading term has no explicit dependence on the number of tasks. They also give static regret and inner-gap control results, and compare the method empirically against existing multi-task optimizers.
papers.why_en: This provides convergence guarantees for norm-aware multi-task/multi-objective weighting schemes relevant to RL post-training with multiple reward signals, useful for designing and comparing optimizers.

papers.title: ReplaySSM: Cache SSM Inputs, Not State
papers.abstract: State-space models (SSMs) maintain a fixed-size recurrent state, but reading and writing it at every decoding step can bottleneck hybrid models. This eager state management causes large state I/O with low arithmetic intensity, leaves speculative decoding no cheap rollback, and feeds state quantization error into subsequent recurrent updates. We introduce ReplaySSM, which unrolls the recurrence to represent the state as a checkpoint and a buffer of recent SSM inputs. This separates output computation from checkpoint updates. By updating the checkpoint periodically, ReplaySSM avoids state writes on most steps and roughly halves the dominant state memory traffic. Keeping recent inputs also makes speculative rollback a buffer-pointer operation and enables output-only verification without materializing intermediate states. The same separation allows a low-precision checkpoint to serve output computation on most steps while a higher-precision checkpoint serves recurrent updates, so rounding error in the low-precision copy never enters later updates. We implement ReplaySSM in vLLM for Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet. At serving batch size 256, it accelerates standard decoding by $1.20$--$1.47\times$ over a tuned vLLM baseline across four hybrid models, and delivers about $1.8\times$ the throughput of vLLM's speculative decoding on the two 120B-class models. Separate state precisions also reduce output KL divergence and downstream accuracy losses compared with a shared low-precision checkpoint.
papers.ja_title: SSM の状態を毎回書き換えない: 入力をキャッシュする ReplaySSM
papers.summary: 状態空間モデル (SSM、固定サイズの要約状態を持つモデル) をハイブリッドモデルで使うと、毎ステップ状態を読み書きするため演算効率が悪く、投機的デコードの巻き戻しも難しいという困りごとがあった。ReplaySSM は状態を「チェックポイント」と「最近の入力バッファ」に分け、チェックポイント更新を間引くことで支配的な状態メモリ転送量をおよそ半分にする。vLLM に実装し、バッチサイズ 256 で 4 つのハイブリッドモデルにおいて通常デコードを調整済み vLLM 比 1.20〜1.47 倍高速化し、120B 級モデル 2 種では vLLM の投機的デコード比で約 1.8 倍のスループットを達成した。
papers.why: SSM 系ハイブリッドモデルのサービング基盤を作る人にとって、状態 I/O の削減、投機的デコードの巻き戻しの単純化、低精度チェックポイントの安全な併用という具体的な高速化手法が得られる。
papers.summary_en: Eager per-step reading/writing of the fixed SSM state bottlenecks hybrid models with low arithmetic intensity and no cheap rollback for speculative decoding. ReplaySSM unrolls the recurrence into a checkpoint plus a buffer of recent inputs, updating the checkpoint only periodically to roughly halve the dominant state memory traffic. Implemented in vLLM for Mamba-2 and Gated DeltaNet, it accelerates standard decoding by 1.20–1.47x over a tuned vLLM baseline across four hybrid models at batch size 256, and delivers about 1.8x the throughput of vLLM's speculative decoding on two 120B-class models.
papers.why_en: Gives builders of hybrid-SSM serving stacks concrete techniques to cut state I/O, make speculative rollback a buffer-pointer operation, and safely mix low- and high-precision checkpoints.

papers.title: Randomized Momentum Transport with Cheap Predictors
papers.abstract: Momentum methods such as STORM and second-order momentum track the gradient by adding a transport correction to momentum, at the cost of an extra oracle call per iteration. We introduce randomized momentum transport, which evaluates the correction with probability $q$ and otherwise uses a cheap prediction, with importance weighting that preserves the conditional mean and adds $(q^{-1}-1)$ times the prediction loss to the variance. Under transport-bias, second-moment, and residual-control assumptions, linear minimization oracle (LMO) updates, including normalized, sign, and exact spectral (Muon) directions, retain an $O(T^{-1/3})$ stationarity bound for each fixed $q>0$ with a single-gradient initialization. For unnormalized STORM, some $q<1$ lowers the leading coefficient of our sufficient gradient budget if and only if the gradient-difference noise modulus exceeds the smoothness constant, by at most about $10\%$. An online diagonal predictor admits a regret-to-convergence guarantee. At approximately equal oracle cost, querying a quarter of the corrections lowers the final training loss by $18$ to $43\%$ on MNIST1D and raises the test accuracy of Hessian-vector transport on CIFAR-10 by $1.5$ points.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 勾量運動量補正を確率的にサボる: 安いコストで STORM/Muon を高速化
papers.summary: STORM や二次モーメント運動量法は、勾量を正確に追跡するため毎ステップ追加のオラクル呼び出し (勾量計算) を必要とし、計算コストが高いという困りごとがあった。この研究は確率 q でのみ正確な補正を計算し、残りは安価な予測で代用する「ランダム化運動量輸送」を提案し、重要度重み付けで平均を保ちつつ理論的な収束保証を維持した。同じ計算量でも補正を 4 分の 1 の頻度で呼ぶ設定が MNIST1D の最終学習損失を 18〜43% 下げ、CIFAR-10 のテスト精度を 1.5 ポイント上げた。
papers.why: 最適化アルゴリズムを作る人にとって、計算コストを抑えつつ理論保証を保ったまま運動量補正を間引く具体的な方法と条件が得られる。
papers.summary_en: Momentum methods like STORM and second-order momentum need an extra oracle call every iteration to compute a transport correction, which is costly. The paper introduces randomized momentum transport, which evaluates the correction with probability q and otherwise substitutes a cheap prediction, using importance weighting to preserve the conditional mean while retaining an O(T^{-1/3}) stationarity bound. At approximately equal oracle cost, querying a quarter of the corrections lowers the final training loss by 18 to 43% on MNIST1D and raises CIFAR-10 test accuracy of Hessian-vector transport by 1.5 points.
papers.why_en: Offers optimizer designers a principled way to skip expensive momentum corrections most of the time while keeping convergence guarantees, with explicit conditions for when it helps.

papers.title: GPU-resident Execution for Timing-predictable Sensor Processing Systems
papers.abstract: Real-time embedded systems increasingly place GPU-accelerated processing of high-bandwidth sensor streams inside closed-loop systems, but the CPU (the host) remains the primary orchestrator of each iteration. The host observes sensor inputs, submits CUDA work, waits for completion, and commits actuation. This host-mediated path exposes the closed-loop end-to-end latency to I/O interrupts, host scheduler decisions, and CUDA API overheads even after common host-side mitigations such as GPU-memory RDMA or CPU core isolation. This paper presents GPU-resident Execution, a new execution model for real-time sensor processing pipelines that keeps I/O and GPU execution in a long-lived device-resident loop. Sensor inputs arrive in GPU memory, trigger GPU-side processing, and reach GPU-visible output endpoints without any host wakeups. We implement the model in the NVIDIA Holoscan C++ framework and provide reference components for building GPU-resident applications. We evaluate our system on NVIDIA GPUs and SoCs with inference, host-contention, multi-loop, and streaming camera workloads. On an industry-grade 1080p, 60 Hz real-time camera-to-display application, GPU-resident Execution reduces photon-to-display jitter from 4.83 ms to 0.66 ms (7.3x) relative to a CPU-driven GPU-memory RDMA baseline and reduces software-processing jitter from 1.70 ms to 0.01 ms (170x).
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: CPU を介さず GPU だけでループを回す: リアルタイムセンサー処理の低遅延化
papers.summary: リアルタイムのセンサー処理システムでは、GPU 処理の結果を毎回 CPU (ホスト) が受け取って判断するため、割り込みやスケジューラの揺れで応答時間がぶれるという困りごとがあった。GPU-resident Execution は、センサー入力から出力まで GPU メモリ内だけでループを回し、ホストを一切起こさない実行モデルを提案し、NVIDIA Holoscan に実装した。1080p・60Hz のカメラ-ディスプレイ実時間アプリでは、画面表示までのジッタを従来の CPU 駆動 RDMA 方式の 4.83ms から 0.66ms (7.3 倍改善) に、ソフト処理のジッタを 1.70ms から 0.01ms (170 倍改善) に抑えた。
papers.why: 低遅延なリアルタイム推論パイプラインを作る人にとって、ホストとの往復をなくすことでジッタを大幅に削る具体的な実行モデルと実装例が得られる。
papers.summary_en: Real-time sensor-processing systems route every GPU-accelerated iteration through a host CPU, exposing end-to-end latency to interrupts, scheduler decisions, and CUDA API overheads even with RDMA or core isolation. GPU-resident Execution keeps I/O and GPU execution in a long-lived device-resident loop with no host wakeups, implemented in NVIDIA Holoscan. On a 1080p, 60Hz real-time camera-to-display application, it reduces photon-to-display jitter from 4.83ms to 0.66ms (7.3x) and software-processing jitter from 1.70ms to 0.01ms (170x) versus a CPU-driven GPU-memory RDMA baseline.
papers.why_en: Gives builders of low-latency real-time inference pipelines a concrete execution model and implementation that removes host round-trips to drastically cut latency jitter.

papers.title: One Model, Multiple Compute Budgets: Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE for Flexible Compute Across Turns
papers.abstract: Large language models typically support different inference budgets through separate model sizes or fixed compute configurations. In multi-turn interactions, however, compute demand can vary substantially across turns. Using a high-compute model for every turn wastes computation, while routing among independent models may require rebuilding model-specific history states after switches. We therefore ask whether a single shared model can support multiple compute budgets that can be flexibly assigned across turns. We introduce Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE, which jointly supports token-to-concept compression ratios of 2, 4, and 8 (CR2/CR4/CR8) within a shared backbone. Lightweight full-token modules reduce compression-independent cost, ratio-specific boundary routers support distinct compression levels, and cross-ratio training enables mixed-ratio processing within the same context. Across PTBench and SFTBench, the three fixed modes outperform their compute-matched MoE baselines in all 6 comparisons while remaining competitive with independently trained fixed-ratio specialists. On CodeChat and CoSQL, mixed-ratio inference improves the accuracy--compute trade-off, outperforming the Large MoE by 5.87 and 2.68 percentage points while reducing FLOPs by 41.1% and 12.3%, respectively. Under the same turn-wise budget schedule, Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE further reduces FLOPs by 78.4% and 46.9% relative to routing among independent models. These results demonstrate that a single shared model can provide multiple compute budgets for flexible compute allocation across turns.
papers.ja_title: 1 つのモデルでターン毎に計算量を切り替える Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルは通常モデルサイズや固定の計算設定で推論予算を決めているが、対話の各ターンで必要な計算量は大きく変わり、毎回高性能モデルを使うのは無駄が多いという困りごとがあった。Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE は、トークンを概念に圧縮する比率 2・4・8 を 1 つの共有バックボーンで同時にサポートし、軽量な全トークンモジュールや比率別ルーター、混合比率学習を導入した。CodeChat と CoSQL では、混合比率推論が大モデル版 MoE より精度を 5.87 ポイントと 2.68 ポイント上回りつつ計算量 (FLOPs) を 41.1% と 12.3% 削減し、同じターン毎の予算スケジュールでは独立モデル間のルーティングに比べ FLOPs を 78.4% と 46.9% さらに削減した。
papers.why: 対話システムのサービング基盤を作る人にとって、ターンごとに計算予算を柔軟に切り替えても履歴状態を再構築せずに済む設計が示されており、マルチターン推論の効率化に直結する。
papers.summary_en: LLMs typically fix inference budgets by model size or configuration, but compute demand varies substantially across turns in multi-turn interactions, wasting compute if a high-compute model is used every turn. Multi-Ratio ConceptMoE jointly supports token-to-concept compression ratios of 2, 4, and 8 within a shared backbone, using lightweight full-token modules, ratio-specific boundary routers, and cross-ratio training. On CodeChat and CoSQL, mixed-ratio inference outperforms the Large MoE by 5.87 and 2.68 percentage points while reducing FLOPs by 41.1% and 12.3%, and under the same turn-wise budget schedule it further reduces FLOPs by 78.4% and 46.9% relative to routing among independent models.
papers.why_en: Shows multi-turn serving system builders a design where a single shared model can flexibly reassign compute budgets across turns without rebuilding model-specific history states, directly improving multi-turn inference efficiency.

papers.title: Correction Training for Diffusion Models
papers.abstract: Iterative sampling in diffusion models can lead to error accumulation due to exposure bias. The denoiser is trained on real images interpolated with noise, but at inference its inputs are constructed from its own imperfect predictions from the earlier steps, something it has never seen at training time. This might be one reason diffusion models often struggle without additional help, such as CFG. We introduce a correction step for diffusion models which attempts to reduce this training-inference gap. The corrector takes the base model's prediction as input and is trained against the same ground-truth target. This makes correction an explicit learning task, with training inputs provided by the base model. During sampling, at each denoising step, we iteratively refine the denoiser's clean-sample prediction. This allows us to correct predictions at intermediate denoising steps, preventing early artifacts from persisting into the final sample. Although the corrector is trained only on predictions from the base denoiser, it can be applied repeatedly to its own outputs at inference for better results. This simple framework leads to substantial improvement in sample quality while largely preserving diversity. We evaluate our method across DiT, SiT, and JiT. Our method substantially improves upon previously reported FID scores for unguided generation and, notably, unconditional generation, where producing high-quality samples without guidance has been particularly challenging. Our method achieves performance competitive with classifier-free guidance (CFG), and combining correction with CFG further improves diversity and reduces oversaturation typical of CFG. Finally, we show that the additional inference cost of correction can be amortized by distilling the refined predictions back into the base diffusion model, retaining the quality gains without additional inference-time overhead.

papers.title: AutoEnvScaling: Automating the Data Flywheel with Terminal Agents
papers.abstract: Terminal agents solve tasks in software engineering and scientific research by executing commands in a terminal. Training them via reinforcement learning (RL) requires diverse and verifiable environments, but these environments are still mostly designed by human researchers, so their supply grows only as fast as researchers can work. We introduce AutoEnvScaling, which treats environment design as a terminal task and uses agents to automate the data flywheel. A proposer agent builds new RL environments from the rollouts of the solver being trained, and the solver's new rollouts guide the next round. By turning environment generation into a terminal task, AutoEnvScaling increases the valid-environment rate by up to 25 times compared to prompt-only generation, at up to 75% lower cost per valid environment. We show that training Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on AutoEnvScaling environments from GPT-5.6-sol improves its Terminal-Bench 2.1 score by 4.3 points over the matched Tmax baseline. The broader goal of AutoEnvScaling is to enable recursive self-improvement (RSI): by making both environment generation and solving terminal tasks, it lets one model co-evolve in both roles. We show that Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, acting in both roles, gains 12.2 points on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and raises its Terminal-Bench 4.0 score from 1.6 to 3.2. The pipeline also generalizes across agentic domains, generating environments for software engineering, computer use, professional work, and GPU kernel programming. Overall, these results show a path toward agents building their own training environments, reducing human reliance and taking a core step toward RSI.
papers.ja_title: エージェントが自分の訓練環境を作る: AutoEnvScaling
papers.summary: ターミナル操作エージェントを強化学習で訓練するには多様で検証可能な環境が必要だが、これまで研究者が手作りしていたため環境の供給速度が人手に制約されるという困りごとがあった。AutoEnvScaling は環境設計自体をターミナル作業として扱い、訓練中のソルバーの実行履歴から提案エージェントが新しい環境を自動生成し、ソルバーの新しい履歴が次の生成を導く仕組みを作った。プロンプトだけの生成に比べ有効な環境の生成率を最大 25 倍に高め、有効環境あたりのコストを最大 75% 削減し、この環境で Qwen3.5-35B-A3B を訓練すると Terminal-Bench 2.1 のスコアが基準より 4.3 ポイント向上した。
papers.why: RL 後学習の基盤を作る人にとって、人手の環境設計のボトルネックを解消し、エージェント自身が訓練環境を生成・改善し続ける自己進化的な仕組みの具体例が得られる。
papers.summary_en: Training terminal agents via RL needs diverse, verifiable environments, but these are still mostly hand-designed by researchers, so supply grows only as fast as researchers can work. AutoEnvScaling treats environment design itself as a terminal task: a proposer agent builds new RL environments from the rollouts of the solver being trained, and the solver's new rollouts guide the next round. This increases the valid-environment rate by up to 25 times compared to prompt-only generation at up to 75% lower cost per valid environment, and training Qwen3.5-35B-A3B on these environments improves its Terminal-Bench 2.1 score by 4.3 points over the matched baseline.
papers.why_en: Gives RL post-training infrastructure builders a concrete path to remove the human-design bottleneck on environments, letting an agent co-evolve as both environment generator and solver toward recursive self-improvement.

papers.title: Latent World Action Model for GUI Agents
papers.abstract: Pixel-space world models have recently emerged as a promising approach for GUI agents, predicting future screens prior to execution and subsequently re-perceiving them for action selection. However, this two-stage paradigm faces two key challenges in GUI environments: (L1) the high computational cost of pixel reconstruction and (L2) the need to reconstruct large and diverse appearance-level details beyond what is required for action selection. In practice, this screen-generation objective can induce an identity shortcut problem, where future-state prediction largely preserves the current state rather than capturing action-induced changes. In this work, we reformulate GUI world modeling by shifting the prediction target from full-screen reconstruction to action-induced future information in latent space. Concretely, we leverage a large multimodal model as the latent world model, whose shared representations support two dedicated heads for both action selection and predictive transition modeling. The action head directly translates these latent representations into action selection, while the transition head captures action-conditioned future information. To mitigate the identity shortcut, we further introduce an action-aware contrastive objective that encourages the transition representations to capture discriminative action-induced changes. Extensive experiments across offline and online GUI settings show that our method achieves up to 31.9% and 40.6% relative gains in success rate over pixel-space world models, respectively, while substantially reducing inference latency by up to 98.9%. Our code is available at https://github.com/sjyu001/latent2world.
papers.ja_title: 画面を丸ごと予測しない GUI エージェント用の潜在世界モデル
papers.summary: GUI エージェント向けの画素空間世界モデル (画面そのものを先に予測して行動を選ぶ方式) は、画素再構成の計算コストが高く、行動によらず現在の画面をそのまま予測してしまう「恒等関数への近道」問題があるという困りごとがあった。本研究は予測対象を画面全体ではなく潜在空間の行動由来の変化情報に変え、大規模マルチモーダルモデルの共有表現から行動選択用と遷移予測用の 2 つの頭部を持たせ、行動を意識した対照学習で近道問題を抑えた。オフライン・オンライン両設定で画素空間世界モデルに対し成功率を最大 31.9% と 40.6% (相対) 改善し、推論遅延を最大 98.9% 削減した。
papers.why: エージェント向け世界モデルの作り方として、画面全体を再構成せず潜在空間で行動由来の変化だけを捉える設計により、精度と推論速度を両方改善できる具体例が得られる。
papers.summary_en: Pixel-space world models for GUI agents predict and re-perceive future screens before acting, but this incurs high pixel-reconstruction cost and can suffer an identity shortcut where the predicted future state largely preserves the current state rather than action-induced changes. This work shifts the prediction target to action-induced future information in latent space, using a large multimodal model's shared representations for both action selection and transition prediction, with an action-aware contrastive objective to mitigate the shortcut. Across offline and online GUI settings, the method achieves up to 31.9% and 40.6% relative gains in success rate over pixel-space world models, respectively, while reducing inference latency by up to 98.9%.
papers.why_en: Offers agent world-model builders a concrete architecture where capturing only action-induced latent changes, instead of reconstructing full screens, improves both accuracy and inference speed.

papers.title: Simulate Before You Scale: High-Fidelity LLM Inference Planning Without GPUs
papers.abstract: Deploying large language model (LLM) inference at scale requires jointly selecting hardware layout, parallelism strategy, scheduling policy, admission control, and request routing to meet latency and throughput targets. These choices interact: a routing decision that improves cache locality can concentrate load, and an admission threshold that triggers only at saturation allows queues to grow deep enough to degrade critical-tier traffic. Evaluating candidates on GPU clusters is too expensive for iterative exploration, yet existing predictive tools either ignore batching and queueing dynamics or model only fragments of the pipeline. In this paper, we present BLIS, a deterministic, CPU-only discrete-event simulator that models the full inference serving pipeline (admission, routing, scheduling, prefill/decode execution, KV-cache management, and preemption). BLIS pairs analytical basis functions with learned scaling coefficients and overhead terms, fit once globally, to predict step latency without per-model or per-GPU profiling. Across 36 experiments spanning six models and three GPU types, BLIS achieves 6.7% median end-to-end error while running around 200 times faster than real execution. In a configuration search over 420 serving configurations for Llama-2-70B, BLIS identifies a 4-GPU deployment that meets a 300ms mean TTFT service-level objective (SLO), whereas competing tools either require double the GPUs or recommend configurations that fail under load. Two policies evolved entirely in simulation were validated on real hardware and merged into llm-d, a widely adopted open-source platform for distributed LLM serving: an admission policy that reduces critical-tier TTFT P90 by up to 82%, and a flow-control policy that reduces E2E P50 latency by 32-48% on overloaded workloads.
papers.ja_title: GPU を使わず LLM サービング構成を事前に試す: BLIS シミュレータ
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルの推論を大規模に展開するにはハードウェア構成、並列化、スケジューリング、ルーティングなどを同時に決める必要があるが、GPU クラスタ上で逐一試すのはコストが高すぎるという困りごとがあった。BLIS は許可・ルーティング・スケジューリング・プリフィル/デコード・KV キャッシュ管理までを含む決定的な CPU 専用の離散イベントシミュレータで、6 モデル・3 種 GPU にわたる 36 実験で中央値 6.7% の誤差ながら実機の約 200 倍速く動く。Llama-2-70B の 420 通りの構成探索では、300ms の TTFT (最初のトークンまでの時間) 目標を満たす 4 GPU 構成を他ツールより少ない GPU 数で見つけ、シミュレーションだけで作ったポリシーは実機検証後に OSS の llm-d に統合され、重要トラフィックの TTFT P90 を最大 82%、過負荷時の E2E レイテンシ P50 を 32〜48% 削減した。
papers.why: 推論サービング基盤を作る人にとって、GPU 実機を使わずに構成探索を 200 倍速く行え、その結果が実際に OSS 本番システムに取り込まれた実例として、設計探索コストを下げる具体的な道具が得られる。
papers.summary_en: Deploying LLM inference at scale requires jointly selecting hardware layout, parallelism, scheduling, admission control, and routing, but evaluating candidates on real GPU clusters is too costly for iterative exploration. BLIS is a deterministic, CPU-only discrete-event simulator modeling the full serving pipeline (admission, routing, scheduling, prefill/decode, KV-cache management, preemption), achieving 6.7% median end-to-end error across 36 experiments spanning six models and three GPU types while running around 200 times faster than real execution.
