In a search over 420 serving configurations for Llama-2-70B, BLIS identifies a 4-GPU deployment meeting a 300ms mean TTFT SLO where competing tools need double the GPUs or recommend configurations that fail under load, and two policies evolved entirely in simulation were validated on real hardware and merged into llm-d, reducing critical-tier TTFT P90 by up to 82% and E2E P50 latency by 32-48% under overload.
papers.why_en: Gives inference-serving infrastructure builders a tool to explore serving configurations roughly 200x faster without GPU hardware, with results concretely validated and merged into the production open-source llm-d platform.

papers.title: On the Depth Transfer of Neural Optimizers via L-Smoothness
papers.abstract: Scaling deep learning models efficiently requires predictable performance transfer across compute regimes. Establishing reliable hyperparameter transfer allows optimal training dynamics and structural choices to be discovered on low-cost proxy models, avoiding catastrophic failures during massive-scale training. Existing depth-transfer analyses are architecture-specific and heuristic: hyperparameter transfer is only justified through toy blocks, and both rely on infinite-depth dynamics, a specific initialization, and feature-learning criteria. Building on $L$-smoothness framework of Xu et al. (2026), we understand hyperparameter transfer as how do the Lipschitz and $L$-smoothness constants of the loss scale with the depth $K$? We show that inverse-depth residual branch scaling $α=Θ(1/K)$ is sufficient to make both constants depth-independent at fixed width, uniformly over the bounded parameter domain and for arbitrary $p\to q$ geometries. Because the bounds depend on each residual branch only through its Lipschitz and smoothness constants, the argument applies to general residual networks (including branches of block depth $\geq 2$ such as transformer and ResNet blocks) without assumptions on initialization or correlations between layer weights. Since the smoothness constant controls the curvature penalty in the descent inequality, our bounds motivate a learning-rate scale without an additional depth-dependent curvature correction for updates bounded in the prescribed norm. This provides a geometric explanation of inverse-depth residual scaling and its application to the operator-norm geometries associated with AdamW, Muon, and MOGA. Learning-rate sweeps on GPT-2 (depths 2--128) and CIFAR-100 ResNets (8--32 residual blocks) confirm that Muon and MOGA exhibit stable learning-rate transfer under these prescriptions, with a common optimal rate across a 64-fold increase in depth.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 深さ方向のハイパーパラメータ転移をL-smoothness理論で説明
papers.summary: 小さいモデルで決めた学習率を大きいモデルにそのまま使う「転移」はこれまで特定のアーキテクチャだけで経験的に正当化されていた。この研究は損失関数のリプシッツ定数と平滑性定数(勾配の変化しやすさを表す量)が深さKにどう依存するかを調べ、残差ブランチのスケーリングをα=Θ(1/K)にすると両方の定数が深さに依存しなくなることを示した。GPT-2 (深さ2〜128) と CIFAR-100 の ResNet (8〜32 ブロック) で学習率を調べ、Muon と MOGA という最適化手法では深さを64倍にしても同じ最適学習率が使えることを確認した。
papers.why: 深さが変わっても学習率などを再探索せずに転移できる理論的根拠を与え、巨大モデルの事前学習コストを下げる設計指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Reliable hyperparameter transfer across depth has only been justified heuristically for specific architectures. This work analyzes how the Lipschitz and L-smoothness constants of the loss scale with depth K, showing that inverse-depth residual branch scaling α=Θ(1/K) makes both constants depth-independent for general residual networks, including transformer and ResNet blocks. Learning-rate sweeps on GPT-2 (depths 2-128) and CIFAR-100 ResNets (8-32 blocks) confirm that Muon and MOGA achieve stable transfer with a common optimal learning rate across a 64-fold increase in depth.
papers.why_en: Provides a geometric, architecture-general justification for depth-transfer of learning rates, letting practitioners tune on cheap small models and scale confidently to huge ones.

papers.title: Measuring the Inference Energy Efficiency of Open-Weight LLMs across Benchmarks, Reasoning Modes, and Hardware
papers.abstract: Benchmark scores tell us what an LLM can do, but not how much energy is required to deliver that capability. We directly measure this trade-off for 86 open-weight model checkpoints, evaluated on seven benchmarks and six hardware platforms ranging from a consumer GPU to an eight-GPU server. We find large differences in energy efficiency even among models with similar capability. Most configurations lie away from the score--energy Pareto frontier: they use a median of 2.6--4.8$\times$ more energy than another configuration that scores at least as well, with differences reaching 27$\times$. Reasoning can improve capability, but enabling thinking increases energy by about 3.7$\times$ on average, and the benefit depends strongly on the model family and output budget. Generated-token count is also an imperfect proxy for energy, misordering 18--24\% of model pairs. In contrast, FP8 reduces energy by roughly a quarter with little change in score, while changing hardware largely rescales energy without changing the relative ranking of models. These results show that capability alone gives an incomplete picture of efficiency. We argue that benchmark scores should be reported together with measured energy consumption under a specified serving regime and output budget.
papers.ja_title: LLM 推論のエネルギー効率をベンチマーク・推論モード・ハードウェア別に実測
papers.summary: LLM (大規模言語モデル) の良さはベンチマークの点数で語られがちだが、その点数を出すのに必要な電力はよく分かっていなかった。研究チームは 86 個の公開重みモデルを 7 つのベンチマーク、6 種類のハードウェア (家庭用 GPU から 8 GPU サーバーまで) で実測し、同程度の性能でも構成によってエネルギー消費が中央値で 2.6〜4.8 倍、最大 27 倍も違うことを示した。思考 (reasoning) モードを使うと平均で約 3.7 倍エネルギーが増え、生成トークン数だけでは 18〜24% のモデルペアでエネルギーの良し悪しを取り違えることも分かった。一方、FP8 (8 ビットの低精度形式) を使うと点数をほとんど落とさずにエネルギーを約 4 分の 1 減らせた。
papers.why: ベンチマーク点数だけでなく実測エネルギーとサービング条件をセットで報告すべきという提案で、推論基盤のコスト評価のやり方を見直す材料になる。
papers.summary_en: Benchmark scores reveal what an LLM can do but not the energy cost of delivering it. Measuring 86 open-weight checkpoints across seven benchmarks and six hardware platforms (consumer GPU to 8-GPU server), the authors find most configurations use a median of 2.6-4.8x more energy than a Pareto-optimal configuration scoring at least as well, with gaps reaching 27x; enabling 'thinking' mode raises energy by about 3.7x on average, generated-token count misorders 18-24% of model-pair energy comparisons, while FP8 cuts energy by roughly a quarter with little change in score.
papers.why_en: Argues benchmark scores should always be reported alongside measured energy under a specified serving regime, offering a concrete way to rethink how inference cost/efficiency claims are evaluated.

review.note: ベンチマーク点数だけでなく実測エネルギーとサービング条件を合わせて見る、という評価方法の落とし穴を示す例。
review.note_en: Shows a pitfall in benchmarking: scores alone are misleading without measured energy and a specified serving regime.

papers.title: Memory Without Curation: Learning Multi-Stream Latent Memory for Robot Policies
papers.abstract: It is widely appreciated that robotic policies require long-term memory to perform complex tasks. However, directly conditioning policies on all past observations leaves policy learning susceptible to learning spurious shortcuts, and introduces large latency at policy deployment. As such, today's memory-augmented policies curate what to remember, either by retaining only recent frames, selected keyframes, or textual summaries, or by learning latent representations of the visual stream alone. In this work, we propose an alternative approach IMPRINT, a policy-agnostic latent memory framework that augments vision-language-action (VLA) models with multi-stream memory without explicitly constraining what the policy should remember. IMPRINT compresses different streams into a latent memory that is updated incrementally at inference, enabling low latency. To avoid shortcut learning, IMPRINT adopts a two-stage training procedure, first supervising memory to reconstruct multiple streams (observations, actions, proprioception) of past information, as well as estimate current task progress, followed by end-to-end finetuning, jointly with the policy, on action prediction. Across both simulation and real-world tasks demanding memory, IMPRINT improves average success over the base VLA by at least 26%, outperforming popular alternatives, and maintaining lowest inference latency among memory-augmented VLAs. Through careful ablations, we demonstrate the utility of incorporating diverse information streams into robotic memory, validating the advantages of foregoing history curation. Project website: https://yilin-wu98.github.io/imprint_website/.

papers.title: Scaling Laws for Multimodal Data Mixtures
papers.abstract: Frontier AI systems are increasingly natively multimodal, jointly pretrained on multiple modalities, such as text, vision, and audio. However, the scientific understanding of the multimodal data mixtures used to pretrain these systems --- how much of each modality to mix, and at what potential interference cost to the others --- is largely absent or gatekept. In this work, we derive data mixing scaling laws for three modalities: text, vision, and audio. Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) increasingly adopt Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures, as MoEs scale efficiently and partially limit cross-modal interference. We therefore use MoEs to conduct 268 experiments ranging from 457M to 8.3B parameters, on up to 150 billion tokens. Our work leads to multiple actionable insights into multimodal data mixing for training MLLMs. First, compute optima are modality-specific: audio modality is model-heavy, favoring scaling parameters over tokens, while text and vision require balanced scaling of model size and data. Second, repeating vision or audio data beyond 2x yields negligible benefits. Finally, cross-modal interactions are highly asymmetric: vision strongly interferes with audio, whereas audio's interference with learning text and vision is negligible. Overall, we provide a principled foundation for understanding the multimodal data mixtures needed to train frontier MLLMs.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: テキスト・画像・音声を混ぜて事前学習するときの最適な配合則
papers.summary: テキスト・画像・音声を同時に学習するマルチモーダル LLM では、各モダリティをどの割合で混ぜるべきかという知見がほとんど公開されていなかった。研究チームは Mixture-of-Experts (専門家ごとに計算を分けるモデル構造) を使い、457M〜8.3B パラメータ、最大 1500 億トークンの範囲で 268 回の実験を行い、モダリティごとのスケーリング則を導いた。その結果、音声はパラメータを増やす方が有利でテキストと画像はパラメータとデータを同じ比率で増やすのが良いこと、画像や音声のデータを 2 倍以上繰り返しても効果が小さいこと、画像は音声の学習を強く妨げるが音声はテキスト・画像の学習をほぼ妨げないという非対称な干渉があることが分かった。
papers.why: 複数モダリティを混ぜて事前学習する際の計算配分・データ配合を決めるための実測に基づく指針を提供し、巨大マルチモーダルモデルの学習計画を立てやすくする。
papers.summary_en: Little is scientifically known about how to mix text, vision, and audio data when pretraining natively multimodal MLLMs. Using Mixture-of-Experts architectures, the authors run 268 experiments from 457M to 8.3B parameters on up to 150B tokens to derive per-modality data-mixing scaling laws, finding that audio is model-heavy (favoring more parameters over tokens) while text and vision need balanced scaling, that repeating vision or audio data beyond 2x gives negligible benefit, and that cross-modal interference is highly asymmetric: vision strongly interferes with audio while audio barely interferes with text or vision.
papers.why_en: Offers a principled, empirically grounded foundation for deciding compute and data allocation across modalities when pretraining frontier multimodal models.

papers.title: KV4-RL: Unlocking Faster Asynchronous Rollouts for RLVR with INT4 KV Cache Quantization
papers.abstract: Asynchronous rollout improves the efficiency of reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) by reducing under-utilization during long-tail generation. Sustained concurrency also concentrates context processing into fewer decode steps, increasing the KV workload per step. We characterize this \emph{KV concentration} and find that KV cache quantization delivers substantially greater acceleration than weight-only and weight-activation quantization in our matched-workload comparisons. However, INT4 KV rollout can degrade learning even with token-level truncated importance sampling (TIS). We propose \emph{KV4-RL}, which combines calibration-free INT4 KV quantization with selective INT8 protection of attention sinks and recent context. Protecting a bounded number of positions reduces sampler mismatch while retaining most of the speedup from INT4. Across 400 iterations of Qwen3-8B-Base GRPO training, KV4-RL achieves $1.80\times$ cumulative rollout speedup and $1.27\times$ cumulative full-iteration speedup over BF16 rollout, reaching $1.97\times$ rollout speedup over the final 50 iterations. Under a common BF16 evaluator, its final six-benchmark mean accuracy is within 0.5 percentage points of BF16-rollout training for both Qwen3-4B-Base and Qwen3-8B-Base.
papers.ja_title: KV キャッシュを 4 ビット量子化して強化学習のロールアウトを高速化
papers.summary: 検証可能な報酬による強化学習 (RLVR) では、非同期で文章生成 (ロールアウト) を進めるほど KV キャッシュ (注意機構が使う中間データ) の処理が 1 ステップに集中して負荷が増える問題があった。研究チームは KV キャッシュを 4 ビット (INT4) に量子化しつつ、注意の「シンク」位置と直近の文脈だけは 8 ビットで保護する KV4-RL という手法を提案した。Qwen3-8B-Base の GRPO 学習 400 イテレーションで、BF16 に比べてロールアウトが累積 1.80 倍、全体では 1.27 倍速くなり、直近 50 イテレーションではロールアウトが 1.97 倍まで速くなった一方、6 つのベンチマークの平均精度は BF16 学習と 0.5 ポイント以内の差に収まった。
papers.why: RL 後学習のロールアウト段階における KV キャッシュ量子化という、学習品質を保ったまま高速化する実用的な手法を示しており、RL 基盤の実装に直接応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Asynchronous rollout in RLVR concentrates context processing into fewer decode steps, increasing KV-cache workload per step; the authors find KV-cache quantization accelerates this far more than weight-only or weight-activation quantization, but naive INT4 KV degrades learning even with truncated importance sampling. Their proposed KV4-RL, which combines calibration-free INT4 KV quantization with selective INT8 protection of attention sinks and recent context, achieves 1.80x cumulative rollout speedup and 1.27x cumulative full-iteration speedup over BF16 (1.97x rollout speedup over the final 50 iterations) across 400 iterations of Qwen3-8B-Base GRPO training, with final six-benchmark mean accuracy within 0.5 points of BF16-rollout training.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates a practical KV-cache quantization recipe for RL rollout that preserves learning quality while speeding up generation, directly applicable to RL post-training infrastructure.

papers.title: GMM: Generalized OS Memory Management for Programmable XPUs
papers.abstract: Since the AI boom, the fast evolving programmable XPU devices utilize high-bandwidth local memory to accelerate domain-specific tasks offloaded from the host CPU, resulting in a proliferation of XPU memory management systems implemented in proprietary drivers. However, existing OS core memory management (MM) continues to lack a high-level software abstraction, excluding the XPUs from leveraging OS advanced memory features. The XPU manufacturers have to reimplement independent XPU MM drivers, exacerbating the fragmented XPU software ecosystem. This paper presents GMM, generalized memory management that provides unified MM subsystems for XPUs. By adding an explicit logical mapping abstraction, GMM 1) provides universal NUMA-aware memory API for XPUs; 2) allows ease of XPU MM delegation; 3) enables sharing of advanced XPU memory features. Lightweight XPU MM drivers are implemented for two representative XPU manufacturers, Nvidia and Huawei. Both GMM-based drivers obtain competitive performance compared with their vendor-supplied drivers. GMM also obtains up to 41% higher fault-driven page migration throughput. Two real-world industrial case studies are exercised, where GMM reduces XPU memory utilization by 10% with up to 22.6x faster inference serving switch latency.
papers.ja_title: XPU 向けに OS のメモリ管理機能を一般化する GMM
papers.summary: GPU や NPU などの XPU は高速な専用メモリを使うが、OS のメモリ管理機能がそれに対応しておらず、各メーカーが独自ドライバをそれぞれ再実装してエコシステムが分断していた。研究チームは「論理マッピング」という抽象化を加えることで、NUMA を意識したメモリ API や高度なメモリ機能を XPU でも共通に使える GMM という仕組みを作り、Nvidia と Huawei 向けの軽量ドライバで実証した。実測ではベンダー公式ドライバと同等の性能を保ちながら、ページマイグレーション (メモリ移動) のスループットが最大 41% 向上し、実際の産業事例ではメモリ使用量を 10% 減らしつつ推論サービングの切り替え遅延を最大 22.6 倍高速化した。
papers.why: 推論基盤を支えるメモリ管理層を XPU ベンダーをまたいで統一する提案で、サービング基盤の設計・移植性を考える人にとって参考になる。
papers.summary_en: XPU accelerators rely on high-bandwidth local memory, but OS memory management lacks a high-level abstraction for them, forcing each vendor to reimplement fragmented proprietary MM drivers. The authors introduce GMM, which adds an explicit logical mapping abstraction to provide a unified, NUMA-aware memory API and shareable advanced memory features across XPUs, implementing lightweight drivers for Nvidia and Huawei that match vendor-supplied driver performance while achieving up to 41% higher fault-driven page migration throughput, and in real industrial case studies reducing XPU memory utilization by 10% with up to 22.6x faster inference serving switch latency.
papers.why_en: Proposes a vendor-agnostic unification of the memory-management layer underlying inference serving infrastructure, relevant to anyone designing portable serving systems across XPU hardware.

papers.title: Reward-Aligned Distillation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards improves the reasoning capabilities of large language models, but remains computationally expensive and sample inefficient. On-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense token-level supervision from a stronger teacher, yet standard OPD distills every token regardless of whether the teacher's preference actually improves task reward. Existing token-selection methods rely on proxies such as uncertainty or teacher--student divergence, which need not identify reward-improving supervision. We introduce Reward-Aligned Distillation (RAD), a bilevel framework that weights distillation signals based on their predicted effect on the student's post-update reward. RAD differentiates through a temporary optimizer step to score each token's supervision, then updates the token weights by projected ascent from the initial token weights. The resulting weights can strengthen, suppress, or reverse individual distillation-gradient contributions. At a matched training-response budget, RAD improves mean accuracy on six competition-math benchmarks over the strongest baselines by 6.5 percentage points for Qwen3-1.7B (non-thinking) and 2.5 points for Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507. RAD-Simple, a simplified variant, achieves comparable math accuracy at the same training-response budget. On LiveCodeBench-v6, RAD reaches 54.69\% and 58.67\% pass@1 with Qwen3-1.7B (non-thinking) and OLMo3-7B-Instruct, respectively, exceeding the strongest baselines by 8.7 and 6.4 points. These results support reward-guided weighting of teacher supervision across model families and tasks.
papers.ja_title: 報酬改善につながるトークンだけを重視する蒸留手法 RAD
papers.summary: 検証可能な報酬による強化学習は計算コストが高く効率が悪いため、強い教師モデルから各トークン単位で学習する On-policy 蒸留が使われるが、従来は教師の好みが実際に報酬を改善するかを無視して全トークンを同じように蒸留していた。研究チームは、生徒モデルを一時的に更新したときの報酬への効果を予測してトークンごとの重みを決める Reward-Aligned Distillation (RAD) を提案した。同じ学習コストのもとで、6 つの競技数学ベンチマークの平均精度を最良の既存手法より Qwen3-1.7B で 6.5 ポイント、Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 で 2.5 ポイント上回り、LiveCodeBench-v6 でも既存手法を 8.7 ポイントと 6.4 ポイント上回った。
papers.why: 蒸留の際にどのトークンを強く学習させるべきかを報酬に基づいて決める仕組みで、RL 後学習と蒸留を組み合わせる基盤設計に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation gives dense token-level supervision from a stronger teacher but standard OPD distills every token regardless of whether the teacher's preference actually improves task reward, and existing token-selection proxies need not identify reward-improving supervision. The authors propose Reward-Aligned Distillation (RAD), which differentiates through a temporary optimizer step to weight each token's supervision by its predicted effect on post-update reward; at a matched training-response budget, RAD improves mean accuracy on six competition-math benchmarks over the strongest baselines by 6.5 points for Qwen3-1.7B and 2.5 points for Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507, and on LiveCodeBench-v6 exceeds the strongest baselines by 8.7 and 6.4 points.
papers.why_en: Offers a reward-guided way to decide which tokens matter most during distillation, directly useful for building infrastructure that combines RL post-training with distillation.

papers.title: Shaping Latent Mixture-of-Experts: From Expert Geometry to Layerwise Capacity Allocation
papers.abstract: Fine-grained mixture-of-experts (MoE) models commonly increase expert count by narrowing each expert, treating expert shape as a by-product of routing granularity. LatentMoE moves expert computation into a lower-dimensional space, exposing the input dimension and intermediate width of each expert as explicit design choices. We show that an expert's local Jacobian rank is jointly bounded by these two dimensions, and that balancing them maximizes the rank ceiling at fixed per-expert parameters. Controlled shape sweeps across model scales and routing granularities consistently favor near-square experts. We further use layerwise intrinsic dimension (ID) to guide capacity allocation across depth, co-varying the number and shape of experts while keeping per-layer parameter count, activated FLOPs, and communication volume constant. Compared with layer-homogeneous baselines, our ID-guided allocation achieves lower validation loss and stronger downstream performance. These results establish expert shape and layerwise allocation as practical design axes for MoEs.
papers.ja_title: LatentMoE で専門家の形と層ごとの容量配分を最適化する
papers.summary: 細粒度の Mixture-of-Experts (専門家ごとに計算を分ける構造) は専門家数を増やすほど各専門家を細くしてきたが、専門家の「形」自体は設計対象として扱われていなかった。この研究は専門家の計算を低次元の潜在空間に移す LatentMoE を使い、入力次元と中間幅という形を明示的に調整できるようにし、両者をバランスさせると局所的な行列のランク上限 (表現力の目安) が最大化されることを示した。層ごとの固有次元 (ID) を使って専門家の数と形を層ごとに配分する手法を作り、パラメータ数・計算量・通信量を一定に保ったまま層が均一な従来構成より検証損失を下げ、下流タスクの性能も改善した。
papers.why: 専門家の形と層ごとの容量配分という新しい設計軸を示し、MoE モデルのアーキテクチャ設計を最適化する際の具体的な指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Fine-grained MoE models typically increase expert count by narrowing each expert, treating expert shape as an afterthought of routing granularity. By moving expert computation into a lower-dimensional latent space (LatentMoE), the authors expose input dimension and intermediate width as explicit design choices, show that an expert's local Jacobian rank is jointly bounded by these two dimensions and maximized when they are balanced, and use layerwise intrinsic dimension to guide capacity allocation across depth; at fixed per-layer parameters, FLOPs, and communication volume, this ID-guided allocation achieves lower validation loss and stronger downstream performance than layer-homogeneous baselines.
papers.why_en: Establishes expert shape and layerwise capacity allocation as new, practical design axes for MoE architectures, giving concrete guidance for architecture design work.

papers.title: Vesta: Queueing-Aware LLM Scheduling for Real-World Workloads
papers.abstract: Agentic applications generate multi-turn sequences of LLM requests, with each new turn extending the context accumulated from prior interactions and tool calls. Prefix caching reuses the KV cache of earlier turns and avoids redundant prefill, but routing every turn to its cache-affine instance can create severe local queues while capacity remains idle elsewhere. Remote KV cache access relaxes this tension, yet migrating execution adds transfer work and is harmful when the cluster is already congested. Thus, deciding where to execute a request requires reasoning jointly about cache locality, queueing, and the current operating point of the cluster. We present Vesta, a queueing-aware scheduler for distributed agentic LLM serving. Vesta assigns each session a stable holder for its authoritative KV cache while independently selecting an executor for every request. Grounded in classical queueing theory, its objective accounts for backlog, reusable prefixes, KV cache transfer, and the queueing externality of additional service demand; it migrates execution to recover idle capacity when beneficial and favors placements that add the least prefill and transfer work as congestion rises. Vesta also migrates reusable prefixes across length buckets to avoid cold starts. On real-world agentic workloads, Vesta improves throughput by 14.0\% and reduces mean TTFT by 57.8\% over the state-of-the-art scheduler in a PD-colocated deployment. In PD-disaggregated deployments, it reduces mean TTFT by up to 18.1\% and P99 TTFT by up to 29.0\% at matched throughput.
papers.ja_title: キュー理論に基づくエージェント型 LLM のスケジューリング
papers.summary: 複数ターンのやり取りを行うエージェント型アプリでは、計算済みの中間結果(KVキャッシュ)を再利用するために毎ターンを同じ装置に送ると、その装置だけ混雑し他が空いてしまう問題がある。Vesta はキュー理論(待ち行列の理論)に基づき、キャッシュの位置と現在の混雑状況を同時に考慮して実行場所を選ぶスケジューラを提案した。実世界のエージェント処理で、既存最良のスケジューラに比べスループットを 14.0% 向上させ、平均 TTFT(最初の応答が出るまでの時間)を 57.8% 削減し、別構成でも同じスループットで TTFT を最大 29.0% 削減した。
papers.why: マルチターンのエージェント処理におけるキャッシュ局所性とキュー混雑のトレードオフを定量的に解いた、分散推論サービングの実践的な配置方式。
papers.summary_en: In agentic multi-turn LLM serving, routing every turn to its cache-affine instance to reuse the KV cache can create severe local queues while other capacity idles. Vesta, grounded in classical queueing theory, jointly reasons about cache locality, backlog, and transfer cost to decide where to execute each request. On real-world agentic workloads it improves throughput by 14.0% and reduces mean TTFT by 57.8% over the state-of-the-art scheduler in a PD-colocated deployment, and reduces mean TTFT by up to 18.1% and P99 TTFT by up to 29.0% at matched throughput in PD-disaggregated deployments.
papers.why_en: Offers a queueing-theory-grounded placement policy that resolves the locality-vs-congestion tradeoff in distributed agentic LLM serving.

papers.title: Accelerating Cross-Model LLM Inference via Attention Map Reuse
papers.abstract: LLM-augmented data workflows often involve multiple heterogeneous models operating over substantial shared context, such as schemas, tool specifications, interaction history, and intermediate results. Although prefix caching can reduce prefilling overhead, existing approaches are largely limited to reuse within the same model because KV states are tightly coupled to model-specific architectures. We present MapFlow, a system for efficient heterogeneous LLM serving via cross-model attention map reuse. Instead of reusing KV states, MapFlow reuses attention maps, which capture token dependency patterns and are more transferable across models. To enable efficient and accurate reuse, we combine partial recomputation with lightweight linear translation across layers and heads. To make attention reuse practical for long contexts, we further introduce block-level sparse compression and a fused retrieval kernel. Experiments show that MapFlow reduces prefilling latency and improves end-to-end serving efficiency while preserving generation quality across heterogeneous model pairs and multi-turn routing workloads. These results suggest that attention maps provide an effective reusable state for heterogeneous LLM serving, especially in prefix-heavy data workflows. Our code is available: https://github.com/PKU-DAIR/MapFlow.
papers.ja_title: アテンションマップ再利用による異種モデル間の前処理高速化
papers.summary: 複数の異なる LLM がスキーマやツール仕様などの大きな共有コンテキストを扱うとき、モデルごとに異なる KV キャッシュ(内部状態)は使い回せず、前処理(プリフィル)が重複してしまう。MapFlow は KV 状態の代わりに、トークン間の依存関係を表し転用しやすいアテンションマップを再利用し、部分再計算と層・ヘッド間の軽量な線形変換、ブロック単位の疎圧縮、融合検索カーネルを組み合わせる。異種モデル間やマルチターンのルーティングで生成品質を保ちながらプリフィル遅延とサービング全体の効率を改善した。
papers.why: 複数モデルを横断するエージェント的データワークフローで、モデルをまたいだキャッシュ再利用という新しい着眼点を示す。
papers.summary_en: In LLM-augmented workflows with multiple heterogeneous models sharing substantial context, KV states are model-specific and cannot be reused, causing redundant prefill. MapFlow instead reuses attention maps, which capture transferable token dependency patterns, combining partial recomputation, lightweight linear translation across layers/heads, block-level sparse compression, and a fused retrieval kernel. Experiments show MapFlow reduces prefilling latency and improves end-to-end serving efficiency while preserving generation quality across heterogeneous model pairs and multi-turn routing workloads.
papers.why_en: Introduces cross-model cache reuse via attention maps as a new reusable state for heterogeneous LLM serving in prefix-heavy workflows.

papers.title: AgentWeave: Efficient Distributed Agent Serving via Flow Decomposition
papers.abstract: Agent applications are evolving into workflows composed of large language model (LLM) calls and tool invocations, termed modules. Existing distributed agent systems typically adopt a disaggregated architecture, deploying different modules on separate devices. While this enables pipeline parallelism, imbalanced module latencies introduce severe pipeline bubbles that limit throughput. A natural alternative is an aggregated architecture that co-deploys all modules across all devices, eliminating bubbles by keeping every device continuously active. However, this introduces request blocking: short requests are forced to progress in lockstep with longer ones in the same batch, and newly arriving requests must wait until the entire ongoing batch completes the full workflow. To address this, we propose AgentWeave, an efficient distributed serving system for agent applications built on the aggregated architecture. Its core mechanism, flow decomposition, decomposes long agent requests into fine-grained execution units while preserving agent semantics, allowing short and newly arriving requests to proceed without being stalled by long-running ones. Complementing this, a flow-adaptive scheduler dynamically balances the throughput gains of decomposition against its scheduling overhead. Experiments across four representative agent applications demonstrate that AgentWeave improves throughput by 1.81x, reduces average latency by 2.45x, and reduces P90 latency by 2.04x over state-of-the-art baselines.
papers.ja_title: フロー分解によるエージェント処理の分散サービング
papers.summary: LLM 呼び出しとツール呼び出しを組み合わせたエージェント処理を複数の装置に分けて配置する「分離構成」はモジュール間の速度差でパイプラインに空き時間(バブル)が生じ、全モジュールを全装置に置く「集約構成」は短い要求が長い要求に足を引かれて待たされてしまう。AgentWeave はエージェントの意味を保ったまま要求を細かい実行単位に分解する「フロー分解」と、分解の利益とスケジューリングコストを動的に調整する仕組みを提案した。4 種類の代表的なエージェント応用で、既存最良手法に比べスループットを 1.81 倍、平均レイテンシを 2.45 倍、P90 レイテンシを 2.04 倍改善した。
papers.why: パイプライン並列の空き時間と要求レベルの待たされ問題という、分散エージェント推論サービングの設計上のジレンマに対する具体的な解決策を示す。
papers.summary_en: Disaggregated agent-serving architectures suffer pipeline bubbles from imbalanced module latencies, while aggregated architectures suffer request blocking where short requests must wait on long ones in the same batch. AgentWeave's flow decomposition breaks long agent requests into fine-grained execution units while preserving agent semantics, paired with a flow-adaptive scheduler balancing decomposition gains against overhead. Across four representative agent applications, it improves throughput by 1.81x, reduces average latency by 2.45x, and reduces P90 latency by 2.04x over state-of-the-art baselines.
papers.why_en: Provides a concrete resolution to the bubble-vs-blocking dilemma in distributed agentic LLM serving architectures.

papers.title: Seamless Deployment of Machine Learning Inference at the Far Edge: An Empirical AWS IoT Greengrass Architecture for Industrial Predictive Maintenance
papers.abstract: Industrial IoT sensors produce continuous, high-volume data streams that predictive maintenance needs to analyse in real time. Cloud-centric architectures send all raw telemetry to central servers, which costs latency, bandwidth and resilience. This paper presents a hybrid cloud-edge architecture for manufacturing predictive maintenance built on AWS IoT Core and AWS IoT Greengrass v2, with local machine learning inference at the edge and selective cloud synchronization. We deploy two configurations on real AWS infrastructure and compare them: a cloud-only baseline (Configuration A) and the proposed hybrid edge architecture (Configuration B). We measure end-to-end inference latency, bandwidth consumption and inference accuracy. Configuration B cuts cloud-bound bandwidth by 86.8% (63.6 KB to 7.2 KB per 200-reading window) and decision latency by 256x (23.1 ms cloud round trip to 0.09 ms local inference). At the edge, with no cloud involvement, it keeps an anomaly-class F1 score of 0.84 and 91% recall. The evaluation also instruments system uptime and Stream Manager queuing under cloud disconnection; the quantitative disconnection experiment is left as planned work. Our review of the literature points to four gaps that this work addresses: the lack of empirically validated Greengrass v2 deployments for predictive maintenance, unquantified bandwidth savings from selective edge synchronization, unmeasured resilience under cloud disconnection, and the open MLOps feedback loop at the edge.

papers.title: Getting Space Right: Agentic Rewards for Image Generation
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is promising for spatial text-to-image generation, but existing work largely focuses on policy optimization, assuming accurate rewards and effective online rollouts. We observe in-domain gains with out-of-domain degradation, exposing two limitations: unreliable spatial rewards in open-world settings and rollouts lacking basic-to-complex progression. We propose a curriculum-guided RL framework. First, we introduce SpatialCritic, an agentic reward model equipped with a spatial perception harness that combines reusable verification guidance with specialized vision tools. We then construct spatial preference datasets through targeted counterfactual perturbations and perform agent-harness alignment to improve tool selection and evidence integration efficiently. Second, curriculum learning organizes shared foundational capabilities and their compositional dependencies in a capability graph for mastery-guided rollouts, periodic review, and targeted remediation. On SpaRW-Eval, SpatialCritic achieves 95.1% verification accuracy, outperforming 320B GLM-5.3-Flash with a 40x smaller 8B backbone and raising average baseline scores from 78.4 to 83.9 on SD3.5-Medium and 83.2 to 86.5 on BAGEL. Project page: https://xiaofeng-tan.github.io/projects/spatialcritic/
papers.ja_title: 空間認識の報酬モデルとカリキュラム学習で画像生成の RL を改善
papers.summary: 物の位置や向きなどの空間関係を正しく描く画像生成の強化学習(RL)では、学習に使った範囲では良くなるのに、それ以外の範囲では逆に悪化してしまう問題があった。原因は、自由な設定での空間に関する報酬(ご褒美の計算)が不正確なことと、簡単な課題から複雑な課題への学習順序(カリキュラム)が欠けていることにある。研究チームは視覚ツールと検証ガイドを組み合わせた報酬モデル SpatialCritic と、能力間の依存関係を整理したカリキュラム学習を提案し、SpaRW-Eval で検証精度 95.1% を達成して 40 倍大きい 320B の GLM-5.3-Flash を 8B のモデルで上回り、SD3.5-Medium の平均スコアを 78.4 から 83.9、BAGEL を 83.2 から 86.5 に改善した。
papers.why: 画像生成の RL 後学習で、未知の範囲に対する性能低下を報酬モデルの信頼性とカリキュラム設計の両面から改善する具体的な方法を示す。
papers.summary_en: RL for spatial text-to-image generation shows in-domain gains but out-of-domain degradation, exposing unreliable spatial rewards in open-world settings and rollouts lacking basic-to-complex progression. The authors propose SpatialCritic, an agentic reward model with a spatial perception harness combining verification guidance and vision tools, plus curriculum learning over a capability graph of foundational skills and dependencies. SpatialCritic achieves 95.1% verification accuracy on SpaRW-Eval, outperforming the 320B GLM-5.3-Flash with a 40x smaller 8B backbone, and raises average scores from 78.4 to 83.9 on SD3.5-Medium and 83.2 to 86.5 on BAGEL.
papers.why_en: Shows a concrete fix for out-of-domain degradation in RL-based image generation by jointly improving reward reliability and curriculum design.

papers.title: TeachGrade: Training-Free Short Answer Scoring with Teacher Evidence
papers.abstract: Multi-subject, multi-step scoring requires consistent partial credit across grading conventions. We introduce TeachGrade, a training-free framework using teacher-graded examples. The Task Adapt module builds two frozen memories: Skill captures contextual teacher preferences beyond the rubric; CaseBank supplies local evidence. PreJudge provides retrieval cues; FinalJudge regrades the answer without preliminary scores. On 3,829 SAS-Bench answers across 12 tasks, official macro collaborative consistency score (CCS) rises from Native's 67.99 to 81.32 (+13.33 points), and pooled step exact match from 54.85% to 62.71%. Macro quadratic weighted kappa (QWK) reaches 84.71, exceeding Native, OpenJudge, ProofGrader, and Trojsten by 9.52, 3.50, 11.37, and 17.43 points, respectively, and leading on 8 tasks. Local Qwen3.8-27B gains 8.83 CCS and 4.08 QWK points, improving CCS on all 12 tasks. QWK gains over Native span 6.38--14.65 points on Portuguese automatic essay scoring (AES) and 2.16--2.24 on ASAP-SAS across label views, with lower mean absolute error. These results support reuse across languages, response formats, and backbones without weight updates.

papers.title: FidelityQ: Preserving Predictive Fidelity in Ultra-Low-Bit Language Model Quantization
papers.abstract: Ultra-low-bit scalar quantization offers a regular arithmetic structure for efficient deployment of large language models, but preserving predictive behavior at extreme precision remains challenging: with only a few reconstruction levels, accurate weight representation must translate into consistent predictions from a small calibration set. We propose FidelityQ, a scalar quantization framework that preserves predictive fidelity at weight precisions down to 2 bits. For accurate quantization, we introduce Information-Aligned Analytic Coding (IAC), which shapes each weight row toward a centered symmetric source via randomized Hadamard mixing and fits a mirrored four-level minimum-distortion quantizer to its empirical weights. Every level set in this family decomposes exactly into two sign-valued bases with associated scales, combining source-adaptive reconstruction with lookup-free decoding compatible with scaled integer arithmetic. Our analysis further shows that residual predictive discrepancies are heavy-tailed and concentrate on tokens the teacher predicts confidently, motivating Knowledge-Intensive Calibration (KIC) for consistent quantization. KIC ranks sequences by the tail of token-wise teacher-student divergence, allocates a limited calibration budget to the highest-scoring samples, and restores predictive agreement by updating only quantization levels and scales under teacher supervision, keeping pretrained weights frozen. Experiments on the LLaMA and Qwen families demonstrate the effectiveness of FidelityQ in weight-only and joint quantization settings. On LLaMA-2-7B, FidelityQ achieves a WikiText2 perplexity of 6.62 at W2A16 and improves the prior state-of-the-art W2A4KV4 result from 8.31 to 6.96, while reducing linear-layer weight memory by 8.0x relative to FP16.
papers.ja_title: 超低ビット量子化でも予測の一致を保つ FidelityQ
papers.summary: LLM を 2 ビットのような極端に少ないビット数で量子化(数値を粗い段階に近似すること)すると、重みをどれだけ正確に再現できても、モデルの予測が元のモデルと一致しなくなりやすい。FidelityQ は、重みの分布をランダム化アダマール変換で整えて 4 段階の最小歪み量子化器を当てる符号化 (IAC) と、教師モデルと生徒モデルの予測差が大きい系列だけに絞って量子化の段階値を再調整する校正 (KIC) を組み合わせる。LLaMA-2-7B で WikiText2 の perplexity(予測の悪さを表す指標)を W2A16 で 6.62 に抑え、既存最良の W2A4KV4 の結果を 8.31 から 6.96 に改善し、線形層の重みメモリを FP16 比で 8.0 倍削減した。
papers.why: 2 ビット級の超低ビット量子化で、単に重みを再現するだけでなく予測の一致度まで保つ具体的な符号化・校正手法を示し、低精度カーネル実装の指針になる。
papers.summary_en: At ultra-low-bit scalar quantization (as low as 2 bits), accurate weight reconstruction does not guarantee consistent predictions from the quantized model. FidelityQ combines Information-Aligned Analytic Coding (IAC), which shapes weight rows via randomized Hadamard mixing into a mirrored four-level minimum-distortion quantizer, with Knowledge-Intensive Calibration (KIC), which allocates a limited calibration budget to sequences with the highest teacher-student divergence and updates only quantization levels/scales. On LLaMA-2-7B, FidelityQ achieves a WikiText2 perplexity of 6.62 at W2A16 and improves the prior state-of-the-art W2A4KV4 result from 8.31 to 6.96, while reducing linear-layer weight memory by 8.0x relative to FP16.
papers.why_en: Provides a concrete coding and calibration approach that preserves predictive fidelity, not just weight accuracy, at 2-bit-class ultra-low-bit quantization, directly relevant to low-precision kernel design.

papers.title: MCPDisCo: Seesaw-Mitigated Tuning for MCP-Native Agents
papers.abstract: The Model Context Protocol provides a shared interaction substrate for the agentic web, allowing heterogeneous services to expose capabilities through a standardized interface. Learning to use this ecosystem entails a hierarchy of capabilities: tool-format skills, server-level transfer, and cross-server composition. We present MCPDisCo, an ecosystem-scale reinforcement learning framework for MCP-native agents. Using a Thought-Markov Decision Process (Thought-MDP), the framework explicitly represents internal reasoning alongside routing, execution, and termination and trains on real-server, long-horizon interactions spanning 70 MCP servers and 527 tools across six domains. We study the reasoning--tool seesaw, a joint-learning failure mode in which improvement in one objective can accompany deterioration in the other. To mitigate potential interference, MCPDisCo combines token-masked reward attribution with bidirectional gradient surgery: the former separates direct supervision for reasoning and action spans, while the latter removes conflicting components from both objective gradients in shared parameters. MCPDisCo achieves higher success with fewer chain-of-thought tokens. On the out-of-distribution MCP-Atlas and the GAIA benchmark, MCPDisCo maintains monotone gains, confirming that the learned behavior generalizes beyond the training server distribution and broader agentic tasks. Model weight and implementation are available.
papers.ja_title: 推論とツール利用の『せめぎ合い』を抑える MCP エージェントの RL
papers.summary: Model Context Protocol (MCP、エージェントが外部サービスを呼ぶための共通規格)を使うエージェントの学習では、推論力とツール利用力を同時に伸ばそうとすると、一方が良くなると他方が悪くなる「せめぎ合い」が起きる。MCPDisCo は内部の思考過程を明示的に扱う Thought-MDP のもと、70 の MCP サーバーと 527 のツールを使った長い対話で学習し、報酬の割り当てをトークン単位で分けつつ、勾配の衝突成分を取り除く双方向勾配手術でこのせめぎ合いを緩和する。より少ない思考トークンで高い成功率を達成し、未知の MCP-Atlas や GAIA ベンチマークでも学習時の傾向を保って性能が一貫して向上した。
papers.why: マルチターン・多ツールのエージェント RL 学習で生じる目的間の干渉を、報酬の帰属分割と勾配操作で緩和する具体的な手法を示す。
papers.summary_en: Training MCP-native agents jointly on reasoning and tool-use objectives can hit the "reasoning--tool seesaw," where improving one objective degrades the other. MCPDisCo uses a Thought-MDP that explicitly represents internal reasoning alongside routing/execution/termination, training on real-server, long-horizon interactions across 70 MCP servers and 527 tools, and mitigates interference via token-masked reward attribution plus bidirectional gradient surgery that removes conflicting gradient components. MCPDisCo achieves higher success with fewer chain-of-thought tokens and maintains monotone gains on the out-of-distribution MCP-Atlas and GAIA benchmarks, confirming the learned behavior generalizes beyond the training server distribution.
papers.why_en: Offers a concrete mechanism—reward attribution splitting plus gradient surgery—to mitigate cross-objective interference in multi-turn, multi-tool agentic RL training.

papers.title: Recurrent In-Context Learning for Tabular Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Tabular foundation models adapt to new datasets through in-context learning (ICL), and, like most transformers, they tie computational depth to the number of independently parameterized layers. We ask whether the ICL stage of such a model needs a distinct set of parameters for every layer, or only depth. We introduce Tab-Loop, which replaces the 12 untied ICL blocks of TabICLv2 with 4 tied blocks applied $k$ times and changes nothing else: the encoders, decoder, synthetic prior and training recipe are shared with an untied baseline trained for the same compute. At matched pretraining compute (18.2 EFLOP) and matched inference compute (12 block applications), Tab-Loop matches the baseline with 62\% fewer parameters (10.4M vs.\ 27.6M): held-out log loss is 0.4583 vs.\ 0.4588, mean accuracy on 200 TALENT datasets is 84.10\% vs.\ 83.92\%, and Elo on 38 TabArena datasets is 1409 vs.\ 1396. A 4-block untied control with Tab-Loop's parameter count, which sees 32\% more training tables for the same compute, trails both (83.46\%; Elo 1343). Because weights are shared, depth becomes a choice made at inference. Accuracy rises with the number of loops through the trained range and holds beyond it, and continued training with deeper loops extends the useful range, reaching the baseline's stage-2 scores at 4--5$\times$ its inference compute. At this scale, the ICL stage of a tabular foundation model needs depth more than it needs distinct parameters.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 表データ基盤モデルの文脈内学習は層を共有しても深さがあれば十分
papers.summary: 表形式データの基盤モデル(TabICLv2)は文脈内学習(ICL、例を見せるだけで新しいタスクに対応する学習法)の各層に別々のパラメータを持つが、本当に必要なのは独立したパラメータではなく層の繰り返し回数(深さ)ではないかと著者らは考えた。12 層の独立したブロックを 4 層の共有ブロックを k 回繰り返す構造 Tab-Loop に置き換え、同じ計算量(事前学習 18.2 EFLOP、推論は 12 回のブロック適用)で比べたところ、パラメータを 62% 削減(1040 万対 2760 万)しても 200 個の TALENT データセットでの平均精度は 84.10% 対 83.92%、38 個の TabArena での Elo は 1409 対 1396 とほぼ同等だった。重みを共有しているため推論時にループ回数を増やすだけで精度をさらに伸ばせることも確認された。
papers.why: 表形式データの基盤モデルを小さく作りながら推論時に深さを自由に調整できるという、パラメータ共有による学習効率の新しい設計指針を示す。
papers.summary_en: Tabular foundation models tie ICL depth to independently parameterized layers, and the authors ask whether distinct parameters per layer are even needed. Replacing TabICLv2's 12 untied ICL blocks with 4 tied blocks applied k times (Tab-Loop), at matched pretraining (18.2 EFLOP) and inference compute (12 block applications), matches the baseline with 62% fewer parameters (10.4M vs. 27.6M): held-out log loss 0.4583 vs. 0.4588, mean accuracy 84.10% vs. 83.92% on 200 TALENT datasets, Elo 1409 vs. 1396 on 38 TabArena datasets. Because weights are shared, accuracy keeps rising with more loops at inference time.
papers.why_en: Shows that the ICL stage of a tabular foundation model needs depth more than distinct parameters, offering a new weight-sharing design for making depth an inference-time choice.

papers.title: UltraBERT: Beyond the Limit of BERT Pre-Training
papers.abstract: Recent bidirectional encoders have been modernized with innovations from causal large language models (LLMs). However, the pretraining recipe itself remains inherited from small-scale conventions, leaving encoders underoptimized, with no single model performing competitively across both classification and retrieval tasks. In this work, we investigate how far encoder performance can be pushed by revisiting core design choices in training, revealing three key findings: (1) Encoders saturate on downstream tasks beyond a few trillion tokens, indicating that additional compute past this point does not help. (2) Across model sizes, lower masking ratios benefit classification while higher ones benefit retrieval, contradicting prior work suggesting larger ratios for larger models. (3) Distillation with pruning improves classification at low masking ratios but degrades retrieval at high ones. Guided by these findings, we present UltraBERT, a single encoder that assigns separate LM heads to low and high masking ratios within a batch and restricts the distillation objective to the low ratio. To our knowledge, UltraBERT is the first encoder to achieve state of the art on both classification and retrieval tasks, reaching 91.0 on GLUE and 47.7 on BEIR. Together, these results show how far encoder performance can be pushed and provide a principled basis for compute allocation, masking ratio design, and knowledge transfer in bidirectional models.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: UltraBERT: 双方向エンコーダの事前学習限界を見直す
papers.summary: 双方向エンコーダ(BERT 系)は最近の大規模言語モデルの工夫を取り入れているが、事前学習の作り方は小規模時代のやり方を引き継いだままで、分類と検索の両タスクで強いモデルが存在しなかった。著者らは、数兆トークンを超えると性能が飽和すること、マスク率(入力のどれだけを隠すかの割合)はモデルサイズに関わらず低いほど分類に、高いほど検索に有利なこと、蒸留と枝刈りの組み合わせは低マスク率で分類を改善するが高マスク率で検索を悪化させることを発見した。これらを踏まえ、バッチ内で低マスク率用と高マスク率用の出力層を分けて持つ UltraBERT を作り、GLUE で 91.0 点、BEIR で 47.7 点を達成し、分類と検索の両方で最高性能を初めて同時に実現した。
papers.why: エンコーダ事前学習における計算量の割り当て・マスク率設計・知識蒸留の指針を具体的な実験結果で示しており、学習効率を上げたい実務者に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Modern bidirectional encoders borrow tricks from causal LLMs but still inherit small-scale pretraining conventions, leaving no single model competitive on both classification and retrieval. The authors find encoders saturate beyond a few trillion tokens, lower masking ratios help classification while higher ones help retrieval regardless of model size (contradicting prior guidance), and distillation-with-pruning improves classification at low ratios but hurts retrieval at high ones. Guided by these findings, UltraBERT assigns separate LM heads to low and high masking ratios within a batch and restricts distillation to the low ratio, reaching 91.0 on GLUE and 47.7 on BEIR, the first encoder to achieve state of the art on both tasks simultaneously.
papers.why_en: Provides a principled, empirically grounded basis for compute allocation, masking ratio design, and distillation in encoder pretraining, directly useful for improving training efficiency.

papers.title: SAFE-KV: Causal Suffix Repair for Behavior-Preserving Non-Prefix KV Cache Reuse in RAG
papers.abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) reuses the same documents across many requests, making non-prefix KV-cache reuse attractive. Yet a cached document state is not reusable text: it is a context-conditioned causal state whose keys and values depend on the prefix, position, and preceding documents under which it was computed. We formulate non-prefix KV reuse as a behavior-preservation problem with full prefill on the exact prompt as the reference, and introduce SAFE-KV, which repairs a composed cache by re-encoding the causal suffix from a selected start document. On Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, prefix-conditioned composition preserves only 47.2% of HotpotQA-500 and 37.8% of 2Wiki-500 full-prefill answers; SAFE-KV with risk-guided K2 selection restores 99.8%/98.4% (donor-copy protocol) and 100.0%/98.4% with actual suffix forwarding. Document-only and fixed-window repairs recover far less, because the document states after the repaired region keep histories that omit it. Reuse without repair is exact up to four documents and degrades at sixteen, where suffix repair recovers 98-100%. Faithful repair re-encodes most of the context, so in a single-request L40S study SAFE-KV's operating rule serves every workload by full prefill. SAFE-KV thus establishes the causal-state contract for non-prefix reuse and a validated repair mechanism that meets it.
papers.ja_title: SAFE-KV: RAG での文書単位 KV キャッシュ再利用を正しさを保って修復する
papers.summary: RAG(検索拡張生成)では同じ文書を複数の問い合わせで使い回すため、注意機構の中間結果である KV キャッシュを文書単位で再利用したいが、キャッシュは前の文脈や位置に依存する「因果的な状態」であり、単純に組み合わせると答えが変わってしまう。著者らは SAFE-KV を提案し、選んだ開始文書以降の因果的な「後半部分」だけを再計算して修復する方法を使ったところ、Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct で単純合成では HotpotQA-500 の 47.2%、2WikiQA-500 の 37.8% しか完全計算と同じ答えにならなかったのに対し、SAFE-KV は 99.8%/98.4%(コピー方式)、100.0%/98.4%(実際の後方転送)まで一致率を回復させた。
papers.why: KV キャッシュ再利用のような最適化を、完全計算との一致率という基準で検証する手法と、実際に正しさを保つ修復アルゴリズムの両方を示している。
papers.summary_en: RAG reuses the same documents across many requests, making non-prefix KV-cache reuse attractive, but a cached document state is a context-conditioned causal state whose keys and values depend on prefix, position, and preceding documents, so naive composition breaks answers. SAFE-KV repairs a composed cache by re-encoding the causal suffix from a selected start document; on Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, prefix-conditioned composition alone preserves only 47.2% of HotpotQA-500 and 37.8% of 2Wiki-500 full-prefill answers, while SAFE-KV restores 99.8%/98.4% (donor-copy) and 100.0%/98.4% (actual suffix forwarding).
papers.why_en: Establishes a behavior-preservation contract for non-prefix KV reuse and a validated repair mechanism, useful both as a testing methodology (compare against full prefill) and as a concrete serving optimization.

papers.title: Sequent-Prover: Training Agents for Formal, Checkable SMT-based Reasoning
papers.abstract: We introduce Sequent-Prover, a family of verifier-using language-model agents, and the post-training framework that produces them. Agents reason in an executable SMT-LIB scratchpad: they write complete SMT-LIB programs, query Z3 across turns, inspect solver feedback, repair formalizations, and terminate with an explicit answer. Our recipe, verifier-conditioned trajectory distillation, bootstraps from a noisy teacher proposal policy by sampling multi-turn trajectories, retaining the successful tail that is correct, non-trivial, grounded, and executable, then applying supervised fine-tuning and trajectory-level preference optimization. Because solver success alone does not guarantee semantic faithfulness, we evaluate task accuracy, k-sample reliability, and SMT program quality. Across 37 benchmarks and 7,254 problems per model family, post-training raises the 4B model's per-attempt accuracy from 85.6% to 97.0% and four-sample all-correct reliability (pass^4}) from 64.1% to 91.7%. It also reduces average SMT calls from 4.10 to 2.52 and tokens per attempt from 18.97k to 12.72k. Sequent-Prover agents give answers backed by executable formal artifacts.
papers.ja_title: Sequent-Prover: SMT ソルバーを使う検証可能な推論エージェントの後学習
papers.summary: 著者らは Z3 などの SMT ソルバーを対話的に呼び出しながら推論する言語モデルエージェント Sequent-Prover と、その後学習手法を提案した。「検証器条件付き軌跡蒸留」という方法で、ノイズの多い教師ポリシーから多段階の試行をサンプリングし、正しく・自明でなく・根拠があり・実行可能な軌跡だけを残して教師あり学習と軌跡単位の好み最適化を行う。37 個のベンチマーク・7254 問題で、4B モデルの 1 回あたり正解率を 85.6% から 97.0% に、4 回全て正解する信頼性(pass^4)を 64.1% から 91.7% に上げ、さらに SMT 呼び出し回数を 4.10 回から 2.52 回、トークン数を 18.97k から 12.72k に減らした。
papers.why: ソルバーからのフィードバックを使った多段階エージェントの後学習手順を具体的な数値で示し、RL 後学習で検証可能な推論を作る際の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Sequent-Prover is a family of verifier-using agents that write SMT-LIB programs, query Z3 across turns, repair formalizations, and terminate with an answer; the post-training recipe, verifier-conditioned trajectory distillation, bootstraps from a noisy teacher by sampling multi-turn trajectories and keeping only the successful, non-trivial, grounded, executable tail for SFT and trajectory-level preference optimization. Across 37 benchmarks and 7,254 problems per model family, post-training raises the 4B model's per-attempt accuracy from 85.6% to 97.0% and pass^4 reliability from 64.1% to 91.7%, while reducing average SMT calls from 4.10 to 2.52 and tokens per attempt from 18.97k to 12.72k.
papers.why_en: Gives a concrete recipe for post-training multi-turn, verifier-grounded reasoning agents, relevant to building RL post-training pipelines with checkable, executable artifacts.

papers.title: RECAP: Calibrating Low-Bit Reasoning Models on the History They Read
papers.abstract: Low-bit quantization reduces the cost of serving reasoning models but can substantially degrade long chains of thought. Each step reads cached keys and values spanning thousands of tokens, allowing quantization errors to accumulate along the trajectory. Standard calibration operates on short segments that omit the earlier context needed by later reasoning steps. Even when this context is retained, cache reconstruction error alone does not capture how quantization errors affect subsequent attention. We present RECAP, a post-training quantization method that calibrates reasoning models on the history they read. Dynamic-prefix calibration separates long historical context from short-block reconstruction. It regenerates prefix keys and values with the current quantizer and rotates the active block to supervise every position along the trajectory. Prefix read geometry further supervises historical cache errors according to their effects on attention outputs, weighting key and value errors asymmetrically. With both components applied only during calibration, RECAP outperforms the baseline across multiple reasoning models and quantization settings. Under W4A4KV4, RECAP improves accuracy over the baseline by 13.3 percentage points on MATH500 with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and 15.8 points on AIME-120 with Qwen3-4B. These results highlight the importance of preserving historical dependencies during calibration for low-bit reasoning.
papers.ja_title: RECAP: 推論モデルの低ビット量子化を「読まれる履歴」に合わせてキャリブレーションする
papers.summary: 低ビット量子化(数値を少ないビット数で表す圧縮)は推論モデルの提供コストを下げるが、長い思考の連鎖では何千トークンにも及ぶ KV キャッシュを毎ステップ読むため誤差が積み重なり、精度が大きく落ちる。従来のキャリブレーション(量子化の調整)は短い区間しか見ないため後の推論ステップが必要とする古い文脈を見落としていた。RECAP は長い履歴部分を現在の量子化器で再生成しつつ短いブロックを順番にずらして全位置を教師データにし、注意機構への影響度に応じてキーとバリューの誤差に重みをつける方法を組み合わせ、W4A4KV4 設定で MATH500 上の DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B の精度を基準より 13.3 ポイント、AIME-120 上の Qwen3-4B の精度を 15.8 ポイント改善した。
papers.why: 長い思考連鎖を持つ推論モデルを低ビットで安く動かす際、キャッシュ量子化のキャリブレーション手法そのものに改善余地があることを示す具体例。
papers.summary_en: Low-bit quantization reduces serving cost for reasoning models but degrades long chains of thought, since each step reads cached KV spanning thousands of tokens and quantization errors accumulate; standard calibration on short segments omits the earlier context later steps need. RECAP's dynamic-prefix calibration regenerates prefix keys/values with the current quantizer and rotates the active block to supervise every trajectory position, plus a prefix-read-geometry term that weights key/value errors by their effect on attention outputs; under W4A4KV4 it improves accuracy over the baseline by 13.3 points on MATH500 with DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B and 15.8 points on AIME-120 with Qwen3-4B.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates that preserving historical dependencies during calibration is key to making low-bit quantization work for long-chain reasoning models, directly relevant to kernel/low-precision serving design.

papers.title: Compositional Performance Modeling of LLM Inference Clusters with Hierarchical KV Caching
papers.abstract: Design-space exploration of LLM inference clusters requires predicting how hardware and serving policies interact with hierarchical key-value (KV) caching. Isolated operation profiles alone do not determine cluster latency: reuse changes computational demand, while KV location, capacity, and contention govern execution order. We present a compositional discrete-event simulator based on separating local service costs from shared resource and KV availability. Compute and transfer models calibrated on one-prefill/one-decode (1P-1D) deployments are reused across compatible workers, enabling policy and topology comparisons without per-configuration latency fitting. Validation against SGLang covers Qwen3-8B and Qwen3-32B on 1P-1D and 3P-1D clusters. Mean request end-to-end latency error is 1.34% for question answering and 6.36% for captured coding sessions, measured as mean absolute percentage error. CPU simulation reduces replay turnaround by 15.33 times on average; real replay includes prescribed arrival gaps. Measured session-affinity and simulated retention studies demonstrate how the framework guides policy selection by predicting the joint effects on computation, latency, and KV occupancy.
papers.ja_title: 階層的 KV キャッシュを持つ LLM 推論クラスタの構成要素ごとの性能モデル
papers.summary: LLM 推論クラスタの設計を検討するには、階層的な KV キャッシュ(複数の保存先に分けて持つ中間計算結果)がハードウェアやサービス方針とどう影響し合うかを予測する必要があるが、単体の性能プロファイルだけでは全体の待ち時間は決まらない。著者らは、各機器のローカルな処理コストと共有資源・KV の空き状況を分けて扱う離散事象シミュレータを作り、1 台の prefill と 1 台の decode の構成で測った計算・転送モデルを他の構成にも再利用できるようにした。実際のサービング系 SGLang との比較では、Qwen3-8B/32B のクラスタでリクエスト全体の待ち時間誤差が質問応答で平均 1.34%、実コーディングセッションの再現で 6.36% に収まり、CPU 上のシミュレーションは実際の再現より平均 15.33 倍速く終わった。
papers.why: 推論クラスタのポリシーやトポロジーを本物のシステムで試す前に、検証済みの誤差で事前比較できる軽量な性能モデルを提供する。
papers.summary_en: Design-space exploration of LLM inference clusters needs to predict how hardware and serving policies interact with hierarchical KV caching, since isolated operation profiles alone don't determine cluster latency. The authors build a compositional discrete-event simulator separating local service costs from shared-resource and KV availability, with compute/transfer models calibrated on 1P-1D deployments reused across configurations; validated against SGLang on Qwen3-8B/32B, mean end-to-end latency error is 1.34% for QA and 6.36% for captured coding sessions, with CPU simulation reducing replay turnaround by 15.33x on average.
papers.why_en: Offers a reusable, validated performance model for comparing serving policies and topologies before deploying on real hardware, directly useful for inference cluster design.

papers.title: ANTE: Anticipate, Then Execute -- Learning Internal World Models for Coding Agents from Verified Beliefs
papers.abstract: Rapid advances in large language models have made software engineering agents capable of tackling complex coding tasks. Within a containerized environment, a coding agent receives tool responses or execution results, and determines its later actions by those earlier results. However, most existing coding agents never look ahead: their policies do not anticipate the consequences of actions, and the terminal reward barely attributes a failure to certain earlier steps, so an ill-judged edit can corrupt the repository state irreversibly before any signal arrives. Recent code world models aim to address these challenges, but they are either trained and then frozen before reinforcement learning (RL), or reduced to an auxiliary next-token loss on the environment's outputs. We present ANTE (Anticipate, Then Execute), an agentic RL framework that verifies the policy's pre-action predictions by real execution and turns them into per-step credit for its actions and trust-or-abstain decisions. With an internal belief stated before each action, Belief-Anchored Policy Optimization (BAPO) turns the settled predictions into per-step advantages by anchoring credit on the policy's own forecasts. To turn the trained forecasts into better actions at inference, thereby facilitating effective test-time scaling, ANTE-TTO (test-time optimization) selects among candidate actions without an external scorer. ANTE raises Qwen3-32B from 25.0% to 57.2% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified, 6.2% above a matched GRPO baseline trained without the belief state; its world model's accuracy climbs from 44% to 69% during RL, and the learned foresight capability transfers across harnesses and out-of-distribution domains. In summary, we aim to build a code world model that knows what has happened, what holds now, and what the next action will achieve.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: ANTE: 行動前の予測を検証して信用度に変えるコーディングエージェントの RL
papers.summary: 多くのコーディングエージェントは先読みをせず、行動の結果を予想せずにツール応答を受け取るだけなので、誤った編集でリポジトリが壊れるまで原因となったステップを特定できない。著者らは ANTE という強化学習の枠組みを提案し、行動の前に立てた「内部の予測(信念)」を実際の実行結果で検証し、Belief-Anchored Policy Optimization(BAPO)という手法でその結果を各ステップの手がかり(信用度)に変える。Qwen3-32B で SWE-bench Verified の pass@1 を 25.0% から 57.2% に上げ、予測を使わない同条件の GRPO ベースラインより 6.2 ポイント高く、学習中にワールドモデルの予測精度も 44% から 69% まで上がった。
papers.why: コーディングエージェントの RL 後学習に「行動前の予測を実行で検証して報酬の手がかりにする」という新しい信号を導入し、学習効率と汎化性を高める具体的な手法を示す。
papers.summary_en: Most coding agents never look ahead: policies don't anticipate consequences, and terminal reward barely attributes failure to earlier steps, so an ill-judged edit can corrupt the repository irreversibly before any signal arrives. ANTE verifies the policy's pre-action beliefs by real execution and turns them into per-step credit via Belief-Anchored Policy Optimization (BAPO); it raises Qwen3-32B from 25.0% to 57.2% pass@1 on SWE-bench Verified, 6.2 points above a matched GRPO baseline without the belief state, with the world model's accuracy climbing from 44% to 69% during RL.
papers.why_en: Introduces a concrete per-step credit signal based on verifying the agent's own pre-action predictions against execution, improving RL post-training efficiency and transfer for coding agents.

papers.title: A Sovereign, Indic-First, Reasoning Model
papers.abstract: Gnani-Evon-v3.3-30B-A3B is a long-context hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts model for reasoning, instruction following, and tool use in English and eight Indian languages. Starting from NVIDIA's Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B checkpoint, it retains the 52-layer backbone and changes the vocabulary, training data, and post-training objectives. An in-place expansion from 131,072 to 163,072 tokens reduces mean Indian-language fertility by 38.6%. The new embedding rows are initialized from their upstream decompositions and warmed before the backbone is updated. Continual pretraining then adds broad English-Indic data, high-quality annealing, and direct training at a 131,072-token sequence length. The central result appears after post-training. Reinforcement learning across four verifiable task environments improves mathematics, graduate-level science, and instruction following, but degrades Indic extractive question answering because the rewards do not require an answer in the requested language. The share of Indic extraction items answered in English rises from 8.7% to 91.7%. Accuracy conditional on answering in the target script roughly doubles, which is consistent with preserved reading ability but is measured on a self-selected subset. Two unreleased studies test repairs. A scoped Indic reward restores the language convention. A 26B-A4B generative judge outperforms a 235B-parameter model on RM-Bench, and distillation restores 81% of the capabilities displaced by optimizing against it. Relative to the architecture-identical starting checkpoint, the released model gains 5.2 points on an Indic aggregate while giving up 1.7 points of English retention. The unreleased Indic-aware branch trades further, gaining 14.6 Indic points at a cost of 5.4 in English. A planned FP8 release reduces the artifact to 32GB with near-zero mean change across 32 paired benchmarks.
papers.ja_title: インド言語対応の Mamba-Transformer 専門家混合推論モデルと RL 後学習の言語崩れ
papers.summary: NVIDIA の Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B(Mamba と Transformer を組み合わせた専門家混合モデル)を土台に、英語とインドの 8 言語に対応する長文脈推論モデル Gnani-Evon-v3.3-30B-A3B を作った。語彙を 131,072 から 163,072 トークンに拡張してインド言語のトークン分割の冗長さを 38.6% 減らし、追加の事前学習と 131,072 トークンの長文脈学習を行った。4 つの検証可能タスクで強化学習をすると数学・科学・指示従順性は上がったが、報酬が回答言語を指定しなかったためインド言語の抽出型質問応答で英語で答える割合が 8.7% から 91.7% に跳ね上がり、専用の報酬設計や蒸留である程度修復できることも示した。FP8 化した公開モデルは 32GB まで縮小し、32 個の対比較ベンチマークでの平均性能変化はほぼゼロだった。
papers.why: 強化学習の報酬設計が多言語モデルの言語選択という暗黙の振る舞いを崩しうることを具体例で示し、後学習時の報酬設計の注意点を与える。
papers.summary_en: Starting from NVIDIA's Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts checkpoint Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B, Gnani-Evon-v3.3-30B-A3B adds long-context reasoning for English and eight Indian languages; an in-place vocabulary expansion from 131,072 to 163,072 tokens reduces mean Indian-language fertility by 38.6%, followed by continual pretraining and direct 131,072-token sequence training. Reinforcement learning across four verifiable task environments improves math, science, and instruction following but degrades Indic extractive QA because rewards didn't require answering in the requested language, pushing the share of English-answered Indic items from 8.7% to 91.7%; a scoped Indic reward and distillation partially restore this, and a planned FP8 release shrinks the artifact to 32GB with near-zero mean change across 32 paired benchmarks.
papers.why_en: Shows concretely how RL post-training reward design can silently break an implicit behavior (answer language) in a multilingual model, a cautionary case for designing verifiable-task rewards.

papers.title: Large Decision Models: Repurposing Large Language Models as Single-Pass Decision Makers
papers.abstract: Large language models make decisions through parallel prefill and sequential decoding. Although effective, this approach incurs decoding costs and does not explicitly expose decision probabilities. Existing task-specific classifiers require per-task training and offer limited generalization to unseen decision schemas. We propose Large Decision Models (LDMs), repurposing language models to return explicit probabilities over labels specified at run time using one prefill forward pass. We first adapt models to this interface through Diverse Decision Supervision (DDS), covering varied domains, rules and labels. To further narrow the performance gap to a reasoning model, Self-Posed Reasoning Distillation (SPRD) adds tasks generated by a frozen teacher, filters them for answer consistency, and trains on label distributions obtained from repeated teacher reasoning. We evaluate on DecisionVista, pairing new-schema tests with held-out human-labelled sources. Across three base models, the recipe improves accuracy over a step-matched baseline by 1.8 and 1.5 percentage points, respectively, achieving a 182-fold speedup in latency over reasoning rollout on Gemma-4-31B. Reasoning remains stronger on the new-schema test, motivating a confidence router for uncertain decisions. On development sets, routing recovers a median 92% of reasoning's accuracy advantage while generating 27-58% of its tokens. Code is available at https://github.com/JianhuiWei7/LDM.
papers.ja_title: 大規模決定モデル:LLM を一発勝負の分類器に転用
papers.summary: LLM は文章を生成するとき、入力を読み込む処理(プリフィル)の後に1トークンずつ生成する処理(デコード)を繰り返すため、決定(ラベル付け)のたびにコストがかかり、確率も明示されない。本研究は「Large Decision Models (LDM)」を提案し、1回のプリフィルだけで実行時に指定したラベルの確率を直接出す仕組みにした。多様な領域・規則・ラベルで学習する DDS と教師モデルの推論を蒸留する SPRD を組み合わせ、3つの基盤モデルで同じ手順数のベースラインより正解率を 1.8 ポイントと 1.5 ポイント改善し、Gemma-4-31B では推論モデルより 182 倍速い応答を実現した。新しい分類基準では推論モデルの方がまだ強いため、不確実なときだけ推論に切り替える「確信度ルーター」を使うと、トークン生成量を 27〜58% に抑えつつ推論の精度優位の中央値 92% を回復できる。
papers.why: 分類・意思決定タスクを LLM サービングの中で高速化したい人にとって、プリフィルのみで確率出力を得る設計と確信度によるルーティング戦略は実用的な指針になる。
papers.summary_en: LLMs make decisions via parallel prefill followed by costly sequential decoding, which incurs latency and does not expose explicit decision probabilities. The authors propose Large Decision Models (LDMs), which repurpose LLMs to output label probabilities in a single prefill pass, trained with Diverse Decision Supervision and Self-Posed Reasoning Distillation; across three base models this improves accuracy over a step-matched baseline by 1.8 and 1.5 percentage points and gives a 182-fold latency speedup over reasoning rollout on Gemma-4-31B. Since reasoning remains stronger on new-schema tests, a confidence router recovers a median 92% of reasoning's accuracy advantage while generating only 27-58% of its tokens.
papers.why_en: For anyone serving classification/decision tasks with LLMs, the single-pass probability interface and confidence-based routing between fast LDM and slow reasoning offer a concrete recipe to cut latency without giving up much accuracy.

papers.title: Apertus 1.5: From Open Text Models to Open Multimodal Reasoners
papers.abstract: Language models are becoming infrastructure, and infrastructure built in the open, by public institutions, on documented data, is the alternative to dependence on a few providers; Apertus shows this is viable at scale. Apertus 1.5 extends the fully open Apertus family from text to multimodal reasoning. Continued pretraining of the Apertus 1.0 models, on 4T additional tokens for the 8B and 2T for the 70B, adds image and audio understanding and extends the context window fourfold to 262,144 tokens; multimodality enters through the tokenizer, the language-model head remains restricted to text, and the architecture is unchanged. Supervised finetuning, long-context finetuning, reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, and preference alignment complete the released models. Thinking is a flag of the chat template rather than a separate model, and lifts mathematical reasoning by up to 20 points on the 8B model. The released models improve over their predecessors on nearly every benchmark; among fully open models of its class, the 8B leads on knowledge, instruction following, and cultural benchmarks, and its instruction following surpasses all compared models, including open-weight ones. On image and audio understanding, a first for the family, the models are competitive with fully open multimodal models, strongest on document understanding and long-form and lower-resource speech recognition, while specialized vision and audio models remain ahead on perception and transcription of English and other high-resource languages. As in Apertus 1.0, we train only on openly available data, respect crawler opt-outs retroactively, and exclude restrictively licensed material. We release the model weights, data preparation and training recipes, and evaluation suites under permissive licenses; openness extends to values, with the Apertus charter guiding alignment stages published alongside the models.
papers.ja_title: Apertus 1.5: 完全オープンなテキストモデルをマルチモーダル推論モデルへ拡張
papers.summary: 公的機関が作る「完全オープン」な LLM が少数企業への依存を減らす選択肢になることを示す狙いで、テキストのみの Apertus 1.0 を土台に、8B モデルは追加 4 兆トークン、70B モデルは追加 2 兆トークンで継続事前学習し、画像・音声理解と 262144 トークン(4倍)への文脈長拡張を加えた。思考(thinking)はチャットテンプレートの切り替えフラグとして実装され、8B モデルの数学推論を最大 20 ポイント引き上げる。公開されている完全オープンモデルの中では、8B は知識・指示追従・文化的ベンチマークで先頭に立ち、指示追従はオープンウェイトモデルも含む比較対象全体を上回る。
papers.why: データ出典・学習手順・評価一式をすべて公開する「完全オープン」な大規模マルチモーダルモデルの作り方の実例として、継続事前学習のレシピを参照できる。
papers.summary_en: Arguing that fully open infrastructure built by public institutions is a viable alternative to dependence on a few providers, Apertus 1.5 continues pretraining Apertus 1.0 (8B on 4T additional tokens, 70B on 2T) to add image and audio understanding and extend the context window fourfold to 262,144 tokens. "Thinking" is implemented as a chat-template flag rather than a separate model and lifts the 8B model's mathematical reasoning by up to 20 points; among fully open models, the 8B leads on knowledge, instruction following, and cultural benchmarks, with instruction following surpassing all compared models including open-weight ones.
papers.why_en: As a documented example of continued pretraining and multimodal extension at scale with fully released data, recipes, and evaluation suites, it offers a concrete reference recipe for building open large multimodal models.

papers.title: The Price of Precision: A Calibrated Cost Model for Mixed-Precision LLM Serving
papers.abstract: Choosing a mixed-precision configuration for large language model (LLM) serving trades speed against accuracy. Allocators that use average bit-width or a memory budget as a speed proxy can miss changes in the resource that limits execution. We argue that served speed can be limited by compute, weight loading, or key-value (KV) cache access, depending on the phase, batch size, and context length. A byte-based proxy does not capture all of these costs, so fewer bits do not always mean faster serving. To address this gap, we build a cost model that accounts for the binding resource and use it in two ways. First, as a predictor: given a configuration and operating point, it estimates serving latency using constants calibrated for the model, GPU, and serving stack. We evaluate its accuracy across three hardware classes. Second, as an allocator: we combine modeled time costs with measured per-tensor accuracy costs and use a dynamic program to select a configuration under a latency or accuracy budget. We compare its configurations against byte-aware and sensitivity-only allocation.
papers.ja_title: 精度の値段:混合精度 LLM サービングのための実測コストモデル
papers.summary: LLM サービングで速度と精度を両立させる混合精度の配分を決めるとき、平均ビット幅やメモリ量だけを速度の目安にすると、実際のボトルネック(計算・重みの読み込み・KV キャッシュのアクセス)がどこにあるか見誤ることがある。本研究は、推論の段階・バッチサイズ・文脈長によってボトルネックが変わることを踏まえた実測コストモデルを作り、モデル・GPU・サービングスタックごとにキャリブレーションした定数で待ち時間を予測し、3種類のハードウェアで精度を評価した。さらに計測した精度損失と組み合わせて動的計画法で配分を選ぶアロケータとしても使い、バイト数だけを見る方式や感度だけを見る方式と比較した。
papers.why: 「ビット数が少ないほど必ず速い」という前提が崩れる場面を具体的に示し、サービング設計で何を測って配分判断に使うべきかの指針を与える。
papers.summary_en: Choosing a mixed-precision configuration for LLM serving trades speed against accuracy, but using average bit-width or memory budget as a speed proxy can miss which resource (compute, weight loading, or KV-cache access) actually limits execution at a given phase, batch size, and context length. The authors build a calibrated cost model that predicts serving latency from constants fit per model, GPU, and serving stack, and use it both as a predictor (evaluated across three hardware classes) and, combined with measured per-tensor accuracy costs, as a dynamic-programming allocator under a latency or accuracy budget, compared against byte-aware and sensitivity-only allocation.
papers.why_en: It shows concretely that "fewer bits does not always mean faster serving," and offers guidance on what to actually measure and calibrate before making mixed-precision allocation decisions.

papers.title: Context-Aware Precision Scheduling for Small Language Models
papers.abstract: Small language models (SLMs) used as on-device agents must balance accuracy and latency as their context grows. Mixed precision helps manage this tradeoff by assigning different precisions to weight tensors according to their size and sensitivity. However, these choices depend on the operating conditions, so a configuration selected for a short context may no longer provide the best tradeoff at a longer one. We calibrate a timing model from measurements at different precisions and context lengths, and combine it with tensor sensitivities to choose configurations under a latency or accuracy budget. We argue that fewer bits do not always mean faster execution, so our predictor estimates latency from calibrated execution costs rather than weight bytes alone. Under a latency budget, reading the larger key-value (KV) cache leaves less time for weight operations, leading the allocator to select lower precisions. This gives a schedule of tensor changes that can be prepared before execution. Our runtime follows the schedule while retaining the session's KV cache. We evaluate executed schedules on a laptop GPU, including a longer-context schedule with three weight formats and a tool-use benchmark measuring full response time and correctness. Under an accuracy budget, measured error from a quantized KV cache determines the budget left for weights. The allocator can raise or lower weight precision as this estimate changes. These experiments show where context-aware precision helps and where accuracy recovery remains limited.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 文脈長に応じて精度を切り替えるオンデバイス小型モデルのスケジューリング
papers.summary: 端末上で動くエージェント用の小型言語モデル(SLM)は、文脈(これまでの対話内容)が長くなるほど精度と速度のバランスが変わり、短い文脈用に選んだ混合精度の設定が長い文脈では最適でなくなる。本研究は、精度と文脈長ごとに実測した時間モデルとテンソルごとの精度への影響を組み合わせ、待ち時間または精度の予算の下で事前に配分計画(スケジュール)を作り、実行中は KV キャッシュを保持したままそのスケジュールに従う実行系を作った。ノート PC の GPU で、3種類の重み形式を使う長文脈スケジュールやツール利用ベンチマークを使って応答時間と正答率を評価し、「ビット数が少ないほど速いとは限らない」ことを確認した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュの読み込みが時間を圧迫すると重み演算に残る時間が減る、という具体的な相互作用を踏まえた配分の考え方は、オンデバイス推論の精度・速度チューニングに直接使える。
papers.summary_en: On-device small language model (SLM) agents must balance accuracy and latency as context grows, so a mixed-precision configuration chosen for a short context may no longer be optimal at a longer one. The authors calibrate a timing model from measurements at different precisions and context lengths, combine it with per-tensor sensitivities to produce a precision schedule under a latency or accuracy budget, and run it with a runtime that follows the prepared schedule while retaining the session's KV cache. Evaluated on a laptop GPU with a longer-context schedule across three weight formats and a tool-use benchmark measuring response time and correctness, they confirm that fewer bits do not always mean faster execution, and show how a growing KV cache squeezes the time budget left for weight operations.
papers.why_en: The concrete interaction they model—larger KV-cache reads leaving less time for weight operations—gives a directly usable framework for tuning accuracy/speed trade-offs in on-device inference as context grows.

review.note: 重みのバイト数ではなく実測した実行コストから速度を推定すべきという教訓と、文脈長ごとの精度/速度トレードオフを事前キャリブレーションで測る手法。
review.note_en: A lesson that latency should be estimated from calibrated execution costs rather than weight bytes alone, plus a method for calibrating accuracy/speed trade-offs per context length before deployment.

papers.title: Drift, Then Spread: Learning One-Step Generative Policies for Online Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Generative policies offer expressive action distributions for online reinforcement learning (RL), but many diffusion- and flow-based policies require costly iterative sampling.
