We propose DriftSpread, a one-step generative policy based on Drifting for online maximum-entropy (MaxEnt) RL. To incorporate entropy without a tractable policy density, we build on an energy-based view of Drifting and derive critic-guided Drift and entropy-induced Spread from the negative MaxEnt objective. Our method learns these updates sequentially in the same actor, using action regression for value improvement and distribution matching to capture the effect of entropy. The actor updates require neither direct samples from the critic-defined Boltzmann target nor policy-density or score estimation. Under exact fitting with a fixed critic, we prove convergence to the Boltzmann target in the small-step limit followed by the long-time limit. On MuJoCo, DriftSpread achieves the highest aggregate normalized return among all evaluated methods, while outperforming the diffusion- and flow-based baselines in both training and inference efficiency.
papers.ja_title: ドリフトして広がる:オンライン強化学習のための1ステップ生成ポリシー
papers.summary: 拡散モデルや flow を使う生成的な方策(ポリシー)は表現力が高い一方、行動を選ぶたびに何度も繰り返し計算するサンプリングが必要でコストが高い。本研究は、エントロピーを明示的な方策密度なしに取り込む「エネルギーベースの見方」から、critic 主導の「Drift」とエントロピー由来の「Spread」という2つの更新を導き、1回の計算で行動を生成する「DriftSpread」を提案した。同じ方策内でこの2つの更新を順に学習する仕組みで、固定された critic のもとでは小さいステップの極限でボルツマン分布に収束することを理論的に示し、MuJoCo の実験で評価した全手法の中で正規化リターンの合計が最も高く、拡散・flow ベースの手法より学習・推論の両方で効率が良かった。
papers.why: 拡散・flow 方策特有の反復サンプリングコストをなくしつつ最大エントロピー RL の性質を保つ設計は、オンライン RL の学習・推論効率を上げる基盤技術として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Expressive diffusion- and flow-based generative policies for online RL typically require costly iterative sampling to act. The authors propose DriftSpread, a one-step generative policy for online maximum-entropy RL that derives critic-guided "Drift" and entropy-induced "Spread" updates from an energy-based view of Drifting, learned sequentially within the same actor without needing samples from the Boltzmann target or density/score estimation; under exact fitting with a fixed critic they prove convergence to the Boltzmann target in the small-step limit. On MuJoCo, DriftSpread achieves the highest aggregate normalized return among all evaluated methods while outperforming diffusion- and flow-based baselines in both training and inference efficiency.
papers.why_en: Removing the iterative-sampling cost of diffusion/flow policies while preserving MaxEnt RL properties is a useful building block for making online RL training and inference more efficient.

papers.title: To Cache or Not to Cache: Understanding and Mitigating Safety Incompatibility in Cross-Model KV Cache Reuse
papers.abstract: Cross-model KV cache sharing reduces prefill computation by allowing a receiver model to reuse prefix KV states generated by a related sender model. Existing methods optimize such reuse for latency and generation quality, but its safety implications remain unclear. In this work, we systematically evaluate this issue across diverse sender-receiver pairs and reuse configurations. We refer to deviations from the receiver's native safety behavior as safety incompatibility. Our study shows that both the direction and magnitude of safety incompatibility depend on the model pair and reuse configuration, with value reuse causing substantially larger deviations than key reuse across all evaluated pairs. Furthermore, we propose VReparo, a technique that learns per-layer and per-KV-head affine maps offline to align reused sender value tensors with their receiver-native counterparts before decoding. Across two model pairs under full KV reuse and the state-of-the-art selective reuse setting, VReparo reduces the average HarmBench attack success rate (ASR) from 57.28% to 39.21% and the average StrongREJECT score from 0.4215 to 0.2163 upon our benchmarks, while retaining an average Time to First Token (TTFT) reduction of 85.62%.
papers.ja_title: キャッシュを使うべきか:モデル間 KV キャッシュ再利用の安全性問題と対処法
papers.summary: モデル間で KV キャッシュ(入力文を処理した中間結果)を共有すると、入力処理(プリフィル)の計算を省けて速くなるが、安全性への影響はこれまで分かっていなかった。本研究は、送信側と受信側のモデル組み合わせや再利用方法を系統的に変えて調べ、受信側本来の安全なふるまいからずれる現象を「安全不整合」と名付け、特に value(値)の再利用が key(鍵)の再利用より大きなずれを生むことを確認した。対策として、送信側の value テンソルを受信側の本来の値に合わせる変換をレイヤー・ヘッドごとに学習する「VReparo」を提案し、2つのモデル組で HarmBench の攻撃成功率を平均 57.28% から 39.21%、StrongREJECT スコアを 0.4215 から 0.2163 に下げながら、初回トークンまでの時間(TTFT)の 85.62% 短縮は維持した。
papers.why: 速度目的のキャッシュ共有が安全性に思わぬ副作用を及ぼすという失敗パターンと、その実測比較は、推論基盤の安全設計レビューで確認すべき観点を示す。
papers.summary_en: Cross-model KV cache sharing speeds up prefill by letting a receiver model reuse a related sender model's prefix KV states, but its safety implications had been unclear. The authors systematically evaluate diverse sender-receiver pairs and reuse configurations, defining "safety incompatibility" as deviation from the receiver's native safety behavior, and find that value reuse causes substantially larger deviations than key reuse across all pairs. They propose VReparo, which learns per-layer, per-KV-head affine maps offline to align reused sender value tensors with receiver-native ones; across two model pairs under full and selective KV reuse, it reduces average HarmBench ASR from 57.28% to 39.21% and average StrongREJECT score from 0.4215 to 0.2163, while retaining an 85.62% average TTFT reduction.
papers.why_en: The systematic measurement of how latency-motivated KV cache sharing can silently shift safety behavior—and by how much, depending on which tensors are reused—is a concrete failure pattern worth checking when reviewing shared-component inference designs.

review.note: 速度最適化のための KV キャッシュ共有が安全性のふるまいをどれだけずらすかを、送受信モデルの組み合わせと再利用方式ごとに実測して分類した例。共有・流用する部品の安全性検証はこうした系統的な比較で行う観点になる。
review.note_en: An example of systematically measuring and classifying how much a latency optimization (KV cache reuse) shifts safety behavior across sender/receiver pairs and reuse configurations—a model for evaluating safety when reusing or sharing components.

papers.title: RSIPO: Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization for Agentic Reinforcement Learning via Skill-Policy Co-Evolution
papers.abstract: Recent focus in agentic reinforcement learning (RL) seeks to improve credit assignment in long-horizon tasks. One promising direction combines reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) and on-policy self-distillation (OPSD), integrating trajectory-level advantages with dense token-level supervision. This line of work often conditions a teacher model on privileged context, such as agentic skills, to score tokens generated by the student policy. Despite their progress, they largely overlook the on-policy evolution of agentic skills and the reliability of teacher supervision. Towards this end, we introduce Recursive Self-Improving Policy Optimization (RSIPO), a self-evolving agentic RL framework that enables agentic skills and the policy model to co-evolve throughout the training process. Specifically, RSIPO enables the policy itself to extract skills from completed trajectories and explicitly optimizes its skill-generation capability through trajectory replay. It further employs empirical Bayes shrinkage to dynamically calibrate the student's trust in teacher scores, accounting for the fact that skill-enhanced teacher guidance can sometimes be less reliable. Experiments with Qwen-family models on embodied interaction and search-based agentic tasks demonstrate that RSIPO outperforms all the compared baseline approaches. With Qwen2.5-7B as the base model, RSIPO achieves an average success rate of 98.6\% on ALFWorld, yielding absolute improvements of 2.5\% and 17.4\% over the second-best baseline and standard GRPO, respectively.
papers.ja_title: RSIPO: スキルと方策を同時進化させる再帰的自己改善型方策最適化
papers.summary: 長い手順を要するエージェントタスクの強化学習では、どの行動が成功に貢献したかを割り当てる「クレジット割り当て」が難しい。既存手法は、エージェントの「スキル」などの特権情報を与えた教師モデルでトークンを採点するが、スキル自体が方策とともに進化することや教師の採点の信頼性を見落としていた。本研究の RSIPO は、方策自身が完了した軌跡からスキルを抽出し、軌跡の再生でスキル生成能力を明示的に最適化し、さらに経験ベイズ縮小を使って教師の採点への信頼度を動的に調整する。Qwen2.5-7B を使った実験では、ALFWorld で平均成功率 98.6% を達成し、2位の手法より 2.5 ポイント、標準的な GRPO より 17.4 ポイント高い成果を得た。
papers.why: スキル生成と方策学習を同時に進化させ、教師の採点の信頼性まで調整するという設計は、長期タスクのエージェント RL のクレジット割り当てを改善する基盤手法として使える。
papers.summary_en: Long-horizon agentic RL struggles with credit assignment, and prior methods that combine RLVR with on-policy self-distillation often condition a teacher on privileged "skill" context to score student tokens while overlooking that skills should co-evolve with the policy and that teacher supervision reliability can vary. RSIPO lets the policy itself extract skills from completed trajectories, explicitly optimizes skill-generation via trajectory replay, and uses empirical Bayes shrinkage to dynamically calibrate trust in teacher scores. With Qwen2.5-7B, RSIPO reaches a 98.6% average success rate on ALFWorld, an absolute improvement of 2.5 points over the second-best baseline and 17.4 points over standard GRPO.
papers.why_en: Co-evolving skill extraction with policy learning, and dynamically calibrating how much to trust teacher supervision, offers a reusable building block for improving credit assignment in long-horizon agentic RL.

papers.title: LLM Value Functions for Credit Assignment in Agentic RL
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) for large language model (LLM) agents remains challenging in long-horizon tasks with sparse outcome rewards, where assigning credit to individual actions is difficult. Methods such as GRPO assign the same trajectory-level advantage to all actions, while critic-based methods require learning an additional value function that can be costly and unstable. We introduce LLM Value Function RL (LVRL), which uses the pretrained knowledge and in-context learning ability of an LLM to estimate policy-aware state values without finetuning a separate critic. LVRL conditions the value model on group context and calibrates its predictions using known values at the initial and terminal states, enabling step-level credit assignment from estimated value differences. We further extend this idea to learning from an expert policy through on-policy distillation (OPD), introducing LLM Value Function OPD (LVOPD), which focuses teacher supervision on actions associated with decreases in estimated value. We evaluate our approach across diverse agentic benchmarks: AppWorld, BabyAI, and SWE-bench Verified. Across policy scales (4B to 32B), LVRL consistently and substantially outperforms both GRPO and PPO. On AppWorld and SWE-bench Verified, LVRL yields absolute improvements of up to 13.6 and 8.6 percentage points over GRPO. Notably, on tasks requiring extended exploration like BabyAI, LVRL bridges the gap from total failure to 75.0% success. Furthermore, LVOPD yields consistent improvements over standard distillation baselines on AppWorld. Finally, Monte-Carlo analysis confirms that our frozen critic accurately identifies semantic pitfalls and recoveries, proving that LVRL extracts robust, policy-aware step-level credit from sparse terminal outcomes.
papers.ja_title: LLM 自身を価値関数にして、疎な成果報酬からステップ単位の手がかりを取り出す
papers.summary: 成功・失敗しか報酬が与えられない長い手順のエージェント RL では、どの行動が良かったかを判断する「クレジット割り当て」が難しく、GRPO は軌跡全体に同じ評価を割り振り、critic を使う手法は別の価値関数の学習にコストと不安定さを伴う。本研究の LVRL は、別途ファインチューニングした critic を使わず、LLM が元から持つ知識と文脈内学習能力を使って状態の価値を推定し、グループの文脈で条件づけ、開始状態と終了状態の既知の価値で補正することでステップ単位の手がかりを得る。AppWorld・BabyAI・SWE-bench Verified など複数のベンチマークと 4B〜32B のモデル規模で、LVRL は GRPO と PPO を一貫して上回り、AppWorld と SWE-bench Verified では GRPO より最大 13.6 ポイントと 8.6 ポイント改善し、探索が必要な BabyAI では成功率をほぼ失敗だった状態から 75.0% まで引き上げた。
papers.why: 追加学習なしで LLM をそのまま価値関数として使い、ステップ単位のクレジット割り当てを得る発想は、エージェント RL の基盤設計を安価かつ安定にする手段として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: RL for long-horizon LLM-agent tasks with sparse outcome rewards struggles with credit assignment: GRPO assigns the same trajectory-level advantage to every action, while critic-based methods require a separately learned value function that can be costly and unstable. LVRL instead uses a pretrained LLM's knowledge and in-context learning to estimate policy-aware state values without finetuning a critic, conditioning on group context and calibrating with known initial/terminal state values to get step-level credit from estimated value differences. Across policy scales from 4B to 32B and benchmarks including AppWorld, BabyAI, and SWE-bench Verified, LVRL consistently and substantially outperforms both GRPO and PPO, yielding absolute improvements of up to 13.6 and 8.6 percentage points over GRPO on AppWorld and SWE-bench Verified, and lifting BabyAI from near-total failure to 75.0% success.
papers.why_en: Using an LLM directly as a frozen, policy-aware value function to obtain step-level credit assignment, without training a separate critic, is a cheap and stable building block worth considering for agentic RL infrastructure.

papers.title: What the Model Cannot See: Covert and Provable Text Invisibility in LLMs
papers.abstract: Text wrapped in a trigger can be made behaviorally invisible to a language model: omitted from summaries and quotations, ignored in question answering, and left unflagged by downstream filtering. We study this selective blindness as a dual-use information-flow primitive, a supply-chain backdoor, and a white-box auditing problem. We first implement it exactly as a serving-time span veto: blocking information flow out of a marked span makes every outside activation bit-identical under same-length substitution of the span's content, a noninterference property we verify across ten models, seven mixer families, and 0.5B-120B parameters. The veto serves as a deployable quarantine, an exact reference for calibrating leakage, and a teacher. Distilled into weights, it yields a backdoor: checkpoints trained on six model families from 4B to 120B ignore marked context at little benchmark cost, and their outputs show no measurable semantic trace of the suppressed content above the veto reference on our held-out suite; an in-domain variant suppresses planted vulnerabilities during AI code review. Detection is therefore a white-box problem. Simpler backdoors remain internally transparent -- linear probes recover suppressed content at 0.57-0.79 accuracy versus 0.025 chance -- but hardening the attack until probes reach chance collapses attention from outside the span into it below the range of base models. Across the attacks we evaluate, probe visibility trades off against routing visibility; we do not establish that this tradeoff is fundamental.
papers.ja_title: 「モデルから見えない文章」を作る隠れ透過マーカーの研究
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデル (LLM) に特定の印をつけた文章を、要約や質問応答で完全に無視させる「透過化」という仕組みを調べた研究である。サーバー側でその区間からの情報流出を禁止する「拒否」操作を実装し、0.5B から 120B パラメータ、10 種類のモデル、7 種類の混合層構成で、区間の内容を同じ長さの別の内容に置き換えても外部の計算結果が完全に一致することを確認した。この仕組みを重みに蒸留するとサプライチェーン型のバックドアになり、4B から 120B まで 6 系列のモデルで、ベンチマーク性能をほとんど落とさずに印のついた文脈を無視させられ、抑制した内容の痕跡も検出されなかった。単純なバックドアでは線形プローブで抑制内容を 0.57〜0.79 の精度 (偶然は 0.025) で復元できたが、検出を逃れるよう攻撃を強化すると、区間への注意の集まり方が通常モデルより小さくなり、これが検出の手がかりになることも分かった。
papers.why: 区間単位で情報流出を遮断する仕組みと、そのバックドア化・検出可能性を具体的な実験で示しており、LLM の内部構造を悪用した攻撃とホワイトボックスでの監査・検出の両面に関わる基盤知識になる。
papers.summary_en: The paper studies "behavioral invisibility," where text marked by a trigger is omitted from summaries, QA, and filtering. The authors implement an exact serving-time "span veto" that blocks information flow out of a marked span, verified as noninterference (bit-identical outside activations under same-length substitution) across ten models, seven mixer families, and 0.5B-120B parameters. Distilled into weights, the veto becomes a supply-chain backdoor: checkpoints across six model families (4B-120B) ignore marked context at little benchmark cost with no measurable semantic trace above the veto reference, and an in-domain variant suppresses planted vulnerabilities during AI code review. Simpler backdoors remain detectable (linear probes recover suppressed content at 0.57-0.79 accuracy vs 0.025 chance), but hardening the attack until probes reach chance collapses attention into the span below the range seen in base models.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates a concrete serving-time mechanism for provably blocking information flow from marked text and its weaponization as a backdoor, giving builders of inference/serving stacks both an attack vector and white-box auditing signals (probe accuracy, attention routing) to watch for.

review.note: バックドアの検出可能性を線形プローブの復元精度と注意のルーティングという二つの指標で測り、攻撃を強化するとどちらかが犠牲になるというトレードオフを示す、検証の観点。
review.note_en: Shows a detection methodology using two measurable signals (linear-probe recoverability and attention routing into the span) and finds a tradeoff where hardening the attack against one signal exposes it via the other.

papers.title: Lightweight Scheduling Policies for Continuously Batched LLM Serving Across GPU Architectures
papers.abstract: Large language model serving is increasingly limited not only by model size and GPU speed, but also by scheduling during autoregressive decoding, where continuous batching interleaves requests at token granularity as sequences arrive and finish. We study whether lightweight scheduling policies can improve latency-throughput tradeoffs without changing model architectures, kernels, or deploying learned schedulers. We implement a Python/PyTorch continuous-batching testbench with real Hugging Face execution and evaluate eight policies across 1,152 GPU-model-scheduler-workload runs using ShareGPT-derived traffic, six Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral models, and Modal L40S, A100, and H100 GPUs. Scheduler choice changes throughput, TTFT, completion latency, and tail behavior under fixed model, GPU, workload, batch size, and prefill budget. Aging shortest-prompt-first is the strongest practical baseline in many L40S and mixed-workload settings, while oracle remaining-length scheduling shows that job-size knowledge alone is insufficient because batching and hardware effects also shape performance. The custom dataset has been uploaded to Hugging Face.
papers.ja_title: GPU 種類をまたいだ連続バッチ処理の軽量スケジューラ比較
papers.summary: LLM サービングでは自己回帰デコード中にリクエストをトークン単位で合流させる「連続バッチ処理」のスケジューリング方法が、レイテンシとスループットの釣り合いを左右する。研究者らは 8 種類の軽量スケジューリング方針を、6 種類の Qwen・Gemma・Mistral モデルと L40S・A100・H100 の 3 種類の GPU 上で、ShareGPT 由来の実トラフィックを使い計 1,152 通りの実験で比較した。結果、L40S や混在ワークロードの多くの設定では「経過時間で重み付けした最短プロンプト優先」が最も実用的な基準となり、ジョブの長さを完全に知っているはずの理想スケジューラでさえ、バッチ処理やハードウェアの影響まで考慮しないと性能が十分でないことが分かった。
papers.why: モデルやカーネルを変えずにスケジューラだけで性能が変わることを大規模な実測で示しており、サービング基盤を作る際のスケジューラ選定の具体的な指針になる。
papers.summary_en: LLM serving latency-throughput tradeoffs depend heavily on continuous-batching scheduler choice. The authors built a Python/PyTorch testbench with real Hugging Face execution and evaluated eight lightweight scheduling policies across 1,152 GPU-model-scheduler-workload runs, using ShareGPT-derived traffic, six Qwen/Gemma/Mistral models, and Modal L40S/A100/H100 GPUs. Aging shortest-prompt-first is the strongest practical baseline in many L40S and mixed-workload settings, while an oracle remaining-length scheduler shows that job-size knowledge alone is insufficient because batching and hardware effects also shape performance.
papers.why_en: A large-scale empirical sweep showing scheduler choice alone (no architecture/kernel changes) moves latency and throughput substantially, giving concrete, hardware-aware guidance for building serving schedulers.

review.note: スケジューラ評価で「ジョブ長を完全に知るオラクル」でも性能が不十分になることを示し、ベンチマーク設計で見落としがちな要因 (バッチ処理・ハードウェア効果) を明らかにする観点。
review.note_en: Shows that even an oracle with perfect job-length knowledge underperforms, exposing overlooked factors (batching and hardware effects) that naive scheduler benchmarks miss.

papers.title: Scaling Repeated-Data Pretraining: Batch Size, Regularization, and GPU-Time Tradeoffs
papers.abstract: We study pretraining when compute is abundant but unique training data are finite, requiring repeated training on the same data. We first revisit infinite-compute pretraining (Kim et al. 2026) and show that its frontier depends critically on choices previously fixed or studied only in isolation. In particular, optimizing batch size together with epoch counts reveals a U-shaped relationship between validation loss and batch size, favoring smaller batches than typical pretraining, likely because small-batch gradient noise provides implicit regularization. We further find that training recipes, previously optimized under a single-pass assumption, can be tuned, e.g., repacking documents into new sequences every epoch, weight tying, and positive embedding weight decay. We then relax the infinite-compute assumption. In particular, smaller-than-typical batch sizes can require prohibitively long sequential training, motivating to treat GPUs and time as separate resources. Tighter deadlines favor larger batches, and latency-oriented parallelism can trade additional GPUs for shorter training. Nevertheless, even under a fixed time budget, a smaller batch with fewer GPUs can achieve lower validation loss than a larger batch with more GPUs, challenging the common practice of increasing data parallelism to maximize GPU utilization under a deadline. Together, our results identify underexplored factors in repeated-data training and provide concrete guidance on how training recipes and resource allocation should change from single-pass pretraining.
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: データを使い切った後の再学習で、バッチサイズと GPU 時間をどう選ぶか
papers.summary: 計算資源は豊富でも学習データが限られ、同じデータを繰り返し学習する場合の最適な設定を調べた研究である。バッチサイズとエポック数を同時に最適化すると、検証データの損失とバッチサイズの関係は U 字型になり、通常の事前学習より小さいバッチサイズが有利になることが分かった。これは小さいバッチの勾配ノイズが暗黙の正則化として働くためと考えられる。さらに、学習時間の制約を GPU 数と別の資源として扱うと、締め切りが厳しいほど大きいバッチが有利になるものの、締め切りを固定したままでも GPU を少なく使う小さいバッチの方が GPU をたくさん使う大きいバッチより損失が低くなる場合があり、「締め切りに合わせて並列度を上げて GPU 利用率を最大化する」という通常の実践に疑問を投げかけている。
papers.why: 繰り返し学習時代の学習レシピと資源配分の指針を、バッチサイズと GPU 時間という二つの軸で具体的に示しており、学習基盤を設計する人にとって実践的な判断材料になる。
papers.summary_en: The paper studies pretraining when compute is abundant but data is finite, requiring repeated passes over the same data. Jointly optimizing batch size with epoch counts reveals a U-shaped relationship between validation loss and batch size, favoring smaller-than-typical batches, likely due to implicit regularization from small-batch gradient noise. Treating GPUs and time as separate resources, tighter deadlines favor larger batches, but even under a fixed time budget, a smaller batch with fewer GPUs can achieve lower validation loss than a larger batch with more GPUs -- challenging the common practice of maximizing data parallelism to use available GPUs under a deadline.
papers.why_en: Provides concrete, measured guidance on how training recipes and GPU/time resource allocation should differ from single-pass pretraining once data is repeated, directly useful for anyone designing training infrastructure under data scarcity.

review.note: 「GPU 利用率を最大化すれば良い」という通常の実践を、固定時間予算下での実測比較で反証する、測り方の観点。
review.note_en: Challenges the common practice of maximizing GPU utilization under a deadline by empirically showing a smaller-batch/fewer-GPU configuration can beat a larger-batch/more-GPU one under the same fixed time budget.

papers.title: Elephant in the Fridge: Constant-Memory Frame Packing for Long Video Understanding
papers.abstract: Hour-long videos, streaming feeds, and movie-length content are pushing vision-language models (VLMs) past their breaking point -- the standard recipe of encoding each frame into visual tokens yields sequences that grow linearly with video length, causing prohibitive memory consumption and inference latency. Existing approaches, such as token reduction and keyframe selection, shorten the token sequence but leave the O(n) scaling intact, failing to resolve the fundamental bottleneck. We propose FramePack-U, a strikingly simple, training-free frame packing framework that compresses arbitrarily long videos into a fixed size visual representation at constant memory cost. FramePack-U requires no fine-tuning or architectural modification -- it plugs directly into off-the-shelf VLMs at inference time. Inspired by FramePack from the generation literature, we propose a content-aware compression strategy for visual understanding under a fixed token budget. Specifically, FramePack-U (1) scores each frame by its semantic similarity to the text prompt and ranks frames in a diversity-driven manner, and (2) packs the selected frames at varying resolutions into a fixed-length context window. This concentrates the memory budget on frames that are both instruction-relevant and visually diverse. While FramePack-U can in theory pack arbitrarily many frames into the fixed budget, we identify an empirical instantiation that generalizes robustly across settings. Extensive experiments on LongVideoBench, MLVU, and Video-MME show that FramePack-U consistently outperforms full-resolution baselines and prior token reduction and keyframe selection methods across diverse model families, parameter scales, and frame budgets. Notably, on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B with a 128-frame budget, FramePack-U yields gains of +12.9\%, +10.6\%, and +9.7\% over the official model on the three benchmarks, respectively.
papers.ja_title: 固定メモリで長時間動画を扱う、学習不要のフレーム圧縮手法
papers.summary: 動画を扱う視覚言語モデル (VLM) は、動画が長くなるほどトークン数が増えてメモリと推論時間が膨らむ問題を抱えている。本研究は FramePack-U という学習不要の手法を提案し、各フレームを文章プロンプトとの関連度と多様性で選び、重要なフレームほど高い解像度で詰め込むことで、動画の長さに関わらず一定サイズの表現に圧縮する。LongVideoBench・MLVU・Video-MME での実験では、Qwen3.5-35B-A3B に 128 フレーム分の予算を与えた場合、公式モデルに対しそれぞれ +12.9%、+10.6%、+9.7% の性能向上を達成した。
papers.why: 既存の VLM にそのまま組み込める学習不要の圧縮手法で、長時間動画推論のメモリとレイテンシ問題を解く実装の工夫として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Vision-language models (VLMs) struggle with hour-long videos because token sequences grow linearly with length, causing prohibitive memory and latency. FramePack-U is a training-free frame-packing framework that scores frames by text-relevance and diversity, then packs selected frames at varying resolutions into a fixed-length context window, compressing arbitrarily long videos into constant-size representations. On LongVideoBench, MLVU, and Video-MME, it consistently outperforms full-resolution baselines and prior token-reduction/keyframe methods; notably, with a 128-frame budget on Qwen3.5-35B-A3B it yields gains of +12.9%, +10.6%, and +9.7% over the official model on the three benchmarks respectively.
papers.why_en: A drop-in, training-free compression technique that plugs into existing VLMs at inference time, directly addressing the memory/latency bottleneck of long-video inference -- useful as an implementation trick for serving long-context multimodal models.

papers.title: Think Before You Speak: Enabling Training-Free Latent Communication Between Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in solving complex tasks in coding, mathematical logic, and iterative reasoning, especially by coordinating effectively within multi-agent systems (MAS). However, language agents traditionally communicate via text exchange, which introduces a bottleneck in information transfer and adds prefill latency for downstream agents. Recent work proposes that directly sharing the key-value (KV) cache between language models can enable efficient latent collaboration, entirely bypassing standard text-based communication. To enable latent communication between heterogeneous models of different sizes, prior work introduces trained fusion adapters for each model pair, which limits practical deployment. We introduce CacheFuse, a training-free method which demonstrates that augmenting a downstream model with an upstream model's KV cache using linear interpolation consistently enables superior performance than the standalone downstream model can achieve. We systematically analyze CacheFuse across four reasoning and knowledge benchmarks and demonstrate up to 8.6 percentage points higher accuracy compared to single-model baselines and up to 12.2x TTFT speedup compared to text-based communication in multi-model inference.
papers.ja_title: 学習不要で言語モデル間の「内部状態」を融合する CacheFuse
papers.summary: 複数の言語モデルが協力するマルチエージェント系では、文章でやり取りすると情報の伝達に無駄が生じ、後段のモデルの応答前計算 (プリフィル) に時間がかかる。CacheFuse は、学習済みの融合アダプタを使わずに、上流モデルのキーバリュー (KV) キャッシュを線形補間で下流モデルに直接混ぜ込む手法である。4 つの推論・知識ベンチマークで検証した結果、単独モデルより最大 8.6 ポイント高い正解率を達成し、文章でやり取りする方式に比べて最初の応答までの時間 (TTFT) を最大 12.2 倍速くできた。
papers.why: 学習不要かつモデル間で追加のアダプタを作らずに KV キャッシュを共有できる手法で、マルチエージェント推論基盤の高速化に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: In multi-agent LLM systems, text-based communication between agents is a bottleneck and adds prefill latency downstream. CacheFuse is a training-free method that augments a downstream model with an upstream model's KV cache via linear interpolation, without the per-model-pair trained fusion adapters used in prior work. Across four reasoning and knowledge benchmarks, CacheFuse demonstrates up to 8.6 percentage points higher accuracy than single-model baselines and up to 12.2x TTFT speedup compared to text-based communication in multi-model inference.
papers.why_en: A training-free, adapter-free way to share KV caches across heterogeneous models is directly applicable to speeding up multi-agent inference serving stacks without added training overhead.

papers.title: A New Lens on Multi-GPU Communication: API-Level Memory Models for Portable Optimization
papers.abstract: As network communication increasingly becomes a performance bottleneck for ML and HPC workloads, it is more important than ever to optimize multi-GPU data transfers. Recently, low-level device APIs have emerged that allow programmers to perform fine-grain optimizations via one-sided put/get operations triggered directly from the device. However, the communication libraries providing these device APIs (e.g., rocSHMEM, MSCCL++, and NCCL/RCCL GIN) currently lack a rigorous memory model defining how their primitives interact with the underlying memory systems. Without this, emerging HPC and ML workloads aggressively optimizing network communication via device APIs can be brittle, error-prone, and face compatibility and inter-operability challenges. This paper proposes the use of API-level memory models for these emerging device communication APIs. An API-level memory model defines the memory semantics of communication API calls in a way that abstracts lower-level details from the API user and simplifies development. This work defines one such model for device-side communication (implemented in AMD's recently open sourced rocSHMEM library) and demonstrates how formal relaxations to such a model can enable low-level LLM performance optimizations while retaining a well-defined standardized interface. Specifically, we describe how updating the SHMEM API implemented by rocSHMEM can properly support cache bypassing for network data, improving performance of a collective communication workload by up to 2.48x, a fused compute+communication workload by up to 1.77x, and a state-of-the-art expert-parallel communication workload by up to 1.18x.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: GPU 間通信 API の「メモリモデル」を正式に定義し高速化する
papers.summary: GPU 同士が直接データを読み書きする低レベル通信 API (rocSHMEM、MSCCL++、NCCL/RCCL GIN など) は、キャッシュやメモリとどう整合するかの厳密な規則が決まっておらず、ML・HPC 向けの最適化が壊れやすく互換性問題を起こしやすい。本研究は AMD の rocSHMEM 向けに API レベルのメモリモデルを定義し、その規則を形式的に緩めることでネットワークデータのキャッシュ回避を安全に実装できることを示した。この最適化により、集団通信ワークロードで最大 2.48 倍、計算と通信を融合したワークロードで最大 1.77 倍、エキスパート並列通信ワークロードで最大 1.18 倍の性能向上を達成した。
papers.why: GPU 間通信ライブラリを安全に最適化するための形式的な土台を示しており、分散学習・推論基盤の低レベル通信を作る・検証する人にとって直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Low-level device-side communication APIs for multi-GPU transfers (rocSHMEM, MSCCL++, NCCL/RCCL GIN) currently lack a rigorous memory model defining how their put/get primitives interact with the underlying memory system, making aggressive network optimizations brittle and hard to port. This paper defines an API-level memory model for AMD's rocSHMEM and shows that formally relaxing it enables cache-bypassing optimizations for network data while retaining a well-defined standardized interface. The resulting optimization improves a collective communication workload by up to 2.48x, a fused compute+communication workload by up to 1.77x, and a state-of-the-art expert-parallel communication workload by up to 1.18x.
papers.why_en: Provides a formal foundation for safely optimizing low-level multi-GPU communication libraries, directly useful for anyone building or verifying the low-level collective communication layer of distributed training/inference stacks.

papers.title: NetRL: Powering Network Decisions via NetGRPO-Driven Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Network decision-making tasks, including adaptive bitrate streaming, load balancing, and congestion control, require policies to process heterogeneous states and actions while balancing near- and long-term consequences. Existing solutions generalize poorly across network tasks, require substantial task-specific redesign, and lack reliable evaluation of long- horizon action consequences. Methods that learn through online interaction additionally face unstable optimization. We present NetRL, a two-stage LLM-based reinforcement learning framework that combines supervised fine-tuning on demonstration trajectories with online policy optimization. A universal mixed-embedding interface combines textual task descriptions with precise numerical states, while a network action head produces valid decisions. At its core, NetGRPO evaluates candidate actions over multiple future trajectories, directs deeper search toward uncertain alternatives through confidence-aware budgeting, and performs group-relative, clipped, and KL-regularized updates. NetRL achieves 23.6% higher QoE than NetLLM, 12.2% lower job completion time than Genet, and 24.1% higher network utility than Orca, yielding state-of-the-art performance among the evaluated methods. Confidence-aware budgeting reduces end-to-end training time by 27.1% without reducing validation QoE. NetRL also converges stably and generalizes to unseen network traces without retraining. Code and model weights are available at the repository linked in this paper.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク

papers.title: REVEAL: Reverse Engineering Agentic Latents from Frontier-Model Traces
papers.abstract: Frontier LLM agents perform complex interactive tasks, but their inference costs motivate transferring their experience to smaller open-source agents. Distillation and latent communication typically require target-model training or access to source-model internals. We study how textual frontier-model trajectories can provide reusable local controls for a frozen agent. Inspired by protocol reverse engineering, we introduce $\textit{Agentic Latents}$, comprising anchored states and dynamic profiles of feedback--response cycles elicited by replay in the target model. Our training-free framework, $\textbf{REVEAL}$ ($\textbf{REV}$erse $\textbf{E}$ngineering $\textbf{A}$gentic $\textbf{L}$atents), uses these profiles and trajectory outcomes to match and select local events from successful and failed rollouts of the same task and source model. Their response-transition contrasts yield a target-specific steering direction, applied before each response. Within-benchmark evaluations on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and Humanity's Last Exam with tools report higher accuracy than unmodified agents across three targets. Representation analyses and behavioral case studies support reusing frontier-model experience as local activation control.
papers.ja_title: 強いモデルの「経験」を凍結した小型エージェントに移す REVEAL
papers.summary: 高性能な LLM エージェントは精度は高いが推論コストも高く、その経験を小型のオープンソースエージェントに移すには通常、対象モデルの学習や内部情報へのアクセスが必要になる。REVEAL は学習を一切行わず、強いモデルの成功例と失敗例のやり取りを比較して得た「応答の変化方向」を、対象モデルの応答生成前に適用することで性能を上げる手法である。Terminal-Bench 2.1 と Humanity's Last Exam (ツール利用あり) での検証では、何も手を加えないエージェントに比べて 3 つの対象モデルすべてで正解率が向上した。
papers.why: 学習や内部パラメータへのアクセスなしに、強いモデルの経験を活性化制御として再利用できる手法で、推論時にエージェント性能を安く引き上げる方法として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Frontier LLM agents perform well but are costly to run, and transferring their experience to smaller open agents typically requires target-model training or access to source-model internals. REVEAL is a training-free framework that derives "Agentic Latents" -- anchored states and feedback-response profiles from frontier-model trajectories -- and matches successful vs. failed rollouts of the same task to compute a target-specific steering direction, applied before each response. Within-benchmark evaluations on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and Humanity's Last Exam with tools report higher accuracy than unmodified agents across three targets.
papers.why_en: Offers a training-free way to reuse frontier-model experience as local activation control without needing target-model training or source-model internals, a cheap inference-time lever for boosting smaller agents' performance.

papers.title: SLDBench v2: Active Scaling Law Discovery
papers.abstract: Scaling laws predict large-model performance from small experiments, but finding a reliable law itself requires costly experiments. SLDBench tests whether language-model agents can discover scaling laws when all experimental results are given upfront. We introduce SLDBench v2 with two extensions. First, we expand the corpus from 8 to 127 scenarios spanning language-model pretraining, downstream performance, and vision-language transfer, and select 30 challenging scenarios on which a reference power-law fit reaches $R^2 \le 0.8$; they represent at least $1.09 \times 10^{23}$ FLOPs of source-reported training compute. Second, we introduce active scaling law discovery: an agent chooses which experiments to run, pays each one's recorded cost (e.g., training FLOPs), and revises its law as outcomes arrive, and is scored on the same hidden extrapolation targets as in the passive setting. Across 8 frontier agent systems, median $R^2$ drops from 0.72-0.75 (passive) to 0.24-0.57 (active), and prediction error rises 1.5-4.7 times, depending on the system. Agents favor cheap experiments, spending 8-44% of the full-pool cost on average; low-cost acquisition can yield strong predictions, but cheap purchases also leave experimental conditions needed for extrapolation unobserved. Experimental planning thus remains a key open challenge for agents that assist model development in the prevailing AI-for-AI study. Project page: https://lingbei-meng.github.io/SLDBench-v2/.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: SLDBench v2:エージェントは自分で実験を選んでスケーリング則を見つけられるか
papers.summary: スケーリング法則(モデルを大きくした時に性能がどう変わるかの規則)を、LLM エージェントが実験結果を自分で選びながら見つけられるかを測るベンチマーク。シナリオを 8 個から 127 個に増やし、特に当てはめが難しい 30 個(当てはめの決定係数 R^2 が 0.8 以下、少なくとも 1.09×10^23 FLOPs の学習計算量を代表)を選んだ。実験を自分で選んで行う「能動的」設定では、結果を先にすべて渡す「受動的」設定に比べ、8 種の最先端エージェントで R^2 が 0.72〜0.75 から 0.24〜0.57 に下がり、予測誤差は 1.5〜4.7 倍に増え、エージェントは安い実験(全体コストの 8〜44%)を好むため外挿に必要な条件を見落としやすいことが分かった。
papers.why: AI がモデル開発を支援する研究で、実験計画の立案そのものが未解決の課題であることを示し、スケーリング則の自動発見ツールを評価する際の観点を提供する。
papers.summary_en: SLDBench v2 expands the scaling-law discovery benchmark from 8 to 127 scenarios and selects 30 challenging ones (reference power-law R^2 <= 0.8, representing at least 1.09e23 FLOPs of training compute). In the new active setting, where agents choose which experiments to run and pay their cost, median R^2 drops from 0.72-0.75 (passive) to 0.24-0.57 (active) across 8 frontier agent systems, with prediction error rising 1.5-4.7x, as agents favor cheap experiments (8-44% of full-pool cost) and miss conditions needed for extrapolation.
papers.why_en: Shows experimental planning remains a key open challenge for AI-for-AI agents assisting model development, and offers a passive-vs-active evaluation lens for scaling-law discovery tools.

review.note: ベンチマークを「全結果を先に渡す」設定と「エージェントが実験を選ぶ」設定に分けて測ると、見えなかった大きな性能差が現れるという評価設計の観点。
review.note_en: A measurement-design observation: splitting evaluation into passive (all results given) vs active (agent chooses experiments) settings reveals a large, otherwise hidden performance gap.

papers.title: LoopQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Looped Transformers
papers.abstract: Looped Language Models (LoopLMs) improve parameter efficiency by recursively reusing shared Transformer modules, yet their repeated computation over evolving recurrent states poses new challenges for low-bit deployment. Existing post-training quantization (PTQ) methods, largely designed for feed-forward Transformers, fail to account for cross-loop activation dynamics, heterogeneous loop sensitivity, and recursive error propagation, leading to substantial performance degradation at low precision. To address these challenges, we propose LoopQuant, a loop-aware PTQ framework for accurate and efficient low-bit quantization of LoopLMs. LoopQuant is built on three core components: 1) Cross-Loop Distribution Canonicalization (CLDC) learns a shared quantization-friendly representation across recurrent states while preserving parameter sharing; 2) Interaction-Aware Loop-wise Precision Allocation (ILPA) allocates activation precision under a fixed bit budget by modeling task-level loop sensitivity and cross-loop interactions; and 3) Loop-Conditioned Task Calibration (LCTC) further aligns quantized inference with the low-bit recursive trajectory through lightweight task-space calibration. Extensive experiments across LoopLM architectures demonstrate that LoopQuant consistently outperforms existing low-bit PTQ methods. On Ouro-2.6B, LoopQuant under W4A4 surpasses all W4A8 baselines in performance, while reducing model memory by 65.3% with only 3.4% additional storage overhead over naive INT4 and achieving a 1.7 times decoding speedup over BF16. These results demonstrate a strong balance among accuracy, compression, and inference efficiency, providing a practical and deployment-friendly solution for low-bit LoopLM inference. The code is available at [https://github.com/Kishon-zzx/LoopQuant].
papers.ja_title: LoopQuant:ループ型 Transformer のための低ビット量子化
papers.summary: 同じ Transformer ブロックを繰り返し使う「ループ型言語モデル(LoopLM)」は省パラメータだが、低ビットに量子化(数値を少ないビットで近似する処理)すると性能が大きく落ちる問題があった。LoopQuant はループ間の活性化分布をそろえる処理、ループごとにビット配分を変える処理、タスクに合わせて再調整する処理の 3 つを組み合わせる。Ouro-2.6B では 4bit 量子化(W4A4)でも従来の 8bit 量子化(W4A8)の性能を上回り、メモリは 65.3% 削減、追加の保存コストはわずか 3.4%、推論速度は BF16 の 1.7 倍になった。
papers.why: ループ構造を持つ新しいモデル系列の低ビット推論を実用化する手法で、既存の量子化手法がループ間の相互作用を見落とす弱点に対処している点が新しい。
papers.summary_en: Looped Language Models (LoopLMs) reuse shared Transformer blocks to save parameters, but existing post-training quantization ignores cross-loop activation dynamics and degrades substantially at low bit-widths. LoopQuant combines cross-loop distribution canonicalization, interaction-aware loop-wise precision allocation, and loop-conditioned task calibration; on Ouro-2.6B, LoopQuant under W4A4 surpasses all W4A8 baselines while reducing model memory by 65.3% with only 3.4% extra storage overhead over naive INT4, and achieves a 1.7x decoding speedup over BF16.
papers.why_en: Addresses a gap existing PTQ methods miss (cross-loop interaction), offering a practical path to deploy the new LoopLM architecture at low precision.

papers.title: Chain Dimension Scaling: Communication-Efficient Loop-Style Scaling for Industrial Short-Video Ranking
papers.abstract: Industrial recommendation rankers keep scaling in width and depth to billions of parameters, but this increasingly incurs costs in parameter growth, distributed communication overhead, and training inefficiency. We introduce \underline{C}hain \underline{D}imension \underline{S}caling (CDS), a scaling strategy orthogonal to width and depth. CDS repeatedly applies a single feature-interaction block with parameters shared across iterations, so the number of iterations (the chain length) becomes a new scaling dimension that adds no parameters. A lightweight intra-chain residual connection stabilizes optimization and improves quality. CDS enables two regimes. In the \emph{compression regime}, shallow blocks with a longer chain match deeper baselines with fewer parameters and faster training; in the \emph{quality-scaling regime}, increasing chain length under a fixed parameter budget yields consistent offline and online gains, suggesting the chain dimension adds modeling capacity beyond parameter reuse. We evaluate CDS in a large-scale multi-task short-video ranking system in production. In the compression regime, CDS stays within $0.03\%$ of baseline offline quality while reducing trainable parameters by 26.6\% and improving training throughput by 6.4\%, with neutral-to-positive online participation. In the quality-scaling regime, quality improves monotonically with chain length. Wall-clock analysis shows the efficiency gain comes mainly not from reduced FLOPs but from lower cross-device synchronization overhead and reduced optimizer update cost. These results position parameter-shared iterative computation as a practical, communication-efficient scaling axis for industrial ranking systems.
papers.ja_title: Chain Dimension Scaling:パラメータを増やさず通信コストを抑える推薦モデルの拡大軸
papers.summary: 産業向け動画推薦ランキングモデルは幅や深さを増やすほど、分散学習の通信コストが増える問題がある。CDS は 1 つの特徴相互作用ブロックをパラメータ共有したまま繰り返し適用し、繰り返し回数(チェーン長)を新しい拡大軸として使う。本番の大規模マルチタスク短編動画ランキングで、オフライン品質の差を 0.03% 以内に保ちながら学習パラメータを 26.6% 削減し学習スループットを 6.4% 向上させ、効率向上は計算量(FLOPs)の削減ではなく通信同期やオプティマイザ更新コストの削減によることを確認した。
papers.why: パラメータを増やさずに通信コストだけを抑えて性能を伸ばせる拡大軸を示し、大規模分散学習の負荷の本質がしばしば同期コストにあることを明示している。
papers.summary_en: Industrial recommendation rankers keep scaling width and depth, incurring growing distributed communication overhead. Chain Dimension Scaling (CDS) repeatedly applies a single parameter-shared feature-interaction block, making the iteration count (chain length) a new, parameter-free scaling axis. In a large-scale production short-video ranking system, CDS stays within 0.03% of baseline offline quality while cutting trainable parameters by 26.6% and raising training throughput by 6.4%, with the gain coming mainly from reduced cross-device synchronization and optimizer-update cost rather than fewer FLOPs.
papers.why_en: Offers a communication-efficient scaling axis orthogonal to width/depth for large distributed training systems, where overhead often stems from synchronization rather than raw compute.

papers.title: Resample the Answer: Where to Spend Test-Time Compute in Recursive Reasoning
papers.abstract: Recursive reasoning models such as the Tiny Recursive Model (TRM) iteratively refine two latent states: an answer state y, decoded into the output, and a reasoning state z, which is never decoded. Many of their failures have been attributed to bad basins, regions of latent space that trap the recursion on wrong answers. Recent test-time approaches perturb y, z or both to recover these failures, but the impact of this choice on performance, test-time compute efficiency and scaling properties remains unclear. Through controlled experiments on TRM, we find that a failed trajectory carries its failure in its answer state. At equal compute, whether retries continue a failed trajectory (depth scaling) or draw multiple trajectories from the initial states (width scaling), resampling y recovers more failures than any perturbation of z we tested, and the performance gap widens as the test-time compute budget grows. Our approach, Gated Answer Resampling (GAR), pairs this resampling of the answer state with the model's own halting head and restarts only the puzzles that the head rejects. With at most 64 restarts per puzzle and no training or hyperparameter search, GAR takes TRM from 85.9% to 99.4% on Sudoku-Extreme and from 68.8% to 85.6% on Pencil Puzzle Bench validation. On the same checkpoints, GAR also outperforms Probabilistic TRM (PTRM), which perturbs z at each step, even when PTRM uses 42 to 197 times as much compute. Our code is available at https://github.com/MaximeILL/GAR.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: どこに推論時の計算を使うべきか:再帰的推論モデルでの答え再サンプリング
papers.summary: 再帰的推論モデル(TRM)は答え状態 y と推論状態 z を繰り返し更新するが、失敗した推論の多くはその失敗が答え状態 y に残っていることを実験で確かめた。GAR は停止判定ヘッドが間違いだと判断したパズルだけ y を再サンプリングしてやり直す手法で、追加の学習やハイパーパラメータ探索なしに、最大 64 回の再試行で Sudoku-Extreme の正解率を 85.9% から 99.4% に、Pencil Puzzle Bench を 68.8% から 85.6% に上げた。z を揺らす既存手法(PTRM)が 42〜197 倍多く計算を使っても、GAR の方が精度が高かった。
papers.why: テスト時計算をどこに使うべきか(答え状態の再サンプリングが有効)という設計判断を具体的に示し、推論時スケーリング手法の作り方に指針を与える。
papers.summary_en: Recursive reasoning models like the Tiny Recursive Model (TRM) refine an answer state y and a never-decoded reasoning state z, and the authors find that failed trajectories carry their failure in the answer state y. Gated Answer Resampling (GAR) resamples y only for puzzles rejected by the model's own halting head, and with at most 64 restarts and no extra training, raises TRM from 85.9% to 99.4% on Sudoku-Extreme and from 68.8% to 85.6% on Pencil Puzzle Bench, outperforming Probabilistic TRM (which perturbs z) even when PTRM uses 42-197x as much compute.
papers.why_en: Gives a concrete, compute-efficient answer to where to spend test-time compute in recursive reasoning, informing how to design test-time scaling methods.

papers.title: StructZO: Structured Zeroth-Order Optimization for Memory-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Fine-tuning large language models at scale is increasingly limited by the memory cost of backpropagation. Zeroth-Order (ZO) optimizers reduce this burden by relying only on forward function evaluations, but they still exhibit a substantial performance gap to first-order (FO) optimizers such as Adam. We argue that this gap does not arise solely from the absence of explicit gradients: FO fine-tuning also benefits from informative low-rank optimization geometry, large-scale signal aggregation, and well-conditioned update directions. Motivated by this, we introduce StructZO, a structured Zeroth-Order optimization framework for memory-efficient LLM fine-tuning. StructZO performs large-query ZO estimation within an activation-induced informative subspace and applies spectral control to the resulting reduced-space update before mapping it back to the original parameters. This lets ZO aggregate useful directional signals in a compact, geometry-aware space while avoiding the activation and optimizer-state memory costs of backpropagation. We show theoretically that, when the induced subspace captures concentrated optimization-relevant directions, StructZO reduces the effective ZO estimation dimension from $mn$ to $mr$, with the remaining projection error governed by the spectral tail of the activation Gram matrix. Empirically, across OPT-series and Llama3.1-8B on diverse downstreamtasks, StructZO improves over the strongest existing ZO baselines by up to $8.7%$ relative on average and up to $26.9%$ relative on individual tasks, while remaining within $1.5%$ of FO-Adam on average. These results suggest that structured and spectrally controlled ZO updates can substantially narrow the gap between ZO and FO optimization.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: StructZO:勾配を使わずに大規模言語モデルを低メモリで微調整する
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルの微調整ではバックプロパゲーション(逆伝播)のメモリ消費が課題で、これを避けるゼロ次最適化(ZO、関数の値だけで更新方向を推定する手法)は Adam などの勾配を使う一次最適化より性能が劣っていた。StructZO は活性化から得た情報量の多い低次元の部分空間内で ZO 推定を行い、スペクトル制御(更新の大きさを整える処理)を加えてから元のパラメータに戻す。OPT 系列や Llama3.1-8B の多様なタスクで、既存の最良 ZO 手法を平均で最大 8.7%、個別タスクで最大 26.9% 改善し、一次最適化の Adam とは平均 1.5% 以内の差に縮まった。
papers.why: メモリ制約の厳しい大規模微調整で、勾配なし最適化と勾配ありの性能差を縮める実用的な手法を示している。
papers.summary_en: Zeroth-Order (ZO) optimizers avoid backprop's memory cost for LLM fine-tuning but lag first-order (FO) methods like Adam substantially. StructZO performs large-query ZO estimation within an activation-induced low-rank subspace and applies spectral control before mapping updates back to full parameters; across OPT models and Llama3.1-8B, it improves over the strongest existing ZO baselines by up to 8.7% relative on average (up to 26.9% on individual tasks) while staying within 1.5% of FO-Adam on average.
papers.why_en: Narrows the long-standing gap between gradient-free and gradient-based fine-tuning, useful for memory-constrained large-scale fine-tuning.

papers.title: SLEM: Spectrum-Aware Latent Expert Merging
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models scale model capacity efficiently by activating only a small subset of experts for each input, while still requiring all parameters to be stored in memory, resulting in substantial memory overhead. Expert merging techniques have recently emerged as a promising compression paradigm that reduces this overhead by consolidating multiple experts into a smaller set. However, existing approaches have two key limitations: (i) direct convex interpolation in parameter space is not generally guaranteed to yield meaningful interpolation of expert functions; and (ii) estimating expert similarity or merging coefficients often relies on calibration data, introducing dependence on the calibration distribution. To address these limitations, we propose Spectrum-Aware Latent Expert Merging (SLEM), a calibration-free expert merging framework that occurs in a structured latent representation of expert weights using a VAE. SLEM groups experts within and across layers based on latent similarities and derives merging coefficients from expert weight spectra. It then performs geometry-aware latent interpolation and decodes the resulting representations into merged expert weights. Compared with existing expert merging methods, SLEM achieves comparable or better performance on general knowledge benchmarks and higher average performance on generation benchmarks involving mathematical reasoning and code generation.
papers.ja_title: SLEM:潜在空間で専門家を統合する校正データ不要な MoE 圧縮
papers.summary: 複数の専門家ネットワークを切り替えて使うモデル(MoE)は全専門家をメモリに保持する必要があり負荷が大きい。既存の専門家統合手法はパラメータ空間で直接補間するため意味のある統合にならない、または校正データに依存するという弱点があった。SLEM は VAE(変分自己符号化器)で専門家の重みを潜在空間に写し、校正データなしで似た専門家をまとめ、重み行列のスペクトル(特異値の分布)から統合係数を求めて潜在空間上で補間し重みに戻す。一般知識ベンチマークでは既存手法と同等以上、数学推論やコード生成を含む生成ベンチマークでは平均性能がより高かった。
papers.why: 校正データ不要で専門家を統合する手法を示し、MoE モデルの圧縮を校正データへの依存なく安定・再現可能にする着眼点を提供する。
papers.summary_en: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models require storing all experts in memory, and existing expert-merging methods either merge directly in parameter space (not guaranteed to preserve function) or depend on calibration data. SLEM is a calibration-free framework that maps expert weights into a VAE latent space, groups experts by latent similarity, derives merging coefficients from expert weight spectra, and performs geometry-aware latent interpolation before decoding back to weights, matching or beating existing merging methods on general knowledge benchmarks and achieving higher average performance on math reasoning and code generation benchmarks.
papers.why_en: Provides a calibration-free, geometry-aware approach to MoE expert merging, a cleaner alternative to calibration-dependent merging for reducing memory overhead.

papers.title: Prorsa: Unleashing the Potential of Prefill-Decode Disaggregation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) is commonly used to enhance the capabilities of large language models (LLMs) in solving complex multi-turn tasks. During rollout, agentic RL exhibits a workload pattern distinct from that of traditional RL: multi-turn interactions repeatedly introduce prefill requests, causing prefill and decode workloads to coexist throughout rollout. This workload makes prefill-decode (PD) disaggregation, a design widely used for online LLM serving, promising for speeding up agentic RL rollout. This paper shows that PD disaggregation can improve rollout efficiency by (a) mitigating interference among data-parallel attention modules, (b) enabling stage-specific parallelism, and (c) reducing end-to-end trajectory completion time. However, a fixed prefill-decode allocation may fail to sustain these benefits as workload composition varies across tasks and over time. We therefore present Prorsa, an agentic RL framework for prediction-guided prefill-decode resource allocation. Prorsa observes the lifecycle of every trajectory to forecast short-horizon prefill and decode demand. These forecasts then guide worker allocation decisions and trigger role switching of rollout engines, aligning prefill and decode capacity with anticipated workload demand. Across synchronous and asynchronous agentic RL settings, Prorsa achieves end-to-end rollout speedups of 1.11x-4.05x over prefill-decode colocation.
papers.ja_title: Prorsa:エージェント型 RL のロールアウトに合わせて動くプレフィル・デコード分離
papers.summary: マルチターン対話を繰り返すエージェント型強化学習(RL)のロールアウトでは、プレフィル(入力処理)とデコード(生成)の負荷が常に混在する独特のワークロードになる。Prorsa は各軌跡のプレフィル・デコード需要を短期的に予測し、その予測に基づいてプレフィルとデコードの計算資源割り当てやワーカーの役割切り替えを動的に行う。同期・非同期どちらのエージェント型 RL 設定でも、プレフィルとデコードを同じワーカーに混在させる方式に比べ、ロールアウト全体の速度が 1.11〜4.05 倍になった。
papers.why: LLM サービングで使われるプレフィル・デコード分離という設計を RL のロールアウトに持ち込み、ワークロード予測で動的に資源配分する点が、RL 基盤の効率化にそのまま使える新しい工夫。
papers.summary_en: Agentic reinforcement learning (RL) rollout produces a distinctive workload where prefill and decode coexist throughout multi-turn interactions, making prefill-decode (PD) disaggregation promising for speedup. Prorsa forecasts each trajectory's short-horizon prefill/decode demand and uses these predictions to dynamically allocate workers and switch rollout engine roles between prefill and decode. Across synchronous and asynchronous agentic RL settings, Prorsa achieves end-to-end rollout speedups of 1.11x-4.05x over PD colocation.
papers.why_en: Brings serving-style PD disaggregation into RL rollout infrastructure with workload-prediction-guided resource allocation, directly useful for scaling agentic RL training systems.

papers.title: Growing to See: Efficient Pretraining of Self-Supervised Vision Transformers
papers.abstract: Progressive depth growth builds large networks by starting with shallow models and inserting layers during training. Recent advances in large language models have renewed interest in this longstanding approach, demonstrating benefits for training efficiency and reasoning alongside changes in internal computations. However, how growing affects representation quality and computational patterns in self-supervised vision transformers remains unclear. In this work, we systematically investigate progressive depth growth in two popular self-supervised families, namely masked autoencoders (MAE) and DINOv3, and analyze how growing affects downstream performance, intermediate representations, and internal computations. Across global and dense tasks, we show that growing improves downstream performance while reducing training FLOPs by 13.9--24.8%, with ImageNet linear-probe accuracy gains of up to 3.36 percentage points. Growing also improves downstream performance at intermediate layers and reshapes internal computational patterns, introducing recurring alternations between global and localized attention in MAE and earlier local-to-global attention progression in self-distilled DINOv3. Together, these findings establish progressive depth growth as an effective and efficient pretraining strategy for improving downstream performance across global and dense visual tasks with less computation, and advance our understanding of how growing shapes visual computation.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: Growing to See:自己教師あり視覚 Transformer を段階的に深くして効率よく事前学習する
papers.summary: 浅いモデルから始めて学習中に層を追加する「段階的な深さ成長」という手法を、自己教師あり視覚 Transformer(MAE と DINOv3)に適用して調べた。全体的な認識タスクと細かい予測タスクの両方で下流性能が向上し、学習に必要な計算量(FLOPs)を 13.9〜24.8% 削減できた一方、ImageNet の線形プローブ精度は最大 3.36 ポイント向上した。層を増やすことで中間層の性能も上がり、注意パターンが MAE ではグローバルとローカルを交互に行う形に、DINOv3 ではローカルからグローバルへより早く移行する形に変化した。
papers.why: 大規模言語モデルで知られる段階的成長を視覚 Transformer の事前学習に適用し、計算量を抑えつつ性能を上げる具体的な効率化手法として使える。
papers.summary_en: Progressive depth growth-starting shallow and inserting layers during training-is studied for self-supervised vision transformers (MAE and DINOv3). Across global and dense downstream tasks, growing improves performance while reducing training FLOPs by 13.9-24.8%, with ImageNet linear-probe accuracy gains of up to 3.36 points, and also reshapes internal attention patterns (alternating global/local in MAE, earlier local-to-global progression in DINOv3).
papers.why_en: Establishes progressive depth growth as an effective pretraining-efficiency strategy for self-supervised vision transformers, extending an LLM-era technique with concrete compute/accuracy trade-offs.

papers.title: Efficient Resource-Shiftable RL Post-training with Generative Rewards
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training with generative reward models (GenRM) has become a central recipe for improving large language models (LLMs), and it is also increasingly resource-intensive: policy rollout, GenRM-based reward evaluation, and policy training all compete for GPU resources. However, existing colocated and disaggregated systems rely on static resource allocation for these roles. Such allocation cannot adapt as each role's workload changes during RL and therefore leaves a role's resources underutilized. We present PivotRL, an RL post-training system that dynamically shifts resources among different roles according to their runtime demands. PivotRL introduces a resource-shiftable runtime built on a Global Parameter Storage, together with a unified mechanism that efficiently shifts role-specific context. A shift-aware scheduler enables sequence migration upon a shift, while a planner considers the aggregate throughput benefit and the shift overhead to determine when and how to shift. We evaluate PivotRL on a 128-GPU cluster using four model groups spanning dense and mixture-of-experts models. PivotRL enables resource shifting within seconds and improves end-to-end throughput by 1.81-2.05 times over colocated deployment and 1.50-1.95 times over disaggregated deployment, while preserving RL convergence.
papers.ja_title: 強化学習の後学習向けに GPU 資源を動的に移すシステム PivotRL
papers.summary: LLM の強化学習後学習では、生成型報酬モデル (GenRM) を使う際にロールアウト・報酬評価・学習の 3 つが GPU を奪い合うが、既存システムは資源配分を固定してしまい使われない資源が生まれる問題がある。PivotRL は Global Parameter Storage 上で動く「資源を移せる」実行基盤と、移動に応じたシーケンス移動のスケジューラ、移動タイミングを判断するプランナーを導入した。128 GPU のクラスタで高密度モデルと MoE モデルを使った評価で、同居配置より 1.81〜2.05 倍、分離配置より 1.50〜1.95 倍スループットが向上し、RL の収束も保たれた。
papers.why: GenRM を使う RL 後学習の GPU 利用効率を上げる実運用システムとして、資源移動の判断と移行機構を具体的に示している点が実装者に役立つ。
papers.summary_en: RL post-training with generative reward models (GenRM) competes for GPU resources across rollout, reward evaluation, and policy training, but existing colocated/disaggregated systems use static allocation that leaves resources underutilized as workloads shift. PivotRL introduces a resource-shiftable runtime built on a Global Parameter Storage, a shift-aware scheduler for sequence migration, and a planner that weighs aggregate throughput benefit against shift overhead. On a 128-GPU cluster across dense and MoE model groups, PivotRL shifts resources within seconds and improves end-to-end throughput by 1.81-2.05x over colocated deployment and 1.50-1.95x over disaggregated deployment, while preserving RL convergence.
papers.why_en: It offers a concrete runtime and scheduling/planning mechanism for dynamically reallocating GPUs across rollout, reward, and training roles in GenRM-based RL post-training, useful for anyone building such systems.

papers.title: FORGE: Procedural Weight Generation for Sparse MoE Inference
papers.abstract: We introduce FORGE (Fast On-chip Rotor Generation for Experts), a procedural weight generation system for Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) inference. Rather than storing and loading every expert weight tensor from HBM, we show how a compact accelerator inside each Streaming Multiprocessor can regenerate them on-the-fly from $O(\log^2 d)$ rotor parameters per projection. Per replaced layer, gigabytes of stored expert weights are approximated with under a megabyte of seeds. This addresses the dual memory bottleneck of autoregressive Sparse MoE decode, where per-expert FFN operations are HBM-bandwidth-bound at small routed-token counts and the aggregate expert footprint forces multi-node Expert Parallelism (EP) with all-to-all traffic. We realize the approach as the Rotor Generation Unit (RGU), a fixed-function datapath that generates FFN weight tiles without competing with Tensor Core execution. With 30% of the MoE FFN layers replaced across five Sparse MoE models, we estimate 1.3-2.8x higher system throughput at matched GPU count and 1.10-1.15x lower per-user decode latency at short context. In exchange, downstream accuracy on three model families falls below that of the same model fine-tuned without rotor replacement, and the replacement ratio controls this tradeoff. FORGE also expands KV cache capacity by 1.2-2.6x. It is agnostic to the bit width at which weights are stored, so it can compose with quantization. The RGU is fully implemented/verified in SystemVerilog at ~0.9% SM area overhead (0.032 mm^2/SM, 7nm).
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: MoE 推論の専門家重みをその場で生成して読み込みを減らす FORGE
papers.summary: 疎な MoE (Mixture-of-Experts) の推論では、各専門家の重みを全部 HBM から読み込む必要があり、小さいトークン数ではメモリ帯域が足りず、重み全体が大きいため複数ノードに分散する通信 (all-to-all) も必要になる困りごとがある。FORGE は各 SM (ストリーミングマルチプロセッサ) に小さな回路 (Rotor Generation Unit) を置き、数十キロバイトの種から専門家の重みをその場で再構成することで、重みの読み込みを減らす。5 つの MoE モデルで FFN 層の 30% を置き換えた結果、同じ GPU 数で 1.3〜2.8 倍のスループット、短い文脈では 1.10〜1.15 倍低いレイテンシ、KV キャッシュ容量は 1.2〜2.6 倍に増えたが、精度は置き換え前のファインチューニング済みモデルより下がる。
papers.why: メモリ帯域制約の MoE デコードに対して専用ハードウェア回路で重み圧縮・生成を行うという、推論システムとカーネル設計の新しい方向性を示す。
papers.summary_en: Autoregressive sparse-MoE decoding is HBM-bandwidth-bound at small routed-token counts, and the large aggregate expert footprint forces multi-node expert parallelism with costly all-to-all traffic. FORGE adds a compact per-SM accelerator (Rotor Generation Unit) that regenerates expert FFN weight tiles on-the-fly from under a megabyte of seed parameters instead of loading gigabytes from HBM. With 30% of MoE FFN layers replaced across five models, the authors estimate 1.3-2.8x higher system throughput at matched GPU count, 1.10-1.15x lower decode latency at short context, and 1.2-2.6x larger KV cache capacity, at the cost of lower downstream accuracy than the same model fine-tuned without rotor replacement.
papers.why_en: It proposes a dedicated hardware datapath trading weight-loading bandwidth for on-chip procedural generation, a novel direction for inference-system and kernel/accelerator design targeting the memory bottleneck of sparse MoE decode.

papers.title: Minimax Optimality of Shampoo for Nonstationary Stochastic Optimization
papers.abstract: We develop a comprehensive theoretical analysis of Matrix Shampoo for tracking time-varying optima in nonstationary stochastic optimization. We derive finite-horizon high-probability bounds for average tracking error that disentangle initialization, optimizer drift, momentum-induced drift penalty, stochastic noise, and adaptive preconditioning, with explicit dependence on momentum parameter \(β_1\) and stabilization parameter \(\varepsilon\). These bounds reveal an explicit drift--noise and stability--geometry tradeoffs: noise-dominated regimes favor larger $β_1$, which provides stronger first-moment averaging and greater suppression of gradient noise, whereas drift-dominated regimes favor smaller $β_1$, allowing faster adaptation to moving optimizer. Larger $\varepsilon$ reduces the preconditioner-perturbation term while weakening Shampoo's ability to exploit matrix geometry, thereby reducing adaptivity. We establish a matching minimax lower bound under squared path-variation constraint, proving the information-theoretic optimality of Shampoo over the class of causal optimization procedures. Under a constant stepsize, we establish high-probability bounds for the average projected stationarity gap along general nonstationary nonconvex objectives. We validate our theoretical findings on both synthetic and multiple real-world problems.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 動く最適値を追う最適化手法 Shampoo の理論的最適性
papers.summary: 深層学習で使われる行列版の二次最適化手法 Shampoo について、目標 (最適値) が時間とともに動く非定常な状況での追跡誤差を初めて細かく分析した研究。モーメンタムの強さ β1 や安定化パラメータ ε が、ノイズを抑える効果と目標の動きに追いつく速さのどちらを優先するかのトレードオフを生むことを示し、この誤差の上限が理論的に最良 (ミニマックス最適) であることも証明した。合成データと複数の実データで理論の予測が当てはまることを確かめた。
papers.why: Shampoo のようなスケールしやすい最適化手法のハイパーパラメータ選択を、理論的な根拠付きで議論できるようにする基礎研究。
papers.summary_en: The paper gives a comprehensive finite-horizon, high-probability analysis of Matrix Shampoo for tracking time-varying optima in nonstationary stochastic optimization, decomposing the tracking error into initialization, optimizer drift, momentum-induced drift penalty, stochastic noise, and adaptive-preconditioning terms, with explicit dependence on momentum β1 and stabilization ε. It establishes a matching minimax lower bound under a squared path-variation constraint, proving Shampoo's information-theoretic optimality among causal optimization procedures, and validates the predictions on synthetic and real-world problems.
papers.why_en: It provides theoretical grounding for choosing Shampoo's hyperparameters (momentum, stabilization) under distribution shift, relevant to anyone reasoning about large-scale optimizer behavior.

papers.title: Mixture of GFlowNets
papers.abstract: Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets) learn a policy that samples compositional objects in proportion to an unnormalized reward $R(x)$. This makes them useful wherever many diverse, high-reward candidates are needed and oracle queries are expensive. In practice, a single GFlowNet often fails to cover all modes of a complex distribution, and the obvious ways to scale compute saturate: larger batches and data-parallel gradient averaging draw every trajectory from one, possibly biased, policy, so extra rollouts rediscover known modes instead of finding new ones. We explore whether this mode-bias problem (mode collapse in the extreme) can be addressed with a population of asynchronously trained policies which divide the state space between them. Mixture of GFlowNets (MoG) replaces the single forward policy with a community of $K$ independent GFlowNets coupled through one jointly trained soft classifier, which assigns each member its own region of the state space through reward shaping. Mixing the members under their learned partition functions provably recovers the target $p(x)\propto R(x)$. MoG exchange (MoGX) also lets the classifier route sampled trajectories: a trajectory the classifier assigns to another member is sent to that member and trained on there, with no importance sampling. We evaluate both methods by keeping the environment-interaction budget fixed while scaling the community size, turning parallel compute into mode coverage without extra oracle calls. On HyperGrid, across six reward landscapes and communities of up to $K{=}64$, MoG and MoGX keep finding new modes as $K$ grows, while data-parallel training saturates. On a genomic ideotype-design task, MoGX covers $39%$ of the $1024$ optima at $K{=}64$, against $31\%$ for independent agents and $20\%$ for data-parallel training. MoG also has a lower per-iteration synchronization cost than data-parallel training.
papers.ja_title: 複数の GFlowNet を並列に動かしてモード抜け漏れを防ぐ Mixture of GFlowNets
papers.summary: GFlowNet は報酬に比例した割合で多様な候補を生成する手法だが、単体では複雑な分布の一部のモード (峰) を見逃しやすく、バッチを増やしたりデータ並列で勾配を平均しても同じ偏った方針から軌跡を引くだけで新しいモードが見つからないという困りごとがある。Mixture of GFlowNets (MoG) は K 個の独立した GFlowNet を、共同学習するソフト分類器で状態空間を分担させながら非同期に学習させ、分担を踏まえて混合すれば元の目標分布に一致することを示した。MoGX という交換版では分類器が軌跡を担当者に振り分ける。ゲノムの設計課題で K=64 のとき、MoGX は 1024 個の最適解の 39% を見つけ、独立エージェント (31%) やデータ並列学習 (20%) を上回った。
papers.why: 同じ計算資源でも方針を分担して並列化すれば探索の多様性が上がるという、分散学習の並列化戦略への具体的な示唆がある。
papers.summary_en: GFlowNets sample compositional objects proportional to reward, but a single policy often fails to cover all modes, and naive scaling via larger batches or data-parallel gradient averaging just rediscovers known modes from one possibly biased policy. Mixture of GFlowNets (MoG) replaces the single policy with K independently trained GFlowNets that partition the state space via a jointly trained soft classifier, provably recovering the target distribution when mixed under their learned partition functions; MoGX additionally lets the classifier route trajectories to the responsible member with no importance sampling. On a genomic ideotype-design task with K=64, MoGX covers 39% of 1024 optima versus 31% for independent agents and 20% for data-parallel training, while incurring lower per-iteration synchronization cost than data-parallel training.
papers.why_en: It demonstrates a concrete parallelization strategy—partitioning the search space across asynchronously trained policies—that converts extra parallel compute into better mode coverage rather than redundant sampling, relevant to distributed training design.

papers.title: In-context classification: Calibration and noise in linear attention with softmax readout
papers.abstract: We study in-context binary classification in a simple attention model trained to minimise a logistic loss. Each prompt has a latent logistic teacher, and the learner must infer its direction from Bernoulli-labeled context examples. We derive an asymptotic prediction for the test logit in a high-dimensional regime with context length proportional to token dimension, and total training prompts proportional to dimension squared. Our formula cleanly separates calibration, test-time context noise, and non-isotropic parameter-estimation noise as interpretable effects on in-context performance. Our analysis also identifies the ridgeless separability regime and addresses the effects of context length, pretraining-set size, regularisation, and sampling temperature on in-context classification performance. The theory's predictions closely agree with finite-dimensional simulations and fully trained linear-attention models, while experiments with standard softmax attention show qualitatively related behaviour beyond the regime assumed by our analysis.
papers.ja_title: 文脈内学習における線形注意の予測を理論式で分解
papers.summary: プロンプトごとに隠れた分類境界 (教師) があり、学習者は文脈中の例から向きを推測する二値分類タスクで、線形注意モデルの訓練後の予測 (ロジット) を高次元の漸近理論で求めた研究。この式は、予測の自信の正しさ (キャリブレーション)、テスト時の文脈ノイズ、学習パラメータの非等方なノイズという 3 つの要因をはっきり分けて説明する。文脈の長さや事前学習データ量、正則化、サンプリング温度が性能にどう影響するかも明らかにし、有限次元の実験や通常のソフトマックス注意でも理論と似た傾向が見られることを確認した。
papers.why: 文脈内学習の性能を支配する要因を数式で分解でき、モデル構造設計やハイパーパラメータ選択の指針になる。
papers.summary_en: The paper studies in-context binary classification in a simple attention model trained with logistic loss, deriving an asymptotic prediction for the test logit in a high-dimensional regime where context length and training-prompt count scale with token dimension and its square. The formula cleanly separates calibration, test-time context noise, and non-isotropic parameter-estimation noise, and characterizes how context length, pretraining-set size, regularization, and sampling temperature affect in-context classification performance; predictions closely match finite-dimensional simulations and fully trained linear-attention models, with standard softmax attention showing qualitatively related behavior beyond the assumed regime.
papers.why_en: It decomposes the drivers of in-context learning performance into interpretable terms, offering theoretical guidance for architecture and hyperparameter choices related to attention-based in-context learning.

papers.title: LocalTrain: Integer-Only Local Learning for Energy-Efficient CNN Training on Edge FPGAs
papers.abstract: Local learning reduces cross-layer training dependencies, but an efficient accelerator must still retain operands, accumulate gradients, and select quantization scales. We present an FPGA system that trains a CNN and its regional auxiliary classifiers using a shared integer matrix engine. Compact errors are expanded on chip, gradients are folded tile by tile, and historical scales permit direct output conversion. At 200 MHz, the KV260 prototype achieves 76.57% accuracy on CIFAR-10 and 91.85% on SVHN at approximately 4.20 W mean module power. Effective matrix throughput is 31.22 and 31.57 GMAC/s, respectively. Against the same integer method on Jetson Orin Nano, measured training energy is 40.4% and 42.1% lower, with $1.86\times$ and $1.82\times$ longer runtime; measurements use the respective platform power domains. Selected state checks and matching complete-run prediction counts support functional agreement with the software reference.
papers.ja_title: エッジ FPGA 上で整数演算だけで CNN を省エネに学習する LocalTrain
papers.summary: 層ごとの依存を減らす局所学習は効率的だが、実際のアクセラレータはオペランドの保持・勾配の蓄積・量子化スケールの選択をきちんとやる必要があるという困りごとがある。LocalTrain は共有の整数行列演算器で CNN と補助分類器を学習し、誤差をオンチップで展開し、勾配をタイルごとに畳み込み、過去のスケールから直接出力変換する FPGA システムを作った。KV260 ボードで 200MHz 動作時に CIFAR-10 で 76.57%、SVHN で 91.85% の精度を、平均 4.20W で達成し、同じ整数手法を使う Jetson Orin Nano と比べて学習エネルギーを 40.4%、42.1% 削減した (実行時間は 1.86 倍、1.82 倍に伸びる)。
papers.why: 整数演算のみでの局所学習をFPGA上に実装する設計の具体例を示し、エッジでの省エネ学習ハードウェア設計の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Local learning reduces cross-layer training dependencies, but an efficient accelerator must still retain operands, accumulate gradients, and select quantization scales correctly. LocalTrain is an FPGA system that trains a CNN and its regional auxiliary classifiers on a shared integer matrix engine, expanding compact errors on-chip, folding gradients tile by tile, and using historical scales for direct output conversion. At 200 MHz on a KV260 board it reaches 76.57% accuracy on CIFAR-10 and 91.85% on SVHN at about 4.20 W mean power, and compared with the same integer method on Jetson Orin Nano, measured training energy is 40.4% and 42.1% lower (at 1.86x and 1.82x longer runtime).
papers.why_en: It provides a concrete integer-only local-learning accelerator design on FPGA, informative for energy-efficient edge training hardware design.

papers.title: DuoDiscover: Scaling Autonomous Discovery Beyond the Evaluation Bottleneck
papers.abstract: Evaluation has been central to advances in AI, and it is equally critical to autonomous discovery. Yet scaling autonomous discovery to real-world engineering challenges faces a fundamental bottleneck: the cost of evaluating progress. In real settings, a single true evaluation, such as a full benchmark or serving trace, can take hours, so a search can afford only a handful of true evaluations. We present DuoDiscover, a search system that jointly discovers what to optimize and how to evaluate progress efficiently, through three mechanisms. First, each worker in a fleet of coding agents co-discovers an optimization target and a fast, tailored proxy evaluator, which we call a yardstick. The agent then hill-climbs the yardstick rather than the true evaluation. Second, since search can exploit gaps between a yardstick and the true objective, fidelity tests continually recheck each yardstick's ranking and invalidate any that drift. Third, the fleet is bottom-up, with no central decomposition of the problem. A lightweight orchestrator spawns and terminates agents, briefs running ones, and seeds new agents with others' confirmed work. DuoDiscover enables autonomous optimization from software to chip architecture. We demonstrate DuoDiscover on two repository-level benchmarks and four GPU and TPU kernel suites covering hundreds of kernels. On SWE-fficiency, it doubles the average speedup of human experts. On SOL-Exec, it ranks first on 121 of 235 kernels and in the top three on 212. On the heavily optimized vLLM and SQLite engines, DuoDiscover achieves 1.92$\times$ and 1.38$\times$ gains over the base code. On a CPU microarchitecture optimization task with evaluations of up to 28 hours, DuoDiscover surpasses both AlphaEvolve-based ArchAgent v2 and the best human design, with 1.65$\times$ ArchAgent v2's gain in 16.7 days versus more than 40 days, advancing the frontier of autonomous chip design.
papers.ja_title: 評価コストがボトルネックの自動探索を「物差し」で突破する DuoDiscover
papers.summary: 本物の評価 (フルベンチマークやサービングトレースなど) に何時間もかかるため、自律探索は探索予算の中でごく少数しか真の評価を行えないという困りごとがある。DuoDiscover は、コーディングエージェントの集団それぞれが最適化対象と、本物の評価に近い速い代用評価指標 (ヤードスティック) を同時に見つけ、ヤードスティックを登る一方、ヤードスティックと本物の評価のズレを定期的に検査して信頼できなくなったものは無効化する。中央で問題を分割しない下から上の構成で、軽量な司令塔がエージェントの起動・終了・引き継ぎを行う。SWE-fficiency では人間の専門家の平均高速化の 2 倍、SOL-Exec の 235 カーネルのうち 121 個で 1 位、vLLM と SQLite ではベースコードから 1.92 倍と 1.38 倍の性能向上を達成し、CPU のマイクロアーキテクチャ最適化では 28 時間かかる評価を使っても AlphaEvolve ベースの ArchAgent v2 やベスト人間設計を上回り、16.7 日で ArchAgent v2 の成果の 1.65 倍に達した (ArchAgent v2 は 40 日超)。
