papers.why: 真の評価が高コストな探索問題で、代用指標の信頼性を継続検査しながら自動最適化を進める仕組みは、カーネル最適化やサービング性能チューニングの自動化に直結する。
papers.summary_en: Real evaluations (a full benchmark or serving trace) can take hours, so autonomous discovery can only afford a handful of true evaluations within a search budget. DuoDiscover has each worker in a fleet of coding agents co-discover an optimization target together with a fast, tailored proxy evaluator ("yardstick"), hill-climb that yardstick, and continually run fidelity tests that recheck each yardstick's ranking and invalidate any that drift, all coordinated bottom-up by a lightweight orchestrator with no central problem decomposition. On SWE-fficiency it doubles the average speedup of human experts; on SOL-Exec it ranks first on 121 of 235 kernels; on heavily optimized vLLM and SQLite it achieves 1.92x and 1.38x gains; and on a CPU microarchitecture task with evaluations up to 28 hours, it surpasses AlphaEvolve-based ArchAgent v2 and the best human design, reaching 1.65x of ArchAgent v2's gain in 16.7 days versus more than 40 days.
papers.why_en: For search problems where true evaluation is costly, the pattern of continually auditing a fast proxy evaluator against the true costly evaluation and invalidating it when it drifts is directly applicable to automating kernel and serving performance tuning.

papers.title: FreeSolo: Linear-time Sparse Attention with Zero-Shot Length Extrapolation
papers.abstract: Linear-time sequence models typically store long-context information in a recurrent state. A fixed-size state limits how much information can be stored, while hybrid architectures that add full attention for better recall incur quadratic sequence cost. Alternatively, sparse attention with continued pretraining (CPT) can extend the effective context length. Generalization beyond the trained length remains challenging, however, and CPT can be costly. We introduce FreeSolo, a native sparse attention mechanism with a short-range sliding window branch and a long-range branch that selects keypoint cells for direct token attention. Its linear-time variant, FS-L, learns to prune the prefix before query-dependent selection through short CPT. FS-B searches balanced trees with $O(N\log^2 N)$ algorithmic cost including radix-sort construction. FreeSolo demonstrates better zero-shot length extrapolation than the baselines without long-context fine-tuning.
papers.ja_title: 線形時間で疎な注意を使い未学習の長さにも一般化する FreeSolo
papers.summary: 線形時間の系列モデルは長い文脈の情報を固定サイズの状態に詰め込むため情報量に限界があり、全注意を混ぜたハイブリッド構造は再現性を上げても計算量が二乗になる。疎な注意を使い続けて事前学習する方法は文脈長を伸ばせるが、訓練した長さを超えた一般化は難しく、追加の事前学習は高コストという困りごとがある。FreeSolo は短距離をスライディングウィンドウで、長距離は要点となるセル (キーポイントセル) を選んで直接トークン注意する二本立ての疎な注意機構を導入し、短い追加学習だけで、長い文脈の微調整を行った既存手法より優れた未学習長さへの一般化を示した。
papers.why: 長文脈処理での状態容量の限界とハイブリッド構造の二乗コストという両方の問題を、疎な注意設計で同時に扱う一つのモデル構造の提案。
papers.summary_en: Linear-time sequence models store long-context information in a fixed-size recurrent state, limiting capacity, while hybrid architectures adding full attention for better recall incur quadratic cost; sparse attention with continued pretraining (CPT) can extend effective context length but generalizing beyond the trained length remains hard and CPT can be costly. FreeSolo introduces a native sparse attention mechanism combining a short-range sliding-window branch with a long-range branch that selects keypoint cells for direct token attention, with a linear-time variant (FS-L) learning to prune the prefix via short CPT and a balanced-tree variant (FS-B) with O(N log^2 N) cost; it demonstrates better zero-shot length extrapolation than baselines without long-context fine-tuning.
papers.why_en: It offers a model architecture that addresses both the fixed-state capacity limit of linear-time models and the quadratic cost of hybrid full-attention designs via a sparse attention mechanism.

papers.title: Releasing the Inner Jev: A Simple Recipe for Open Decision Models
papers.abstract: LLM-based decision-making systems, also called System One models, have recently gained popularity, most notably through Jev (Almeida, 2026). Given a typed input state, a question, and a set of options, they return a probability for each option in a single forward pass, without text generation. We show that existing open instruction-tuned language models can achieve comparable performance \textit{without any additional training}, by reading out answers from letters (A, B, C, etc.) in the model's output logits at the last token position. Furthermore, we show how a simple supervised fine-tuning recipe can improve their performance further. We evaluate four open instruction-tuned language models: Gemma 4 31B, Gemma 4 12B, Qwen3.6-27B, and Qwen3.5-4B. We fine-tune each using LoRA and a decision head initialized from a slice of the language model head. Furthermore, we introduce OpenDecisions, a novel 2,352-question validation dataset designed to reflect the task composition of JevBench (JevBench main- tainers, 2026) and which computes a Capability score based on accuracy and calibration metrics. Without fine-tuning, Gemma 4 31B scores 79.6 on OpenDecisions, compared to Jev's 80.1. After undergoing our fine-tuning recipe, it scores 84.4 on OpenDecisions and 81.5 on JevBench v1.7, outperforming Jev by 4.3 and 4.4 Capability points respectively and setting a new state-of-the-art on OpenDecisions. On a suite of public decision datasets, our models achieve accuracy comparable to Jev, with lower calibration error. Our results show that open language models already possess System One capabilities, and with simple fine-tuning they outperform Jev on a wide range of decision tasks. We release our models, serving code, and OpenDecisions.
papers.ja_title: ロジット読み取りだけで動く意思決定モデル:オープン LLM で Jev を超える
papers.summary: Jev という閉じた意思決定モデル(選択肢ごとに確率を一発で出す System One モデル)に対し、既存のオープンな指示チューニング済み LLM (大規模言語モデル) から追加学習なしで同等の性能を再現できることを示した。さらに LoRA (低ランク適応) による簡単な微調整を加えると、Gemma 4 31B は独自ベンチマーク OpenDecisions で 79.6 から 84.4 に向上し、JevBench v1.7 では Jev を 4.3〜4.4 ポイント上回った。著者らはモデルとサービングコード、新データセット OpenDecisions を公開した。
papers.why: オープンモデルでも追加学習なしで専用の意思決定システムに匹敵・超えられることを示し、推論コストを抑えた意思決定サービングの選択肢を広げる。
papers.summary_en: Against Jev, a closed "System One" decision model that outputs per-option probabilities in a single forward pass, the authors show open instruction-tuned LLMs can match its performance without any additional training by reading answer letters from output logits. With a simple LoRA fine-tuning recipe, Gemma 4 31B rises from 79.6 to 84.4 on their new OpenDecisions benchmark and outperforms Jev by 4.3-4.4 Capability points on OpenDecisions and JevBench v1.7 respectively. They release the models, serving code, and the OpenDecisions dataset.
papers.why_en: It shows open LLMs already have "System One" decision capability and can surpass a closed specialized model with lightweight fine-tuning, widening low-cost serving options for decision-making systems.

papers.title: Compute-optimal data scaling for neural surrogates via multi-fidelity training
papers.abstract: Neural surrogates for Partial Differential Equations (PDEs) are usually trained on synthetic data from numerical simulators. As models grow and scaling laws demand larger datasets, the cost of data generation often outweighs the training cost and becomes the bottleneck in the scaling quest. Unlike data in other domains, however, each PDE sample has a tunable cost that depends on its numerical fidelity, with the resulting cost-accuracy trade-off governed by known convergence rates. We exploit this property by formalizing neural surrogate training as a function of both data quantity and fidelity under a fixed data generation compute budget, treating fidelity as a fine-grained discrete spectrum rather than a binary distinction. Building on this, we show that multi-fidelity training enables Pareto-optimal error scaling against data generation compute. By using simulations at lower fidelities as an additional training signal, training on the optimal fidelity mixture matches the accuracy of high-fidelity-only training, with up to $6.3\times$ less data generation compute across our settings. We validate these findings across six PDE problems spanning structured grids and unstructured meshes, two distinct error sources (discretization and iterative-solver error), and four surrogate architectures, totaling over 7,000 training runs.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: PDE 代理モデル学習、精度を落としたデータも使えば生成コストを最大 6.3 倍節約
papers.summary: 偏微分方程式 (PDE) の数値計算を模倣するニューラル代理モデルは、学習データを数値シミュレータで作る必要があり、そのデータ生成コストが学習全体のボトルネックになっている。この研究は、シミュレーションの精度(フィデリティ)を細かく変えられる点を利用し、精度と量の配分を最適化する学習法を提案した。6 種類の PDE 問題・7000 件以上の学習実験で、低精度データを混ぜた最適配分は高精度データのみの学習と同じ精度を、データ生成計算量を最大 6.3 倍少なく達成した。
papers.why: データ生成コストが支配的な科学計算系モデルの学習効率化に、精度と量のトレードオフを使った計算予算配分という新しい視点を与える。
papers.summary_en: Neural surrogates for PDEs are trained on simulator-generated data whose generation cost, not training cost, becomes the bottleneck as data demands grow. By treating simulation fidelity as a tunable, fine-grained cost-accuracy knob, the authors show multi-fidelity training achieves Pareto-optimal error scaling against data-generation compute, matching high-fidelity-only accuracy with up to 6.3x less data generation compute, validated across six PDE problems and over 7,000 training runs.
papers.why_en: It offers a new compute-budget allocation perspective—trading data fidelity for quantity—for efficiently training scientific surrogate models where data generation, not training, dominates cost.

papers.title: Which Geometry on Which Layer? Measured Sign-Spectral Assignment in Mixed-Optimizer Training
papers.abstract: Modern neural-network training uses mixed recipes, assigning AdamW-like or sign-based updates to embedding and output layers and spectral updates to hidden matrices. These assignments are usually fixed by layer type, without a clear criterion for selecting the appropriate geometry. We turn sign-versus-spectral assignment into a measurable, layerwise decision problem. For ideal memoryless steps, we derive a finite-batch ratio of conservative descent-lemma lower bounds for spectral and sign updates. Its closed form separates signal efficiency from a geometry-dependent global curvature factor. In the positive-signal regime, the same smoothness assumption gives two-sided bounds that determine which step has the larger conditional expected decrease when the ratio crosses explicit noise-dependent thresholds. We then derive a local directional quadratic score from gradient alignments and Hessian-vector products and use it in Generalized-Scion (G-Scion) to control layerwise routing. In a controlled input-rank experiment, including directional curvature matches the measured same-iterate ordering in all seven aggregate settings, whereas the curvature-free proxy selects the opposite geometry. On 31M GPT-2, the output score routes the output layer from spectral warmup to sign, and G-Scion improves validation loss over fixed Scion in memoryless and matched-momentum comparisons. ViT-B/16 results further show that a spectral edge assignment can outperform fixed Scion outside language modelling. These results suggest that optimizer geometry need not be hard-coded by layer type and are a first step toward understanding how it should be assigned.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 層ごとに最適な更新則を選ぶ:符号法とスペクトル法の切り替えを測って決める
papers.summary: ニューラルネット学習では埋め込み層や出力層に符号ベース (sign) の更新、隠れ層にスペクトル更新を使う配合が経験的に固定されてきたが、どちらを選ぶべきかの明確な基準がなかった。この研究は、有限バッチでの降下量の下限比から、どちらの更新がより損失を減らすかを判定する指標を導き、勾配方向とヘッセ行列を使った局所的な曲率スコアで層ごとの切り替え (ルーティング) を行う G-Scion を提案した。31M パラメータの GPT-2 では出力層をスペクトルから符号へ自動で切り替え、固定配合の Scion よりも検証損失を改善し、ViT-B/16 でも固定配合を上回る場合があることを確認した。
papers.why: 最適化器の幾何(更新方向の選び方)を層種別で決め打ちせず測定で決めるという考え方を示し、学習効率を上げる新しい設計指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Mixed training recipes typically hard-code sign-based updates for embedding/output layers and spectral updates for hidden layers, with no clear criterion for the choice. The authors derive a measurable, finite-batch descent-lemma ratio that determines which update geometry yields a larger expected loss decrease, and use a local curvature score to drive layerwise routing in Generalized-Scion (G-Scion). On 31M-parameter GPT-2, G-Scion automatically routes the output layer from spectral to sign updates and improves validation loss over fixed Scion, with similar gains observed on ViT-B/16.
papers.why_en: It suggests optimizer geometry need not be fixed by layer type but can be assigned based on measurement, offering a new design principle for training efficiency.

papers.title: GPU Goldmines: Tunable WebGPU Kernels for Edge LLM Inference
papers.abstract: As demand for LLM inference grows and consumer GPUs grow more capable, edge deployment is becoming increasingly attractive. WebGPU is compelling in this setting because it offers cross-platform portability and browser accessibility. However, these same strengths also make high performance difficult to achieve, as an implementation that performs well in one context may not perform well in another. To address this, we present GPU Goldmines, a framework for specifying, executing, and tuning WebGPU kernels. We instantiate GPU Goldmines with kernels for key LLM building blocks: matrix multiplication, matrix-vector multiplication, and flash attention. We characterize performance across diverse devices, shapes, and browsers, and use the resulting database to accelerate subsequent autotuning and configuration selection. On shapes drawn from Llama and Qwen models, our matrix multiplication kernels outperform ONNX Runtime and llama.cpp WebGPU kernels by 7.0x and 1.41x geometric mean, respectively, and deliver end-to-end improvements of 1.48x in the prefill stage of llama.cpp for chat workloads.
papers.ja_title: ブラウザでも速い LLM 推論:チューニング可能な WebGPU カーネル集 GPU Goldmines
papers.summary: ブラウザで動く WebGPU はどの端末でも動く利点があるが、環境によって速いカーネル実装が変わるため高性能を出しにくい。この研究は行列積・行列ベクトル積・フラッシュアテンションなど LLM (大規模言語モデル) の基本演算について、様々な端末・形状・ブラウザで性能を計測し、その結果を使って自動チューニングを加速するフレームワーク GPU Goldmines を作った。Llama や Qwen の演算形状で、行列積カーネルは ONNX Runtime より幾何平均 7.0 倍、llama.cpp の WebGPU カーネルより 1.41 倍速く、チャット用途の prefill 段階全体では 1.48 倍の高速化を達成した。
papers.why: ブラウザ上のエッジ LLM 推論を高速化する、端末差を測って活用するカーネル自動チューニングの実例として、サービング実装の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: WebGPU offers cross-platform portability for browser-based LLM inference, but achieving high performance is hard because the best kernel implementation varies by device and browser. GPU Goldmines characterizes performance of core LLM kernels (matmul, matrix-vector multiply, flash attention) across devices, shapes, and browsers, and uses this database to accelerate autotuning. On shapes from Llama and Qwen models, its matmul kernels beat ONNX Runtime by 7.0x and llama.cpp's WebGPU kernels by 1.41x geometric mean, yielding a 1.48x end-to-end speedup in llama.cpp's prefill stage for chat workloads.
papers.why_en: It provides a concrete, measurement-driven kernel autotuning approach for accelerating browser-based edge LLM inference, useful as a reference for serving implementations.

papers.title: When Goals Leak Across Relationships: How Cached Goal Representations Shape Cross-Client Decisions
papers.abstract: As LLM agents take on more autonomous roles, they may interact with multiple clients and counterparties whose goals and incentives conflict. If an agent maintains shared inference state across these interactions, information associated with one relationship may influence decisions made for another. We test OLMo-3-7B-Instruct in a controlled two-client environment with 20 market scenarios, where each client is assigned an opposing objective. With shared conversational memory, the model deviates from the current client's objective in 22% of eligible decisions. We then investigate how these goals are represented in the KV cache. Linear probes show that client-goal ownership becomes highly recoverable in middle layers and is concentrated in particular attention heads. We use these results to identify where to intervene in the cache and test whether these representations affect the model's decisions. Ablating the competitor's cached goal representations at these locations shifts the model toward the current client. The effect is larger for heads identified by probing than for randomly selected heads, and larger when ablating goal tokens than matched non-goal tokens from the same client. Our results show that client-specific goal representations persist in the KV cache and can causally influence decisions made for other clients, highlighting the importance of relationship-specific state isolation in persistent LLM agents.
papers.ja_title: 複数クライアントの目標が KV キャッシュで混ざる:LLM エージェントの情報漏えいリスク
papers.summary: LLM エージェントが複数の利益相反するクライアントとやり取りするとき、会話の推論状態 (KV キャッシュ) を共有していると、一方のクライアント向けの情報がもう一方の判断に漏れ込む恐れがある。OLMo-3-7B-Instruct を使った 20 件の市場シナリオ実験で、共有メモリがあると現在のクライアントの目標から外れた判断を 22% のケースで行うことが分かった。さらに線形プローブで KV キャッシュの中間層に目標の所有者情報が強く現れることを示し、特定のアテンションヘッドでその目標表現を消す (アブレーション) と、現在のクライアント向けの判断に戻ることを確認した。
papers.why: 永続的な状態を持つ LLM エージェントでは関係ごとの状態分離が必要であることを、KV キャッシュへの因果的な介入実験で裏付けており、エージェントのサービング設計・セキュリティレビューに関わる。
papers.summary_en: When LLM agents interact with multiple clients whose goals conflict, sharing inference state (the KV cache) across conversations can let information from one relationship leak into decisions for another. Testing OLMo-3-7B-Instruct on 20 market scenarios with two clients holding opposing objectives, the authors find the model deviates from the current client's objective in 22% of eligible decisions when memory is shared. Linear probes show client-goal ownership becomes highly recoverable in middle layers and concentrated in specific attention heads, and ablating the competitor's cached goal representations there causally shifts the model back toward the current client.
papers.why_en: It provides a causal-intervention demonstration that relationship-specific state isolation matters for persistent LLM agents, relevant to serving design and security review of agent systems with shared KV caches.

review.note: 共有状態 (KV キャッシュなど) を持つエージェントを見るとき、プローブとアブレーションで情報漏えいの因果性を検証するという観点。
review.note_en: A review angle for agents with shared state (e.g., the KV cache): verify causal information leakage using probing plus targeted ablation, not just correlation.

papers.title: HarnessTTT: Learn to Optimize Harness at Test-Time for Scientific Discovery
papers.abstract: Scientific discovery with language models requires finding the best valid solution within a finite computational budget. We study how feedback from this search can improve the procedure used to conduct it. We introduce HarnessTTT, a test-time learning framework that trains a harness proposer while keeping the executor frozen. The proposer generates executable harnesses comprising system prompts, reusable skills, tools, middleware, and execution controls. Each harness guides a budgeted discovery rollout, whose outcome provides feedback for updating the proposer. A discovery-oriented policy-gradient objective combines gap-normalized rewards, leave-one-out advantages (RLOO), and max-sharpening to favor high-performing proposals. Generated components are validated before execution, and the search retains the best valid solution and selected harnesses across rounds. Across fourteen discovery tasks in mathematics, systems, GPU kernels, heuristic programming, astrodynamics, and biology, HarnessTTT with a frozen 9B executor improves on OpenEvolve with the same executor on all eleven benchmark tasks (e.g., from 1.17 to 2.64 on circle packing), improves on the discovery-fine-tuned Finch-9B by up to 92%, holds the best open-weight sub-10B result on nine, and reaches 0.380919 on Erdős minimum overlap, better than the best human reference of 0.380927. Scaling the proposer and frozen executor to 27B improves on eleven of fourteen tasks, and transferring the learned harnesses to GPT-5.5 matches or exceeds the strongest reported system of any backbone on nine of fourteen tasks. Together, these results show that harness search can itself be learned at test time: a trained proposer lets a small frozen executor search effectively, and the harnesses it finds carry over to stronger executors.
papers.ja_title: ハーネス自体を学習する:科学探索のための試行手順を鍛える HarnessTTT
papers.summary: 言語モデルを使った科学的発見は、限られた計算予算の中で最良の解を探す作業だが、その探索の「やり方」自体を改善する方法は未開拓だった。この研究は実行役のモデルを固定したまま、システムプロンプトやツール・制御手順などの「ハーネス」を提案する側だけをテスト時に強化学習 (方策勾配) で鍛える HarnessTTT を提案した。数学・システム・GPU カーネル・天体力学・生物学など 14 の探索課題で、同じ実行役を使う既存手法 OpenEvolve を 11 課題すべてで上回り (円充填問題では 1.17 から 2.64 に改善)、提案役と実行役を 27B に拡大すると 14 課題中 11 課題で改善し、学習したハーネスを GPT-5.5 に移植しても 14 課題中 9 課題で最強の報告結果と同等以上だった。
papers.why: 実行モデルを固定したまま探索手順(プロンプト・ツール構成)をテスト時学習で鍛えるという発想は、RL 後学習や推論時探索の設計に新しい自由度を与える。
papers.summary_en: Scientific discovery with language models means finding the best valid solution within a finite compute budget, but improving the search procedure itself has been largely unexplored. HarnessTTT trains a harness proposer—generating system prompts, tools, and execution controls—via test-time policy-gradient learning while keeping the executor frozen. Across fourteen discovery tasks, a frozen 9B executor guided by HarnessTTT beats OpenEvolve with the same executor on all eleven benchmark tasks (e.g., 1.17 to 2.64 on circle packing), scaling to 27B improves eleven of fourteen tasks, and the learned harnesses transfer to GPT-5.5, matching or exceeding the strongest reported system on nine of fourteen tasks.
papers.why_en: Training the search harness itself at test time, rather than the executor, gives a new lever for designing RL post-training and inference-time search systems with small frozen models.

papers.title: FlashVSR+: Efficient Video Super-Resolution via Hybrid Attention and Reward-Yield Distribution Matching
papers.abstract: Recent video super-resolution (VSR) models achieve efficient one-step generation through diffusion distillation. However, high-resolution inference remains costly, and distilled models are difficult to align with human preferences. These challenges call for improvements in both model architecture and training strategy. We present \textbf{FlashVSR+} to address both limitations. On the architecture side, we introduce hybrid attention based on the strong locality observed in pretrained VSR models, while retaining sparse global interaction for long-range consistency. It achieves up to $2\times$ DiT speedup and 45\% lower peak memory, enabling spatially untiled 4K VSR on a single 24GB RTX 4090. On the training side, we propose Reward-Yield Distribution Matching Distillation (Ry-DMD) for preference-aligned one-step generation. Ry-DMD uses reward-weighted teacher rollouts to incorporate black-box rewards into distribution matching, without backpropagating through the reward model. We further show that Ry-DMD generalizes beyond VSR to T2I generation. Together, FlashVSR+ delivers stronger restoration quality and substantially improves high-resolution efficiency, with consistent gains in user preference. We release our code, models, and training data at \href{https://www.flashvsr.tech}{\textcolor{FlashBlue}{\textbf{www.flashvsr.tech}}}.
papers.ja_title: FlashVSR+:ハイブリッドアテンションと報酬整合蒸留で高速・高画質な動画超解像
papers.summary: 動画の超解像(低解像度動画を高画質化する技術)を一歩で生成する拡散蒸留モデルは、高解像度での推論コストが高く、人間の好みに合わせにくいという課題がある。この研究はローカルな注意の強さに着目したハイブリッドアテンション構造で DiT (拡散トランスフォーマー) を最大 2 倍高速化・メモリ 45% 削減し、24GB の RTX 4090 1 枚で非タイル分割の 4K 超解像を可能にした。さらに報酬モデルへの逆伝播なしで好みを反映できる蒸留手法 Ry-DMD を提案し、画質と速度、好みのすべてで改善を示した。
papers.why: 一段階生成モデルの高速化と好み整合の両方を、既存の報酬逆伝播を避けた蒸留手法で同時に実現しており、効率的な生成モデルの構造設計に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: One-step diffusion-distilled video super-resolution (VSR) models are costly at high resolution and hard to align with human preferences. FlashVSR+ introduces a hybrid attention architecture exploiting the strong locality observed in pretrained VSR models while retaining sparse global interaction, achieving up to 2x DiT speedup and 45% lower peak memory, enabling untiled 4K VSR on a single 24GB RTX 4090. It also proposes Ry-DMD, a reward-weighted distribution-matching distillation that incorporates preferences without backpropagating through the reward model, improving restoration quality, efficiency, and user preference together, and generalizing to T2I generation.
papers.why_en: It jointly tackles speed and preference-alignment for one-step generative models via an efficient architecture and a backprop-free reward distillation method, offering a reference design for efficient generative model structures.

papers.title: Revisiting the 16x Pretraining Compute Gap between Diffusion and Autoregressive Language Models
papers.abstract: Diffusion language models (DLMs) have attracted wide attention for their fast, parallel decoding, but they are believed to be far less efficient to train than autoregressive language models (ARMs): a widely cited study reports that a DLM needs roughly 16x the training compute of an ARM to match its likelihood, a figure that has made pretraining DLMs from scratch look prohibitive at scale. We find that the methodology behind this figure has fallen out of step with current DLM practice: it scores the model with its evidence lower bound (ELBO) and trains a full-sequence, decoder-only model. We therefore revisit the scaling laws of DLMs, adopting the exact likelihood under the model's own decoding order, block diffusion training, an encoder-decoder architecture, and a sweep over the block sizes used in practice. Under this new protocol, we study across ten model variants, about 1,700 models in total, and find that pretraining DLMs is far cheaper than previously thought. Concretely, scoring with the exact likelihood reduces the compute multiple to 12.8x; block diffusion training and an encoder-decoder architecture further reduce it to 7.8x at block size 32, and smaller block sizes narrow it to 4.6x at block size 8 and 3.0x at block size 4. We complement these scaling analyses with an empirical rule for the optimal decoder depth of encoder-decoder block diffusion, a held-out compute budget beyond the fitting range at which the gap between variants persists, and downstream benchmark results where likelihood improvements carry over to accuracy. Overall, the 16x figure substantially overstates the pretraining cost gap between DLMs and ARMs, and pretraining DLMs from scratch is far more viable than previously assumed.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 拡散言語モデルは本当に 16 倍非効率か?測り方を見直すと差は 3 倍まで縮む
papers.summary: 拡散言語モデル (DLM) は自己回帰モデル (ARM) に比べて学習計算量が 16 倍も必要という広く引用された数字があり、これが DLM をゼロから事前学習することを非現実的に見せてきた。この研究はその測定方法(下限 ELBO での評価・全列デコーダのみ構成)が今の DLM の実践とずれていることを指摘し、モデル自身のデコード順での厳密な対数尤度評価、ブロック拡散学習、エンコーダ・デコーダ構成、ブロックサイズの調整を導入して約 1700 モデルで再検証した。その結果、計算量の差は厳密尤度評価だけで 12.8 倍に、ブロック拡散とエンコーダ・デコーダ構成でブロックサイズ 32 なら 7.8 倍、さらに小さいブロックサイズ 8 で 4.6 倍、4 で 3.0 倍まで縮まり、下流タスクの精度にも尤度改善が反映されることを確認した。
papers.why: 広く引用されてきた性能比較の数字が測定方法のズレによって過大評価されていたことを、大規模な再実験で示しており、スケーリング則の主張を検証する際の測り方そのものを問う好例。
papers.summary_en: Diffusion language models (DLMs) are widely believed to need roughly 16x the training compute of autoregressive models (ARMs) to match likelihood, a figure that has made pretraining DLMs from scratch look prohibitive. The authors show this methodology—scoring via the ELBO and training a full-sequence decoder-only model—is out of step with current DLM practice, and after adopting exact likelihood under the model's own decoding order, block diffusion training, an encoder-decoder architecture, and tuned block sizes, across roughly 1,700 models they find the compute multiple drops to 12.8x from exact likelihood alone, 7.8x at block size 32, 4.6x at block size 8, and 3.0x at block size 4, with likelihood gains carrying over to downstream accuracy.
papers.why_en: It shows a widely cited performance-gap figure was substantially overstated due to a mismatched evaluation methodology, a strong example of questioning how scaling-law claims are measured, through large-scale re-experimentation.

review.note: 以前の研究のベンチマーク手法(評価指標やアーキテクチャの前提)が今の実践とズレていないかを、大規模な再実験で検証するという研究の進め方。
review.note_en: A research approach of large-scale re-experimentation to check whether a prior study's evaluation methodology (metric choice, architectural assumptions) has drifted out of step with current practice.

papers.title: The Tokens Strike Back: Safety-Aware Denoising with Directional Embedding-based Revision
papers.abstract: The Safety-Aware Denoiser (SAD) is a recent, training-free, safety-guidance framework for text diffusion models. During inference, SAD steers text samples toward safe regions of the token probability space. In this paper, we propose $\mathit{SADDER}$ (Safety-Aware Denoising with Directional Embedding-based Revision), which improves the safety and quality trade-offs of SAD by exploiting a safety-guidance signal in the embedding (or activation) space for each token position, then updating the token positions using the SAD update rule multiplied by the guidance signal. This multiplication acts as a gating mechanism: tokens with a high unsafe signal are more likely to be modified during inference following the SAD update rule. However, such an update does not automatically preserve the conditional mean, i.e., the denoiser of a fixed target distribution. We therefore theoretically derive new position-wise target distributions for which the modified denoiser is exact. Furthermore, we derive conditions under which the position-wise target distributions match a global target distribution. We test our $\mathit{SADDER}$ method on popular Masked Diffusion Language Models (MDLMs) and Uniform-State Diffusion Models (USDMs) across unsafe continuation and jailbreak settings, and show that $\mathit{SADDER}$ achieves a better balance between safety, generation quality, and inference cost than existing methods.

papers.title: Mixed Precision Scaling Laws for Quantized Pretraining
papers.abstract: Since scaling laws were introduced for modern LLMs (Kaplan et al., 2020), several works have extended them to account for quantization, tracking the emerging low-precision data types supported on AI accelerators. We develop a more accurate scaling law for quantized pretraining with mixed precision across the forward and backward passes, grounded in optimization theory and validated empirically. Our formulation separates the effects of quantization on model capacity and on optimization efficiency, and explicitly models the persistent optimization error from forward and backward quantization identified through convergence analysis. To select the regimes for fitting and evaluating our law, we first decompose existing 4-bit training recipes into their forward and backward components, isolating those that most affect loss. Our Qwen3 experiments under selected 4-bit regimes, together with published Llama-style experiments, show that our law predicts loss with up to $11\times$ lower MSE than existing laws as model size and token count scale. Finally, we extend our law to layer-wise mixed precision and identify the optimal quantized-pretraining recipe, i.e., model size, training tokens, and per-layer forward/backward precision, under a hardware-aware compute budget. Unlike prior precision scaling laws, our law predicts that the optimal precision increases with the compute budget.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 量子化事前学習のための混合精度スケーリング則
papers.summary: 大規模言語モデルの量子化学習 (数値の精度を落として学習する手法) には、前向き・後ろ向き計算を混ぜた混合精度を正しく扱うスケーリング則が不足していた。この研究は、量子化がモデルの表現力と最適化の効率に与える影響を理論的に分け、Qwen3 の 4-bit 学習実験や公開されている Llama 系実験で検証した。その結果、既存のスケーリング則に比べ損失の予測誤差 (平均二乗誤差、MSE) を最大 11 倍小さくでき、計算予算が増えるほど最適な精度も上がることを示した。
papers.why: ハードウェア予算に応じた量子化精度や層ごとの精度配分を事前に設計する指針になり、低精度学習のレシピ最適化に直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Scaling laws for quantized pretraining previously failed to accurately capture mixed-precision effects across forward and backward passes. The authors develop a scaling law grounded in optimization theory that separates quantization's effect on model capacity from its effect on optimization efficiency, validated on selected Qwen3 4-bit regimes and published Llama-style experiments, achieving up to 11x lower MSE than existing laws as model size and token count scale. They further derive the optimal layer-wise mixed-precision recipe under a hardware-aware compute budget, finding that, unlike prior precision scaling laws, the optimal precision increases with compute budget.
papers.why_en: Gives a principled way to pick per-layer precision and quantized-pretraining recipes under a fixed hardware compute budget, directly useful for designing low-precision training.

papers.title: DisaggKD: Efficient Knowledge Distillation through Teacher-Student Disaggregation and a Fused Loss
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) frameworks place teacher and student on the same GPUs, so per-GPU memory limits the teachers that fit. DisaggKD separates them across nodes: teacher replicas stream hidden states to the student, a KD loss over row windows and vocabulary shards equals the full-vocabulary loss in exact arithmetic without forming the full-vocabulary logits, and a prefetch ring paces producer and trainer. Closed-form memory and traffic models locate the memory limits of each layout. On the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B to 9B pair, the disaggregated layout matches the LM loss of the colocated run with the same loss and is faster than that run; our fused loss also lets a colocated run train on as few nodes at faster speed, while the split is memory efficient when the student spans several nodes. On the larger pairs, colocated runs with a fused loss still run OOM where the split trains, because teacher weights and student states fill the budget.
papers.ja_title: 教師モデルと生徒モデルを別ノードに分けて行う省メモリな知識蒸留
papers.summary: 知識蒸留 (教師モデルの出力を使って小さい生徒モデルを学習する手法) は通常、教師と生徒を同じ GPU に置くため、GPU のメモリ容量が使える教師モデルの大きさを制限していた。DisaggKD は教師と生徒を別ノードに分け、教師から隠れ状態だけを送って、語彙全体のロジットを作らずに厳密に同じ値の損失を計算する仕組みを作った。Qwen3.5-35B-A3B から 9B への蒸留では、分離した構成が同じ場所に置く構成と同じ損失値を保ちながらより速く学習でき、さらに大きいモデルの組では同じ場所に置く構成がメモリ不足 (OOM) になる場面でも分離構成は学習できた。
papers.why: 大きな教師モデルを使う知識蒸留を複数ノードに分散しつつ損失の数学的な正確性を保つ設計で、蒸留パイプラインのメモリ制約を解く実装の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Knowledge distillation usually co-locates teacher and student on the same GPUs, so per-GPU memory limits which teachers fit. DisaggKD disaggregates them across nodes, streaming only hidden states from teacher replicas and computing a KD loss over row windows and vocabulary shards that exactly equals the full-vocabulary loss without ever forming full-vocabulary logits. On the Qwen3.5-35B-A3B to 9B pair, the disaggregated layout matches the colocated run's loss while training faster, and on larger pairs colocated runs with the fused loss still go OOM where the disaggregated split succeeds.
papers.why_en: Shows how to split large-teacher distillation across nodes while keeping the loss mathematically exact, a useful pattern for memory-constrained distillation pipelines.

papers.title: Cowork-Gym: Synthesizing Interactive Work Environments at Scale
papers.abstract: Cowork agents navigate dependencies across tools and files while adapting to changing user requirements and edits to shared workspaces. Scaling such environments requires maintaining consistency among task objectives, executable resources, user behavior, and success criteria. We introduce Cowork-Gym, a framework that synthesizes Cowork environments through a build-execute-revise loop that uses execution evidence and review feedback to validate and repair generated environments. To capture realistic Cowork dynamics, a stateful user simulator responds to the agent's actions through dialogue and direct edits to the shared workspace. We synthesize 64.9K environments across 14 application scenarios and use them to post-train 9B, 27B, and 35B-A3B Qwen models with supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and on-policy distillation. Averaged across six agentic benchmarks, these models outperform their corresponding base checkpoints by 8.7, 6.4, and 4.1 points, respectively. Ours-27B ranks second overall among the evaluated models and achieves the highest average scores on PawBench and ClawEval, outperforming models with over 100B total parameters on both benchmarks.
papers.ja_title: 共同作業エージェントを育てるための大規模シミュレーション環境生成
papers.summary: 共同作業 (Cowork) を行う AI エージェントを訓練するには、ツールやファイルの依存関係、ユーザーの要求変化に対応できる環境が必要だが、こうした環境を一貫性を保ちながら大量に作るのは難しかった。Cowork-Gym は、構築・実行・修正を繰り返して環境を自動生成し、ユーザーの振る舞いを模すシミュレータも組み込んだ。14 種類の業務シナリオで 6 万 4900 件の環境を作り、Qwen 系の 9B・27B・35B-A3B モデルを教師あり学習・強化学習・オンポリシー蒸留で後学習させたところ、6 つのエージェントベンチマークの平均でそれぞれ素の基盤モデルより 8.7, 6.4, 4.1 点向上し、27B モデルは PawBench と ClawEval で 100B 超のモデルより高得点だった。
papers.why: エージェント向け強化学習・後学習のための大規模な学習環境を自動生成する手法で、RL 後学習の訓練データ・環境構築の基盤として使える。
papers.summary_en: Training cowork agents requires environments that capture tool/file dependencies, changing user requirements, and shared workspace edits, but synthesizing many such environments consistently is hard. Cowork-Gym synthesizes environments via a build-execute-revise loop with a stateful user simulator, producing 64.9K environments across 14 application scenarios used to post-train 9B, 27B, and 35B-A3B Qwen models with SFT, RL, and on-policy distillation. Averaged across six agentic benchmarks, these models outperform their base checkpoints by 8.7, 6.4, and 4.1 points respectively, with the 27B model ranking second overall and topping PawBench/ClawEval even against models with over 100B total parameters.
papers.why_en: Provides a scalable method to auto-generate training environments for agentic RL/post-training, useful as infrastructure for building RL post-training data and environments.

papers.title: Encoding Context into LLM Weights: What Makes It Context?
papers.abstract: Longer contexts allow large language models (LLMs) to condition their predictions on more information, but inference costs grow prohibitively with context length. An emerging alternative uses test-time updates to encode context as temporary changes to model weights. However, encoding this information into weights that already represent general knowledge obscures its role as context, so the LLM may fail to use it properly to condition subsequent inference. To restore this contextual role, we first associate each context with an identifier during encoding, thereby distinguishing the newly encoded information from pre-existing knowledge. Invoking the identifier at inference then enables the LLM to recite the encoded context. Nevertheless, successful recitation does not ensure that the LLM will use the recalled information as context. We therefore further introduce a prompting framework that explicitly guides the LLM to use this information as context. Across diverse controlled tasks and practical benchmarks, our method outperformed the baseline using only off-the-shelf LLMs, showing its advances in context encoding.
papers.ja_title: 文脈を重みに焼き込んで長い入力のコストを減らす方法
papers.summary: 長い文脈をそのまま入力すると推論コストが膨らむため、文脈を一時的な重みの変化として埋め込む手法が注目されているが、すでに一般知識を表している重みに文脈を混ぜると、モデルがそれを今の文脈として正しく使えなくなる問題があった。この研究は、埋め込む文脈ごとに識別子を付けて既存知識と区別し、推論時に識別子を呼び出すことで文脈を正しく思い出させ、さらにそれを文脈として使うよう明示的に導くプロンプト手法を加えた。複数の制御されたタスクと実用的なベンチマークで、既製の LLM だけを使う手法より性能が上回った。
papers.why: 長文脈を毎回入力し直すコストを抑えつつ、重みへの焼き込みでも文脈としての役割を保つ手法で、長文脈推論のコスト削減に関わる技術として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Longer contexts let LLMs condition on more information but inference cost grows prohibitively with context length; encoding context as temporary weight updates is an emerging alternative, but mixing it into weights that already represent general knowledge obscures its role as context. The authors attach an identifier to each encoded context so it is distinguishable from pre-existing knowledge, and add a prompting framework that explicitly guides the LLM to use the recalled information as context rather than merely reciting it. Across diverse controlled tasks and practical benchmarks, the method outperformed baselines using only off-the-shelf LLMs.
papers.why_en: Offers a way to reduce the cost of re-feeding long context at inference while preserving its functional role as context when baked into weights, relevant to long-context inference cost reduction.

papers.title: Learning from fracture: Teaching language models to design through physical experience
papers.abstract: How can language models learn to optimize physical designs through experience? We introduce FracLearn, an experience-abstraction-generalization framework evaluated through a deliberately unfamiliar, Tetris-inspired fracture game. The model first proposes architectures and examines simulated fracture responses to accumulate experience. Abstraction organizes these observations into conditional principles linking reinforcement placement, crack evolution and load transfer, with supporting evidence and failure conditions. Generalization challenges the model to combine these principles in new architectures and surpass the earlier design record. Campaigns demonstrate progressive refinement and recovery through hypothesis revision, yielding a best composite score 11.0% above the experience-stage record. Fracture analyses connect improved performance to crack deflection and temporary trapping as toughening mechanisms, alongside greater residual load capacity. Learning occurs through external knowledge and decisions, without model-weight updates. This approach offers a route to scientific agents that turn computational experiments into reusable physical knowledge for materials discovery and engineering design.

papers.title: MMTA: Benchmarking Multimodal Temporal Analysis with Time Series, Text, and Vision
papers.abstract: Time-series analysis is increasingly studied in multimodal settings, yet most benchmarks pair temporal signals with text or with visualizations derived from the same signal. This leaves open whether multimodal large language models (MLLMs) can integrate time series with real-world visual evidence. We introduce MMTA (multimodal temporal analysis), a benchmark of tri-modal tasks with diverse cross-modal complementarity patterns among time series, text, and vision. MMTA spans nine domains -- robotics, autonomous driving, human action, manufacturing, AR assistance, healthcare, recommendation, finance, and climate -- under video+TS and image+TS layouts, with a 3,524-sample test split covering classification and forecasting. The benchmark standardizes heterogeneous real-world sources into a shared schema with domain-specific prompts, provenance documentation, and success-weighted metrics that penalize both wrong answers and failed generations. Evaluating eight open-source and proprietary MLLMs reveals a shared bottleneck: representing time series as text creates very long token sequences and weakens fine-grained alignment with visual evidence, especially in long-video settings. We then introduce TimeOmni-v, a multimodal LLM extension with a dedicated time-series encoder, temporal positional alignment, modality-aware token layout, and a forecasting head. TimeOmni-v improves long-video classification and time-series inference efficiency, showing that MMTA not only exposes representation and grounding failures but also motivates targeted model design.

papers.title: RT-J: Large-Scale Pretraining of Relational Transformers for Context-Efficient Predictions
papers.abstract: Foundation models for tables and relational databases are increasingly used for predictive tasks across various scientific and industrial domains. However, adapting existing models to unseen datasets requires tens of thousands of examples. Here we introduce RT-J, an 86M-parameter relational foundation model (RFM) that makes accurate predictions even with hundreds of in-context examples or fewer. To achieve this, we first assemble the Join, a large collection of 639 web-crawled databases with 6,023 LLM-generated forecasting tasks. We pretrain with long contexts of up to 8,192 database cells, using in-context examples from a novel lightweight random-walk retriever. Finally, we leverage context tuning and ensembling to scale up test-time compute. On in-context regression tasks from RelBench, RT-J requires 10x fewer examples on average to match strong feature engineering pipelines with LLM-agent or RDBLearn featurizers and TabICLv2 or LightGBM predictors. Overall, our work pushes the frontier for context-efficient predictions on relational data and highlights the importance of real-world semantics, context engineering and large-scale pretraining for RFMs.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 表データ向け基盤モデルを文脈内学習で効率化する事前学習
papers.summary: 表やリレーショナルデータベースの予測に使う基盤モデルは、未知のデータセットに適応させるには数万件もの例が必要だった。この研究は 86M パラメータの関係基盤モデル (RFM) である RT-J を作り、639 個のウェブ収集データベースと 6,023 個の LLM 生成予測タスクからなる「Join」という大規模データで、最大 8,192 セルの長い文脈を使って事前学習した。RelBench の文脈内回帰タスクでは、LLM エージェントや RDBLearn の特徴抽出と TabICLv2 や LightGBM を組み合わせた強力な既存手法と同等の性能に、平均で 10 分の 1 の例数で到達した。
papers.why: 少数の例から表データを予測する基盤モデルの事前学習・文脈内学習の設計を示し、長文脈での効率的な学習・推論の構築に関わる参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Foundation models for tables and relational databases typically need tens of thousands of examples to adapt to unseen datasets. The authors introduce RT-J, an 86M-parameter relational foundation model pretrained with long contexts of up to 8,192 database cells on "the Join," a collection of 639 web-crawled databases with 6,023 LLM-generated forecasting tasks, using a lightweight random-walk in-context retriever. On RelBench in-context regression tasks, RT-J matches strong feature-engineering pipelines (LLM-agent or RDBLearn featurizers with TabICLv2 or LightGBM predictors) while requiring 10x fewer examples on average.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates a pretraining and in-context-learning design for context-efficient tabular prediction foundation models, relevant to building efficient long-context training/inference systems.

papers.title: PaceReasoner: Label-Free Learning to Answer Briefly from Long Reasoning
papers.abstract: Extended chain-of-thought reasoning improves problem-solving performance but increases inference cost and latency, motivating more accurate answers with shorter reasoning. We introduce PaceReasoner, a label-free test-time reinforcement learning framework that uses a model's LONG responses to improve its SHORT-mode accuracy. Both modes share a trainable policy, creating a need for reliable supervision, sufficient SHORT training samples, and continued LONG responses to guide learning. PaceReasoner combines all-response and LONG-only answer consensus through progressive, confidence-weighted supervision. A behavior reward gradually shifts from encouraging SHORT exploration to rewarding agreement with LONG answers, while a ratio controller regulates the balance between modes. Across three model backbones and four benchmarks, PaceReasoner improves average SHORT accuracy over the baselines by 7.4--13.5 percentage points, with fewer than 25 reasoning tokens per response on average. Ablations support the key components, and cross-dataset results demonstrate transfer beyond the adaptation set.
papers.ja_title: ラベルなしで短く答える推論モデルの訓練手法 PaceReasoner
papers.summary: 長い思考過程(chain-of-thought)を使うと正答率は上がるが、推論コストと待ち時間が増える問題がある。PaceReasoner は正解ラベルを使わず、モデル自身が出した長い推論の答えを頼りにして、短いモードの正答率をテスト時強化学習で改善する枠組みで、信頼度に応じた段階的な教師信号と短答支持から長答支持へ徐々に切り替わる報酬を使う。3 つのモデル基盤と 4 つのベンチマークで短いモードの正答率をベースラインより平均 7.4〜13.5 ポイント改善し、1 回答あたり平均 25 トークン未満の推論で済む。
papers.why: 推論コストを抑えつつ精度を落とさない RL 後学習の手法として、低レイテンシな推論サービングに直結する知見を与える。
papers.summary_en: Extended chain-of-thought reasoning improves accuracy but raises inference cost and latency. PaceReasoner is a label-free test-time RL framework that uses a model's LONG responses to improve its SHORT-mode accuracy, combining confidence-weighted supervision with a behavior reward that shifts from SHORT exploration to LONG-answer agreement. Across three model backbones and four benchmarks, it improves average SHORT accuracy over baselines by 7.4–13.5 percentage points, using fewer than 25 reasoning tokens per response on average.
papers.why_en: Offers a concrete RL post-training recipe for cutting reasoning-token cost while keeping/raising accuracy, directly useful for low-latency serving.

papers.title: FlashMask-3: Efficient and Expressive Mask-Aware Distributed Attention
papers.abstract: Long-context training of large language and multimodal models couples structured attention masks (document, prefix-LM, share-question, sliding-window, block-sparse) with multi-node context parallelism, making the mask a dominant bottleneck. FlashMask's column-wise sparse mask compresses them from $O(n^2)$ to $O(n)$ via four query-axis boundary vectors, covering broad structured patterns. Implemented for Ampere GPUs, it neither exploits FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA warp-specialized pipeline on Hopper nor supports distribution. The column-wise sparse mask is indexed by key positions but stores query-axis interval boundaries. Under any multi-chunk context-parallel assignment, it reduces per-rank mask localization to a provably zero-communication \emph{clip--shift--max} on the boundary vectors, compatible with the single-GPU kernel. FlashMask-3 introduces a mask-aware Hopper kernel with three-role warp specialization atop FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA pipeline, plus a mask-aware distributed extension: zero-communication mask localization, a sparsity-aware load balancer (HCC-IPO), and a mask-aware compute-communication overlap with mask-driven communication pruning, whose forward all-gather uses topology-aware hierarchical routing. On a single H100 across 12 masks at 4K--128K context, it improves achieved TFLOPs over FlashMask, FlexAttention, and MagiAttention by 45--141%, 34--71%, and 2--44%. At context-parallel degrees 4--32 with 8K sequence per device, it attains 31--75% compute-communication overlap efficiency and improves throughput over Megatron-Core CP ring, Megatron-Core CP all-gather, and MagiAttention by $1.80\times$--$3.71\times$, $1.71\times$--$2.92\times$, and $1.09\times$--$1.46\times$. In end-to-end training of a 118B-A14B MoE at 128K on 128 H100 GPUs, it raises throughput by 7.3--11.0% over a Dual Chunk all-gather baseline, with attention forward+backward 24.5--44.9% faster.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: FlashMask-3: Hopper 対応のマスク認識分散アテンション
papers.summary: 長文脈の学習では文書やブロックスパースなどの構造化アテンションマスクがコンテキスト並列と結びつき、処理の大きなボトルネックになっていた。FlashMask-3 は Hopper GPU 向けにワープを特化させたカーネルと、通信を発生させないマスク位置特定・負荷分散・計算通信オーバーラップを組み合わせた分散拡張を導入した。単一 H100 では既存の FlashMask や FlexAttention、MagiAttention に対し達成演算性能を 45〜141%、34〜71%、2〜44% 向上させ、128 H100 上の 118B-A14B の MoE 学習でもスループットを 7.3〜11.0% 向上させた。
papers.why: 長文脈 LLM の分散学習において、マスク処理と通信オーバーラップを両立させる具体的なカーネル・システム設計を実測つきで示している。
papers.summary_en: Long-context training couples structured attention masks with multi-node context parallelism, making the mask a dominant bottleneck. FlashMask-3 introduces a mask-aware Hopper kernel with warp specialization atop FlashAttention-3's TMA/WGMMA pipeline, plus a distributed extension providing provably zero-communication mask localization, a sparsity-aware load balancer, and mask-driven compute-communication overlap. On a single H100 it improves achieved TFLOPs over FlashMask, FlexAttention, and MagiAttention by 45–141%, 34–71%, and 2–44%; in end-to-end training of a 118B-A14B MoE at 128K on 128 H100 GPUs it raises throughput by 7.3–11.0% over a Dual Chunk all-gather baseline.
papers.why_en: Shows concrete kernel- and communication-level techniques for scaling structured-mask attention under context parallelism, directly applicable to distributed training infrastructure.

papers.title: CineMem: Attention-Aligned Fine-grained Memory Retrieval for Multi-Shot Long Video Generation
papers.abstract: Autoregressive video generation relies on memory retrieval to model long-range dependencies. This capability becomes particularly critical for multi-shot generation, where models must reconcile substantial visual changes across shot transitions with persistent semantic continuity. Existing methods tend to perform memory retrieval at the frame level and share the same historical context across all query tokens, overlooking the heterogeneous information needs and leading to redundant retrieval and inefficient use of historical memory. To bridge this gap, we introduce CineMem, an attention-aligned fine-grained memory retrieval framework that combines online memory organization with query-adaptive retrieval for autoregressive multi-shot video generation. Specifically, guided by intrinsic memory-access patterns revealed through attention analysis, we propose an online-clustered KV cache as a memory organization strategy over all historical tokens, enabling semantic-aware memory grouping and more precise retrieval. In addition, we introduce a query-level retrieval mechanism that provides broader access to historical information under a fixed retrieval budget, thereby improving long-term memory utilization. Together, these designs enable the multi-shot video generator to preserve long-range consistency across shot transitions, particularly in revisitation scenarios, while approximating full-memory access under a constrained memory budget. To facilitate evaluation, we further introduce a suite of task-specific, VLM-assisted metrics for faithful inter-shot consistency assessment. Extensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework.

papers.title: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
papers.abstract: Large language models have evolved from single-turn chatbots into interactive agents capable of long-horizon reasoning. In real deployments, MCP tool services can return noisy feedback and users may intervene to correct the agent, but existing methods provide limited supervision for reflection learning and failure recovery. To bridge this gap, we propose Agent-Reflex, a general training framework for incentivizing proactive reflection in agents. Specifically, Agent-Reflex comprises three stages. First, Environment Reflection Skill Discovery (RSD) injects grounded tool-feedback perturbations into environment scaling, samples a capability-diverse LLM pool, mines matched success-failure pairs, and summarizes reusable reflection meta-skills. Building on this skill library, we then apply Reflective Supervised Fine-Tuning (ReSFT) that converts each skill into supervision for self-reflection, skill recovery, and user-centric correction, strengthening complementary reflective behaviors. Finally, we propose On-Policy Reflective Policy Optimization (ORPO) to combine agentic reinforcement learning under noisy interactions with reflection-guided on-policy distillation to further elicit proactive reflection. Built on Qwen3-8B, Agent-Reflex reaches 58.6 overall on five long-horizon tool-use benchmarks and 29.1 on AgentNoiseBench, surpassing strong environment-scaling and reflection baselines. Experiments on six challenging agent benchmark suites demonstrate the effectiveness of Agent-Reflex. Further analyses show that Agent-Reflex improves agents' robustness to noise while maintaining stable training dynamics, supporting scalable agent training. Our code is available at https://github.com/RUC-NLPIR/Agent-Reflex.
papers.ja_title: Agent-Reflex: ノイズに強い反省機能を持つエージェントの学習法
papers.summary: 実運用のエージェントは外部ツールからの雑音の多い応答やユーザーからの訂正に遭遇するが、既存手法は失敗からの立て直し(反省)を学ぶための教師信号が乏しい。Agent-Reflex は環境にわざと雑音を混ぜて成功と失敗のペアを集め、そこから反省スキルを抽出して教師付き微調整とオンポリシー強化学習を組み合わせ、3段階で反省的な振る舞いを引き出す枠組みを提案する。Qwen3-8B を用いた実験では、5つの長期ツール利用ベンチマークで総合 58.6 点、雑音耐性ベンチマーク AgentNoiseBench で 29.1 点を達成し、既存の環境拡張・反省手法を上回った。
papers.why: ノイズを含む対話での RL 後学習と反省学習の設計を具体的に示しており、頑健なエージェント訓練基盤の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: In real deployments MCP tool services can return noisy feedback and users may intervene, but existing methods give limited supervision for reflection and failure recovery. Agent-Reflex is a three-stage framework that mines success-failure pairs under injected tool-feedback perturbations, converts them into supervised fine-tuning for reflective behaviors, and applies on-policy reflective policy optimization combining RL under noisy interactions with reflection-guided distillation. Built on Qwen3-8B, it reaches 58.6 overall on five long-horizon tool-use benchmarks and 29.1 on AgentNoiseBench, surpassing strong environment-scaling and reflection baselines.
papers.why_en: Gives a concrete recipe for RL post-training that improves robustness to noisy tool feedback, useful for building resilient agent training pipelines.

papers.title: Virtual Head Attention
papers.abstract: The design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an ``impossible triangle'' among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality. GQA achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as MLA and MFA can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute. We propose Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which simultaneously improves all three vertices through two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix applies a near-identity transformation to queries within each KV group to recover virtual head diversity from halved physical query heads, and Linear Postmix fuses inter-head features via a low-rank $I + AB^\top$ residual structure. Since VHA introduces no nonlinear operations, Premix can be folded into the query projection and Postmix into the output projection at inference time, reducing the model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that directly reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations. With only two KV heads, the group size in large models readily reaches 64, fully exploiting Tensor Core parallelism during decoding. Across four scales with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the standard GQA baseline at every scale ($+$0.05\% to $+$0.81\%), while reducing KV cache by $4\times$ vs.\ GQA-8 at dense scales and $2\times$ vs.\ GQA-4 at the MoE scale, and lowering training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9\% (1.7B, $S{=}4096$). On an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens at 8K context, VHA outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by $+$0.70\,/\,$+$2.60\,\% on a 12-benchmark base-model evaluation suite; in a separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison after long-context mid-training, VHA attains an average RULER score of 84.4 over 8K--128K versus 73.0 for GQA, while using two rather than four KV heads in the full-attention layers.
papers.ja_title: Virtual Head Attention: KV キャッシュ・計算量・品質を同時に良くするアテンション設計
papers.summary: 長文脈 LLM のアテンション設計では、KV キャッシュの大きさと学習・プリフィルの計算量、モデル品質の3つを同時に良くすることが難しいとされていた。Virtual Head Attention (VHA) は、クエリにほぼ恒等な変換を施す Q Premix と低ランクで特徴を融合する Linear Postmix という軽量な線形演算を加え、推論時には既存の GQA(グループ化クエリアテンション)の高速化手法をそのまま使える形に畳み込める。4規模・4K文脈・500億トークンの事前学習で GQA ベースラインより常に性能が向上(+0.05〜+0.81%)し、KV キャッシュを GQA-8 比で4倍削減、産業規模の 30B-A3B MoE モデルでは MLA や GQA-4 を +0.70〜+2.60% 上回った。
papers.why: KV ヘッド数を2つまで減らしても既存の GQA 推論最適化をそのまま使える構造を示し、推論高速化とモデル品質の両立という実装者の悩みに答えている。
papers.summary_en: Attention design in long-context LLMs faces an "impossible triangle" among KV cache size, training/prefill FLOPs, and quality. Virtual Head Attention (VHA) adds two lightweight linear operations—Q Premix (a near-identity transform recovering virtual head diversity from halved physical query heads) and Linear Postmix (a low-rank residual fusion)—that fold into existing projections at inference, reducing to standard GQA-2 that reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations. Across four scales with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the GQA baseline (+0.05% to +0.81%) while cutting KV cache 4x vs. GQA-8, and on an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model it outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by +0.70/+2.60%.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates a drop-in architecture that improves all three corners of the KV-cache/compute/quality trade-off while remaining compatible with existing GQA decoding kernels.

papers.title: BELT : BEhavior-Aligned Low-Rank KV Cache Compression with Learned Top-k Rank Allocation
papers.abstract: Long-context inference makes the key-value (KV) cache a major memory bottleneck for large language models. We propose BELT, a low-rank KV cache compression framework. Its key-side objective targets attention distributions rather than raw keys or pre-softmax logits, yielding a quadratic surrogate with a closed-form low-rank solution. A learned global rank allocator uses differentiable soft selection during training and hard selection at deployment to meet a user-specified component budget. Experiments demonstrate improved model quality under aggressive compression and increased decoding throughput at comparable accuracy. Evaluated across three LLMs and multiple benchmarks, BELT achieves up to 70% low-rank KV cache compression while outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 23.3 points on LongBench, and up to 17.8x overall KV cache reduction when combined with quantization. With Triton-based GPU kernels and a quantized cache, BELT delivers up to 2.7x speedup for the attention module and 3.3x end-to-end decoding throughput.
papers.ja_title: BELT: 学習で割り振る低ランク KV キャッシュ圧縮
papers.summary: 長文脈推論では KV キャッシュがメモリの大きなボトルネックになる。BELT は生のキーではなくアテンション分布そのものを近似する低ランク圧縮を行い、学習時は微分可能なソフト選択、実運用時はハード選択でユーザー指定の圧縮量を自動的に割り振る手法。3 つの LLM と複数ベンチマークで、最大 70% の低ランク圧縮をしつつ最強ベースラインを LongBench で最大 23.3 ポイント上回り、量子化と組み合わせると最大 17.8 倍の KV キャッシュ削減、Triton カーネルによりアテンションを最大 2.7 倍、デコードのスループットを最大 3.3 倍高速化した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュ圧縮のアルゴリズムとカーネル実装の両方を数値で示しており、推論基盤の省メモリ化に直接応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Long-context inference makes the KV cache a major memory bottleneck. BELT is a low-rank KV cache compression framework whose key-side objective targets attention distributions rather than raw keys, with a learned global rank allocator using differentiable soft selection in training and hard selection at deployment. Across three LLMs and multiple benchmarks, BELT achieves up to 70% low-rank KV cache compression while outperforming the strongest baseline by up to 23.3 points on LongBench, up to 17.8x overall KV cache reduction when combined with quantization, and with Triton kernels delivers up to 2.7x attention speedup and 3.3x end-to-end decoding throughput.
papers.why_en: Combines an accuracy-preserving compression objective with a concrete Triton kernel implementation, giving a practical path to shrink KV cache memory in serving systems.

papers.title: AlignPred: Error-Controlled KV Cache Compression via Alignment and Predictive Coding
papers.abstract: Long-running agents retain KV caches across turns and sessions for hours or days. Compressing these persistent caches requires reducing storage while controlling reconstruction error. We present AlignPred, a codec that combines local alignment with predictive coding under a configurable KV reconstruction-error budget. Local orthogonal transforms align related heads or layers into a common coordinate frame, allowing AlignPred to combine token-wise prediction with same-token prediction across heads or layers. Residuals are quantized on an error-bounded lattice and entropy-coded, without learned predictors, encoder-side mode search, or large joint transforms. Across three attention mechanisms, AlignPred requires less storage than the evaluated baselines at comparable measured reconstruction error. Against the evaluated CPU codec implementations, it decodes at least 1.6 times faster while matching or improving encode time. AlignPred achieves near-native task scores at substantially compressed operating points on LongBench-Pro at 128K context. AlignPred's SGLang HiCache integration reduces persistent target-KV storage by 42-72% relative to native HiCache, with comparable latency.
papers.ja_title: AlignPred: 誤差を制御できる長時間稼働エージェント向け KV キャッシュ圧縮
papers.summary: 何時間も稼働するエージェントはターンやセッションをまたいで KV キャッシュを保持するため、保存容量を抑えつつ復元誤差を制御できる圧縮が必要になる。AlignPred は関連するヘッドやレイヤーを共通の座標系に合わせる局所直交変換と予測符号化を組み合わせ、学習済み予測器や大きな結合変換を使わずに誤差を抑えた量子化とエントロピー符号化を行うコーデック。評価した CPU 実装のコーデックに対して復号を 1.6 倍以上高速化し、SGLang の HiCache への統合では永続的な KV 保存容量をネイティブの HiCache 比で 42〜72% 削減しつつ、レイテンシは同等だった。
papers.why: 長時間稼働エージェントのための誤差制御付き永続 KV 圧縮という具体的な運用課題に、既存サービング基盤 (SGLang HiCache) への統合実績つきで答えている。
papers.summary_en: Long-running agents retain KV caches across turns and sessions for hours or days, requiring compression that controls reconstruction error while reducing storage. AlignPred is a codec combining local orthogonal alignment of related heads/layers with predictive coding and error-bounded lattice quantization plus entropy coding, without learned predictors or large joint transforms. It requires less storage than evaluated baselines at comparable measured reconstruction error, decodes at least 1.6x faster than evaluated CPU codecs, and its SGLang HiCache integration reduces persistent target-KV storage by 42–72% relative to native HiCache with comparable latency.
papers.why_en: Addresses the concrete operational problem of error-controlled, persistent KV cache compression and demonstrates integration into an existing serving system (SGLang HiCache).

papers.title: LatentRemedy: Efficient Remedy For Non-Prefix KV Cache Reuse in Multi-Agent Systems
papers.abstract: Non-prefix KV cache reuse is a promising approach for improving inference efficiency in multi-agent systems as agents share the same context blocks. However, when agents have conflicting tasks, directly reusing non-prefix KV caches across agents can severely degrade model performance, causing up to a 90% drop. Existing remedies, including selective recomputation and offset-based calibration, recover a limited fraction of this loss. We argue that the problem lies not only in contaminated KV representations but also in the agent's difficulty interpreting reused context under its own instructions. To this end, we introduce LatentRemedy, which uses a few task-conditioned latent tokens to help the target agent leverage reused context without recomputing the shared block. Specifically, we use an MLP to map the last hidden state of the target prefix into a small number of latent tokens, which are placed after the reused KV block to interact with the shared context. To guide subsequent predictions toward the target task, we train the MLP through full-prefill distillation. Experiments show that LatentRemedy consistently outperforms existing reuse baselines on conflicting tasks while maintaining TTFT close to direct reuse as cache size grows. Code and data are available at https://github.com/chenzhwsysu57/kvreuse.
papers.ja_title: LatentRemedy: マルチエージェントでの非接頭 KV キャッシュ再利用の精度低下を直す手法
papers.summary: マルチエージェントシステムでは共有文脈ブロックの非接頭 (先頭以外) の KV キャッシュ再利用が推論効率化に有効だが、エージェントの課題が競合すると性能が最大 90% も落ちる問題がある。LatentRemedy は、対象エージェントの最後の隠れ状態を少数の潜在トークンに変換し、共有ブロックを再計算せずにその潜在トークンを使って再利用文脈を自分の指示に合わせて解釈できるようにし、全プリフィル蒸留でこの変換器を学習する。実験では既存の再利用手法より一貫して高い性能を示し、キャッシュサイズが大きくなっても最初のトークンまでの時間 (TTFT) を直接再利用に近い水準に保った。
papers.why: マルチエージェント推論サービングでの KV キャッシュ再利用の性能劣化という実運用課題に、軽量な追加モジュールで対処する具体策を示す。
papers.summary_en: Non-prefix KV cache reuse improves inference efficiency in multi-agent systems, but directly reusing caches across agents with conflicting tasks can cause up to a 90% performance drop, which existing remedies only partially recover. LatentRemedy maps the target agent's last hidden state into a few task-conditioned latent tokens placed after the reused KV block, trained via full-prefill distillation, so the target agent can interpret reused context under its own instructions without recomputing the shared block. Experiments show it consistently outperforms existing reuse baselines on conflicting tasks while keeping TTFT close to direct reuse as cache size grows.
papers.why_en: Provides a lightweight fix for a concrete failure mode (conflicting-task KV reuse degradation) in multi-agent serving, useful for systems aiming to maximize cache reuse without sacrificing correctness.

papers.title: SHELDON: Reasoning through Dual Search over Hypothesis and Observation Spaces
papers.abstract: Test-time scaling has enabled LLMs to solve increasingly complex reasoning, discovery, and optimization tasks. However, existing approaches often gather observations while seeking evidence for current hypotheses, then generate new hypotheses conditioned on those hypotheses and their associated evidence. This couples observation discovery to existing hypotheses, favoring local refinements over exploration of unknown hypotheses regions. Inspired by the hypothetico-deductive method (Hempel, 1945) and dual-space models of scientific discovery (Klahr & Dunbar, 1988), we introduce SHELDON, a scientific reasoning harness that separately represents and jointly explores hypothesis and observation spaces. By actively seeking new observations along with new hypotheses, SHELDON can discover observations that its current hypotheses do not explain. These unexplained observations expose gaps in its understanding, motivate new investigations, and guide the generation of hypotheses beyond refinements of existing ones. Across diagnosis, abstract reasoning, and optimization benchmarks, SHELDON outperforms evaluated baselines by up to 26.7 points. Additional analysis shows that SHELDON generates up to 4.5x more novel solutions.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング

papers.title: Failure Recovery via Belief Updates and World Modeling for Long-Horizon Agents
papers.abstract: Long-horizon agents often struggle to recover from failures whose causes lie several steps earlier, beyond what local reflection or backtracking can resolve. We introduce BELIEFWEAVER, a framework that combines persistent evidence across attempts with prospective reasoning over repair directions. It maintains a relational belief state over frontiers, attempts, observations, and checkpoints. Execution evidence updates related frontier priorities across attempts and rollback, while diagnostic evidence gates execution. An implicit world model (IWM) evaluates repair hypotheses, predicts progress, and identifies relations among frontiers to guide exploration. We further distill these recurring IWM reasoning components into a 9B student through supervised fine-tuning and on-policy distillation (OPD). Across three terminal-based benchmarks, BELIEFWEAVER improves aggregate final score by 5.1 percentage points over native Terminus-2 continuation, with positive trends in exploration efficiency. The distilled 9B student improves final score by 9.8 percentage points over the reported native baseline while reducing estimated teacher API cost by 54.8% relative to the matched teacher. These results show that persistent evidence and prospective reasoning can improve recovery in long-horizon agent tasks while substantially reducing reliance on teacher-model inference.

papers.title: AReaL-RSI: Adaptive Scaling and Coordination of Recursive Self-Improvement
papers.abstract: Scaling recursive self-improvement requires additional computation to produce useful research progress in reaching persistent objectives. Intuitively, more researcher agents can explore more hypotheses, but early evaluation scores might misrepresent their promise, shared findings could lose their applicability conditions, and useful procedures could remain confined to completed investigations. In this paper, we present AReaL-RSI, a framework for organizing a persistent research team of agents without updating backbone LLM weights. We formulate the scaling problem in terms of evaluated outcomes and whole-system resource expenditure. Concretely, a leader agent selects task-appropriate research orientations and guides ongoing investigations; conditional memory sharing distinguishes unresolved problems from supported findings and enables recipient adaptation. During recursive evolution, after each campaign, evidence-based review revises researcher orientation, knowledge, and skills for later campaigns. Experiments compare AReaL-RSI with Codex-Goal on downstream harness optimization, GPU kernel optimization, and AI research tasks using two backbones. Under the reported resource allocations, AReaL-RSI improves Terminal Bench performance by 2.2 percentage points for each backbone and increases mean KernelBench speedup by 32.2-36.8%; further scalability comparisons favor the design of AReaL-RSI over native scaling: combining experience sharing with specialized researcher roles yields 1.9-27.5% lower kernel latency than independent exploration and 1.3-33.9% lower latency than sharing alone across all seven comparable task-backbone pairs.

papers.title: PrismStencil: Transforming Stencil Computations into Matrix Multiplications
papers.abstract: Stencil computations are a fundamental class of workloads in scientific and engineering applications. Although Tensor Cores offer new opportunities for stencil acceleration, existing tensorization methods suffer from substantial redundant computation and insufficient data reuse. We propose PrismStencil, a stencil tensorization algorithm that introduces a novel mapping scheme between matrices and stencil grid points. PrismStencil employs multidimensional vector mapping to accommodate the multidimensional data dependencies of stencil computations and a unified gather--scatter tensorization scheme to exploit the relative sizes of the matrix dimensions in Tensor Core operations, thereby reducing the redundant computation introduced by tensorization. Moreover, it introduces a cross-product data-reuse mechanism that exploits the overlap among neighboring stencil updates to further enhance data reuse. Across representative stencil kernels on an NVIDIA A100 GPU, PrismStencil achieves average speedups of 2.13x and 2.17x over state-of-the-art Tensor Core stencil methods with FP64 and TF32 precision, respectively.
papers.ja_title: ステンシル計算をテンソルコア行列積に変換して高速化
papers.summary: 気象や流体のシミュレーションで使うステンシル計算 (格子点の近くの値を使う計算) は、GPU のテンソルコア (行列積専用回路) に載せようとすると、計算の重複や使い回し不足で性能が出にくいという課題があった。PrismStencil は行列と格子点の新しい対応付けと、データを集めて配る処理を統一した方式を導入し、重複計算を減らしつつ近隣の更新の重なりを利用してデータ再利用を増やす仕組みを作った。NVIDIA A100 GPU 上の代表的なステンシルカーネルで、既存の最先端テンソルコア手法に比べて FP64 で平均 2.13 倍、TF32 で平均 2.17 倍の高速化を達成した。
papers.why: テンソルコアを行列積以外の計算に活用する設計の実例を示し、科学計算カーネルを低精度・高性能に実装する人の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Stencil computations, common in scientific simulations, often waste Tensor Core potential because existing tensorization methods introduce redundant computation and insufficient data reuse. PrismStencil introduces a new mapping between matrices and stencil grid points plus a unified gather-scatter tensorization scheme to cut redundant computation, together with a cross-product data-reuse mechanism exploiting overlap among neighboring stencil updates. Across representative stencil kernels on an NVIDIA A100 GPU, it achieves average speedups of 2.13x (FP64) and 2.17x (TF32) over state-of-the-art Tensor Core stencil methods.
papers.why_en: It offers a concrete design pattern for mapping non-matmul workloads onto Tensor Cores, useful for anyone building low-precision, high-performance scientific computing kernels.

papers.title: STAMP as a topology-aware molecular language for fragment-level learning and editing
papers.abstract: Molecular fragments provide chemically meaningful units, but existing molecular languages rarely make their locations and connections explicit for editing. Here we introduce STAMP (Sequential Tree Attachment-based Motif-Preserving representation), a topology-aware molecular language that connects fragment-level representation learning with precise structural editing. STAMP separately encodes motif identity, attachment sites and tree topology, making fragments reusable across contexts and subtrees directly accessible. Learned representations capture motif similarity and recurring transformations, and lower activity-cliff prediction error on 23 of 30 targets versus a matched SMILES encoder. Compatible subtree operations support scaffold-preserving optimization, ranking first among six methods on 15 of 23 benchmark objectives. A deterministic compiler enables frozen language models to act on indexed fragments, improving molecular editing, optimization, transformation transfer and change identification by 9 to 56 percentage points over plain SMILES. Together, these results establish an executable molecular language in which learned chemical units remain directly operable during design.

papers.title: An Optical KV Cache Network for Disaggregated LLM Serving
papers.abstract: In disaggregated LLM serving, each request's KV cache moves from a prefill GPU to a decode GPU before the response begins, and a coding-agent turn often moves the KV cache of its whole long context. Behind an oversubscribed packet fabric, this transfer adds to the time to first token (TTFT). An optical circuit switch (OCS) can give every transfer a full-rate circuit for less than an oversubscribed packet fabric costs, but a mechanical OCS needs tens of milliseconds to reconfigure. We hide this delay inside the prefill. A reservation scheduler commits each circuit while the prefill is still computing, so the circuit is ready when the KV cache is, and each GPU reaches the OCS through its own wavelength-multiplexed (WDM) optics on one fiber pair. In simulations of GPU clusters on real serving traces with prefill times measured on H100 GPUs, this optical KV cache network matches 400G packet fabrics with adaptive routing at 0.55 to 0.78 times the cost of a 2:1 fabric and tolerates the 50 ms reconfiguration delay of a 384-port mechanical OCS.
papers.ja_title: 機械式光スイッチで隠す、分散 LLM 推論の KV キャッシュ転送ネットワーク
papers.summary: 入力処理 (プリフィル) と文生成 (デコード) を別々の GPU で行う分散 LLM 推論では、各リクエストの KV キャッシュ (注意機構の中間結果) をプリフィル用 GPU からデコード用 GPU へ丸ごと移す必要があり、混雑したパケット網ではこの転送が最初の一文字が出るまでの時間 (TTFT) を伸ばしてしまう。光回路スイッチ (OCS) は混雑パケット網より安く専用の全速回線を用意できるが、機械式切り替えには数十ミリ秒かかる欠点がある。本研究はプリフィル計算がまだ終わらないうちに回線を予約しておく予約スケジューラと、GPU ごとの波長多重光ファイバー接続を組み合わせ、実際のサービング記録と H100 GPU 実測のプリフィル時間を使ったシミュレーションで、400G パケット網 (適応ルーティング付き) と同等の性能を 2:1 構成コストの 0.55〜0.78 倍で実現し、384 ポート機械式 OCS の 50 ミリ秒の切り替え遅延も問題なく吸収できることを示した。
papers.why: KV キャッシュ転送のボトルネックを光ネットワークとスケジューリングの組み合わせで解決する設計を示し、分散推論基盤のネットワーク層を考える人に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: In disaggregated LLM serving, each request's KV cache must move wholesale from a prefill GPU to a decode GPU, and behind an oversubscribed packet fabric this transfer adds to time-to-first-token (TTFT). An optical circuit switch (OCS) can give every transfer a full-rate circuit for less than an oversubscribed packet fabric costs, but a mechanical OCS needs tens of milliseconds to reconfigure; the authors hide this delay by having a reservation scheduler commit each circuit while the prefill is still computing, paired with per-GPU wavelength-multiplexed optics on one fiber pair. In simulations on real serving traces with prefill times measured on H100 GPUs, this optical KV cache network matches 400G packet fabrics with adaptive routing at 0.55 to 0.78 times the cost of a 2:1 fabric, and tolerates the 50 ms reconfiguration delay of a 384-port mechanical OCS.
papers.why_en: It gives a concrete network design that hides optical circuit switch reconfiguration latency behind prefill compute, directly relevant to anyone building the networking layer for disaggregated LLM serving infrastructure.

papers.title: Simplifying and Improving On-Policy Distillation for Few-Step Diffusion
papers.abstract: Few-step distillation reduces the sampling cost of diffusion and flow models, but existing approaches often require auxiliary score models or specialized architectures. We show that simple on-policy velocity regression already provides a strong foundation for 4-NFE generation. To represent teacher velocity variation within each coarse transition, we introduce Pivot, a training-only residual proxy that separates local corrections from the student's interval-mean prediction. We further repel the student from weaker teacher predictions, providing a lightweight mechanism for avoiding undesirable modes. The resulting framework, Simplified Matching Distillation (SMD), remains entirely regression-based, requires neither online score estimation nor adversarial training, and leaves the deployed generator unchanged.
