We evaluate SMD on image generation and editing, 3D generation, video synthesis, and joint audio--video generation, scaling to 33 billion parameters. At 4-NFE, SMD outperforms strong few-step baselines and surpasses multi-step teachers on several benchmarks. It also supports cross-model, multi-teacher, and causal-video distillation.

papers.title: ProTok: Unified Protein Tokenization via Modular Multi-Codebook Quantization
papers.abstract: Protein sequence, structure, and functional annotations each capture complementary aspects of protein biology, yet existing tokenizers encode each modality independently, limiting the expressiveness of discrete protein representations. We present ProTok, a unified protein tokenizer that maps all three modalities into a modular discrete vocabulary via product quantization with per-modality codebook groups and modality dropout. A single ProTok checkpoint supports flexible inference from any modality subset without retraining. On seven StructTokenBench benchmarks spanning 14 tasks and 28 test splits, ProTok achieves an average rank of 1.4 across all structure-only tokenizers, placing first on 21 splits and among the top two on 27 of the 28. These gains come without sacrificing reconstruction: ProTok's tokens reach 0.939 lDDT on CATH 4.2, showing that multi-codebook quantization and multi-modal training yield tokens that are both reconstructable and informative. ProTok's structure tokens further lead all baseline structure tokenizers on zero-shot functional retrieval across CATH, Enzyme Commission, and Gene Ontology label hierarchies. The vocabulary also supports generation: a compact language model trained from scratch over ProTok tokens jointly generates backbone and sequence, with 52% of sampled backbones designable versus 21% for a parameter-matched GeoBPE baseline. ProTok shows that structure, sequence, and function can share one discrete vocabulary, motivating protein language models that reason over a unified token stream.

papers.title: Revisiting Cauchy-Schwarz Norm Bounds for SDC Detection in LLM Inference
papers.abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) execute billions of floating-point operations per output token across many hardware accelerators. At this scale, hardware-induced faults can bypass system-level detection mechanisms and cause Silent Data Corruption (SDC). Algorithm-Based Fault Tolerance (ABFT) is the state-of-the-art technique for protecting matrix multiplication from such faults, but it incurs non-negligible computational overhead and requires thresholds to distinguish hardware-induced errors from floating-point roundoff. In this paper, we revisit Cauchy--Schwarz Norm Bounds (CSNB) as a low-overhead alternative for detecting SDC during LLM inference. We compare CSNB against ABFT through controlled fault injection and evaluate the runtime overhead of both verification and threshold determination across multiple model sizes, batch sizes, and generation lengths. Our results show that, on average, CSNB retains 99% of the fault detection capability of ABFT for the evaluated linear layers in dense LLMs, while reducing verification overhead by 87% and threshold determination overhead by 67%. For Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) router gate computations, however, CSNB retains only 55% of the fault detection capability of ABFT. These findings suggest that CSNB is a promising low-overhead alternative for protecting linear layers in dense LLMs, while checksum-based verification remains preferable for the evaluated MoE router gate.
papers.ja_title: LLM 推論におけるハードウェア故障検出: Cauchy-Schwarz Norm Bounds の再評価
papers.summary: LLM 推論では巨大な行列演算をハードウェア上で行うため、検出されないまま結果が狂う故障 (Silent Data Corruption, SDC) が起こり得る。既存の ABFT (Algorithm-Based Fault Tolerance) は検出精度が高いが計算オーバーヘッドが大きい。本研究は低コストな代替手法 Cauchy-Schwarz Norm Bounds (CSNB) を検証し、dense な LLM の線形層では ABFT の検出能力の 99% を保ちながら検証オーバーヘッドを 87%、閾値決定オーバーヘッドを 67% 削減できることを示した。一方 Mixture-of-Experts のルーター計算では検出能力は 55% にとどまり、そこでは checksum ベースの手法が望ましいとした。
papers.why: LLM 推論基盤でハードウェア故障を低コストに検出する手法の選び方 (dense 層には CSNB、MoE ルーターには ABFT 系) を具体的な数値で示している。
papers.summary_en: Running LLM inference performs billions of floating-point operations across accelerators, where hardware faults can silently corrupt results (Silent Data Corruption, SDC) undetected. State-of-the-art Algorithm-Based Fault Tolerance (ABFT) catches such errors but adds non-negligible overhead; this paper revisits Cauchy-Schwarz Norm Bounds (CSNB) as a low-overhead alternative, showing that for dense LLM linear layers CSNB retains 99% of ABFT's fault detection capability while cutting verification overhead by 87% and threshold determination overhead by 67%. For Mixture-of-Experts router gate computations, however, CSNB retains only 55% of ABFT's detection capability, so checksum-based verification remains preferable there.
papers.why_en: Gives concrete numbers for choosing a low-overhead fault-detection method for LLM inference infrastructure: CSNB for dense linear layers, but ABFT/checksum-style methods for MoE router gates.

review.note: ABFT と CSNB の検出能力維持率・オーバーヘッド削減率を dense 層と MoE ルーターで分けて実測しており、信頼性検証手法を層の種類別に比較評価する観点が得られる。
review.note_en: Measures fault-detection retention and overhead reduction separately for dense linear layers vs MoE router gates via controlled fault injection, illustrating how to evaluate reliability techniques per layer type.

papers.title: ACCRUE: Continual Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Robot Foundation Models
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) post-training improves robot foundation models (RFMs) beyond their demonstrations, but real-world deployment demands more: learning new tasks efficiently while retaining previously acquired behaviors. Existing continual RL methods on top of VLAs mitigate forgetting but rely on on-policy updates with limited forward transfer, whereas off-policy methods improve single-task sample efficiency without addressing learner persistence across tasks. We propose ACCRUE, a continual off-policy RL framework that carries lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks, allowing each stage to reuse behavioral and value knowledge acquired through prior RL. The inherited critic adapts only on current-task transitions and guides current-task actor learning, while prior behavior is preserved by distilling the actor toward cached targets on a small number of retained episodes. Fixed visual features keep the inherited learner and its replay compatible with base-policy updates. Across contact-rich assembly sequences in simulation and on real-robot hardware, ACCRUE accelerates subsequent-task learning with near-zero forgetting and significantly reduces real-robot training time by 31.0\% to 68.5\%.
papers.ja_title: ロボット基盤モデルのための継続 off-policy 強化学習 ACCRUE
papers.summary: 実機ロボットでは基盤モデルに新しいタスクを効率よく追加学習させつつ、前に学んだ動作を忘れさせたくない。既存の継続強化学習は on-policy 更新で過去タスクの知識を転用しにくく、off-policy 手法は単一タスクの効率は良いが学習器をタスク間で持続させる仕組みがなかった。ACCRUE は軽量な actor と critic をタスクをまたいで引き継ぎ、受け継いだ critic を現在タスクの遷移データだけで適応させ、少量の保存エピソードへの蒸留で過去の振る舞いを保つ。接触の多い組み立てタスクのシミュレーションと実機実験で、ほぼ忘却なしに次タスクの学習を加速し、実機の学習時間を 31.0% から 68.5% 短縮した。
papers.why: ロボット基盤モデルの RL 後学習において、タスクをまたいで actor/critic を再利用しつつ忘却を抑える継続学習の具体的な仕組みを示している。
papers.summary_en: Real-world robot deployment requires learning new tasks efficiently while retaining previously acquired behaviors on top of robot foundation models (RFMs). Existing continual RL methods on VLAs rely on on-policy updates with limited forward transfer, while off-policy methods improve single-task efficiency without addressing learner persistence across tasks. ACCRUE carries lightweight actor and critic networks across tasks, adapting the inherited critic only on current-task transitions while distilling the actor toward cached targets on a small number of retained episodes to preserve prior behavior. Across contact-rich assembly sequences in simulation and on real-robot hardware, ACCRUE accelerates subsequent-task learning with near-zero forgetting and reduces real-robot training time by 31.0% to 68.5%.
papers.why_en: Shows a concrete continual off-policy RL mechanism for robot foundation model post-training that reuses actor/critic knowledge across tasks while keeping forgetting near zero.

papers.title: UniW(A)M: A Unified Mixture-of-Experts Framework for World and World-Action Models
papers.abstract: World models (WMs) and world-action models (WAMs) focus on future world prediction and executable action generation, respectively. Although these models learn shared physical dynamics and interaction semantics from embodied trajectories, they are typically trained in isolation, which restricts knowledge reuse between prediction and control. The central challenge is therefore to develop a unified learning framework that shares these dynamics while preserving the distinct modeling capabilities required by each paradigm. We propose UniW(A)M, a mixture-of-experts world-(action) model built upon diffusion Transformers that unifies action-conditioned world modeling and diverse WAM variants. Shared experts capture common dynamics, while atomic capability experts are reused across interfaces so that each interface keeps its own conditional pathway. At deployment, a plug-in adaptive interface router (PAIR) learns from a small subset of target-task chunk scenarios to select a suitable WAM interface for each execution chunk, balancing task success and execution efficiency while keeping the backbone frozen. We evaluate UniW(A)M on LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and three real-world manipulation tasks, where it achieves 88.3% average real-world success versus 76.7% for the strongest baseline. On WorldArena, it leads action-conditioned world modeling on all three tasks. AC-WM co-training contributes to action generation on every action interface and PAIR raises OOD success from 63.3% to 76.7%.
papers.ja_title: 世界モデルと行動モデルを統一する Mixture-of-Experts フレームワーク UniW(A)M
papers.summary: 世界モデル (将来予測) と world-action モデル (行動生成) は共通の物理ダイナミクスを学ぶはずなのに、別々に訓練されて知識を再利用できていなかった。UniW(A)M は拡散 Transformer 上に構築した Mixture-of-Experts で、共有 expert が共通ダイナミクスを担い、能力別 expert を複数のインタフェースで再利用する。さらに実行時には少量のターゲットタスクデータだけで学習する PAIR というルーターが、各実行チャンクに適したインタフェースを選ぶ。LIBERO・RoboTwin 2.0・実機 3 タスクで平均 88.3% の成功率を達成し、最強ベースラインの 76.7% を上回った。
papers.why: 世界モデルと行動モデルを 1 つの MoE 構造に統合し、インタフェースをタスクに応じて切り替えるアーキテクチャ設計の具体例を示している。
papers.summary_en: World models (WMs) and world-action models (WAMs) learn shared physical dynamics but are typically trained in isolation, preventing knowledge reuse between prediction and control. UniW(A)M is a mixture-of-experts world-(action) model built on diffusion Transformers, where shared experts capture common dynamics and atomic capability experts are reused across interfaces while keeping each interface's own conditional pathway. A plug-in adaptive interface router (PAIR), learned from a small subset of target-task scenarios, selects a suitable WAM interface per execution chunk at deployment. On LIBERO, RoboTwin 2.0, and three real-world manipulation tasks, UniW(A)M achieves 88.3% average real-world success versus 76.7% for the strongest baseline, and PAIR raises OOD success from 63.3% to 76.7%.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates a concrete MoE architecture that unifies world and action models and dynamically routes between interfaces, offering an architectural design pattern for shared dynamics with specialized capability pathways.

papers.title: SP$^2$ec: Adaptive Self-Speculative Decoding for Vision-Language Models
papers.abstract: Speculative Decoding (SD) has demonstrated its efficacy in accelerating large language model inference, but for Vision-Language Models (VLMs), the diverse input modalities make it difficult for a small trained drafter to achieve consistently high throughput. Self-speculative decoding reuses parts of the target model as a drafter which retains the multi-modal capability of the VLMs, yet its efficiency depends on choosing a suitable draft configuration for each prompt. We propose Single-Peak SPeculative decoding (SP$^2$ec), a training-free bandit algorithm that adapts the draft configuration during generation. SP$^2$ec exploits the single-peak throughput pattern observed in existing self-speculative methods, including SWIFT, KnapSpec, SpecVLM, and our simple cosSim. Our algorithmic design explicitly minimizes a novel notion of wall-time regret for each given query, corresponding to the empirical wall-time latency. Theoretical guarantees on the wall-time regret show that SP$^2$ec can exploit the optimal draft configuration, with negligible exploration cost. Extensive experiments on Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B across visual and textual tasks show consistent improvements of up to 11% over the original self-speculative methods, demonstrating the wide applicability of the proposed SP$^2$ec algorithm.
papers.ja_title: 自己投機的デコードの設定を動的に選ぶバンディット手法 SP2ec
papers.summary: 視覚言語モデル (VLM) の推論を高速化する投機的デコードは、入力がテキストと画像など多様なため小さな専用 drafter では安定した高速化が難しい。自己投機的デコードは本体モデルの一部を drafter として使い回すが、どの draft 設定を選ぶかが prompt ごとに最適解が異なり効率を左右する。SP2ec は訓練不要のバンディットアルゴリズムで、生成中に draft 設定を適応的に切り替え、実測の wall-time に基づく後悔量を直接最小化する。Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct と LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B での実験で、既存の自己投機的手法 (SWIFT, KnapSpec, SpecVLM, cosSim) に対し最大 11% の改善を示した。
papers.why: 推論サービング中に投機的デコードの設定を学習不要で動的に最適化する実用的なアルゴリズムで、既存の自己投機的デコード実装にそのまま組み込める。
papers.summary_en: Speculative decoding speeds up LLM inference, but for vision-language models (VLMs) the diverse input modalities make it hard for a small trained drafter to achieve consistently high throughput; self-speculative decoding reuses parts of the target model as a drafter but its efficiency depends on choosing a suitable draft configuration per prompt. SP2ec is a training-free bandit algorithm that adapts the draft configuration during generation by minimizing a wall-time regret defined on empirical latency, exploiting the single-peak throughput pattern observed in methods like SWIFT, KnapSpec, SpecVLM, and the authors' own cosSim. On Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct and LLaVA-NeXT-Mistral-7B across visual and textual tasks, SP2ec gives consistent improvements of up to 11% over the original self-speculative methods.
papers.why_en: Offers a practical, training-free way to dynamically optimize self-speculative decoding configurations at serving time, with theoretical wall-time regret guarantees, pluggable into existing self-speculative decoding implementations.

papers.title: Beyond the Verdict: Agentic Code Judging with Verifiable Feedback
papers.abstract: Test-time scaling for large language models (LLMs) can involve generating multiple candidate solutions for selection or revising an earlier attempt. To guide selection and revision, we need a verifier that can estimate candidate correctness and provide evidence of failure. In competitive programming, however, official judging systems provide authoritative verdicts under finite submission budgets, without revealing failure explanations or failing inputs. To provide informative feedback without consuming official submissions, we formulate a task in which a model judges and diagnoses a candidate program using only the problem statement and source code, with generated counterexamples serving as checkable evidence. To evaluate this task, we build USACO-JUDGE from the USACO 2026 contests, using accepted and unaccepted programs written by human experts and multiple LLMs. We then train ARBITER, a 35B mixture-of-experts (MoE) agentic verifier, with reinforcement learning in a generic execution sandbox. Training raises counterexample success on incorrect programs from 40.61% to 62.67% and mean binary verdict accuracy on USACO-JUDGE from 71.41% to 87.41%, approaching frontier verification performance. Beyond verification, ARBITER outperforms baselines in both code selection and refinement. In an IOI 2026 case study, ARBITER-guided refinement raises GPT-OSS-120B's expected score above the gold-medal threshold under the official submission limit.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 反例で診断する競技プログラミング用エージェント型コード検証器 ARBITER
papers.summary: LLM の test-time scaling では複数の解答候補を作って選んだり書き直したりするが、そのためには正しさを見極める検証器が必要になる。競技プログラミングの公式 judge は限られた提出回数しか結果を返さず、失敗の理由や反例を教えてくれない。本研究は問題文とソースコードだけから反例を生成して診断するタスクを作り USACO-JUDGE ベンチマークを構築し、35B の Mixture-of-Experts エージェント型検証器 ARBITER を強化学習で訓練した。学習により誤ったプログラムへの反例生成成功率は 40.61% から 62.67% に、二値判定の精度は 71.41% から 87.41% に向上し、フロンティアの検証性能に近づいた。IOI 2026 のケーススタディでは ARBITER による修正支援で GPT-OSS-120B の期待得点が金メダル基準を上回った。
papers.why: RL で訓練したエージェント型検証器を使い、公式ジャッジに依存せずコード候補の選択・修正を支援する仕組みは、推論時の検証・自己修正基盤の設計に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Test-time scaling for LLMs needs a verifier that can estimate candidate correctness and provide evidence of failure, but official competitive-programming judges give only authoritative verdicts under a finite submission budget without explanations or failing inputs. This paper builds USACO-JUDGE from USACO 2026 contests and trains ARBITER, a 35B mixture-of-experts agentic verifier, with reinforcement learning in an execution sandbox to judge and diagnose candidate programs using only the problem statement and source code, with generated counterexamples as checkable evidence. Training raises counterexample success on incorrect programs from 40.61% to 62.67% and mean binary verdict accuracy from 71.41% to 87.41%, approaching frontier verification performance, and in an IOI 2026 case study ARBITER-guided refinement raises GPT-OSS-120B's expected score above the gold-medal threshold under the official submission limit.
papers.why_en: Shows how an RL-trained agentic verifier that produces checkable counterexamples can support test-time code selection and refinement without consuming official judge submissions, a useful pattern for inference-time verification infrastructure.

papers.title: Scaling Online Optimal Transport Minibatches for Flow Matching
papers.abstract: A central challenge in scaling flow models is maintaining stability in training and integration. In flow matching, this stability depends critically on how source samples are paired with data. Independent random pairing introduces substantial stochasticity, motivating minibatch optimal transport (OT) to construct online source-target couplings that reduce this randomness (Tong et al., 2024). However, as applications extend to larger and higher-dimensional datasets, small minibatches can limit these benefits, while scaling the coupling to substantially larger minibatches at every iteration is computationally prohibitive. Moreover, how OT coupling affects the full stochastic gradient and integration remains theoretically unresolved. In this work, we develop a scalable online entropic OT approximation that enables substantially larger source-target couplings while preserving the benefits of OT. We close the theoretical gap for both unregularized and entropic OT by proving strict reductions in full stochastic-gradient variance and integration error relative to independent pairing, and further characterize how these improvements strengthen as the online coupling minibatch grows. Experiments on single-cell gene interpolation-flow and image-flow training validate these predictions, showing that larger online couplings consistently improve training stability and final generation performance.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 大きな online optimal transport ミニバッチで flow matching の学習を安定化
papers.summary: flow matching モデルの学習・生成の安定性は、出発点のサンプルとデータをどう対応付けるかに大きく左右される。独立なランダム対応付けはゆらぎが大きく、ミニバッチ単位の最適輸送 (OT) 対応付けがこれを減らすとされてきたが、データが大きく高次元になるとミニバッチが小さいままでは効果が限られ、毎イテレーションで大きな OT を計算するのは計算コストが高すぎた。本研究はスケール可能な online entropic OT 近似を開発し、独立対応付けに比べて確率的勾配の分散と積分誤差が厳密に減ることを理論的に示し、ミニバッチが大きいほど改善が強まることを明らかにした。単一細胞遺伝子の補間フローと画像フローの実験で、大きな online coupling が一貫して学習の安定性と最終的な生成性能を改善することを確認した。
papers.why: 大規模データで flow matching を安定かつ効率よく学習させるための、計算量を抑えた OT 対応付け手法と、その効果を保証する理論を提供している。
papers.summary_en: Training stability in flow matching critically depends on how source samples are paired with data: independent random pairing introduces substantial stochasticity, and minibatch optimal transport (OT) couplings reduce this but become computationally prohibitive to scale to larger minibatches on larger, higher-dimensional datasets. This work develops a scalable online entropic OT approximation that preserves OT's benefits at much larger coupling sizes, proving strict reductions in full stochastic-gradient variance and integration error relative to independent pairing for both unregularized and entropic OT, with improvements strengthening as the online coupling minibatch grows. Experiments on single-cell gene interpolation-flow and image-flow training confirm that larger online couplings consistently improve training stability and final generation performance.
papers.why_en: Provides a computationally scalable OT coupling method with accompanying theory guaranteeing reduced gradient variance and integration error, directly useful for stabilizing and scaling flow-matching training on large datasets.

papers.title: CacheSmith: Accurate RAG Serving under Latency SLOs with Adaptive KV Reuse
papers.abstract: This paper presents CacheSmith, a KV cache reuse system for RAG prefill that maximizes quality-gated SLO attainment. While context caching lowers prefill latency by reusing precomputed KV states for retrieved chunks, it misses cross-chunk attention that a full prefill would compute over concatenated inputs. Prior selective recomputation schemes tackle this problem but enforce static, one-size-fits-all configurations that fail to effectively handle request heterogeneity or dynamic latency budgets. CacheSmith decomposes selective recomputation into a three-phase workflow of WarmUp, Probe, and Patch that can be dynamically configured to exploit a wide range of cost-accuracy trade-offs. At serving time, an SLO-aware scheduler in CacheSmith forms batches to mitigate inter-request interference during layer-by-layer prefill, while a budget-aware planner configures recomputation phases across the batch to maximize the number of requests satisfying both generation quality and latency targets. Both components make fast, solver-free decisions over profiled cost-accuracy bands. On four benchmarks across varying arrival rates and burstiness levels, CacheSmith improves quality-gated SLO attainment by up to 27.5%, over four state-of-the-art baselines.
papers.ja_title: レイテンシ SLO を守りながら RAG の KV キャッシュ再利用を調整する CacheSmith
papers.summary: RAG (検索拡張生成) の前処理 (prefill) では取得した文書チャンクの KV キャッシュを再利用して遅延を減らせるが、本来は結合した入力全体で計算すべきチャンク間の attention を見落としてしまう。既存の選択的再計算手法は一律の静的設定しか使えず、request ごとの違いや変動する遅延予算にうまく対応できなかった。CacheSmith は再計算を WarmUp・Probe・Patch の 3 段階に分けて動的に設定し、SLO を考慮したスケジューラでバッチ編成し、予算を考慮したプランナーで品質と遅延の両方を満たす request 数を最大化する。4 つのベンチマークで、4 つの最先端手法と比べて品質条件つき SLO 達成率を最大 27.5% 改善した。
papers.why: RAG 推論サービングで品質とレイテンシのトレードオフを request ごとに動的制御する具体的な仕組みを示し、サービング基盤の設計にそのまま応用できる。
papers.summary_en: In RAG prefill, context caching lowers latency by reusing precomputed KV states for retrieved chunks but misses the cross-chunk attention that a full prefill over concatenated inputs would compute; prior selective recomputation schemes use static, one-size-fits-all configurations that fail to handle request heterogeneity or dynamic latency budgets. CacheSmith decomposes selective recomputation into a dynamically configurable WarmUp-Probe-Patch workflow, with an SLO-aware scheduler that batches requests to mitigate interference and a budget-aware planner that configures recomputation to maximize requests meeting both quality and latency targets. Across four benchmarks under varying arrival rates and burstiness, CacheSmith improves quality-gated SLO attainment by up to 27.5% over four state-of-the-art baselines.
papers.why_en: Shows a concrete serving-system design for dynamically trading off quality and latency per request in RAG prefill, directly applicable to building latency-aware LLM serving infrastructure.

papers.title: Non-Abelian quantum Hall states at strong Landau level mixing: finding anyons with first-principles AI
papers.abstract: Non-Abelian anyons, strange particles forming the basis of fault-tolerant topological quantum computing, are predicted to emerge in fractional quantum Hall states at even-denominator filling factors. Identifying which topological order is realized has proven to be a challenging problem that requires an accurate, non-perturbative treatment of realistic Landau level mixing, which has so far been missing from theoretical studies. Here we present the first complete solution of non-Abelian quantum Hall problem that includes all electrons and all Landau levels, for spin-polarized electrons at filling factor $ν= 3/2$. We develop a momentum-resolved neural-network variational wave function, optimized solely on the microscopic Hamiltonian, which gives direct access to the topologically degenerate ground states. Without any physics input about the expected outcome, it discovers a degenerate ground-state manifold whose entanglement reveals anyons with quantum dimension $\sqrt{2}$, the hallmark of Ising-type non-Abelian order. By directly computing the overlap with trial wave functions, we further show that Landau level mixing favors the anti-Pfaffian over other candidate states. Our results demonstrate the power of neural-network wave functions in finding and characterizing non-Abelian anyons from first principles, in regimes of strong Landau level mixing, relevant to many recent experiments.

papers.title: How Inner Optimizers Shape Replica Scaling
papers.abstract: Training large language models (LLMs) across geographically distributed and poorly interconnected compute pools or data centers has become a topic of significant interest. This has led to increased study of local optimization methods such as DiLoco for LLMs, especially those that use local (or inner) adaptive or preconditioned optimizers, which are critical for high-performance LLM training. However, a central challenge remains: it is well known that increasing the number of model replicas (replica scaling) while fixing the total training budget leads to monotonically decreasing performance. Existing work has empirically demonstrated that the choice of inner optimizer (Muon v.s. AdamW) can significantly improve this trend, but offers only limited explanation of the performance difference. In this work, we consider a range of inner-optimizers and identify two important factors that impact replica scaling: (1) the covariance structure of the pseudo-gradients and (2) the impact of batch size on the pseudogradient's noise scale. Based on these insights, we theoretically and empirically demonstrate that whitening-based pre-conditioning is a powerful inner-optimizer desideratum. Our empirical evaluation extends the results to reveal that whitening-based inner-optimizers achieve strong replica scaling (for 8-96 replicas), with performance relative to DP improving as parameters and data are scaled.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク
学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: DiLoco 型分散学習でレプリカ数を増やしても性能が落ちない内部最適化法
papers.summary: 地理的に離れたデータセンター間で LLM (大規模言語モデル) を分散学習する DiLoco のような手法では、計算予算を固定したままレプリカ (複製されたモデル) の数を増やすと性能が単調に下がる問題がある。本研究は、疑似勾定の共分散構造とバッチサイズがノイズに与える影響という 2 つの要因を特定し、ホワイトニング (勾配の方向のばらつきを均す処理) に基づく前処理をする内部最適化器がこの劣化を大きく抑えられることを示した。8 から 96 レプリカまでの実験で、パラメータ数とデータ量を増やすほど、通常のデータ並列学習に対する性能差が縮まることを確認した。
papers.why: 複数データセンターをまたぐ LLM 学習基盤を作る人にとって、内部最適化器 (Muon や AdamW など) の選び方がレプリカ数スケーリングの性能劣化を左右する鍵であることを、理論と実験の両面から示している。
papers.summary_en: In DiLoco-style distributed LLM training across geographically separated compute pools, increasing the number of model replicas at fixed total compute budget is known to monotonically hurt performance. The authors identify the pseudo-gradient covariance structure and the effect of batch size on pseudo-gradient noise scale as key factors, and show that whitening-based preconditioning inner-optimizers substantially mitigate this degradation, achieving strong replica scaling for 8-96 replicas with performance relative to data-parallel (DP) training improving as parameters and data are scaled.
papers.why_en: Provides theoretical and empirical grounding for choosing inner optimizers in local/DiLoco-style distributed training, directly informing optimizer design for multi-datacenter LLM training.

papers.title: Plan or Retrieve First? A Scale Study of Tool Discovery Architectures
papers.abstract: Tool-augmented LLM agents discover relevant APIs from large registries before planning execution, yet finite context windows prohibit injecting all tool definitions into a single prompt. The dominant approach, which we term Retrieve-then-Plan (RtP), embeds the user query and retrieves similar tools via approximate nearest-neighbor search. We study an alternative Plan-then-Retrieve (PtR) paradigm in which the LLM first generates Abstract Tool Stubs (hypothesized function signatures describing needed capabilities) which then serve as retrieval queries against the registry. Evaluating on ToolBench (46,984 unique API endpoints, 50 categories) across single-tool (G1), intra-category multi-tool (G2), and cross-category multi-tool (G3) query subsets, we find a clear complexity-dependent crossover: RtP outperforms PtR on single-tool queries while PtR outperforms RtP on multi-tool queries. This crossover holds at every retrieval budget (k=1 to 20), is robust across registry sizes from 1k to 47k APIs, and is consistent across model families (Gemini 2.5 Flash and gpt-oss-120b). We characterize a stub-hallucination failure mode (the LLM invents plausible but non-existent API names) that acts as a double-edged sword: on simple queries PtR's stubs abstract away proper-noun signals that RtP matches directly, yet on complex queries the same mechanism decomposes multi-faceted intent into functional sub-needs. We further analyze token overhead and show that PtR's extra discovery call roughly doubles inference cost, which pays off on multi-tool queries but hurts on single-tool ones, motivating complexity-adaptive routing as a practical direction, one that can be driven by a zero-cost signal already present in the pipeline (RtP's top-1 retrieval score).

papers.title: DexMimic: A Generalist Dexterous Hand-Object Tracking Policy via Value-Guided Reset Allocation
papers.abstract: Achieving human-like dexterous manipulation remains a central challenge in robotics. Learning from human hand-object interaction (HOI) datasets offers a promising pathway to diverse dexterous skills, yet existing physics-based approaches train specialist policies for individual trajectories, thereby limiting skill reuse at scale. We introduce DexMimic, a generalist dexterous hand-object tracking policy jointly trained across diverse HOI trajectories. Efficient joint training requires allocating each rollout to both an undertrained phase and a starting state that supports continued tracking. DexMimic realizes this insight through Value-Guided Reset Allocation, which adapts the initialization distribution online to prioritize difficult phases and select reset states with higher expected tracking returns. We further introduce a benchmark spanning training, fine-tuning, and generalization. Experiments show improved tracking success and training efficiency, faster fine-tuning, and the potential for zero-shot generalization to unseen trajectories and objects; larger training sets further improve efficiency and generalization. Finally, we validate DexMimic on a real-world dexterous manipulation platform.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング

papers.title: Learning in Strategic Queuing with Geometric Recharge: From Bandits to Systems
papers.abstract: We study packet routing in queuing systems where queues act as selfish, myopic agents that use no-regret learning algorithms to select servers with unknown service rates. To model the small buffers used in data centers, we assume that each server has a single-packet buffer. Even such a tiny buffer already captures the features of buffering: routers can exploit multiple servers while accepted packets remain in service, but packets can occupy servers for multiple rounds, complicating future service and learning. We first analyze a single queue routing packets to $m$ buffered servers with service rates $μ_1, \dots, μ_m$. This setting is equivalent to an instance of the recharging bandits problem with geometric recharge. We prove that any no-regret learner achieves a long-run average throughput of at least the Hamacher sum of the server rates, and that this bound is tight. Consequently, a single no-regret queue is stable if and only if its arrival rate is below the Hamacher sum of the server rates. Moreover, comparing against an optimal policy, we show that any no-regret learner is at least $0.77$-competitive, which is also tight. We then study multi-queue systems where $n$ queues with arrival rates $λ_1, \dots, λ_n$, each at most $λ_{\max}$, compete for service from $m$ buffered servers. We show that the smallest overprovisioning factor that guarantees the system to be stable under high-probability no-regret learning is $\frac{1}{1-λ_{\max}}$. Equivalently, in terms of the total arrival and service rates, the condition $\sum_{i=1}^n λ_i < (1-λ_{\max})\sum_{j=1}^m μ_j$ is sufficient, and sometimes necessary, for stability under no-regret learning. In particular, for $λ_{\max} = 1/2$, this improves the upper bound of Abel et al. (EC 2026) from $3$ to $2$, matching their lower bound and resolving their open question.
papers.theme: 集団通信・ネットワーク
papers.ja_title: 小さいバッファを持つデータセンター型キューイングの安定性を後悔なし学習で解析
papers.summary: データセンターのルーターのように、キュー (待ち行列) がどのサーバにパケットを送るかを後悔なし学習 (無反省学習、過去の損失を見て徐々に賢くなる手法) で選ぶ状況を調べた。1 個のパケットしか保持できない極小バッファのサーバ群でも、単一キューはサーバの処理速度の「ハマッハー和」以上のスループット (処理量) を確実に出せることを証明し、最適な方策との比較でも 0.77 倍以上の性能を保証できることを示した。さらに複数キューが同時に競合する場合に必要な過剰プロビジョニング (余裕を持たせた処理能力の確保) の係数を導き、先行研究の上界 3 を 2 に改善して下界と一致させ、未解決だった問題を解決した。
papers.why: データセンター内のロードバランシングやパケットルーティングの安定性保証に関する理論的な土台を与え、ネットワーク設計やスケジューリングアルゴリズムの検証基準として使える。
papers.summary_en: The paper studies packet routing in data-center-like queuing systems where queues act as selfish agents using no-regret learning to pick servers with single-packet buffers. It proves that any no-regret queue achieves throughput at least the Hamacher sum of server service rates (tight), and is at least 0.77-competitive against an optimal policy (also tight). For multi-queue systems, it derives the minimal overprovisioning factor needed for stability under no-regret learning, improving the prior upper bound from 3 to 2 for λ_max=1/2 and matching the known lower bound, resolving an open question.
papers.why_en: Offers a theoretical foundation for stability guarantees of load balancing and packet routing in data centers, useful as a benchmark for designing and verifying network scheduling algorithms.

papers.title: Titan-Llama: Retrofitting Pre-trained LLMs with External Neural Memory Modules
papers.abstract: Transformers are efficient to pre-train at scale because attention permits parallel computation across sequence positions, but long-context inference requires increasingly large KV caches. Efficient recurrent alternatives reduce the asymptotic complexity of inference, but their sequential dependence limits token-wise parallelism during training, making them harder to scale. Further, the current paradigm of extending long context tasks creates competing notions of retaining information precisely and keeping long-context inference efficient. To address this gap, we introduce Titan-Llama, a post-training method for retrofitting attention-based language models with a hierarchical memory architecture that updates parameters at test-time. Titan-Llama applies a blockwise attention mask and preserves full-fidelity attention over recent tokens while compressing historical context into recurrent, fixed-size neural memory modules (NMMs). Our formulation allows pre-trained attention layers to be replaced without training a new language model from scratch. On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, Titan-Llama raises accuracy over segmented attention windows from 23.87\% to 40.51\% on QuALITY and from 14.50\% to 40.75\% on LongHealth. Inference benchmarks show more than 20\% faster prefill, 37\% faster decode at medium context lengths, and 24\% lower steady-state decode memory usage in the evaluated configurations. Together, these results demonstrate that incorporating memory architecture mechanisms that utilize test-time training effectively modulates long-context behavior of pre-trained models, offering a practical route to adapting pre-trained transformers for efficient long-context inference. Our code is released on Github \href{https://github.com/sarahpannn/titans-pytorch/tree/main}{GitHub}
papers.ja_title: Titan-Llama: 事前学習済み LLM に外部メモリを追加して長文脈推論を効率化
papers.summary: 長い文脈を扱う Transformer は、KV キャッシュ (過去の計算結果を保存する仕組み) が肥大化して推論が重くなる課題がある。本研究は、事前学習済みの Llama モデルに、直近のトークンには通常通りの注意 (アテンション) を使い、古い情報は固定サイズの神経メモリモジュールに圧縮して保持する仕組みを後付けする Titan-Llama を提案した。Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct で、区切りウィンドウ型の注意と比べて QuALITY の精度を 23.87% から 40.51% に、LongHealth を 14.50% から 40.75% に上げ、さらに prefill (入力処理) を 20% 以上、decode (生成) を中程度の文脈長で 37% 高速化し、定常状態の decode メモリ使用量を 24% 減らした。
papers.why: ゼロから再学習せずに既存の注意ベース LLM を長文脈対応の省メモリモデルに作り変える方法を示しており、推論基盤のメモリ削減・高速化を検討する人に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Transformers are efficient to pretrain but suffer from growing KV caches during long-context inference. Titan-Llama retrofits pretrained attention-based LLMs with a hierarchical memory architecture that keeps full-fidelity attention over recent tokens while compressing older context into fixed-size recurrent neural memory modules (NMMs), without retraining from scratch. On Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct, it raises accuracy over segmented-attention baselines from 23.87% to 40.51% on QuALITY and 14.50% to 40.75% on LongHealth, while giving more than 20% faster prefill, 37% faster decode at medium context lengths, and 24% lower steady-state decode memory in the evaluated configurations.
papers.why_en: Shows a practical post-training route to convert existing pretrained attention LLMs into memory-efficient, fast long-context models without training a new model from scratch, directly relevant to anyone building memory- and latency-conscious inference infrastructure.

papers.title: Spectral-MoE: Heterogeneous Per-Layer Expert Utilization in Dense-to-MoE Conversion
papers.abstract: Large language models impose substantial memory demands and arithmetic costs during inference. Dense-to-mixture-of-experts (MoE) conversion is a model optimization technique that aims to reduce these arithmetic costs. Dense-to-MoE conversion partitions pretrained feed-forward network (FFN) neurons into experts and selects a subset for each token. Leading methods fall into two categories: analytic methods produce a converted model quickly using heuristics, while learning methods produce a model much more slowly by optimizing via gradients. Both approaches, however, fix the same active expert count, or "utilization," at every layer. We introduce Spectral-MoE, which learns to allocate a utilization budget heterogeneously across layers. Its name draws a metaphor between separating a dense FFN into experts and separating a light beam into its spectrum. Spectral-MoE consists of two distinct approaches: a static approach that uses a single per-layer scalar which is shared across tokens, and a dynamic approach which emits a per-token schedule. We demonstrate that both allocators improve performance over uniform on both the analytic-based and learning-based SOTA dense-to-MoE methods. At 25% FFN utilization, dynamic allocation reduces WikiText-2 perplexity relative to uniform by 1.04, 2.96, and 2.71 points on the learned base for Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B, respectively. The corresponding reductions on the analytic base are 2.45, 6.26, and 2.17 points. On the learned base, dynamic allocation improves six-task mean accuracy over uniform by an average of 1.5, 4.2, and 3.6 percentage points across the three models at FFN utilizations of 12.5%, 25%, and 50%, respectively. These results establish per-layer expert utilization as a novel optimization axis in dense-to-MoE conversion.
papers.ja_title: Spectral-MoE: 層ごとに専門家の使用量を変える Dense から MoE への変換
papers.summary: 通常の密な (dense) LLM を推論コストの低い MoE (専門家の集まりモデル) に変換する既存手法は、どの層でも同じ数の専門家を使う「均一利用」が前提だった。Spectral-MoE は、層ごとに最適な専門家利用量を学習して割り当てる手法を提案し、静的 (層ごとに固定値) と動的 (トークンごとに変える) の 2 方式を実装した。FFN (順伝播層) 利用率 25% の設定で、Llama-2-7B・Llama-3-8B・Qwen2.5-7B において WikiText-2 のパープレキシティ (予測の不確かさを示す指標、低いほど良い) を均一割り当てより最大 6.26 ポイント改善し、6 タスクの平均精度も最大 4.2 ポイント向上させた。
papers.why: Dense から MoE への変換において「層ごとの利用量配分」という新しい最適化軸を示しており、推論コストを抑えたいモデル圧縮・サービング担当者にとって追加の改善余地を与える。
papers.summary_en: Existing dense-to-MoE conversion methods fix the same active-expert count ("utilization") at every layer. Spectral-MoE learns to allocate this utilization budget heterogeneously across layers, via a static per-layer scalar or a dynamic per-token schedule. At 25% FFN utilization, dynamic allocation reduces WikiText-2 perplexity relative to uniform allocation by up to 6.26 points and improves six-task mean accuracy by up to 4.2 percentage points across Llama-2-7B, Llama-3-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B, on both analytic- and learning-based conversion baselines.
papers.why_en: Establishes per-layer expert utilization as a new optimization axis for dense-to-MoE conversion, giving model-compression and serving engineers an additional lever to cut inference cost without extra accuracy loss.

papers.title: Write Once, Plan Many: Building Reusable Visual Planning Systems from One Scene
papers.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) can reason about visual planning tasks, but querying them for every instance incurs repeated inference cost and latency. Generating reusable planning programs offers an alternative, but constructing reliable planning systems for new problem domains without extensive supervision remains challenging. We present a training-free framework that constructs reusable perception and planning programs from a domain specification and a single practice scene without a paired solution. The central challenge is obtaining useful feedback from the limited input. Our framework addresses it by leveraging VLM's ability to provide a renderer and a dynamic model based on its scene understanding. Rendering detected states enables comparison with the practice scene, while checking simulated action outcomes against the domain specification helps expose errors in rule implementation. Together, these checks guide refinement of the grounding program and planner without requiring solution labels. After refinement and component selection, the programs are frozen and solve new instances without further VLM calls. The same framework constructs systems across domains without manual pipeline redesign. Across fifteen domain variants spanning 2D and 3D scenes with discrete and continuous state, our systems achieve 99.3% average planning success, compared with 80.9% for the strongest domain-level program-generation baseline and 90.7% for the strongest instance-level baseline. Cost analyses show a favorable success-cost trade-off, and ablations confirm the contributions of the executable domain model, execution feedback, and component selection.

papers.title: Copy-Paste Language Models
papers.abstract: Transformers are intuitively considered to be efficient at copying from their inputs. We actually show that the ability of LLMs to copy in context can be improved through explicit modeling. We propose Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs), which add a lightweight Copy-Paste head to the conventional language modeling (LM) head. CPLMs improve training efficiency, downstream performance, and offer new operating points in long-context and retrieval setups. We validate our approach by pretraining models from 135M to 1.7B parameters, showing improvements across all scales and backbones with negligible training and inference overheads. We explain the success of CPLMs by showing that they partially mitigate the LM head gradient bottleneck through an alternative gradient path.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: Copy-Paste Language Models: コピーを明示的に学習させる軽量な追加ヘッド
papers.summary: Transformer は入力をそのまま書き出す「コピー」が得意なはずだが、実際には苦手な場面があるという問題意識から、通常の言語モデルヘッドに軽量な Copy-Paste ヘッドを追加する CPLM を提案した。135M から 1.7B パラメータのモデルで事前学習を行い、学習効率・下流タスク性能の両方を、学習・推論のコスト増加をほとんどかけずに改善できることを示した。この改善は、言語モデルヘッドの勾定が詰まりやすい問題 (勾配の通り道が狭くなる現象) を、追加の勾配経路で緩和しているためだと説明している。
papers.why: ほぼコストなしで学習効率と長文脈・検索タスクの性能を上げる軽量なアーキテクチャ変更であり、LLM の構造改善や学習効率化を検討する人に実用的な選択肢を増やす。
papers.summary_en: Although transformers are intuitively thought to be good at copying from their input, the authors show this ability can be improved through explicit modeling. Copy-Paste Language Models (CPLMs) add a lightweight Copy-Paste head alongside the conventional LM head, improving training efficiency and downstream performance with negligible training and inference overhead, validated by pretraining models from 135M to 1.7B parameters across scales and backbones. They attribute the gain to CPLMs partially mitigating the LM head gradient bottleneck via an alternative gradient path.
papers.why_en: Offers a near-cost-free architectural tweak that improves training efficiency and long-context/retrieval performance, giving a practical option for anyone working on LLM architecture or training-efficiency improvements.

papers.title: Dimension-Free Scaling Laws for Size Generalization: An Exponential Separation
papers.abstract: Modern machine learning models increasingly operate on variable-size structured data, such as sets and graphs. A central requirement is \emph{size generalization}: the ability of a model trained on inputs of one size to generalize to inputs of a different, potentially much larger, size. Classical statistical learning theory, however, primarily considers fixed input domains, and its guarantees often deteriorate with input dimension. Although extensive work has established when models on sets and graphs can be transferred across input sizes, such results do not characterize the statistical cost of doing so: the sample complexity of size generalization, and its relationship to classical in-domain learning, remain largely unknown. We develop a statistical learning theory of size generalization and establish a sharp exponential separation in sample complexity. Letting $n$ denote the number of training samples, we show that polynomial source decay is insufficient for efficient size generalization: while it yields error $n^{-Θ(1)}$ and hence polynomial sample complexity for in-domain learning, size-generalization error decays only as $(\log n)^{-Θ(1)}$, yielding an exponential separation. Thus, polynomial in-domain sample complexity can become exponential across sizes. We then identify an exponential source condition under which size generalization achieves error $n^{-Θ(1)}$, recovering polynomial sample complexity. These guarantees are independent of input dimension and depend only on the number of training samples, yielding dimension-free scaling laws. We also provide matching minimax lower bounds, establishing optimality. To our knowledge, this work provides the first dimension-free minimax theory of size generalization and a rigorous characterization of when, and at what statistical cost, learning can transfer across input sizes.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: サイズ一般化のための次元フリーなスケーリング法則
papers.summary: 可変サイズの集合やグラフを扱うモデルは、小さい入力で学習して大きい入力にも対応できる「サイズ一般化」が必要だが、その統計的コストはこれまで分かっていなかった。本研究は、多項式的なデータ減衰では訓練内学習(in-domain)の誤差が n^-Θ(1) と多項式的に減る一方、サイズ一般化の誤差は (log n)^-Θ(1) としか減らず、指数関数的なギャップがあることを示した。さらに「指数的ソース条件」を満たせばサイズ一般化でも多項式的な誤差減少 (n^-Θ(1)) が得られることを示し、この上下限は入力の次元に依存しない。
papers.why: 集合・グラフ系モデルをより大きい入力サイズへ安全に拡張する際の理論的な保証と限界を与える、学習効率・スケーリングの基礎研究。
papers.summary_en: Modern models on variable-size sets/graphs need "size generalization"—transferring from training sizes to larger test sizes—but its statistical cost was largely unknown. The paper proves an exponential separation: polynomial source decay yields error n^{-Θ(1)} (polynomial sample complexity) for in-domain learning, but only (log n)^{-Θ(1)} error for size generalization, and identifies an "exponential source condition" under which size generalization regains n^{-Θ(1)} error, with matching minimax lower bounds that are dimension-free.
papers.why_en: Gives rigorous, dimension-free statistical guarantees (and fundamental limits) for transferring models trained on small sets/graphs to much larger inputs, informing scaling-law theory for structured-data learning.

papers.title: Exact Scaling Laws for a Random-Features Bigram Model
papers.abstract: Understanding neural scaling laws is increasingly important for theory and practice, yet first-principles explanations remain limited even in simple settings. In this work, we study capacity-limited scaling in a bottlenecked bigram model with power-law (Zipf) token statistics, viewed as an analytically tractable toy model of a large language model. Fixed random embeddings serve as a proxy for representational capacity and induce an explicit bottleneck of width, allowing us to derive scaling laws for prediction regret as a function of model width, vocabulary size, and the Zipf exponent. Our results complement recent theoretical accounts based on optimization dynamics by isolating scaling due purely to representational constraints. In the appropriate regime, the theory recovers the functional form of classical neural scaling laws and suggests that heavy-tailed language statistics may underlie both optimization- and capacity-driven scaling. Experiments natural language datasets (WikiText2, OpenWebText) closely match the predicted curves.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: ランダム特徴バイグラムモデルで導く厳密なスケーリング法則
papers.summary: ニューラルネットの「スケーリング法則」がなぜ成り立つのかは、単純な設定でもまだよく分かっていない。この研究は、べき乗則(Zipf 則)に従う単語頻度を持つバイグラム(2 語連鎖)モデルに、固定されたランダムな埋め込みで表現力の「幅」を制限した、解析しやすいおもちゃのモデルを作った。モデルの幅・語彙サイズ・Zipf 指数に対する予測誤差(regret)のスケーリング法則を厳密に導出し、WikiText2 や OpenWebText といった自然言語データでも理論曲線とよく一致することを確かめた。
papers.why: 最適化のダイナミクスとは別に、表現力(容量)の制約だけから生じるスケーリング法則を理論的に分離して示した点が、スケーリング則の理解を深める。
papers.summary_en: Why neural scaling laws hold remains poorly understood even in simple settings. The authors study a capacity-limited bigram model with Zipf-distributed token statistics and fixed random embeddings as an explicit width bottleneck, deriving scaling laws for prediction regret as a function of width, vocabulary size, and the Zipf exponent, and show the predicted curves closely match experiments on WikiText2 and OpenWebText.
papers.why_en: By isolating scaling behavior that arises purely from representational (capacity) constraints—separate from optimization dynamics—this gives a complementary theoretical account of why heavy-tailed language statistics produce classical neural scaling-law shapes.

papers.title: Whose turn is it? Context-guided model routing for stateful agents
papers.abstract: Model routing can reduce the cost of LLM applications by assigning simpler requests to cheaper models without sacrificing the quality of the response. However, most routers treat requests as independent. Stateful agents do not operate under this assumption: a user turn may require multiple model and tool calls, its difficulty depends on the state produced by earlier turns, and changing models can sacrifice reuse of the conversational prompt cache. We study zero-shot, cost-aware routing at the user-turn boundary, systematically varying the routing rule, access to session history, candidate models that differ in size, reasoning effort, or model provider, and prompt-cache behavior. We evaluate on multi-turn versions of SheetCopilot and SpreadsheetBench 2, where persistent workbooks and cross-turn dependencies make isolated routing decisions especially brittle. At a matched offloading rate, giving the router session history improves task pass rate over the same router without history, with gains for every model pair; history-aware routing remains within one point of always using the expensive model. We also found that cost depends on execution dynamics rather than token prices alone: the cheaper model's per-task cost advantage narrows from 6.8x to 3.2x on longer sessions. A closed form cache analysis further shows that downward switches (expensive to cheap) recover their cache cost within two LLM calls, whereas upward switches do not break even under the evaluated conditions. Together, these results show that agent routing is a sequential decision problem: effective policies must account for what happened earlier in the session and for the asymmetric cost of switching models.
papers.ja_title: 会話の履歴を見て LLM を使い分ける、状態を持つエージェントのためのルーティング
papers.summary: LLM アプリのコストを下げるために安いモデルと高いモデルを使い分ける「ルーティング」は、これまで各リクエストを独立に扱っていたが、複数ターンに渡るエージェントでは前のターンの状態次第で難易度が変わり、モデルを切り替えるとプロンプトキャッシュの再利用も失われる。本研究は会話履歴を使った「状態を考慮したルーティング」を評価し、同じオフロード率で履歴なしのルーターより正答率が改善し、常に高性能モデルを使う場合と比べて 1 ポイント以内の差に収まることを示した。また、長いセッションでは安いモデルのコスト優位が 6.8 倍から 3.2 倍に縮むこと、キャッシュコストは安いモデルへの切り替え(下方)なら 2 回の呼び出しで回収できるが、高いモデルへの切り替え(上方)では評価条件下で回収できないことを示した。
papers.why: マルチターンのエージェント基盤を運用する人にとって、トークン価格だけでなくキャッシュの損益分岐やセッション履歴を考慮したルーティング設計の指針を与える。
papers.summary_en: Model routing cuts LLM app costs by sending easy requests to cheaper models, but prior routers treat requests independently, ignoring that in stateful, multi-turn agents a turn's difficulty depends on prior state and that switching models forfeits prompt-cache reuse. The paper shows that giving a zero-shot router session history improves task pass rate at matched offloading rates (within one point of always using the expensive model) across every model pair tested, that the cheap model's per-task cost advantage narrows from 6.8x to 3.2x on longer sessions, and that a closed-form cache analysis shows downward (expensive→cheap) switches recover their cache cost within two calls while upward switches do not break even under the evaluated conditions.
papers.why_en: Offers concrete guidance for building cost-aware routing in multi-turn agent serving stacks, showing routing is a sequential decision problem shaped by cache economics and session history, not just per-request token price.

review.note: オフロード率を揃えて比較する、キャッシュの損益分岐点を事前に計算するといった、ルーティング評価で陥りやすい落とし穴を示す観点。
review.note_en: Shows an evaluation pitfall in routing research: compare at matched offloading rates and account for cache break-even costs, not raw price-per-token alone.

papers.title: Verifier-Grounded Agentic RL for Provably Correct Code
papers.abstract: Reinforcement learning for code usually rewards passing tests, which a model can do while remaining wrong on the inputs the tests do not cover. A program verifier instead decides whether a program satisfies a formal specification for all inputs. Language models are almost always paired with verifiers at inference time only, and turning a verifier into a reward raises two difficulties. It reports only acceptance or rejection, which gives no gradient when every attempt fails, and a policy can cheat it, most simply by telling it to assume what the proof was supposed to establish. We build an agentic environment and reward that address both. The reward reads the verifier's diagnostics rather than its verdict, scoring a candidate by the weighted fraction of proof obligations it discharges, extended with hidden probes from a reference proof's annotations. An integrity audit outranks the verifier, rejecting any candidate that alters the specification or assumes what it was meant to prove. The model works as an agent against a live verifier over many turns, with a separately trained proof specialist as a frozen collaborator. Across Qwen3 models from 1.7B to 14B and a 35B Qwen3.6 mixture-of-experts model, held-out verification on code generation rises from 66.1% to 93.5% on DafnyBench and from 56.3% to 100% on SWE-Proof. This reward leads every other training signal we compare, including a binary pass-or-fail reward trained under otherwise identical settings, with the widest margin on code generation. When the agent must also deliver the repository patch, graded by each project's withheld tests, the fraction of held-out issues it resolves rises from 59.6% to 72.5%. Evaluated unchanged on three verification suites withheld from training, the checkpoints improve on all of them, including one whose language and verifier are absent from training.
papers.ja_title: 証明の中身まで読んで報酬にする、検証器付きコード生成の強化学習
papers.summary: コード生成の強化学習では通常テストの合格だけを報酬にするが、テストが通っても未検証の入力では誤っている場合がある。本研究はプログラム検証器(formal specification を満たすか判定する仕組み)の合格/不合格だけでなく、検証器が出す診断情報(証明すべき義務のうちどれだけ果たせたか)を重み付き割合として報酬にし、仕様を改ざんするなどの不正を検出する監査機構も組み合わせた。Qwen3 の 1.7B から 14B、35B の MoE モデルで学習したところ、DafnyBench での検証成功率が 66.1% から 93.5% に、SWE-Proof では 56.3% から 100% に向上し、合否のみの二値報酬より一貫して高い性能を示した。
papers.why: 合否だけでは学習の勾配が得られないという検証器報酬の根本課題に、診断情報の重み付け利用と不正検出の監査で対処する、RL 後学習の報酬設計の具体例。
papers.summary_en: RL for code usually rewards passing tests, which a model can satisfy while still being wrong on uncovered inputs, whereas a formal verifier checks whether a program meets a specification for all inputs. The paper turns verifier diagnostics (the weighted fraction of proof obligations discharged, plus hidden probes from reference proofs) into a dense reward, combined with an integrity audit that rejects candidates cheating the specification; across Qwen3 models from 1.7B to 14B and a 35B MoE model, held-out verification rises from 66.1% to 93.5% on DafnyBench and from 56.3% to 100% on SWE-Proof, outperforming a binary pass/fail reward under identical settings.
papers.why_en: Addresses the core difficulty that binary verifier rewards give no gradient when every attempt fails and are gameable, offering a concrete reward-design pattern (diagnostic-based dense reward plus an anti-cheating audit) for RL post-training on formally-checkable tasks.

papers.title: DTDD: Divergence-Triggered Dynamic Distillation for Reliable On-Policy Supervision
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense token-level supervision on student rollouts, but this supervision can become unreliable when the student and teacher diverge, either because of a large initial policy gap or compounding errors in long-horizon reasoning and tool use. We introduce Divergence-Triggered Dynamic Distillation (DTDD), an adaptive OPD framework that uses segment-level student-teacher divergence to trigger teacher takeover during training. When divergence triggers an intervention during reasoning, the student prefix continues to receive standard OPD supervision. The teacher then generates a recovery suffix, which the student learns through behavior cloning, using cross-entropy on the teacher-generated tokens. We evaluate DTDD in three regimes: long-horizon reasoning, distillation from a base initialization without offline supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and multi-turn agents. We also compare alternative trigger designs and teacher-intervention rates. DTDD reduces the post-warmup peak gradient norm by $8.6\times$ and, from a base initialization, reaches $21.3\%$ held-out math accuracy in $2.6\times$ fewer optimizer updates than OPD; both methods finish near $22\%$. It improves best-observed performance by $4.8$ and $4.1$ percentage points on ALFWorld with LoRA and agentic code, respectively. Ablations show that segment-averaged triggers outperform token-spike triggers. Behavior cloning is also more effective than the tested OPD surrogate for training teacher-generated recoveries. Across 23 experimental arms, takeover tends to help when the teacher substantially outperforms the OPD-trained student, provided that the teacher can recover from student-visited states, the student can learn those recoveries, and teacher intervention is neither excessive nor insufficient.
papers.ja_title: 生徒と教師のズレを検知してだけ教師が介入する蒸留手法 DTDD
papers.summary: オンポリシー蒸留(生徒自身の行動列に対してトークンごとに教師の助言を与える手法)は、生徒と教師の方針が大きくズレると信頼できなくなる。本研究は、セグメント単位でのズレを検知したときだけ教師が続きを生成し、生徒がそれを模倣学習で学ぶ DTDD を提案した。ウォームアップ後の勾配ノルムの最大値を 8.6 倍小さくし、SFT なしの初期状態からの学習では通常の OPD より 2.6 倍少ない更新回数で同等の正解率(約 21〜22%)に到達し、ALFWorld や agentic code タスクでも最良性能を 4.1〜4.8 ポイント改善した。
papers.why: 教師への過度な依存や不要な介入を避けながら、長い推論やツール利用を伴う RL 後学習を安定させる具体的な蒸留トリガー設計を示す。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation gives dense token-level teacher supervision on student rollouts, but this becomes unreliable once student and teacher diverge. DTDD monitors segment-level student-teacher divergence and lets the teacher take over and generate a recovery suffix (learned via behavior cloning) only when divergence is triggered; it cuts the post-warmup peak gradient norm by 8.6x, reaches 21.3% held-out math accuracy in 2.6x fewer optimizer updates than OPD from a base initialization (both finishing near 22%), and improves best-observed performance by 4.1-4.8 points on ALFWorld and agentic code.
papers.why_en: Provides a concrete trigger-based intervention design for making long-horizon, tool-using RL post-training more stable without over- or under-relying on a teacher.

papers.title: Parallel Sparse Outputs for Tensor Compilers
papers.abstract: Sparse tensor compilers are commonly used high-performance tools that optimize tensor algebra programs over notoriously complex sparse data structures. Despite the ever-increasing size and scale of sparse datasets, there exists astonishingly little research on developing a parallel sparse tensor compiler. Existing approaches fail to parallelize or make assumptions about access patterns or output formats that limit generality. This paper presents Birdseed, the first tensor compiler to support all loop orderings over any standard sparse format in parallel. More specifically, Birdseed supports parallel sparse scatters and directly writes into list, bytemap, hash, and dense levels of fibertree sparse formats. Our approach exhibits asymptotic memory and time improvements over all previous work. We additionally demonstrate empirical speedups on challenging kernels to parallelize, such as histogram construction and SpMSpV.
papers.ja_title: あらゆるループ順序・スパース形式を並列化できるテンソルコンパイラ Birdseed
papers.summary: スパース(疎)なテンソル演算を最適化するコンパイラは広く使われるが、並列化を扱う研究はほとんどなく、既存手法はアクセスパターンや出力形式を限定していた。本研究は、list・bytemap・hash・dense の各レベル(fibertree 形式のスパース表現)に対して、どんなループ順序でも並列にスパースな書き込み(scatter)ができる初のテンソルコンパイラ Birdseed を作った。既存手法に対して漸近的なメモリ・時間効率が改善し、ヒストグラム構築や SpMSpV といった並列化が難しいカーネルで実際に高速化を確認した。
papers.why: カーネル実装の低レベルな最適化として、スパーステンソル演算を汎用的かつ並列に扱える基盤を示しており、カーネル・低精度分野の実装に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: Sparse tensor compilers are widely used but parallel sparse tensor compilation is barely studied, with existing approaches restricting access patterns or output formats. Birdseed is presented as the first tensor compiler to support all loop orderings over any standard sparse format in parallel, directly writing parallel sparse scatters into list, bytemap, hash, and dense levels of fibertree sparse formats, with asymptotic memory and time improvements over prior work and empirical speedups on hard-to-parallelize kernels like histogram construction and SpMSpV.
papers.why_en: Gives kernel engineers a general, provably more efficient way to parallelize sparse tensor operations across arbitrary formats and loop orders, directly relevant to building faster sparse kernels.

papers.title: SERO: Learning from Executable Oracle Continuations for Long-Horizon Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Long-horizon agentic RL is constrained by the futures visited by the current policy. When rollouts fail to reach useful behaviors, improved credit assignment cannot provide supervision for states and actions that were never encountered. On-policy distillation (OPD) introduces teacher guidance on policy-induced states, and recent multi-turn variants improve how this guidance is scheduled, replayed, refined, or validated. However, they do not directly use the oracle-controlled future itself as the training trajectory. We introduce \textbf{State-Rooted Executable Rollout Optimization (SERO)}, which augments on-policy agentic RL with executable oracle continuations. SERO restores a state actually reached by the current policy and lets a training-only oracle continue interacting with the real environment, making the downstream observations and oracle actions themselves available for learning. It then applies \textbf{policy-reachability weighting}, which weights each oracle step by the frozen behavior policy's compatibility with the preceding oracle actions. This allows deeper supervision to become effective as the policy becomes more compatible with the oracle branch. The oracle loss is optimized separately from the base RL estimator and no oracle is used at inference time. We evaluate SERO on two challenging interactive-agent benchmarks, ALFWorld and WebShop, using Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. On ALFWorld, learning the full executable continuation is substantially more effective than supervising only the root oracle action, while policy-reachability weighting further improves out-of-distribution performance.
papers.ja_title: オラクルに環境を実際に先まで動かしてもらう長期タスク向け強化学習 SERO
papers.summary: 長期タスクの強化学習では、方針(ポリシー)が到達できなかった状態には学習の手がかりを与えられないという制約がある。本研究は、方針が実際に到達した状態から、学習専用の「オラクル(訓練時だけ使える理想的な行動者)」に実環境を先まで動かしてもらい、その先の観測と行動をそのまま学習データにする SERO を提案した。さらにオラクルの各手順を、それ以前のオラクル行動と現在の方針がどれだけ合っているかで重み付ける「方針到達可能性重み付け」を導入し、ALFWorld と WebShop で Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct を用いて評価し、根本のオラクル行動だけを教えるより続きまで学ぶ方が効果的であること、重み付けが分布外性能をさらに高めることを示した。
papers.why: 方針が訪れた先の未知の状況に対しても、実環境でオラクルを走らせて教師データを作るという、長期タスク RL のデータ不足問題への実践的な対処法を示す。
papers.summary_en: Long-horizon agentic RL is limited to futures the current policy actually visits, so improved credit assignment cannot supervise states/actions it never reaches. SERO restores a state the policy actually reached and lets a training-only oracle keep interacting with the real environment, using the resulting observations and oracle actions as training data, weighted by how compatible the frozen policy is with the preceding oracle actions ("policy-reachability weighting"); on ALFWorld and WebShop with Qwen2.5-1.5B/7B-Instruct, learning the full executable continuation beats supervising only the root oracle action, and reachability weighting further improves out-of-distribution performance.
papers.why_en: Offers a practical way to generate deeper teacher supervision for long-horizon RL by actually executing an oracle continuation in the real environment from policy-reached states, rather than relying only on single-step oracle guidance.

papers.title: AgentSafeEvo: Adversarial Co-Evolution for LLM Agent Safety
papers.abstract: Large language model (LLM) agents accomplish complex tasks through multi-turn interactions with external tools. However, malicious content embedded in user queries, tool descriptions, or environment observations can manipulate their decisions and induce unsafe actions. Adversarial co-evolution has emerged as an effective approach to strengthening LLM safety, but existing work primarily focuses on language-level safety or indirect prompt injection in web tasks. In this paper, we introduce AgentSafeEvo, a co-evolutionary reinforcement learning framework for agent safety built on an attacker-defender game spanning diverse tasks and attack types. The attacker learns to construct adversarial agent tasks that expose weaknesses in the defender's tool use, while the defender learns to complete tasks safely under these attacks. We further introduce learnability-guided task weighting, which uses within-task defender-reward variability to adjust each task's contribution to attacker and defender updates. Extensive experiments on agent safety and general capability benchmarks demonstrate that our method improves adversarial robustness while maintaining general agent capabilities.
papers.ja_title: 攻撃者とエージェントを同時に鍛える安全性強化のための共進化強化学習
papers.summary: ツールを使う LLM エージェントは、ユーザーの問い合わせやツールの説明、環境からの観測に埋め込まれた悪意ある内容によって危険な行動を誘導されうる。本研究は、攻撃側(防御側の弱点を突く課題を作る)と防御側(攻撃を受けながら安全に課題を達成する)を交互に強くしていく共進化型強化学習の枠組み AgentSafeEvo を提案し、各課題内で防御側の報酬のばらつきを見て課題の重みを調整する手法も加えた。安全性ベンチマークと汎用能力ベンチマークの両方で、敵対的攻撃への強さを高めつつ通常の性能も保てることを確認した。
papers.why: 言語レベルの安全性やウェブタスクの間接的プロンプト注入に限られていた従来の共進化研究を、多様なタスク・攻撃タイプに広げた安全性強化の RL 枠組みを示す。
papers.summary_en: Tool-using LLM agents can be manipulated into unsafe actions by malicious content embedded in user queries, tool descriptions, or environment observations. AgentSafeEvo introduces a co-evolutionary RL framework in which an attacker learns to craft adversarial agent tasks exposing weaknesses in the defender's tool use while the defender learns to complete tasks safely, plus a learnability-guided task weighting scheme based on within-task reward variability; experiments show improved adversarial robustness while maintaining general agent capability.
papers.why_en: Extends prior adversarial co-evolution work (previously limited to language-level safety or web prompt injection) into an RL post-training framework spanning diverse agentic tasks and attack types.

papers.title: Beyond the Trial-and-Error Loop: Hybrid Projection and Automated Tuning for Distributed Training
papers.abstract: Configuring distributed LLM training across hundreds of GPUs requires jointly optimizing tensor, pipeline, expert, context, and data parallelism alongside micro-batch size, recomputation, sharding, and overlap, a combinatorial space where memory legality can hinge on a single byte of activation accounting. Today, teams navigate it through expensive multi-node trial and error, burning GPU-hours on crashes and suboptimal recipes. We present Primus Projection, which closes this loop with two coupled components. First, a hybrid projection engine that measures what it can and simulates what it cannot: GPU microbenchmarks on as few as a single device capture compute kernels and any in-scope communication; a sub-node downscale-measure-upscale workflow analytically restores out-of-scope collectives, FSDP overlap, and the full pipeline schedule at the multi-node target. A pure simulation mode runs entirely on CPU, enabling pre-silicon planning without any GPU. Second, the Primus Tuning Agent treats the projection engine as a fast scoring oracle (seconds per candidate instead of tens of minutes) and uses it to drive an intelligent search over the configuration space. A deterministic seed planner sweeps single axes; an LLM investigation loop proposes cross-axis combinations the planner cannot reach, with an analytic memory pre-filter that rejects infeasible candidates before any GPU time is spent. Validated on Llama 3.1 (dense) and Mixtral 8x22B (MoE) across two GPU generations, all projections stay within ~10% of measured multi-node throughput, and fidelity holds at production scale: 4.7% error on DeepSeek V3 671B at 1,024 GPUs and 1.9% on Qwen3-235B-A22B at 256 GPUs. In a Mixtral 8x22B case study, the Primus Tuning Agent discovers a configuration delivering +27% throughput over the published 4-node BF16 reference at the same scale, in under 30 minutes of single-node exploration.
papers.ja_title: 分散学習の設定探索を高速化する Primus Projection
papers.summary: LLM の分散学習では GPU 数百台にわたるテンソル並列・パイプライン並列などの設定探索に多大な GPU 時間がかかる。Primus Projection は少数の GPU での実測とシミュレーションを組み合わせて多数ノードでのスループットを予測するハイブリッド投影エンジンと、それを高速なスコアリングに使う探索エージェントを提案した。1,024 GPU で DeepSeek V3 671B の予測誤差を 4.7%、256 GPU で Qwen3-235B-A22B で 1.9% に抑え、Mixtral 8x22B では 30 分以内の単一ノード探索で公開レシピより 27% 高いスループットの設定を見つけた。
papers.why: 分散学習基盤を作る人にとって、実機を使わずに巨大クラスタの設定探索コストを削減できる実践的な手法であり、低コストな測定とシミュレーションの組み合わせが新しい。
papers.summary_en: Configuring distributed LLM training across hundreds of GPUs is costly, burning GPU-hours on crashes from trial and error. Primus Projection combines single/few-GPU microbenchmarks with analytic simulation to project multi-node throughput, then drives a tuning agent that scores candidate configs in seconds instead of tens of minutes. Projections stay within ~10% of measured throughput, reaching 4.7% error on DeepSeek V3 671B at 1,024 GPUs and 1.9% on Qwen3-235B-A22B at 256 GPUs, and in a Mixtral 8x22B case study the agent discovers a config giving +27% throughput over the published 4-node BF16 reference in under 30 minutes of single-node exploration.
papers.why_en: Offers a practical way for distributed-training infrastructure builders to prune the combinatorial configuration space without burning multi-node GPU-hours, using measured microbenchmarks plus simulation as a fast scoring oracle for search.

papers.title: VideoHarness-SRSI: Structured Recursive Self-Improvement for Video Understanding Harness
papers.abstract: LLM system capabilities depend not only on model parameters but also on the executable harnesses that organize information acquisition, tool use, reasoning, and memory. Recursive harness evolution can automate their design, but how it can reliably discover generalizable systems from limited, noisy, and repeatedly reused feedback remains unclear. We study this question in agentic video understanding, where rich multimodal evidence and coupled mechanisms make harness optimization challenging. We first introduce VHarness-BRSI, a recursive self-improvement framework that evolves video harnesses around a frozen vision-language model. Analyzing over 4,000 evolved candidates, we find it competitive with hand-engineered systems but identify three interconnected failure modes: validation overfitting, search-budget dilution, and the early-experience trap. We trace all three to a common root: the same imperfect validation evidence drives both harness revisions and the proposer's search strategy. We therefore propose VHarness-SRSI, an evidence-governed framework in which every search decision rests on evidence that is transferable, sufficient, and gathered before the search commits. It restricts the proposer to content-free feedback, informs exploration with instrumented warm-up experiments, and develops mechanisms in isolated probe-race branches before factorial composition and joint refinement. Across four video understanding benchmarks, VideoHarness-SRSI improves the equally weighted mean held-out score by 6.2% relative to VideoHarness-BRSI and reduces the mean validation-test gap by 37.9%. Reliable harness evolution thus depends on how search is organized and informed, not only on how well it optimizes validation performance.
topics: 集団通信・ネットワーク

papers.title: Progress-Aware Distillation for Mitigating Stagnation in Small Language Model Agents
papers.abstract: While LLM-based agent systems have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in reasoning and solving complex real-world tasks, they also come with substantial token consumption and inference latency, limiting their practical deployment. To enhance the efficiency of agent systems, recent efforts have focused on transferring agentic capabilities from large-scale models to small language models (SLMs) via supervised fine-tuning-based distillation. Nevertheless, as interaction trajectories grow longer, involving extended reasoning-action chains and extensive environmental feedback, distilled student agents tend to experience progress stagnation: becoming trapped in unproductive loops characterized by persistent failed strategies and difficulty making meaningful progress. Our systematic analysis shows that this phenomenon consistently occurs across diverse SLMs and task domains. To address this issue, we propose Progress-Aware Distillation (ProD), which explicitly detects and penalizes stagnation in student-generated trajectories. ProD encodes the stagnation gap between student and teacher into an adaptive margin for dynamically penalizing possible stagnation. By iteratively applying this procedure, ProD enables student agents to progressively approximate teacher behavior. Extensive experiments involving 8 SLMs, ranging from 0.6B to 8B parameters, on both in-domain and out-of-domain benchmarks, demonstrate that ProD substantially mitigates progress stagnation while enhancing both the success rates and task-completion efficiency of distilled SLM agents.
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 停滞を防ぐ小型言語モデルエージェントの蒸留手法 ProD
papers.summary: 大型モデル (LLM) の推論能力を小型モデル (SLM) に蒸留すると、長い対話では学生モデルが同じ失敗戦略を繰り返す「停滞」に陥りやすいという問題がある。ProD は学生と教師の停滞差を適応的なマージンとして損失に組み込み、停滞を検知して罰則を与える蒸留手法を提案した。0.6B から 8B までの 8 個の SLM で実験し、タスク内外のベンチマークで成功率とタスク完了効率を大きく改善した。
papers.why: エージェント型 LLM を軽量モデルへ蒸留する際の典型的な失敗モードとその対処法を示しており、推論コスト削減を目指す開発者に実践的な指針となる。
papers.summary_en: Distilling agentic reasoning from large LLMs into small language models (SLMs) via supervised fine-tuning often causes "progress stagnation," where the distilled student gets stuck repeating failed strategies in long trajectories. Progress-Aware Distillation (ProD) explicitly detects this stagnation gap between student and teacher and encodes it as an adaptive margin to penalize it during training. Across 8 SLMs from 0.6B to 8B parameters on in- and out-of-domain benchmarks, ProD substantially mitigates stagnation while improving both success rate and task-completion efficiency.
papers.why_en: Identifies a concrete, recurring failure mode in SFT-based agent distillation and offers a targeted fix, useful for teams trying to deploy cheaper SLM-based agents without losing capability.

papers.title: Retrieve What Helps, Only When It Helps: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Selective Retrieval-Augmented Machine Translation
papers.abstract: Retrieving external knowledge can improve large language model (LLM) translation by providing supplementary information such as idiom interpretations and terminology. However, existing retrieval-augmented machine translation systems typically apply predefined retrieval strategies uniformly across all inputs. We argue that translation operates in a partial-evidence regime: LLM's parametric knowledge suffices for many inputs, while external evidence benefits a subset and usually supports rather than directly provides the desired translation. This creates two challenges: deciding when to retrieve and what evidence to acquire. We introduce Selective Retrieval-Augmented Translation (SRAT), an agentic reinforcement learning framework that learns when to translate directly or retrieve, what to retrieve, and how to integrate these decisions by optimizing final translation quality. To align evidence retrieval with downstream translation quality rather than simple semantic similarity, we further develop joint Plackett--Luce optimization and translation-quality contrastive training for retriever-training. Experiments on idiom, knowledge-intensive, and document-level translation with offline or online retrieval show that SRAT consistently outperforms never- and always-retrieve baselines, and quality-aligned retriever training provides further gains when similarity-based retrieval is insufficient. The results demonstrate the benefit of treating retrieval as a learnable translation action rather than fixed preprocessing.
papers.ja_title: 必要な時だけ検索する翻訳向け強化学習フレームワーク SRAT
papers.summary: 機械翻訳に外部知識検索を組み込む既存手法は、入力の性質にかかわらず同じ検索戦略を一律に使ってしまう。SRAT は強化学習 (RL) を使い、最終的な翻訳品質を指標として「検索するか」「何を検索するか」をエージェントに学習させる手法を提案した。慣用句・専門知識・文書レベルの翻訳実験で、常に検索する・一度も検索しないベースラインより一貫して高い品質を達成した。
papers.why: 検索を固定の前処理ではなく学習可能な行動として RL で最適化するという発想は、検索拡張生成 (RAG) を含む agentic RL の基盤設計に応用できる。
papers.summary_en: Existing retrieval-augmented machine translation systems apply the same fixed retrieval strategy regardless of input, even though an LLM's parametric knowledge already suffices for many sentences. SRAT is an agentic reinforcement learning framework that learns when to retrieve, what evidence to retrieve, and how to integrate it by optimizing final translation quality directly, using joint Plackett-Luce optimization and translation-quality contrastive retriever training. Across idiom, knowledge-intensive, and document-level translation, SRAT consistently outperforms both never-retrieve and always-retrieve baselines.
papers.why_en: Treating retrieval as a learnable action optimized end-to-end via RL, rather than fixed preprocessing, is a generalizable idea for building agentic RAG systems beyond translation.
