papers.title: LabCompiler: A Framework for Verifiable Human-Machine Laboratory Execution from Imperfect Protocols
papers.abstract: Closing the loop of AI-driven science requires reliably translating natural-language protocols into executable laboratory workflows despite protocol defects and heterogeneous hardware. Existing approaches often couple scientific interpretation with device-specific code generation, making errors difficult to localize and limiting reuse across laboratory platforms. We introduce LabCompiler, a robust protocol-to-execution framework that transforms imperfect natural-language protocols into verifiable human-machine workflows. Its protocol firewall diagnoses and repairs defects before compilation while preserving unaffected content, guided by troubleshooting knowledge accumulated through perturbation-guided self-evolution. A two-level, device-agnostic graph representation separates experimental semantics from hardware-specific implementation and supports capability-based device assignment with coordinated human execution. We further introduce a protocol recovery benchmark covering four controlled perturbation types and naturally occurring errors collected from protocols written by iGEM participants. Experiments show that LabCompiler outperforms frontier LLMs in protocol error correction while enabling coordinated human-machine execution across heterogeneous, partially automated laboratory settings.

papers.title: Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation for Language Models
papers.abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) transfers knowledge from a teacher model to a student along student-generated trajectories, typically by minimizing the reverse Kullback-Leibler (RKL) divergence. However, RKL can provide weak corrective signals for teacher-supported tokens to which the student assigns very low probability. This raises two questions: which positions are most consequential for the behavioral gap between the student and teacher, and what additional supervision is needed at these positions? Through cross-sampling, we find that divergence-based routing more effectively pinpoints positions contributing to the teacher-student performance gap than entropy-based routing. Further analysis reveals teacher-mode under-coverage at high Jensen-Shannon (JS) divergence positions, where standard OPD increases the large teacher-student probability gaps. Motivated by these findings, we propose Divergence-Routed On-Policy Distillation (DrOPD). DrOPD retains RKL supervision at all positions and selectively adds forward Kullback-Leibler (FKL) divergence supervision at positions with high JS divergence. Experiments across six math benchmarks show that DrOPD improves over standard OPD and entropy-based routing. DrOPD also reduces severe under-coverage cases by 37.9 percent relative to OPD, supporting targeted FKL as an effective complement to OPD.
papers.ja_title: 教師とのずれが大きい位置を狙う分布蒸留手法 DrOPD
papers.summary: 学生モデルを教師モデルの軌道に沿って学習させるオンポリシー蒸留 (OPD) は、逆 KL ダイバージェンスだけでは学生が低い確率しか割り当てていない重要なトークンへの補正が弱いという課題がある。DrOPD は交差サンプリングでダイバージェンスに基づき問題箇所を特定し、Jensen-Shannon ダイバージェンスが高い位置にだけ順 KL の監督を追加する手法を提案した。6 つの数学ベンチマークで通常の OPD やエントロピーに基づく位置選択を上回り、教師の分布をカバーしきれない重大な事例を OPD 比で 37.9% 減らした。
papers.why: 蒸留で「どこを補正すべきか」を定量的に特定する手法を示しており、LLM の効率的な学習・蒸留パイプラインを作る人に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: On-policy distillation (OPD), which trains a student along its own trajectories by minimizing reverse KL divergence, gives weak corrective signal at teacher-supported tokens the student assigns very low probability to. DrOPD uses cross-sampling to identify these consequential positions via divergence-based routing, found more effective than entropy-based routing, and adds forward KL supervision selectively at positions with high Jensen-Shannon divergence. Across six math benchmarks, DrOPD improves over standard OPD and entropy-based routing, and reduces severe teacher-mode under-coverage cases by 37.9% relative to OPD.
papers.why_en: Offers a principled, measurable way to decide where extra supervision matters most in distillation, directly useful for anyone building efficient LLM distillation/post-training pipelines.

papers.title: PA1-OPD: One-Step Prefix-Augmented On-Policy Distillation for Language Model Pretraining
papers.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) improves language-model pretraining by matching teacher distributions at corpus prefixes, but provides no direct supervision at contexts induced by student predictions. We introduce PA1-OPD, which augments corpus-path distillation with teacher feedback after one student-sampled transition per selected prefix. This expands the supervised states while retaining next-token prediction and corpus-path KD. Data-anchored roots support parallel sampling, and differentiable tree attention shares prefix computation without changing inference. In two continued-pretraining settings, full coverage improves held-out cross-entropy over KD across C4, PG-19, and Pile at every evaluated checkpoint. In Stage2, selecting the 10% of roots with highest student surprisal adds 48.85% to KD's Macro cross-entropy gain over next-token training. Gains remain when branch supervision excludes successor states already on the corpus path, supporting the value of feedback beyond observed contexts. Additional depth or breadth improves aggregate results at unchanged per-term supervision weight, with benefits varying by corpus. These findings support local student-induced supervision as a complement to pretraining distillation.
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 事前学習の蒸留を一歩先の文脈まで広げる PA1-OPD
papers.summary: 通常の知識蒸留 (KD) は学習データの文脈だけで教師の分布に合わせるため、学生が自分で生成した先の文脈には直接の指導が与えられない。PA1-OPD は選んだ文脈ごとに学生が 1 回サンプリングした続きに対して教師の指導を追加し、差分計算可能な木構造の注意機構で計算コストを抑える手法を提案した。C4・PG-19・Pile の継続事前学習で全チェックポイントにわたり通常の KD より保留データの交差エントロピーを改善し、学生の驚き度が高い文脈の上位 10% だけを選んでも KD に対する改善幅を 48.85% 増やした。
papers.why: 事前学習時の蒸留に、学生が実際に迷う地点への追加指導を低コストで組み込むアイデアは、大規模言語モデルの学習効率化に直接活かせる。
papers.summary_en: Standard knowledge distillation (KD) during pretraining matches teacher distributions only at corpus prefixes, giving no direct supervision at contexts induced by the student's own predictions. PA1-OPD adds teacher feedback after one student-sampled transition per selected prefix, using data-anchored roots for parallel sampling and differentiable tree attention to share prefix computation without changing inference. In continued-pretraining on C4, PG-19, and Pile, full coverage improves held-out cross-entropy over KD at every checkpoint, and selecting the 10% of roots with highest student surprisal adds 48.85% to KD's cross-entropy gain over next-token training.
papers.why_en: Cheaply injecting teacher guidance exactly at the contexts where the student is likely to err is a directly usable idea for improving large-scale pretraining distillation efficiency.

papers.title: Risk-Controlled DFT Selection for Machine-Learned Interatomic Potentials
papers.abstract: Automated materials discovery requires evaluating large pools of candidate configurations, with density functional theory (DFT) as a major throughput bottleneck. Pretrained machine-learned interatomic potentials (MLIPs) approximate DFT cheaply, but their errors vary by orders of magnitude across configurations, making it difficult to decide when to trust the MLIP predictions and when to fall back to DFT. We frame this decision as a risk-controlled selection problem and solve it within a conformal risk control (CRC) framework. Each configuration is mapped from atomic numbers and Cartesian coordinates to a fixed geometric descriptor, which a lightweight predictor uses to estimate an MLIP-DFT disagreement score in energy, average force, and maximum force. CRC then calibrates this score into a selection threshold for DFT labeling such that the MLIP error on the unselected configurations, which keep their MLIP labels, stays below a user-chosen fraction $α$ of the expected error. Under an identical guarantee across eight dataset-MLIP pairs, our predictor routes 7% and 14% fewer configurations to DFT at $α=0.3$ than committee baselines. Because committee disagreement overlooks errors the MLIPs share, our gains are largest when the DFT labels and MLIP training data differ in DFT functional and basis set, and narrow when the two agree. Without model access, the structure-only predictor also ranks errors as well as the target MLIP's latent representation and outperforms widely used descriptors such as Smooth Overlap of Atomic Positions (SOAP) and Atom-Centered Symmetry Functions (ACSF).
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング

papers.title: MFSA: A Multi-Format Systolic Array with Native Micro Scaling Support
papers.abstract: AI workloads increasingly employ low-precision formats such as BF16 / FP16, FP8 variants, FP4, Micro Scaling (MX), and INT modes across models, layers, and execution stages to balance accuracy, memory footprint, and throughput, which in turn requires hardware to support these formats in a flexible and efficient way. We present MFSA, a weight-stationary multi-format systolic array that achieves area efficiency through two architectural choices. At the PE level, MFSA uses dot-product-accumulator-based processing elements extended from an existing open-source trans-precision FPU to support reduced-precision formats (FP32/FP16/BF16/CFP8/FP4/INT16/INT8/INT4) with a shared datapath and proportional throughput scaling. At the array level, MFSA employs Online Block-Scale Rebasing (OBSR) for block-scaled formats, which folds each block scale into the running FP32 partial sum at block boundaries without adding a second cross-block accumulator, thereby reducing the additional overhead of block-scaling support. In TSMC 28 nm at 1 GHz, matched-throughput BF16/FP8/FP4 cascaded FMA-PE baselines are 1.5x/2.5x/4.5x larger than the single-format DPA-PE, the gap growing with subword parallelism. A routed 16x16 MFSA reaches a peak 0.5/1/2/4 TOPS of FP32/BF16/FP8/FP4, and OBSR cuts the incremental MX overhead by 64.2% in area and 67.5% in energy versus a naive MX implementation baseline, without hurting the numerical stability on real LLM traces. Adding support for all other formats based on a BF16+CFP8 systolic array costs 25.7% additional area. OBSR also extends to non-power-of-two block scales: folding the fractional part of an E4M3 scale into the MFPE dot product supports NVFP4 alongside OCP MX for 11.8% area and 7.3% power over a CFP8+FP4 base, less than half the cost of a naive implementation.
papers.ja_title: 多フォーマット対応シストリックアレイ MFSA
papers.summary: AI 向けのチップは BF16 や FP8、FP4 など複数のビット幅 (精度) に対応する必要があるが、精度ごとに別回路を用意すると面積が増えてしまうという困りごとがある。本研究は共有のデータパスを持つ演算器と、ブロックごとの倍率をその場で足し込む OBSR という仕組みを使い、1 つの 16x16 アレイで FP32/BF16/FP8/FP4 を最大 4 TOPS まで扱えるようにした。28nm 設計では、同じ性能の従来方式に比べ面積が最大 4.5 倍小さく、MX 形式への対応で生じる追加コストも面積 64.2%・エネルギー 67.5% 削減できた。
papers.why: 低精度推論チップの回路設計で、精度ごとの専用回路を避けつつ面積・電力を抑える具体的な手法を示しており、カーネル・低精度分野のハード設計者に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: AI chips must support many precisions (BF16, FP8, FP4, MX, INT) but separate per-format datapaths blow up chip area. MFSA uses a shared dot-product-accumulator PE and an "Online Block-Scale Rebasing" (OBSR) scheme that folds block scales into the running FP32 sum, letting a single 16x16 systolic array hit up to 4 TOPS across FP32/BF16/FP8/FP4. In TSMC 28nm, matched-throughput per-format baselines are up to 4.5x larger, and OBSR cuts MX-format overhead by 64.2% in area and 67.5% in energy versus a naive implementation.
papers.why_en: Gives concrete area/power-efficient circuit techniques for natively supporting many low-precision formats in a systolic array, useful to hardware designers working on low-precision inference kernels.

papers.title: ReGRA: Residual-Gradient Adaptation for Complementary Low-Rank Fine-Tuning
papers.abstract: Low-rank adaptation (LoRA) enables parameter-efficient fine-tuning by learning low-rank weight updates. Increasing rank expands adaptation capacity, but does not guarantee that all learned directions improve downstream performance. In a diagnostic experiment with rank-16 LoRA, we show that retaining only the top singular components achieves the best performance, whereas adding further components degrades it. Motivated by this, we propose Residual-Gradient Adaptation (ReGRA), a two-stage method for making more effective use of a fixed rank budget. After the first stage, ReGRA estimates task gradients on a calibration set and removes their projections onto the two-sided subspace induced by the first-stage update. It then aggregates the residual-gradient directions to initialize a second-stage adapter without changing the first-stage update. An orthogonality regularizer encourages the two updates to capture complementary directions. Both updates can be merged into the pretrained weights, incurring no additional inference overhead. Across diverse benchmark sets, ReGRA achieves stronger performance than alternatives with the same total rank and even matches LoRA adapters with twice the rank. Ablation studies and further analysis support the contribution of its core design choices. Code is available at https://github.com/Fanyao-Li/ReGRA.
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: LoRA のランクを使い切る: 勾配残差で補い合う ReGRA
papers.summary: LoRA (低ランクに絞った追従学習) はランクを増やすほど調整力が増えるはずだが、実際には上位の特異成分だけを残した方が性能が良く、成分を増やすと逆に悪化することが分かった。そこで ReGRA は、1 段目の更新がまだ捉えていない勾配方向だけを取り出して 2 段目のアダプタを初期化し、直交性を促す正則化で 2 つの更新が重ならないようにする。同じ総ランク数の既存手法より性能が高く、ランクを 2 倍にした単純な LoRA と同等の性能に達した。
papers.why: 固定の計算・メモリ予算 (ランク数) の中で学習効率を上げる具体策であり、パラメータ効率的な微調整を使う人にとってランクの使い方を見直す視点を与える。
papers.summary_en: Increasing LoRA rank should boost adaptation capacity, but the authors find that keeping only the top singular components of a rank-16 LoRA update gives the best performance while adding more components hurts it. ReGRA addresses this by estimating task gradients, removing parts already captured by the first-stage update, and using the residual directions to initialize a second-stage adapter with an orthogonality regularizer. Across benchmarks, ReGRA beats same-total-rank alternatives and even matches LoRA adapters with twice the rank.
papers.why_en: Offers a concrete way to use a fixed rank budget more effectively in parameter-efficient fine-tuning, relevant to anyone optimizing training efficiency under compute/memory constraints.

papers.title: New Model, Old Habits: Behavior Transfer under Model Swapping in Multi-Session LLM Agents
papers.abstract: Multi-session agents can switch between LLMs to balance performance and inference cost. Such switches require transferring a history for continuity, yet their effects on the recipient remain underexplored. Through controlled experiments with multi-session tasks, we uncover behavior transfer: recipients tend to adopt reasoning and action patterns from the models that generated their histories. This effect is most evident with raw-history transfer but is substantially reduced by summarization. Based on these findings, we propose Direction- and Authorship-aware Summarization of History (DASH) that preserves stronger-model behavior while minimizing weak-to-strong transfer via summarization. Experiments with repeated swaps show that DASH outperforms raw-history transfer and naive summarization baselines. These results suggest that effective multi-model orchestration requires considering not only which model to use, but also which behavioral patterns to carry forward.

papers.title: Articulation Upper Bounds for Language Models
papers.abstract: Language captures only a subset of the perceptions, intuitions and intents that form meaning between speakers. What, then, are the limits of language? We take steps towards measuring this in LLMs as follows: for a set of concepts, we measure how well each concept can be transmitted between two LLMs as their capabilities scale. This requires novel measurement tools: (1) optimal messages: we introduce a prompt optimization algorithm that beats existing algorithms by up to 14% on benchmarks and accurately estimates prompt upper bounds. (2) A transmission measure: the sender is asked to label text; the receiver then tries to recover the sender's prompt, and recovery is measured; we find this correlates strongly with human label error. With these measures, we use observational scaling laws to study how transmissibility of a concept, conveyed with optimal messages, increases as transmitter and receiver capacity grows: does it asymptote below or above a threshold? Measuring 1.2k concepts in eight domains, we find concepts that (a) can be fully articulated; these concepts usually depend on local patterns, e.g. "joke ends with surprise"; (b) might be articulated by future, stronger models; these rely on whole-text structural patterns, e.g. "story's worldbuilding coherence"; (c) concepts that face articulability limits; these concepts' meaning, we find, is tied to identity and social-group awareness, e.g. "comic voice". Interesting, these same concepts are not all challenging for humans: humans have moderate-to-high levels of agreement in 76% of concepts that LLMs struggle with; articulation limits, we find, are executor relative. Finally, we characterize the nature of improvement in each case: while recoverable concepts can be articulated through definitions and explanations, irrecoverable concepts cannot be transmitted, even with examples, and might require novel learning mechanisms.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング

papers.title: Discriminative Score Function: Turning Pretrained Models into Functional Generative Priors
papers.abstract: Discriminative models are trained with task-specific objectives such as classification, detection, or representation learning, yet their practical utility depends on generalizing beyond the training task to unseen samples from the same domain. This suggests that a discriminative model may retain an implicit trace of the data manifold beyond its task labels. We ask whether this trace can be exposed as a generative signal without task-specific guidance. We introduce the Discriminative Score Function (DSF), which extracts an image-space generative field from the loss-gradient geometry of a pretrained discriminative model. DSF provides a training-free update rule that moves images toward model-consistent visual regions without retraining or task-specific targets. We apply DSF to diverse pretrained discriminative models, including ResNet classifiers, DETR detectors, and DINOv2 ViT encoders. DSF generates unconditional images from noise and supports conditional guidance, editing, inpainting, and explanation through the same field. DSF-generated samples also provide effective zero-shot quantization calibration when real images or labels are unavailable, preserving feature geometry better than data-free calibration baselines. These results show that discriminative training leaves a generative functional signal for synthesis and calibration. Project page: https://junhoo.me/dsf.

papers.title: Qwen-MT-Lumen at WMT2026: Instruction-Specialized Translation via Quality-Aware Training and On-Policy Distillation
papers.abstract: We present Lumen, The open-source model is available at, our submission to the WMT 2026 General Machine Translation Shared Task. We focus on instruction-specialized translation, where systems must produce accurate translations while satisfying fine-grained requirements on style, terminology, and structured output. Lumen follows a four-stage pipeline. First, continued pre-training and supervised fine-tuning jointly strengthen multilingual translation competence and the ability to follow translation-specific instructions, such as terminology, style, and format constraints. Second, we extend the originally offline M^{2}PO preference-optimization framework into an online preference-optimization stage: the current policy samples candidate translations, an LLM judge assigns continuous direct-assessment scores, and the resulting multi-pair preferences are used to update the model. Third, on-policy distillation transfers stronger translation-instruction-following behavior from a larger teacher model to the Qwen3-14B student, improving translation-instruction adherence while retaining a 14B primary translation backbone. Finally, structure-aware inference and postprocessing preserve required formats, while selective repair addresses clear structural or decoding failures before submission. We participate in 23 translation directions. Under an absolute 1--5 LLM-judge rubric that evaluates translation-instruction following and translation quality separately, Lumen reaches an overall mean score of 4.60. Despite using a 14B translation backbone, it achieves performance comparable to leading proprietary systems in both translation quality and translation-instruction following.
papers.ja_title: 翻訳特化モデル Lumen: 品質重視学習とオンポリシー蒸留による指示対応翻訳
papers.summary: 機械翻訳では、文体や用語、出力形式といった細かい指示に従いながら正確に訳す必要があるが、小さいモデルではこの両立が難しいという課題がある。Lumen は継続事前学習・指示追従学習に加え、LLM 審判が翻訳を採点してオンラインで好みを学習するオンライン版 M2PO、さらに大きな教師モデルからオンポリシー蒸留で指示追従力を移す、という 4 段階の手順を踏む。23 の翻訳方向で 5 段階評価の平均 4.60 点を達成し、14B というバックボーンながら大手の非公開システムに匹敵する性能を示した。
papers.why: LLM の構造を大きくせずに指示追従能力を強モデルから移す蒸留・オンライン好み学習の手順を具体的に示しており、RL 後学習パイプラインの設計に参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Translation systems must follow fine-grained style/terminology/format instructions while staying accurate, which is hard for smaller models. Lumen uses a four-stage pipeline: continued pretraining plus instruction SFT, an online extension of the M2PO preference-optimization framework scored by an LLM judge, on-policy distillation from a larger teacher into a Qwen3-14B student, and structure-aware post-processing. Across 23 translation directions, Lumen reaches an overall mean score of 4.60 on a 1-5 LLM-judge rubric and, despite its 14B backbone, performs comparably to leading proprietary systems.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates a concrete recipe for transferring instruction-following strength from a larger teacher via on-policy distillation plus online preference optimization, useful for designing RL-style post-training pipelines without scaling up model size.

papers.title: More Methods, Better Agents? A Reality Check on Self-Distillation in Agentic Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Self-distillation in agentic reinforcement learning has produced a growing number of methods. However, existing evaluations often reuse published baseline scores under differing experimental conditions, provide few direct comparisons among contemporaneous methods, and give limited attention to training stability and computational cost. These limitations obscure the source of reported gains and the practical strengths and weaknesses of competing methods. Costly agent training further motivates a common basis for comparison. To address these gaps, we compare ten representative methods against GRPO on ALFWorld, ScienceWorld, Search-QA, and WebShop across three model sizes. Our study comprises 132 training runs totaling 12,124.4 recorded H800 GPU-hours, with repeated evaluations over eight rollout seeds for the pretrained backbones and all eleven trained methods. Beyond final task performance, we examine training progress, stability, and measured computational cost. Our evaluation yields three key findings. First, gains over GRPO remain limited in scope, with no method consistently outperforming it across settings. Second, strong final performance can mask unstable training. Third, additional training cost does not consistently translate into better performance. We establish this benchmark to support fair, comprehensive comparison and guide future research toward reliable and cost-effective improvements in agent training. Project page: https://aim-uofa.github.io/Self-Distillation-AgentRL/
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: エージェント型強化学習の自己蒸留手法、本当に GRPO より良いのか: 大規模比較で検証
papers.summary: エージェント向けの強化学習では自己蒸留を使う手法が次々と提案されているが、それぞれ異なる条件で比較され、学習の安定性や計算コストはあまり検証されていない、という問題がある。本研究は代表的な 10 手法と基本手法 GRPO を、4 つのタスク・3 つのモデルサイズで揃えて比較し、合計 132 回の学習・12,124.4 GPU 時間 (H800) をかけて評価した。結果、GRPO より一貫して優れる手法はなく、最終性能が高く見えても学習が不安定な場合があり、計算コストを増やしても性能向上につながらない場合が多いことが分かった。
papers.why: 手法同士を同じ条件で比較する評価基盤を示し、計算コストと安定性も含めて本当に良くなっているかを見極める観点を与える。
papers.summary_en: Agentic-RL self-distillation methods keep multiplying, but they're often evaluated under different conditions with little direct head-to-head comparison and little attention to training stability or compute cost. This work compares ten representative methods against GRPO across four tasks and three model sizes, running 132 training runs totaling 12,124.4 H800 GPU-hours with repeated seeds. They find no method consistently beats GRPO, strong final scores can hide unstable training, and extra training cost doesn't reliably buy better performance.
papers.why_en: Provides a fair, controlled benchmark for agentic-RL self-distillation methods that accounts for stability and compute cost, offering a methodological lesson in how to evaluate "better" training methods honestly.

review.note: 公表済みのベースライン数値をそのまま使わず、同じ条件・同じ回数の実験で手法を再比較し、最終性能だけでなく学習の安定性と計算コストも合わせて評価するという測り方の観点。
review.note_en: A methodological lesson in re-running baselines under matched conditions rather than reusing published numbers, and evaluating training stability and compute cost alongside final performance.

papers.title: JetSpec++: Foresight Parallel Drafting with Self Refinements
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding's effectiveness is governed by two quantities: the acceptance rate of drafted tokens and the cost of producing them. We show the two objectives can be co-optimized with algorithm-system co-design, and present JetSpec++, which retains a strong learned draft model while hiding its cost almost entirely. JetSpec++ combines three components: intra-block self refinement, which trains the draft model to iteratively correct its own parallel predictions within a block of tokens; inter-block foresight drafting, which begins the next block before the current one is verified; and pipelined drafting and verification, which overlaps the two stages so drafting's marginal wall-clock cost approaches zero. In comparison with state-of-the-art speculative decoding methods, JetSpec++ attains a wall-clock speedup of up to $7.45\times$ over autoregressive (AR) decoding and $1.54\times$ over DSpark, with up to 1,361 tokens per second for a single request on GB200, and an average acceptance length of 8.94 across seven benchmarks, while preserving the target model's output distribution. Our code and models are available at https://github.com/hao-ai-lab/JetSpec.
papers.ja_title: JetSpec++: 下書きコストをほぼゼロにする先読み型投機的デコーディング
papers.summary: 投機的デコーディング (候補トークンをまとめて作って検証する高速化手法) では、候補の採用率とその生成コストの両方が速度を決めるが、両立は難しいという課題がある。JetSpec++ は、下書きモデルがブロック内で自分の予測を直し続ける仕組み、前のブロックの検証が終わる前に次のブロックの下書きを始める仕組み、下書きと検証を重ねて実行する仕組みを組み合わせ、下書きの実質コストをほぼゼロにした。通常のトークンずつの生成 (自己回帰) に比べ最大 7.45 倍、最新手法 DSpark 比でも 1.54 倍速く、GB200 上で 1 リクエストあたり毎秒最大 1,361 トークンを達成した。
papers.why: 出力分布を変えずに推論を高速化する投機的デコーディングの実装上の工夫 (パイプライン化・自己修正下書き) を示し、推論サービング基盤の高速化策として直接使える。
papers.summary_en: Speculative decoding's speed depends on both the acceptance rate of drafted tokens and the cost of producing them, and the two are hard to optimize together. JetSpec++ combines intra-block self-refinement (the draft model iteratively corrects its own parallel predictions), inter-block foresight drafting (starting the next block before the current one is verified), and pipelined drafting/verification, pushing drafting's marginal wall-clock cost toward zero. It reaches up to a 7.45x speedup over autoregressive decoding and 1.54x over DSpark, with up to 1,361 tokens/second for a single request on GB200, while preserving the target model's output distribution.
papers.why_en: Shows concrete algorithm-system co-design tricks (self-correcting drafts plus pipelining) to speed up speculative decoding without changing output distribution, directly applicable to inference-serving infrastructure.

papers.title: ActionOPD: Distilling Decisions, Not Tokens
papers.abstract: Distilling capable language-model agents into smaller models requires aligning the student's behavior with the teacher's. This raises a fundamental question: at which states and at what granularity should this alignment be performed? Offline imitation provides dense but token-specific supervision and can suffer from state-distribution mismatch. Token-level on-policy distillation (OPD) addresses this mismatch but typically requires teacher token probabilities and compatible tokenization. We argue that semantic actions provide a natural unit of supervision for agent distillation. We introduce ActionOPD, an action-level on-policy distillation method motivated by maximizing expected teacher-action likelihood at student-encountered states. At each such state, ActionOPD samples actions from both the student and a black-box teacher, rewarding student actions according to their semantic agreement with the sampled teacher actions. Through policy optimization, ActionOPD aligns the student's action-level behavior with the teacher's decisions without requiring reproduction of teacher-written reasoning or access to teacher token probabilities. Training Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with two teachers on diverse, curated tool-use tasks yields average gains of 3.3-6.9 percentage points across four out-of-distribution benchmarks. ActionOPD scales favorably with student size and teacher capability, without requiring the teacher and student to share a model family or tokenizer. On $τ^2$-bench, ActionOPD achieves competitive performance against offline distillation and token-level OPD. We further explore Self-ActionOPD with a same-model teacher and privileged context. These results establish ActionOPD as a promising approach to agent distillation.
papers.ja_title: 行動単位で教師に合わせる蒸留手法 ActionOPD
papers.summary: 大きな教師モデルの判断を小さな生徒モデルに写す「蒸留」では、どの粒度で揃えるかが課題である。トークンごとに揃える従来手法は教師のトークン確率やトークン分割の一致を必要とするが、ActionOPD は「行動 (action)」単位で揃える新しい方法を提案し、生徒と教師の行動の意味的な一致度を報酬として強化学習的に最適化する。Qwen3-4B と Qwen3-8B を 2 種類の教師で学習したところ、4 つの未知のベンチマークで平均 3.3〜6.9 ポイントの性能向上を達成した。
papers.why: モデルファミリーやトークナイザが異なる教師・生徒間でも使える蒸留法として、エージェント蒸留の基盤に利用できる。
papers.summary_en: Distilling a teacher language-model agent into a smaller student requires choosing the right granularity for behavior alignment; token-level on-policy distillation needs teacher token probabilities and compatible tokenization. ActionOPD instead aligns at the level of semantic actions, sampling actions from both student and black-box teacher and rewarding the student for semantic agreement via policy optimization, without needing teacher token probabilities or a shared tokenizer. Training Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B with two teachers yields average gains of 3.3-6.9 percentage points across four out-of-distribution benchmarks, scaling favorably with student size and teacher capability.
papers.why_en: Offers an agent-distillation recipe that works across model families and tokenizers, giving a new building block for training small deployable agents from strong teachers.

papers.title: Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon
papers.abstract: Memory-efficient subspace optimization has emerged as a practical approach to reducing the memory cost of LLM training while preserving optimization performance. Previous algorithms typically rely on the leading singular subspace of stochastic gradients, yet the gradient noise may dominate the subspace in later training stages and can prevent convergence. To overcome this limitation, we adopt a residual correction framework, which maintains the optimizer states in the subspace and adds the orthogonal residual gradient to the parameter update. We first integrate this scheme into momentum SGD to develop SMRC, which attains an $O(T^{-1/4})$ convergence rate for a fixed orthonormal basis, matching that of full-space momentum SGD. Our analysis introduces a subspace virtual iterate to resolve the coupling between the momentum and the residual correction. Furthermore, we extend SMRC to a multi-stage variant which periodically recomputes bases to track the evolving dominant subspace and retains the same rate. Since each basis refresh breaks the consistency of the virtual iterates, we devise a boundary correction approach that aligns them across stages. Beyond momentum SGD, we incorporate our framework into Muon and propose PMRC, which applies the matrix sign to the projected momentum. Through a weighted momentum tracking analysis that accounts for the residual gradient, we establish an $O(T^{-1/4})$ convergence rate for PMRC, which matches the rate of full-space Muon. We also design a multi-stage PMRC with periodically refreshed bases, which maintains a convergence rate of the same order. Extensive experimental results confirm the effectiveness and efficiency of our algorithms.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 残差補正で省メモリ最適化を Momentum SGD から Muon へ拡張
papers.summary: LLM の学習でメモリを節約する部分空間最適化は、学習の後半でノイズが部分空間を支配し収束を妨げる問題があった。本研究は部分空間に加えて直交した残差勾配もパラメータ更新に加える「残差補正」の枠組みを提案し、Momentum SGD 向けの SMRC と Muon 向けの PMRC を設計、どちらも通常の全空間最適化と同じ O(T^{-1/4}) の収束速度を理論的に保証した。基底を周期的に更新する多段階版も同じ収束速度を保つことを示した。
papers.why: 省メモリ最適化の理論的な弱点を補正しつつ、Muon のような新しい最適化手法にも収束保証付きで拡張できる点が実務上重要。
papers.summary_en: Memory-efficient subspace optimization for LLM training can fail to converge once gradient noise dominates the leading subspace in later training stages. The authors propose a residual-correction framework that keeps optimizer states in the subspace while adding the orthogonal residual gradient to the update, yielding SMRC for momentum SGD and PMRC for Muon, both proven to match the O(T^{-1/4}) convergence rate of their full-space counterparts, including multi-stage variants with periodically refreshed bases.
papers.why_en: Fixes a known convergence weakness of memory-efficient subspace optimizers and extends the approach with matching guarantees to Muon, relevant to anyone building memory-constrained LLM training pipelines.

papers.title: LatentLoop: Scaling Looped MoE Models with Asymmetric Compute Allocation
papers.abstract: Looped Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models combine parameter reuse with sparse computation to improve performance under matched budgets. Prior work demonstrates that different loop visits can play different roles even when they share parameters. To probe the contributions of different loop visits, we learn separate residual coefficients in a model that applies a shared block twice, observing a smaller scale in the first visit. Fixed coefficient experiments show that reducing the first visit's scale preserves or improves performance, whereas the same reductions to the second hurt it. This asymmetry motivates us to explore asymmetric compute allocation. We propose \textbf{LatentLoop}, which compresses the first visit's sequence, retains full resolution in the second, and reallocates saved computation to increase the hidden size. We further learn how strongly the first visit updates the full sequence, and share MoE weights across visits while using separate attention parameters to accommodate their different sequence resolutions. Across 15 configurations spanning 1.3B--7B parameters, with the largest budget exceeding $10^{21}$ FLOPs, LatentLoop consistently lowers validation NLL. At a fitted NLL of 1.988, predicted compute savings are 19.0\% and 7.9\% relative to vanilla MoE and the looped baseline. It also improves average scores on nine benchmarks at all sizes in 0-shot and 5-shot settings. These results suggest asymmetric compute allocation is a promising direction for looped MoE models.
papers.ja_title: ループ型 MoE で計算配分を非対称にする LatentLoop
papers.summary: パラメータを共有して何度も通す「ループ型 MoE (専門家混合)」モデルでは、1 回目と 2 回目の通過が異なる役割を持つことが分かった。本研究は 1 回目の通過では系列を圧縮して計算量を浮かせ、その分を隠れ層サイズの拡大に回す LatentLoop を提案した。1.3B〜7B パラメータの 15 設定で検証損失 (NLL) を一貫して下げ、NLL 1.988 の地点で通常の MoE に対して 19.0%、ループ版ベースラインに対して 7.9% の計算量削減を予測した。
papers.why: モデル構造の工夫だけで計算効率を上げる手法で、ループ型アーキテクチャを使う際の計算予算設計に直結する知見。
papers.summary_en: Looped MoE models reuse parameters across visits, but the authors observe that different loop visits play asymmetric roles, with the first visit operating at smaller scale. LatentLoop exploits this by compressing the sequence on the first visit and reallocating the saved compute to a larger hidden size while keeping the second visit at full resolution. Across 15 configurations from 1.3B to 7B parameters, it consistently lowers validation NLL, with predicted compute savings of 19.0% versus vanilla MoE and 7.9% versus the looped baseline at matched NLL of 1.988, and improves scores on nine benchmarks at all sizes.
papers.why_en: Shows that asymmetric compute allocation across loop visits, not just looping itself, is a lever for improving compute efficiency in looped MoE architectures, relevant to compute-budget planning for large-scale training.

papers.title: Beyond Correctness: Compute-Responsive Data Selection for Reasoning Model Post-Training
papers.abstract: Reasoning language models increasingly rely on test-time compute scaling, yet most existing work studies how to allocate inference computation while treating the model itself as fixed. We ask a complementary question: can reasoning models be post-trained to make better use of a given amount of test-time compute, and which examples are most useful for this goal? Our key observation is that reasoning problems differ substantially in their response to additional computation. Some are already solved under limited compute, others remain unresolved even after further reasoning, while a distinct subset changes from complete initial failure to success when additional reasoning is provided. We call these compute-responsive (CR) examples and introduce Compute-Responsive Data Selection (CRDS), a post-training data-selection principle that prioritizes examples with empirically demonstrated marginal utility from additional reasoning. On Qwen3-8B, SFT on CR examples recovers 45.3\% of held-out low-compute failures, compared with 40.6\% when training on already-solved examples. The advantage extends beyond the selected CR split: SFT-CR reaches 51.8\% overall accuracy on an independently sampled test distribution, with the gain concentrated on compute-responsive problems. CR training also shifts the compute--accuracy frontier across inference budgets from 512 to 4,096 tokens, outperforming matched non-CR training throughout and reaching 48.1\% recovery at the largest budget. The same pattern is supported across multiple data sources, remains visible under on-policy distillation, and extends to Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct when CR sets are reconstructed separately for that model. Better test-time compute utilization can therefore be learned through post-training, with recoverable responses to additional reasoning providing a particularly informative signal for selecting training examples.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 推論に反応する問題を選んで事後学習する CRDS
papers.summary: 推論言語モデルの事後学習では、問題が正解かどうかだけでなく、追加の推論計算でどれだけ性能が変わるかに着目した。追加の推論で失敗から成功に変わる「計算反応性 (compute-responsive)」な問題を優先して選ぶ CRDS を提案し、Qwen3-8B でこのデータだけを学習すると、保留データの低計算失敗の 45.3% を回復し、既に解けている問題で学習した場合の 40.6% を上回った。独立なテスト分布でも全体精度 51.8% を達成し、推論予算 512〜4096 トークンの範囲で常に非 CR 学習を上回った。
papers.why: 正解率だけでなく「追加計算への反応性」という基準でデータを選ぶ発想は、テスト時計算の活用効率を測る評価設計や学習データ選定の参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Reasoning models respond unevenly to extra test-time compute: some problems are already solved, some never get solved, and a distinct subset flips from complete failure to success given more reasoning. The authors introduce Compute-Responsive Data Selection (CRDS), prioritizing these "compute-responsive" examples for post-training; on Qwen3-8B, SFT on CR examples recovers 45.3% of held-out low-compute failures versus 40.6% for training on already-solved examples, reaches 51.8% overall accuracy on an independent test set, and shifts the compute-accuracy frontier favorably from 512 to 4,096 token budgets.
papers.why_en: Proposes a selection signal beyond correctness—empirically measured marginal utility of extra reasoning—offering a reusable criterion for curating post-training data and evaluating test-time compute utilization.

papers.title: TreeSpark: Learning to Draft the Trees You Verify for Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Parallel drafters such as DFlash and DSpark reduce proposal latency, but early mismatches limit how much of each block can be accepted. Retaining alternatives introduces parent states and candidate choices that reference-conditioned training does not directly supervise. We introduce TreeSpark, a unified training and inference framework extending the semi-autoregressive DSpark architecture. It constructs parent-conditioned candidate trees from one backbone pass and replays their expansion, pruning, and budgeted packing during training. Survival negative log-likelihood weights retained edges by reference-derived path mass, while a capped coverage hinge promotes target-important alternatives near local selection boundaries. Both objectives reuse reference-chain target distributions without additional target forward passes. We evaluate greedy decoding with Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B on nine general benchmarks and six writing domains. Across targets and suites, TreeSpark improves mean acceptance length over DSpark by 23.4% to 31.6% and mean single-request throughput by 15.1% to 25.0%. Batched Qwen3-4B throughput improves by 12.6% to 17.2%. At fixed attention capacity and inference policy, the proposed supervision further improves mean acceptance length by approximately 6.4% and mean system throughput by 4.2% to 5.0% on Qwen3-4B.
papers.ja_title: 検証木に合わせてドラフトを学習する TreeSpark
papers.summary: 並列ドラフト方式の投機的デコーディングは提案の遅延を減らせるが、途中で予測がずれるとブロック全体の採用率が下がる問題がある。TreeSpark は 1 回のバックボーン計算から親状態に条件づけた候補木を作り、その展開・刈り込み・予算付きパッキングを学習時にも再現し、採用されなかった枝にも教師分布由来の重みを与えて学習する。Qwen3-4B と Qwen3-8B での評価で、DSpark に対し平均採択長を 23.4〜31.6%、単一リクエストのスループットを 15.1〜25.0% 改善した。
papers.why: 投機的デコーディングのドラフト学習に木構造の教師信号を正しく与える手法で、推論サービングの高速化に直結する。
papers.summary_en: Parallel drafters for speculative decoding reduce proposal latency, but early mismatches limit how much of each block gets accepted. TreeSpark builds parent-conditioned candidate trees from a single backbone pass and replays their expansion, pruning, and budgeted packing during training, weighting retained and alternative edges by reference-derived path mass without extra teacher forward passes. On Qwen3-4B and Qwen3-8B, it improves mean acceptance length over DSpark by 23.4% to 31.6% and single-request throughput by 15.1% to 25.0%, with batched throughput gains of 12.6% to 17.2%.
papers.why_en: Provides correctly-structured tree supervision for training speculative decoding drafters, directly relevant to speeding up LLM inference serving.

papers.title: Cross-Model In-Context Neurofeedback Reveals (Limited) Activation Control in LLMs
papers.abstract: Probes on activation vectors are widely used to detect misbehavior in language models, but their success relies on the assumption that models cannot control what their activations encode. Humans can learn, through neurofeedback, to control the firing of even single neurons, and recent studies investigated whether this ability extends to language models, reaching conflicting conclusions. No experimental design so far disentangles competence at the task from genuine access to one's own activations. We fill this gap with in-context neurofeedback sessions, in which a "subject" model is asked to maximize (or minimize) a score derived from its activations, shown back to it at every turn. In our first experiment, the sentences are generated either by the subject or by a second "writer" model, while the score always derives from the activations of the subject. We test ten open-weight models from five families, with sizes from 9B to 32B. Some models move their own scores considerably, but no more than a writer of comparable competence moves them. Is this because the task requires no privileged access, or because the subject controls its activations while processing the sentences, whoever wrote them? To answer this, we prefill a fixed sentence as the subject's reply at every turn and ask it to increase or decrease the score. Three out of ten models show small but consistent control effects. We further ask whether models can control their activations to the point of fooling an activation monitor. We make models repeat sentences a monitor would flag, such as a deceptive answer for a deception monitor, and ask them to raise or lower the monitor's score. No model learns to lower it, but one model can raise it. In-context control of a model's own activations might not yet be a threat to activation monitors, but it exists in a few models and needs to be tracked as models evolve.

papers.title: TreeFlex: Agents Navigating Their Own Search Trees
papers.abstract: A ReAct-style agent accumulates observations, intermediate results, and failed attempts in a single context. As this context grows, stale and off-path information consumes its limited capacity and obscures relevant evidence, making focused reasoning increasingly difficult. We introduce TreeFlex, a framework in which the agent's own policy decides where to search. The agent records each intermediate state, with a short summary, as a node in a search tree maintained by the harness. The policy is a single language model that acts in two roles. In the Reflection role, it has a global view of the tree through these summaries and picks a node to resume, together with an instruction. In the Execution role, the harness restores the path that led to that node, and the model carries out the instruction with the usual task tools until it saves a new node or proposes a solution, which Reflection then approves or sends back to another node. Through these choices, the policy decides whether to deepen the current line, branch from or revisit an earlier state, verify a proposal, or stop, without a fixed traversal order or a score for each node. We train navigation, task actions, checkpointing, and proposal review jointly with a tree-aware adaptation of GRPO, using task-level outcome rewards augmented by process rewards. After small-scale RL of a 4B model, with the same active-context limit for all methods, TreeFlex reaches 48.8% accuracy on a challenging deep-research benchmark, versus 41.5% for flat ReAct and 42.8% for FoldAgent, and its Pass@8 is about ten points higher than either. On SWE-bench Verified, with all three systems trained with RL from the same 9B model, TreeFlex resolves 54.9% of tasks, versus 43.3% for FoldAgent and 45.2% for its step-wise variant.
papers.ja_title: エージェントが自分の探索木を辿る TreeFlex フレームワーク
papers.summary: ReAct 型のエージェントは観察や失敗履歴を一つの文脈に詰め込むため、文脈が大きくなるほど古い情報が邪魔になり集中した推論が難しくなる。TreeFlex はエージェント自身の方針が探索木のどのノードから再開するかを選ぶ仕組みを導入し、木構造を考慮した GRPO で探索・実行・チェックポイント・提案審査を同時に学習する。4B モデルの小規模 RL 後、深い調査ベンチマークで 48.8% の精度を達成し、フラットな ReAct の 41.5%、FoldAgent の 42.8% を上回った。SWE-bench Verified でも 9B モデルで 54.9% を解決し、FoldAgent の 43.3% を上回った。
papers.why: 長文脈の劣化を避けつつ木構造の探索を方針学習に組み込む手法で、RL によるエージェント学習基盤の設計に新しい選択肢を与える。
papers.summary_en: A ReAct-style agent's single growing context accumulates stale observations and failed attempts, making focused reasoning harder over time. TreeFlex lets the agent's own policy, acting in Reflection and Execution roles, decide which node of its own search tree to resume, trained jointly with a tree-aware GRPO using outcome plus process rewards. After small-scale RL of a 4B model, TreeFlex reaches 48.8% accuracy on a challenging deep-research benchmark versus 41.5% for flat ReAct and 42.8% for FoldAgent, and resolves 54.9% of SWE-bench Verified tasks at 9B scale versus 43.3% for FoldAgent.
papers.why_en: Offers a way to embed tree-structured search directly into the trained policy rather than a fixed harness, giving a new design option for RL-based agent training infrastructure under limited context.

papers.title: Beyond Expert Rankings: Contrast Calibration for Mixed-Precision MoE Quantization
papers.abstract: Mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models activate only a few experts per token, yet all expert weights must be stored. Mixed-precision quantization reduces this storage cost by assigning higher bit-widths to sensitive experts and lower bit-widths to resilient ones, but expert rankings alone do not determine how strongly to weight their errors. To address this gap, we propose NatScale, a contrast-calibrated allocation framework for mixed-precision MoE quantization. It uses a model-specific power transformation to calibrate gradient-based expert weights to an information-theoretic contrast target while preserving rankings. We jointly evaluate each expert's gate, up and down configurations to estimate its output error. We then combine these errors and calibrated weights with an existing prior based on weight spectra, variance and precision decay to select configurations under a storage budget. Across three models, NatScale achieves the lowest native-to-quantized KL divergence and the highest top-token agreement in all nine settings against five allocation baselines. It also yields the lowest perplexity in seven settings. These findings highlight the importance of objective-aware precision allocation.
papers.ja_title: 専門家の重要度較正で混合精度 MoE 量子化を改善する NatScale
papers.summary: MoE (専門家混合) モデルはトークンごとに少数の専門家しか使わないが、重みは全専門家分を保存する必要があるため、重要な専門家に高い bit 幅を割り当てる混合精度量子化が使われる。しかし専門家の順位だけでは誤差をどの程度重視すべきか分からないため、本研究は勾配ベースの重要度を情報理論的な対比目標に較正する NatScale を提案した。3 モデル・9 設定すべてで量子化前後の KL ダイバージェンスと上位トークンの一致率が最良となり、7 設定で困惑度 (perplexity) も最良だった。
papers.why: 量子化の割り当て基準を単なる順位から較正済みの重み付けに変える発想は、低精度カーネル設計やメモリ削減の実装者に直接役立つ。
papers.summary_en: MoE language models activate only a few experts per token but must still store all expert weights, so mixed-precision quantization assigns higher bit-widths to sensitive experts—yet expert rankings alone don't say how strongly to weight their errors. NatScale calibrates gradient-based expert weights to an information-theoretic contrast target via a model-specific power transformation while preserving rankings, jointly estimating gate, up, and down configuration errors. It achieves the lowest native-to-quantized KL divergence and highest top-token agreement in all nine settings across three models against five allocation baselines, and the lowest perplexity in seven settings.
papers.why_en: Replaces rank-only precision allocation with a calibrated, objective-aware weighting scheme, directly useful for anyone designing mixed-precision quantization for memory-constrained MoE deployment.

papers.title: FOLD: Position-Free Far Memory with Local Order for Long-Context Speculative Decoding
papers.abstract: Speculative decoding accelerates LLM generation through lightweight drafting and parallel verification. It is particularly promising for long inputs, where KV-cache access costs can be amortized over multiple accepted tokens. Yet most drafters are trained on short sequences and degrade on long inputs, while long-context training is costly. Existing training-free approaches restrict the context window, rescale positions, or augment recent context with retrieved distant entries. Drafters, however, read target hidden states that already encode contextual and positional information, and their lightweight architecture makes full-history attention affordable. We propose FOLD, a training-free method that preserves exact local positions and treats all distant entries as far memory at a shared position. To counter attention dilution as the memory grows, we sharpen attention within it to emphasize relevant entries while separately controlling its total weight relative to the local window. Across six target-drafter pairs and diverse benchmarks of up to 256K tokens, FOLD predominantly delivers the highest speedup, with the best case more than doubling the speedup over autoregressive decoding, from 2.08$\times$ to 4.22$\times$.
papers.ja_title: FOLD: 長文脈でも投機的デコードを速くする学習不要の遠距離メモリ手法
papers.summary: 投機的デコード(speculative decoding、軽量な下書きモデルで候補トークンを作り本体で検証して高速化する手法)の下書きモデルは短い文脈で学習されているため、長い入力では性能が落ちてしまう。FOLD は学習をせずに、近い位置の情報はそのまま保ち、遠い文脈は「far memory」として共有の位置にまとめ、その中のアテンション(注意)を鋭くして重要な部分を強調する手法を提案した。最大 256K トークンの長文ベンチマークで、自己回帰デコードに対する高速化を最良ケースで 2.08 倍から 4.22 倍へと 2 倍以上に伸ばした。
papers.why: 長文脈での投機的デコードを学習なしで高速化できる手法で、実運用の LLM 推論サービング基盤にそのまま適用しやすい。
papers.summary_en: Drafters used in speculative decoding are trained on short sequences and degrade on long inputs, while long-context training is costly. FOLD is a training-free method that preserves exact local positions while treating all distant entries as far memory at a shared position, sharpening attention within that memory to counter attention dilution. Across six target-drafter pairs on benchmarks up to 256K tokens, FOLD predominantly delivers the highest speedup, with the best case more than doubling the speedup over autoregressive decoding from 2.08x to 4.22x.
papers.why_en: A training-free way to accelerate speculative decoding on long contexts, directly applicable to real LLM inference-serving stacks.

papers.title: Cortex: Consolidating Context into Parametric Memory
papers.abstract: Context can improve large language model performance, but these gains may be lost after context removal. Inspired by biological systems consolidation, we formulate Memory Consolidation (MC) as internalizing these gains while preserving non-target capabilities, connecting context-specified editing, skill learning, and behavioral steering under a common objective. We introduce a five-task-family testbed measuring consolidation and retention under single, batch, and sequential updates. We propose Cortex, which generates prospective queries to anticipate uses of context and distills context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural feed-forward network updates. Across 4B--120B dense and mixture-of-experts backbones, including both text-only and multimodal models, Cortex lies on the empirical consolidation--retention Pareto frontier in most evaluated settings. After 50 sequential factual edits on a 14B model, Cortex-Structural recovers 88.9% of the context-induced gain while retaining 99.8% of original non-target performance.
papers.ja_title: Cortex: 文脈で得た効果をパラメータに焼き付ける記憶統合手法
papers.summary: LLM は文脈(context)を与えると性能が上がるが、その文脈を外すと効果も消えてしまう。Cortex は、文脈の使われ方を予想する質問を自動生成し、文脈付きの出力を低ランクまたは FFN(フィードフォワード層)構造の更新に蒸留して、文脈の効果をパラメータ側に定着させる「記憶統合(Memory Consolidation)」手法を提案した。4B〜120B の密モデル・MoE モデルで評価し、14B モデルに 50 回の逐次的な事実編集を行った後も、文脈由来の利得の 88.9% を回復しつつ、元の性能の 99.8% を保持した。
papers.why: 文脈で一時的に得た知識やスキルを恒久的にモデルへ取り込む仕組みで、継続学習・モデル編集の基盤として使える。
papers.summary_en: Context improves LLM performance, but these gains are lost once the context is removed. Cortex formulates this as Memory Consolidation: it generates prospective queries anticipating uses of context and distills context-conditioned outputs into mergeable low-rank or structural FFN updates. Across 4B-120B dense and MoE backbones, Cortex lies on the empirical consolidation-retention Pareto frontier in most settings, and after 50 sequential factual edits on a 14B model, Cortex-Structural recovers 88.9% of the context-induced gain while retaining 99.8% of original non-target performance.
papers.why_en: Offers a way to permanently internalize temporary context-driven gains into model parameters, useful infrastructure for continual learning and model editing.

papers.title: When Does Momentum Help in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards?
papers.abstract: Momentum is a classical tool for accelerating convex optimization and a standard component of modern large language model training. Yet recent empirical work has questioned the usefulness of first-moment momentum in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). We study this question through a bandit formulation of RLVR with bias-corrected exponential moving average (EMA) momentum, where the EMA coefficient $β$ controls how quickly the weights on past gradients decay. When policy gradients are evaluated exactly, we prove that increasing $β$ within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization. When gradients are estimated from sampled responses, a positive expected gain can be obscured by sampling fluctuations. We show that as the learning rate $η$ decreases, the expected gain with fixed $β$ vanishes faster than these fluctuations, whereas increasing $β$ to keep $η/(1-β)$ within the safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain that eventually dominates them. Bandit simulations quantitatively validate these predictions. RLVR experiments on Qwen3-4B-Base using SGD with EMA and AdamW support our principle of choosing larger coefficients in practical LLM post-training. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing $β_1$ improves mean validation accuracy by nearly $2$ percentage points over the conventional choice, demonstrating the principle's effectiveness at a larger model scale.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 検証可能な報酬での強化学習(RLVR)でモーメンタムはいつ効くのか
papers.summary: モーメンタム(過去の勾度を使って更新を加速する手法)は LLM 学習で広く使われるが、検証可能な報酬での強化学習(RLVR)では効果が疑問視されていた。筆者らはバンディット問題としてモデル化し、指数移動平均(EMA)の係数βを「暴走を防ぐ範囲内で大きくすると最適化が速くなる」ことを理論的に示し、サンプルから推定した勾度でも学習率η とβ の比η/(1-β) を安全な範囲に保てば利得が消えないことを示した。Qwen2.5-32B で AdamW のβ1 を単純に大きくするだけで、従来の設定より検証精度が平均で約 2 ポイント改善した。
papers.why: RL 後学習(post-training)でモーメンタム係数をどう選ぶべきかに理論的な裏付けを与え、大規模モデルの実運用設定にそのまま生かせる指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Momentum is standard in LLM training, but recent empirical work has questioned its usefulness in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR). Through a bandit formulation with bias-corrected EMA momentum, the authors prove that increasing the EMA coefficient β within a range that prevents overshoot strictly accelerates optimization, and show that keeping η/(1-β) within a safe regime preserves a nonvanishing gain even under sampled gradients. On Qwen2.5-32B with AdamW, simply increasing β1 improves mean validation accuracy by nearly 2 percentage points over the conventional choice.
papers.why_en: Provides a theoretical basis for choosing momentum coefficients in RL post-training, with a practical guideline that scales to a 32B-parameter model.

papers.title: Generative Representation Learning for Scalable Latent Tokenization
papers.abstract: We introduce an approach for self-supervised representation learning designed to be used as a tokenizer for generative modeling. Our objective supervises a representation loss by factorizing the pointwise mutual information of the data, which we estimate by taking information differences between conditional predictions from a learned generative model. We justify our algorithm theoretically and empirically, demonstrating that our generative approach to representation learning avoids dimensional collapse and feature suppression in cases where commonly used methods like DINO and LeJEPA fail. Moreover, we show our representation learning technique is scalable; expending more compute leads to predictably better latent tokenization. For the first time, we perform a careful analysis of the combined flop efficiency of tokenizer and generative model and demonstrate that our approach is a compute-optimal improvement over direct diffusion for pixel-space generation, obtaining an FID-50K of 2.18 with JiT-L. Applied to ImageNet and the text-to-image dataset GPIC, we show tokenizer encoder scaling laws for diffusability, where extrapolating our approach achieves representations in 7x fewer FLOPs than DINOv2 on ImageNet and 8x fewer FLOPs than WebSSL on GPIC.
topics: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.theme: 学習効率・スケーリング
papers.ja_title: 生成モデルで情報量を見積もり、生成用トークナイザの表現を計算効率よく学ぶ
papers.summary: 生成モデルのトークナイザとして使う自己教師学習の表現を作ろうとすると、DINO や LeJEPA のような既存手法は次元崩壊(表現がつぶれてしまう現象)や特徴抑制を起こすことがある。この研究では、データの点ごとの相互情報量を、学習した生成モデルの条件付き予測の差分として推定する新しい目的関数を提案した。ImageNet とテキスト画像データセット GPIC で、提案手法は DINOv2 より 7 倍少ない計算量(FLOPs)、WebSSL より 8 倍少ない計算量で同等の表現を獲得し、ピクセル空間生成では直接拡散より計算最適で FID-50K 2.18(JiT-L)を達成した。
papers.why: トークナイザと生成モデルの計算量を合わせて最適化するという視点を示し、学習効率・スケーリング則の設計指針として使える。
papers.summary_en: Self-supervised representations intended for use as generative-model tokenizers often suffer from dimensional collapse or feature suppression, as seen with DINO and LeJEPA. The authors propose a generative objective that estimates pointwise mutual information via differences between conditional predictions of a learned generative model, which they show scales predictably with compute. On ImageNet and the text-to-image dataset GPIC, the approach obtains representations in 7x fewer FLOPs than DINOv2 and 8x fewer FLOPs than WebSSL, and for pixel-space generation it is a compute-optimal improvement over direct diffusion, obtaining FID-50K of 2.18 with JiT-L.
papers.why_en: Offers a joint tokenizer-plus-generative-model compute accounting and a scalable alternative to DINO/LeJEPA-style representation learning, informing compute-efficiency and scaling-law design.

papers.title: Latent Compaction with Test-Time Training
papers.abstract: Long contexts enlarge key--value (KV) caches, increasing memory use and attention costs during generation. Compressing these caches must preserve information for unseen questions. We introduce **Latent Compaction**, which learns a compact document-specific cache through test-time training. We initialize cache entries using reconstruction importance, teacher attention, and key-space diversity. Training first fits attention outputs and log-normalizers to those of the full cache, with reconstruction-selected entries held fixed. It then jointly optimizes the entire cache through end-to-end distillation from the full-cache model. Model weights remain frozen throughout, and training uses only generic prompts about the document, without access to downstream questions or answers. Experiments on RULER, LongBench, and Phonebook Lookup demonstrate substantial gains over budget-matched compression baselines. On a RULER, for example, our method achieves 96.7% accuracy at 32$\times$ compression, compared with 40.0% for KVZip+. The method also transfers across model scales and families, with retrieval gains on both Qwen3 and MiniCPM5. These results show that treating the KV cache as a neural network and optimizing it with test-time training can preserve retrieval accuracy under aggressive compression. The code is released at https://www.github.com/THUNLP/latent-compaction
papers.ja_title: KV キャッシュをテスト時に学習して文書ごとに小さく圧縮する Latent Compaction
papers.summary: 長い文脈を扱うと KV キャッシュ(注意機構で使う過去の情報の保存領域)が大きくなり、メモリと計算のコストが増える。Latent Compaction は、モデルの重みを固定したまま、テスト時にその文書専用の小さなキャッシュをアテンション出力の一致と蒸留で学習する手法で、下流の質問や答えは一切使わない。RULER ベンチマークでは 32 倍圧縮時に 96.7% の精度を達成し、既存手法 KVZip+ の 40.0% を大きく上回った。
papers.why: KV キャッシュを「学習対象のニューラルネットワーク」として扱う発想で、長文脈推論のメモリ圧縮をさらに攻める新しい設計の方向を示す。
papers.summary_en: Long contexts enlarge KV caches, increasing memory and attention costs during generation. Latent Compaction learns a compact document-specific cache through test-time training, keeping model weights frozen and using only generic prompts about the document rather than downstream questions. On RULER, the method achieves 96.7% accuracy at 32x compression, compared with 40.0% for KVZip+, and transfers across model families including Qwen3 and MiniCPM5.
papers.why_en: Treating the KV cache itself as a trainable neural network opens a new design direction for aggressive, retrieval-preserving long-context memory compression.

papers.title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
papers.abstract: Computer-use agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in interpreting screens and executing keyboard and mouse actions. However, games, with their visually rich worlds and diverse mechanics, remain challenging and offer a demanding next step toward general digital control. Current game-agent learning pipelines often rely on large-scale demonstrations with limited coverage of dynamic game states, while scalable environments for interactive training remain difficult to obtain. We introduce Player-1, a post-training framework for learning game control beyond demonstrations through synthetic experience. We extend the computer-use action space with relative pointer motion, sustained inputs, and composite actions. For supervised initialization, we fine-tune computer-use models on 6,044 curated gameplay trajectories that pair recorded actions with task instructions and visual reasoning. We construct Player-1-Gym, sixteen synthetic 2D and 3D environments designed around control demands shared across games. Programmatically verifiable rewards and randomized observations and control dynamics support multi-environment reinforcement learning with PPO. The resulting Player-1-9B and Player-1-35B-A3B improve MineDojo-300 success over their SFT policies by 27.8 and 17.7 percentage points, respectively. Player-1-9B reaches 38.33% success compared with 12.63% for the strongest evaluated baseline, with further gains over SFT on ViZDoom-10 and GameWorld. Further analyses show that broader synthetic environment coverage improves transfer, while the use of composite actions that combine multiple keyboard and mouse inputs increases during RL. We demonstrate that learning from synthetic experience substantially improves game control beyond supervised initialization, with gains that generalize beyond the RL training suite.
papers.ja_title: Player-1: 合成環境での経験からゲーム操作を学ぶエージェント
papers.summary: ゲームエージェントの学習は大量の人によるデモンストレーションに頼りがちで、動的な場面を網羅しにくく、対話的に学べる環境もスケールしにくい。Player-1 は、相対ポインタ移動や複合操作を含む拡張された行動空間を使い、まず 6,044 件のゲーム操作データで教師あり学習(SFT)し、その後 16 種類の合成 2D/3D 環境(Player-1-Gym)で検証可能な報酬を使った PPO による多環境強化学習を行う。結果、Player-1-9B/35B は MineDojo-300 の成功率を SFT だけの方策より 27.8/17.7 ポイント改善し、Player-1-9B は 38.33% の成功率で最強ベースラインの 12.63% を大きく上回った。
papers.why: 検証可能な報酬と合成環境を使った多環境 PPO の実運用設計を示し、ゲーム以外の操作系エージェントの RL 後学習基盤構築にも応用できる知見。
papers.summary_en: Game-agent learning pipelines often rely on large-scale demonstrations with limited coverage of dynamic states, while scalable interactive-training environments remain hard to obtain. Player-1 extends the computer-use action space, fine-tunes on 6,044 curated gameplay trajectories for SFT initialization, and then runs multi-environment PPO using programmatically verifiable rewards across 16 synthetic 2D/3D environments (Player-1-Gym). Player-1-9B and Player-1-35B-A3B improve MineDojo-300 success over their SFT policies by 27.8 and 17.7 percentage points respectively, with Player-1-9B reaching 38.33% success versus 12.63% for the strongest baseline.
papers.why_en: Demonstrates a practical multi-environment PPO pipeline with verifiable rewards and synthetic environments, offering transferable lessons for RL post-training infrastructure beyond games.

papers.title: Price of Anarchy of First-Price Auctions in Agentic Markets
papers.abstract: An agentic market is a decentralized serving-time market where AI agents bid to claim each user prompt. An agent's bid is based on its expected value for the prompt, which is the expectation of the reward for its response minus its inference costs. First-price auctions (FPAs), in which the highest bidder pays its bid and receives the prompt, are a natural way to allocate prompts in such a market, since they are simple and transparent to run, and do not require central knowledge of private capabilities and costs. However, FPAs are not truthful: participants may bid less than their true value in the hope of a larger profit, and the prompt may then be allocated to someone other than the bidder who values it the most. This welfare loss is quantified by the $\textit{price-of-anarchy}$ (PoA). In this paper, we argue that agentic markets are likely to possess features that reduce the price-of-anarchy. The first is a $\textit{competitive floor}$, which occurs when multiple bidders usually value the prompt above some baseline share of the optimal welfare (e.g., because the best models are often distilled into cheaper alternatives, which perform similarly). We show that competition among them then limits the welfare loss, which can be driven to zero as the floor rises. The second feature is $\textit{near-independence}$ of values after conditioning on the prompt, which occurs when most of the predictable variation in the expected value is determined by the difficulty of the prompt. As the value distribution approaches conditional independence, we can derive an efficiency guarantee that approaches a factor of $1 - 1/e^2$ of the optimal welfare. Thus, both features give rise to welfare lower bounds that are significantly better than the well-known general case of $1 - 1/e$. We validate these results empirically using auctions with strategic bidders simulated on the EmbedLLM prompt routing dataset.
papers.ja_title: AI エージェント市場でのオークションの非効率さ(price of anarchy)を理論的に抑える
papers.summary: 複数の AI エージェントがユーザのプロンプトを競り合って受け取る「エージェント市場」では、第一価格オークション(最高額提示者がその額を払って獲得する方式)は単純だが、真実の価値どおりに入札するとは限らず、最も価値を生むエージェントに渡らない福祉損失(price of anarchy、PoA)が生じる。この研究は、複数の入札者が最適福祉に近い価値を持つ「競争の下限」と、プロンプトの難易度で条件付けるとほぼ独立になる「準独立性」という 2 つの性質がある市場では PoA が小さく抑えられることを理論的に示し、既知の一般的な下限 1-1/e より良い 1-1/e^2 に近い効率保証を導いた。EmbedLLM のプロンプトルーティングデータを使ったシミュレーションでこれを確かめた。
papers.why: LLM エージェント間でプロンプトを割り振る実運用のオークション/ルーティング設計に、理論的な効率保証を与える。
papers.summary_en: In agentic markets where AI agents bid to claim user prompts, first-price auctions are simple but not truthful, causing welfare loss quantified by the price-of-anarchy (PoA). The authors argue agentic markets tend to have a competitive floor (multiple bidders valuing prompts near the optimal welfare) and near-independence of values conditioned on prompt difficulty, both of which drive PoA well below the known general bound of 1-1/e, approaching 1-1/e^2 under near-independence. They validate these bounds with strategic-bidder auction simulations on the EmbedLLM prompt-routing dataset.
papers.why_en: Gives a theoretical efficiency guarantee for auction-based prompt routing among competing AI agents in serving-time markets.

papers.title: RoLaQ: Joint Rotation and Range Calibration for 2-Bit KV Caches in Multi-Head Latent Attention
papers.abstract: Multi-head latent attention (MLA) compresses the content of a key-value cache into a shared latent per token, making low-bit storage attractive for long-context inference. At two bits, errors in this representation perturb both attention matching and value readout, with effects that depend on error direction and reconstruction scale. We introduce RoLaQ (Rotation-calibrated Latent Quantization), an offline method for joint rotation and range calibration. RoLaQ refines a shared rotation within subspaces defined by the frozen key and value projections, and jointly learns quantization ranges whose thresholds and reconstruction gains are coupled to control the shared signal's response. Prediction matching and attention-output supervision guide calibration with model weights frozen. Across three MLA models and six benchmarks, RoLaQ achieves the highest average accuracy among the compared 2-bit methods both without and with token protection. On DeepSeek-V2-Lite, an SGLang implementation provides 3.96 times the BF16 KV capacity under the same memory budget and 2.51 times its decode throughput with 256K input tokens.
papers.ja_title: RoLaQ: MLA の KV キャッシュを 2 ビットまで量子化する回転・レンジ同時較正
papers.summary: Multi-head latent attention(MLA)は KV キャッシュをトークンごとの共有の潜在表現に圧縮するが、2 ビットまで量子化すると誤差がアテンションの照合と値の読み出しの両方を乱してしまう。RoLaQ は、固定したキー・値の射影が定める部分空間内で共有の回転を精緻化し、量子化のしきい値と再構成の倍率を結びつけてレンジも同時に学習するオフライン較正手法。DeepSeek-V2-Lite では SGLang 実装で同じメモリ予算のもと BF16 の 3.96 倍の KV 容量、256K 入力トークンで 2.51 倍のデコードスループットを達成した。
papers.why: MLA 方式の長文脈 KV キャッシュを 2 ビットまで圧縮しつつ精度を保つ具体的な較正手法で、長文脈推論サービングのメモリ効率に直結する。
papers.summary_en: Multi-head latent attention (MLA) compresses the KV cache into a shared latent per token, but at two bits, quantization errors perturb both attention matching and value readout. RoLaQ is an offline calibration method that refines a shared rotation within subspaces defined by frozen key/value projections and jointly learns quantization ranges whose thresholds and reconstruction gains are coupled. On DeepSeek-V2-Lite, an SGLang implementation provides 3.96x the BF16 KV capacity under the same memory budget and 2.51x its decode throughput at 256K input tokens.
papers.why_en: A concrete rotation-and-range calibration method for pushing MLA-style long-context KV caches down to 2 bits while retaining accuracy, directly relevant to serving-time memory efficiency.

papers.title: On-Policy Residual Learning for Diffusion Language Models
papers.abstract: Residual context is key to unlocking the speed-quality Pareto frontier of diffusion language models (DLMs) by carrying forward predictive distributions across denoising steps. Yet turning this seemingly simple mechanism into an effective learning paradigm is far from simple: there is no clear recipe for how residual context should be learned. We introduce ORL, a framework for on-policy residual learning in DLMs. Algorithmically, we identify that residual learning is inherently on-policy. ORL learns from model-induced residual trajectories on the fly and introduces an entropy-contraction objective that sharpens predictions as the model revisits its own predictions. System-wise, exact residual supervision requires capturing, retaining, and reprocessing many trajectory-dependent states. ORL co-designs the algorithm with asynchronous residual capture and transport, specialized block-diffusion attention, and packed compute-balanced training, making it practical at scale. On a 4B DLM converted from Qwen3-4B, ORL improves tokens per forward (TPF) by up to 6.2x and, with our dlmrt engine, end-to-end throughput by approximately 6.9x at comparable or better quality. In single-request serving on one H100, this mode achieves a stronger speed-quality Pareto frontier than autoregressive models with EAGLE3 and DFlash speculative decoding under both strict and relaxed verification, running 1.74x faster than DFlash at matched accuracy. ORL also transfers to existing DLMs: on LLaDA-2.1-mini, 36 H100-hours and 4.2M self-generated tokens, about 10x less data than prior LLaDA recipes, yield up to 1.5x higher TPF and up to 3x higher throughput at comparable quality, and on DiffusionGemma, ORL raises TPF by 1.1-1.2x. With dlmrt and NVFP4 quantization, ORL models decode a single request at up to 5,046 tokens/s on one B200, 7,708 on eight B200s, and 2,788 on a consumer RTX 5090, with comparable quality.
papers.ja_title: オンポリシー残差学習で拡散言語モデルの生成を高速化
papers.summary: 拡散言語モデル (ノイズを段々取り除いて文章を作る仕組み) は、前のステップの予測分布 (残差コンテキスト) を次のステップに持ち越すと速くなるが、学習方法が定まっていなかった。ORL はモデル自身が生成した軌跡からオンポリシーで残差を学び、エントロピーを縮める目的関数と非同期の残差転送、専用アテンションを組み合わせる。Qwen3-4B から変換した 4B モデルで 1 回の前進で処理するトークン数 (TPF) が最大 6.2 倍、エンドツーエンドのスループットが約 6.9 倍になり、同等以上の品質で DFlash という投機的デコード手法より 1.74 倍速く動いた。LLaDA-2.1-mini では従来より約 10 倍少ないデータで TPF 最大 1.5 倍、スループット最大 3 倍を達成し、NVFP4 量子化と合わせ B200 1 枚で 1 秒あたり 5,046 トークンのデコードを実現した。
papers.why: 拡散言語モデルの推論高速化を狙う研究者・サービング基盤の開発者にとって、残差コンテキストの学習法とシステム設計 (非同期転送・専用アテンション・量子化) をセットで示した実用的な指針になる。
papers.summary_en: Diffusion language models (DLMs) can get faster by carrying forward predictive distributions (residual context) across denoising steps, but there was no clear recipe for learning this residual context. ORL learns residuals on-policy from model-induced trajectories with an entropy-contraction objective, paired with asynchronous residual capture/transport and specialized block-diffusion attention. On a 4B DLM converted from Qwen3-4B, ORL improves tokens-per-forward (TPF) by up to 6.2x and end-to-end throughput by approximately 6.9x at comparable or better quality, running 1.74x faster than DFlash speculative decoding at matched accuracy; on LLaDA-2.1-mini it needs about 10x less data than prior recipes for up to 1.5x higher TPF and 3x higher throughput, and with NVFP4 quantization reaches 5,046 tokens/s on one B200.
papers.why_en: For people building DLM serving stacks, ORL offers a concrete algorithm-plus-system recipe (on-policy residual learning, asynchronous transport, specialized attention, quantization) for pushing the speed-quality frontier.

papers.title: ReasonUni: Reasoning-Augmented Reconstruction Advances Unified Multimodal Models
papers.abstract: Image-to-text (I2T) understanding and text-to-image (T2I) generation are dual tasks in unified multimodal models (UMMs). Reconstructive post-training couples these tasks, but existing reconstruction-based methods remain perception-centric and provide limited supervision for reasoning about structure, intent, and transformation. We propose ReasonUni, a reasoning-augmented reconstructive post-training framework that extends this coupling beyond perception. Given an original image and an editing instruction, the UMM first reasons about what and how to edit and describes the target state, then generates the corresponding target image conditioned on this understanding output. To jointly optimize both modules, we introduce TreeGRPO, a tree-structured reinforcement learning method that samples multiple reasoning paths and candidate images per path, then aggregates visual rewards to update both modules under a unified objective. Experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate consistent gains in both understanding and generation, showing that reasoning-augmented reconstruction yields genuine mutual gains for UMMs.
papers.ja_title: 推論を挟んだ再構成学習で統合マルチモーダルモデルの理解と生成を同時に伸ばす
papers.summary: 画像を理解する力 (I2T) と画像を生成する力 (T2I) を一つのモデルで両立させる統合マルチモーダルモデルは、従来の再構成による事後学習だと見た目の復元 (知覚) ばかり学び、構造や意図を推論する力が伸びにくかった。ReasonUni は編集前の画像と指示から「何をどう変えるか」をまず言葉で推論させてから画像を生成させ、TreeGRPO という木構造の強化学習で複数の推論経路と候補画像をまとめて評価し、理解モジュールと生成モジュールを同じ目的関数で同時に更新する。複数のベンチマークで理解・生成の両方が一貫して向上し、推論を挟んだ再構成が両タスクに本当に良い影響を与えることを示した。
papers.why: 統合マルチモーダルモデルを強化学習で後学習させる際、推論経路と生成結果をまとめて報酬評価する木構造サンプリング (TreeGRPO) は、理解と生成を一体で最適化する RL 基盤の設計例として参考になる。
papers.summary_en: Unified multimodal models (UMMs) couple image understanding (I2T) and generation (T2I), but existing reconstruction-based post-training stays perception-centric and gives limited supervision for reasoning about structure and intent. ReasonUni makes the model first reason in text about what and how to edit, then generate the target image conditioned on that reasoning, and jointly optimizes both modules with TreeGRPO, a tree-structured RL method that samples multiple reasoning paths and candidate images per path and aggregates visual rewards. Across multiple benchmarks the approach yields consistent gains in both understanding and generation, showing genuine mutual benefit from reasoning-augmented reconstruction.
papers.why_en: The tree-structured sampling and joint-objective RL recipe (TreeGRPO) for optimizing both understanding and generation modules together is a useful design reference for RL post-training infrastructure for unified multimodal models.

papers.title: Open-world AI: a Tale of Three Requirements
papers.abstract: The closed world asks AI for specialized competence and lets it manufacture the iid data its theory assumes: a fixed criterion licenses collecting examples until the task is covered. The open world asks for versatility --- taking up tasks a machine was not built for, from few examples and with little prior from a human designer --- and offers data that is grouped, not shuffled. Its tasks are not known in advance, so a machine must do inference-time learning (1st requirement). Modeling tasks as sharing latent factors and decomposing the training objective, we derive two more: a *rich representation*, retaining more than iid generalization requires, and a predictive disentanglement that aligns inputs and outputs into matched low-dimensional groups. The analysis further predicts the need for a consistent inner learner, and the benefit of long contexts spanning related tasks. We test these claims on language models up to 8B, asking whether a model has a property (qualitative) rather than how much it wins (quantitative). Models that meet the requirements improve as data from related tasks accumulates; the rest degrade, and neither scale nor layer-type interleaving repairs this.
